chat: Show only the selected harness's Copilot models in Manage Models (#339840)

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.

Fixes #326538

## Problem

The Manage Models (Language Models) editor can show several groups that
are all labelled **Copilot**. Copilot models come from:

- the regular Copilot provider (`copilot`)
- the Copilot CLI extension (`copilotcli`)
- each agent host harness. The Copilot CLI agent host groups its models
under `copilotcli`; the Claude and Codex agent hosts group theirs under
`copilot`, reaching them through the Copilot subscription (Claude via
its `copilot` transport, Codex via `vscode-proxy`).

Each of these lists only works in its own harness, but they all appear
together with the same label.

## Change

Manage Models now scopes the "Copilot" lists to the harness it was
opened for:

- If the harness publishes its own Copilot models (models with
`targetChatSessionType` equal to the harness), only that list is shown.
- Otherwise, only the regular Copilot models are shown.
- Models from other providers (BYOK, Ollama, OpenRouter, a harness's
non-Copilot groups, …) are unaffected.

How the editor learns the harness:

- The model picker's **Manage Models...** action passes the harness it
picks models for: `ChatInputPart.modelTargetSessionType` in the chat
input, or the current model's target in the Agents window picker.
- Other entry points (Command Palette, account menu, notifications) fall
back to the last focused chat's harness, then to the active
customization harness.

Scope is limited to the Manage Models editor. The Chat Customizations
editor's Models section and the model picker contents are unchanged.

## How to test

1. Make sure Copilot models from more than one harness are registered
(e.g. local, Copilot CLI agent host, Claude/Codex agent hosts).
2. In a chat, select the **Local** harness, open the model picker and
choose **Manage Models...**. Only the regular **Copilot** group is
listed; other providers are unchanged.
3. Switch the chat to the **Copilot CLI** agent host harness and open
**Manage Models...** again. Only the agent host's Copilot group is
listed.
4. Repeat with the **Claude** and **Codex** agent host harnesses. Each
shows only its own Copilot group.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep
"ChatModelsViewModel|ChatModelsWidget|modelPicker|ModelPicker|ChatInputPart"`:
passed, 372 tests, including a new `ChatModelsViewModel` test covering
all four Copilot sources plus a non-Copilot harness group.
- `npx eslint` on the changed files: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in the changed files. It fails
only on errors that already exist in
`src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/*` (`proxyCa`), which this change
doesn't touch.
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- Manual steps 2–4 above have not been run yet.

commit.message:
chat: restore Codex continuation with safe session routing (#339790)

* chat: restore Codex continuation with safe session routing

Reapply the continuation feature from #339074 while preserving the parent-session resolver and the peer-chat recovery added in #339476. Decline reverse mappings that cannot resolve back to the exact backend identity.

Add real configuration-control regression coverage for local and remote Copilot, Codex, and Claude peer selections. The six cases fail when the original fragment-preserving behavior is reintroduced. Validated 2,930 tests, compilation, lint, layers, hygiene, and an isolated persistence replay. Signed-in UI validation remains pending macOS Keychain access.

* chat: address continuation review and add hidden preview

Release failed visibility claims and use the shared dismiss button. Add an excluded experimental setting and a private preview command that leaves shared suppression and experiment telemetry untouched.

* chat: make Codex continuation threshold experimental

Add a hidden percentage setting with a 90 percent default and automatic ExP updates. Preserve the threshold in saved warning boundaries so other windows cannot clear suppression using a different assignment.

commit.message:
agentHost: forward tool-result images to BYOK models (#339830)

Fixes #339595
Fixes #339439

## Problem

In agent-host sessions, a BYOK (OpenAI-compatible) model never received
images returned by tools such as `view`. It only received the text
receipt `Viewed image file successfully.`

## Root cause

There were two problems:

1. **Vision capability never reached the runtime.**
`synthesizeByokSessionConfig` registered BYOK models with token limits
only. The renderer already reports `supportsVision`, but it wasn't
passed on, so the Copilot runtime treated every BYOK model as text-only.
It replaced tool-result images with the text receipt before the request
reached the BYOK proxy. I confirmed this by running the SDK runtime
against a stub `/responses` server. Without the capability,
`function_call_output.output` is the plain string. With
`capabilities.supports.vision: true`, it's an `[input_text,
input_image]` array.
2. **The BYOK LM bridge had no image channel for tool outputs.** Once
vision is declared, the array output was passed through untyped, and the
renderer wrapped it in a text part.

## Changes

- `copilotSessionLauncher.ts`: forward `supportsVision` as
`capabilities.supports.vision` on each BYOK `ProviderModelConfig`.
- `agentHostByokLm.ts`: add an optional `images` field to the two
tool-output bridge items. `output` stays text, so a renderer that
doesn't know the new field still gets today's text result.
- `byokResponsesTranslation.ts`: split array tool outputs into text plus
images, reusing the existing data-URL and MIME validation from user
messages.
- `agentHostByokLmHandler.ts`: forward the images as `data` parts inside
the LM API `tool_result`, the same shape the in-extension path produces.

## How to test

1. Turn on `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`.
2. Add an OpenAI-compatible BYOK model that supports images (e.g.
`gpt-4o`), with `"vision": true` and `"toolCalling": true`.
3. Put an image containing text the model can't guess (e.g.
`ZEBRA-7341`) in the workspace.
4. In an agent-host session with that model, ask: *"Use the view tool to
open probe.png and tell me exactly what text it contains. If you didn't
receive image pixels, say so."*
- Before this change: the model says it only got "Viewed image file
successfully."
   - After this change: the model reads the text.
5. With `"vision": false`, the model should still get the text receipt
and the turn should finish cleanly.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts
--run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts
--run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokLmProxyService.test.ts
--run
src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostByokLmHandler.test.ts`:
passed, 145 tests.
- New tests use the exact payload captured from the runtime, plus a
renderer `tool_result` mapping test. The launcher snapshot test now
covers `supportsVision`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: reports 20 errors, the same 20 as without
this change. They come from the locally installed `@github/copilot-sdk`
(1.0.16) being older than the version pinned in `package.json`. None are
in files this PR touches.

commit.message:
chat: Open model picker on touch and pen taps (#339777)

The Chat view's pane container registers as a Gesture target, which cancels touchstart/touchend and suppresses the compatibility mousedown. The model picker buttons only listened for mousedown, so finger and pen taps never opened them. Register the buttons as Gesture targets and handle Tap.

Fixes #339467

commit.message:
agentHost: let chats switch workspace or move to a worktree via tools (#339778)

* agentHost: isolate all chats in an existing session

Add the main-chat-only isolate_session tool, defer conversion until active chats finish, and preserve session histories while switching all Copilot backings to one worktree.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: support Codex isolation and preserve worktree branch identity

Enable session-wide Codex isolation with durable directory updates and rollback handling. Seed the generated branch before exposing the worktree and simplify the isolation divider.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: isolate only the calling chat in a worktree

Allow main and peer chats to request isolation while preserving other chat scopes. Persist exact-chat provider directories, update the Sessions workspace and branch model, and quarantine uncertain changes per chat.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: refine chat isolation scope and workspace conversion

Allow single-chat isolation without multi-root support while preserving repository identity. Keep multi-chat isolation gated, correct Git-state ownership, avoid refresh cooldown waits, and remove the superseded session-wide provider path.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: change a chat workspace through the set_workspace and isolate_session tools

A chat can now move to another folder or into a new Git worktree when the model calls set_workspace or isolate_session, including in sessions that already have a workspace. The change is deferred until the requesting turn ends and the original task then continues automatically. Only the addressed chat changes: a single user chat replaces the session roots under the chat catalog lock, and with several chats the siblings keep their folders.

Host: restore sibling chats before the provider moves, validate the chat identity across the asynchronous steps, quarantine the exact chat durably when the outcome is uncertain, and reject cancel, steering, new turns, truncation and archive while the host-owned conversion turn is running. Publish a per-chat workspace change state so clients can block input and show a blocked notice.

Providers: pin sibling working directories before a main chat move, guard archived-history resume, distinguish definitive Codex rejections from uncertain outcomes, and retain or reconcile worktrees through ownership records.

Client: block input while a conversion runs, render the workspace transition notice, and roll back an archive that the host rejects. There is no UI for changing the workspace; the tools are the only entry point.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: keep the workspace change feature to the tool path

There is no UI to start a workspace change, so remove the client reactions that only supported a user-initiated change: the workbench input blocking and notice, the Sessions archive rollback and bulk archive handling, and the published per-chat state they read. The host still rejects cancel, steering, new turns, truncation and archive while a conversion owns the turn.

Drop incidental churn from the feature diff and keep the project and worktree handling the Agents Window adapter needs after a tool-driven change. The transition notice now reads 'Workspace changed to a new worktree of {0}' for a worktree and 'Workspace changed to {0}' for a folder.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: shorten the worktree workspace transition label

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Revert "agentHost: shorten the worktree workspace transition label"

This reverts commit a155fcbaa2d8ee469baebd8df4a99afcd04269bf.

* agentHost: allow set_workspace to move a worktree chat to a worktree of another folder

A chat already in its session's worktree was refused a new worktree of a
different folder with a generic error. Only reject when the target is the
chat's current folder, keep the old worktree on disk, and explain the
rejection.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: update e2e expectations for set_workspace on chats with a workspace

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: update Copilot prompt snapshots for the workspace tools

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Agents window: make bottom panel alignment configurable (#339736)

Fixes #336738

This makes the Agents window bottom panel configurable so it can remain
full-span or align beneath chat without squeezing the side pane.

### Changes

- Add a checkable **Align Panel with Chat** action to the existing panel
overflow and persist the selected alignment per profile.
- Reparent the existing Grid views while preserving panel height,
side-pane width, focus, hidden views, and maximize/restore behavior.
- Preserve hidden leaf and branch visibility in the shared Grid
operations exercised by these transitions.
- Keep the panel inset when the primary sidebar is collapsed, match
native macOS lower-corner geometry, and retain the full-span layout on
mobile.
- Add focused Grid, layout-action, topology, sizing, and styling
regression coverage.

### Validation

- `npm run compile` — passed with 0 errors.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/browser/ui/grid/grid.test.ts
--run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/workbench.test.ts --run
src/vs/sessions/test/browser/layoutActions.test.ts` — passed, 172 tests.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Targeted ESLint for all changed TypeScript files — passed.
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/browser/media/workbench.css` —
passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Agents window Dev UI scenario PA-01 through PA-08 — passed, covering
both alignments, existing-overflow placement, collapsed-sidebar spacing,
native macOS corners, maximization restoration, hidden views, and sash
regressions.


### UI validation

area](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f85de9d-9730-4012-80f8-b7e78a59fd63)

![Chat-aligned panel showing the left inset and native macOS lower
corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f855373d-be8d-4c20-8d74-16cc5873aa90)

**Full-span panel after maximization and alignment restoration**

commit.message:
github: migrate Dev Container sample reads (#339533)

* github: migrate Dev Container sample reads

Use the local anonymous GitHub engine to resolve repository HEAD and read commit-pinned Contents API JSON. Preserve the sample cache and container lifecycle, validate bounded base64 envelopes, and cover cancellation and lease ownership.

The desktop migration must not merge until compatible shared-process proxy and certificate transport is available and verified.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: expose repository reads through a service domain

Compose the public repository workflow under IGitHubService.repositories instead of requiring consumers to pass the service into a free helper. Keep anonymous client leases, commit pinning, cancellation and deadlines owned by the domain, and cover service startup and disposal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: use AbortSignal for repository file reads

Align the repository domain with the existing GitHub cancellation APIs. Forward the caller signal and abort reason unchanged, and adapt Dev Container cancellation tokens only at the caller boundary with scoped listener cleanup.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: normalize cancellation inputs inside the service

Accept AbortSignal or CancellationToken for repository reads and share operation-scoped normalization with the GitHub IPC boundary. Preserve caller signals and abort reasons, release token listeners with the request lifetime, and remove adapter boilerplate from Dev Container callers.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: scope repository reads to anonymous clients

Move the repository domain from the root service to IGitHubAnonymousClient and rename readPublicFile to readFile. Use the owning client endpoint and get capability without nested lease acquisition; preserve shared cancellation normalization and explicit caller lease ownership.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: simplify anonymous client API

Move the anonymous client into its own module and expose readFile directly. Default omitted acquisition options to GitHub.com while preserving explicit endpoints, shorten the cancellation helper name, and remove the requested sample-cancellation test suite.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: consolidate anonymous client tests

Rename the client tests to anonymousClient.test.ts and include the repository file-read coverage in the same module. Retain all existing test definitions and update documented test selectors.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: let anonymous callers supply request options

Accept GitHubCancellation in get and readFile, use signal parameter names, and remove the IPC token adapter. Forward readFile caller, priority and deadline options; attribute interactive Dev Container reads at their call site instead of hardcoding github.query in the reusable client.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Updates

* github: use governed raw downloads for repository files

Add a configurable raw-content base to anonymous host options and retain one REST commit lookup followed by a SHA-pinned raw download. Reuse bounded download handling with credential omission, pinned redirects and raw-origin quota isolation, preserving the sample cache and author SHA/path helpers.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Updates

* PR feedback

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Apply an explicit session read action before synchronizing its sole chat so the chat transition does not recursively promote and persist the same session state twice.

commit.message:
Keep background shell output visible while it streams (#339636)

* Keep background shell output visible while the elapsed time updates

The Background Shells picker refreshes each row once a second, and a row's
description includes its elapsed time. The dropdown pill's hover cache took
the changed description for a different resource and released the row's
hover disposable, which closed the live output terminal. The picker then
rebuilt it in the open details, so the output vanished and came back on
every update.

The pill now releases a cached hover disposable only when the entry that
replaces it no longer carries it. A removed entry still releases its hover.

* Keep a shared hover disposable cached until its entry is removed

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339636#discussion_r4180441849.

When an entry updated while the dropdown was closed, the pill dropped its
cached hover without releasing the disposable the entry still carried, and
nothing cached it again until the dropdown reopened. Removing the entry or
disposing the pill then no longer released it. The cached hover now stays
until the entry is removed or stops carrying that disposable.

commit.message:
Describe result_token_count as a local text-output estimate (#339601)

The GDPR comment for `copilotSdk/tool_call_executed.result_token_count`
said the value is measured with the model tokenizer. The Copilot runtime
computes it locally with `o200k_base` scaled by a per-model multiplier, and
only for successful text results up to 20 KiB that carry no binary or
structured-reference content. Say so, and state that absence is not zero,
so consumers do not read the column as an exact or billed token count.

Comment-only. The forwarder already passes SDK metrics through unchanged.

Refs github/copilot-agent-runtime#20172
Refs #335623

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: tell HydraFusion phase chats apart from subagents in telemetry (#339560)

* agentHost: tell HydraFusion phase chats apart from subagents in telemetry

Each HydraFusion phase opens a child chat through a synthetic
subagent_started signal, so the host reported every phase as a subagent
turn with no model and no task model source. That inflated subagent
launch counts and lowered the share of subagents with a known model.

Add a bounded subagentKind property (task | fusionPhase) to the events
that decide isSubagentSession per chat, and report the phase's model on
the phase chat's turn and tool-call events.

Fixes #339326

commit.message:
github: avoid throttling generic 403 denials (#339521)

Address GitHub protocol-audit finding: a generic HTTP 403 permission refusal containing "Rate Limit Exceeded" must remain an authorization error, not invent a shared quota cooldown.

Share one internal HTTP evidence classifier between transport errors, response telemetry and the GitHub cooldown coordinator.
Retain primary exhaustion from valid remaining-zero headers, HTTP 429, valid Retry-After, or an explicit primary-limit message without usable remaining-quota feedback. Retain explicit secondary-limit headers/messages, reset timing, Retry-After precedence and the existing unhinted cooldown floor.
Reject malformed numeric and Retry-After evidence on HTTP refusals, and preserve already-established cooldowns when a concurrent response reports healthy quota.
Keep storage-origin download 403s as authorization failures. Reads/mutations, bootstrap credentials, cancellation/deadlines and account/host isolation keep their existing execution paths.

commit.message:
github: add shared process fetch implementation (#339301)

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678

- Add a GitHub-local, proxy-aware Node fetch implementation in `src/vs/platform/github/electron-utility/githubFetch.ts`. `SharedProcessGitHubService` creates its fetch in its constructor, with networking initialized lazily on the first request.
- Honor local-user/default proxy settings and merge the resolved login-shell environment over the inherited environment, preserving shell-configured proxies for GUI launches.
- Use existing native-host APIs for system/PAC proxy resolution, Basic/Kerberos proxy authentication, and system certificates. Preserve Node's default CA set and send configured proxy authorization to the proxy rather than the origin.
- Extend the existing native-host `resolveProxy` implementation to use `app.resolveProxy` when there is no window session. No new native-host interface method is introduced.
- Remove the test-only fetch constructor argument and its obsolete shared-process service test. Update the networking documentation and client inventory.

commit.message:
agentHost: report empty BYOK turn responses instead of "No response was returned" (#339426)

Related to #335405, #324335, #322728, #333490

## What

When a BYOK model call that answers a user message returns no visible
output (no non-whitespace text, no tool calls, no non-whitespace
reasoning summary), the Copilot Agent Host BYOK proxy now returns a
descriptive **422** error instead of an empty `response.completed`. It
also logs the session, vendor/model, output item types, and output token
count.

A request counts as answering a user message when its input ends with a
user message, ignoring trailing system/developer messages. That covers a
turn's first call, a replacement turn after a cancelled turn that kept
its tool results, and a call after an `immediate` steering message. All
three failed with the generic error on an empty reply when run against
the bundled SDK. Empty responses that continue after tool results still
pass through unchanged, because the Copilot runtime completes those
turns normally.

## Why

Telemetry shows `No response was returned. Send your message again to
retry.` (`agenthost.turnfailed`, stage `provider`, errorType `query`) is
the largest unfixed BYOK failure. It affects about 8% of BYOK turns on
older Insiders builds and 13.7% on the newest.

I ran the bundled SDK (`@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.17-preview.0) against
the proxy and confirmed:
- The renderer bridge returns `{ output: [] }` successfully whenever the
provider streams nothing useful. Examples are empty text, `"\n\n"`, or
reasoning that is only encrypted.
- `bridgeResultToResponsesSseFrames` turns that into a valid but empty
completion.
- The runtime accepts it, emits an empty `assistant.message`, and then
fails the turn with the generic message. The real reason is lost.
- A 5xx from the proxy is retried 5 times (~15s), which is the `502
Response contained no choices.` signature. A 4xx is shown to the user
verbatim with no retry. An empty response is deterministic, so 422 is
used.

The underlying empty provider responses look like context-window or
output-limit overflows on OpenAI-compatible and local providers (Ollama,
OpenRouter, vLLM, DeepSeek), as described in the linked issues. This is
a hypothesis; I couldn't confirm it in telemetry. This PR doesn't change
provider behavior. It makes the failure visible and actionable, and
gives it a separate telemetry signature to confirm the hypothesis.

## Notes for reviewers

- `endsWithUserMessage` and `hasVisibleBridgeOutput` live in
`byokResponsesTranslation.ts`. The visibility rule matches what the
runtime treats as a response, which I checked empirically for each
output kind.
- The 502 retry behavior for real bridge or provider errors is
unchanged.
- Possible follow-ups, not in this PR:
- `languageModelAccess.ts` treats `finish_reason: length` with no
content as success.
- Deterministic bridge errors (model not found, BYOK disabled by policy)
are still sent as retryable 502s.

## How to test

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep
"ByokLmProxyService|byokResponsesTranslation|ByokLmBridgeRegistry|AgentHostClientByokLmChannel|AgentHostByokLmHandler|CopilotSessionLauncher"`:
**126 passing**
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotByokResponses.integrationTest.ts`:
**3 passing**. This includes a new real-SDK test that checks the
descriptive error is shown after a single call, with no retries.
- `npm run typecheck-client` and eslint on changed files: clean
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep CopilotAgent` has 12 failures, all in
session-state discovery and debug-log tests. The same 12 fail on
unmodified `main` locally, so they are unrelated to this change.

Manual: configure a BYOK model whose provider returns an empty
completion (e.g. a local model with a context size that's too small),
then send a message in an Agent Host (Copilot CLI) session. You should
see the descriptive error right away instead of "No response was
returned" after a delay.

commit.message:
agentHost: degrade BYOK input_file parts instead of failing the turn (#339425)

BYOK turns in the Copilot Agent Host (`copilotcli`) failed with `400
Unsupported input[0].content[2] type 'input_file'` when the user
attached a PDF. With this change the PDF is replaced by a short note to
the model, and the turn continues.

## What changed
- `responsesRequestToBridge`
(`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/byokResponsesTranslation.ts`)
now replaces Responses `input_file` parts with a text note, e.g.
`[spec.pdf (application/pdf) omitted: this model does not accept file
inputs]`. Before this change it threw `ResponsesTranslationError`. The
runtime already handles images that a model can't read the same way.
- Added a unit test in `byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts`. It uses the
exact content shape captured from the runtime, plus a part that has only
a `file_id`.

## Why
Every BYOK model is registered with the Copilot runtime as an `openai` /
`wireApi: 'responses'` provider pointed at the local BYOK proxy
(`copilotSessionLauncher.ts`). The runtime sends a document attachment
(a `#file` reference to a `.pdf`, or an `application/pdf` blob) as an
`input_file` part.

commit.message:
mcp: shorten migration property-removal warnings (#339424) Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/339357 Follow-up to #338998. When migrating an MCP server removes unsupported properties (`gallery`, `version`, `dev`, `sandboxEnabled`), the warnings were long enough to wrap across several lines. In the Migrations list they spilled out of the row and overlapped the next server. In the MCP server detail view they made the *Partially supported by Copilot* card dense. This shortens each message to one line in both places. ### Migrations list (`customizationMigrationCategories.ts`) | Property | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `gallery` | The 'gallery' property will be removed. This MCP server will no longer be automatically updated from the registry. | Removes 'gallery'. Registry updates will stop. | | `gallery` (updates already off) | The 'gallery' property will be removed. Automatic updates from the registry are already disabled for this MCP server. | Removes 'gallery'. Registry updates are already off. | | `version` | The 'version' property will be removed. The migrated configuration will no longer record version metadata. Version pins in the command, arguments, or URL will not change. | Removes 'version'. Version pins are kept. | | `dev` | The 'dev' property will be removed. VS Code will no longer auto-start this server in development mode, restart it when watched files change, attach a debugger, or enable development-mode logging. | Removes 'dev'. Development mode will stop. | | `sandboxEnabled` | Two variants (sandbox on / already off). Each explained that VS Code's per-server sandbox no longer applies and that sandboxing after migration is controlled by the harness. | Removes 'sandboxEnabled'. Sandboxing is handled by {harness}. | ### Compatibility card in the MCP server detail (`agentHostMcpServerSupportScope.ts`) | Reason | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Gallery metadata | Gallery metadata is not supported in the destination MCP configuration.
Migration can remove the gallery property. After migration, this MCP server will not receive automatic updates from the registry. | Gallery metadata isn't supported. Migrating removes it and stops registry updates. | | Server version | Server version metadata is not supported in the destination MCP configuration.
Migration can remove the version property after you confirm the loss of version metadata. Version pins in the command, arguments, or URL will not change. | Version metadata isn't supported. Migrating removes it; version pins are kept. | | Development mode | MCP development mode is not supported by the Copilot harness.
Migration can remove dev after you confirm the loss of development-mode auto-start, file-watch restarts, debugging, and logging. | Development mode isn't supported. Migrating removes dev. | | Per-server sandbox | Per-server sandbox settings are not supported by the Copilot harness.
Migration can remove sandboxEnabled after you confirm that VS Code's per-server sandbox restrictions will no longer be applied. | Per-server sandboxing isn't supported. Migrating removes sandboxEnabled. | ### Notes for reviewers - The separate `sandboxEnabled: false` message (`mcpMigrationRemoveDisabledSandbox`) is merged into the single sandbox message, because "Sandboxing is handled by {harness}" is accurate whether or not VS Code's sandbox was enabled. The "updates already off" variant for `gallery` is kept. - The other compatibility messages (unsupported location, input variables, `cwd`, SSE, OAuth, and so on) are unchanged because they tell the user what to edit. - Only strings changed; how the Migrations list measures row height is unchanged. At typical widths each warning now fits on one line, so rows no longer overlap. ### How to test 1. Set `chat.customizations.migration.enabled` to `true`. 2. In the user `mcp.json`, add (or install from the registry) an MCP server that has `gallery` and `version` properties. 3. With the Copilot harness active, open Chat Customizations > **Migrations**. Under *MCP Servers (User)*, the server row shows one short line per removed property and doesn't overlap the next row. 4. Open the server from **MCP Servers**. The *Partially supported by Copilot* card lists one-line bullets. ### Validation - `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMigration.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostMcpServerSupport.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/mcpServerCustomizationMigration.test.ts`: passed (165 passing) - `npm run typecheck-client`: passed - `npx eslint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostMcpServerSupportScope.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMigrationCategories.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostMcpServerSupport.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMigration.test.ts`: passed - Rendered the `MigrationDashboard` and `EmbeddedMcpDetailPartiallySupported` component fixtures locally (temporarily seeded with `gallery`/`version`; those fixture edits aren't included here) and checked both views.

commit.message:
agentHost: report empty BYOK turn responses instead of "No response was returned"

When a BYOK model's first call in a user turn finished with no visible
output (no non-whitespace text, no tool calls, no reasoning summary), the
BYOK proxy sent the Copilot runtime a valid, empty Responses completion.
The runtime then failed the turn with the generic "No response was
returned. Send your message again to retry." error, and the reason was
lost.

The proxy now detects this case, logs the session, model, and output item
types, and returns a descriptive 422 error that the runtime shows as-is
and does not retry. Empty responses later in a turn (after tool results)
still pass through, because the runtime completes those turns normally.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: degrade BYOK input_file parts instead of failing the turn

The Copilot runtime sends document attachments (e.g. a referenced PDF) as
Responses `input_file` parts. The BYOK loopback proxy only translated text and
image parts, so these turns failed with `400 Unsupported input[N].content[M]
type 'input_file'`. BYOK models are served through the LM API, which has no
capability declaring document input, so replace the file with a note telling
the model it was omitted.

chat: Enrich reference previews and add pill context copying (#339342)

* chat: Enrich reference previews and add pill context copying

Resolve GitHub reference metadata on demand without promoting references to authored artifacts. Prefetch a bounded initial set, preserve hover intent through updates, and share copy actions with pill context menus. Replace isolated hover galleries with interactive reference fixtures and deterministic rich-preview captures.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Harden lazy reference resolution and cache retention

Address Copilot review by validating canonical reference numbers, evicting metadata and hover descriptors no longer referenced, preserving resolved titles during checks enrichment, and treating checks failures as optional. Cover eviction races and partial failures with targeted tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Stabilize visible reference fetching and checks enrichment

Notify only newly visible rows after layout settles, preserve reference identity during scroll updates, and resolve PR core before subscribing to head-specific checks. Use URLs after metadata failure and update the toolbar test harness for its GitHub service dependency.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Format lazy reference regression coverage

Apply the repository formatter after the review and CI fixes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Cancel evicted GitHub reference requests

Give each lazy resolution its own abort scope and cancel credential acquisition and resource refreshes when references are removed, sessions change, accounts change, or the resolver is disposed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Preserve reference dropdown scroll position during updates

Keep the viewport stable when asynchronously resolved metadata rebuilds the dropdown, rather than revealing its previously focused row.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Discard canceled metadata and scope fixture hover routing

Do not publish stale results after reference eviction, account changes or disposal. Preserve cancellation through optional checks and validate both rejecting and resolving canceled requests. Register base hover routing only while reference fixtures are mounted and restore the previous delegate afterward.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Preserve resource previews during reference metadata updates

Reuse image and location hover content by stable entry identity while keeping actions current, disposing replaced or removed resources. Forward fixture fallback hover methods explicitly so prototype methods retain their receiver.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Validate reference hosts and seed scroll prefetch visibility

Reject enterprise credentials for public GitHub references before subscribing. Seed the initial visible row identities so a small first scroll does not retry failed initial prefetches. Cover both behaviors and use realistic API hosts in mocks.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Complete visible reference prefetch without duplicate retries

Track prefetch attempts per dropdown opening so the first scroll can resolve initially visible entries beyond the first five without retrying that initial batch. Avoid repeating URLs in accessible descriptions when the visible fallback label already contains the URL.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: retire legacy sandbox policy enforcement (#339396)

## Summary

Retire legacy VS Code sandbox policies from the Copilot Agent Host
policy contract and roll back the mandatory legacy sandbox requirement
added by #339144. Enterprise sandbox enforcement in Agent Host should
use [Copilot managed
settings](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/administer-copilot/manage-for-enterprise/use-managed-settings/get-started),
not migration of the old preview device policies.

- Remove the connection-owned legacy sandbox requirement, while
retaining native managed sandbox enforcement and the later
session-restoration/reconciliation fixes.
- Mark nine legacy sandbox settings deprecated, keep their migration
notices visible, and preserve their defaults. Add deprecation and
replacement guidance to the four device-policy descriptions and
generated catalog.
- Classify those four retired policies as `notApplicable`, rather than
outstanding Agent Host parity gaps. Update diagnostics, tests, and
contributor documentation together. New Agent Host sandbox controls are
not deprecated.

## Admin and user impact

**`ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` no longer guarantees sandboxing in Agent
Host.** Existing setting forwarding remains, so it can supply an On
default, but a session Off selection can override it.

To require sandboxing in Copilot Agent Host, use native managed
`sandbox.enabled: true`. Use `sandbox.allowBypass: false` when bypass
must be prohibited. Outbound network restrictions use
`sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowOutbound`.

Local harness behavior is unchanged. Native managed restrictions,
permitted-bypass controls, restored-session reconciliation, and other
legacy permission translations remain intact. `notApplicable` records
the retirement of the legacy policy contract; it does not mean forwarded
settings have no effect or certify enforcement parity.

The deprecated device policies are `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled`,
`ChatAgentSandboxAllowNetwork`,
`ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands`, and
`ChatAgentSandboxAllowAutoApprove`.

## Validation

- Rebased onto current `main`; core compilation completed with zero
errors.
- 528 focused tests passed, covering native sandbox enforcement,
restoration, bypass/fail-closed behavior, ordinary forwarding,
connection lifecycle, deprecation metadata, catalog classifications, and
diagnostics.
- A test-only follow-up fixes two stale CI expectations. Both failures
were reproduced locally, then the affected suites passed 69 tests in
Electron and 68 in WebKit, including unchanged Local/Copilot rollout
selection.
- Targeted hygiene and whitespace checks passed.
- Canonical Workbench and Agents policy-export check passed.

Live MDM deployment was not exercised. Release notes and sandbox
migration guidance have also been updated locally in `vscode-docs` for
separate publication.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

Don't treat a failed GitHub session lookup as a sign-out (#339393)

Refreshing the default account can hit a session lookup error while the
GitHub authentication provider is briefly unavailable, for example when
the extension host restarts to apply managed telemetry policy. That error
was handled like a sign-out: the account was cleared and, with
forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, the managed settings gate blocked AI and asked
a signed-in user to sign in.

Keep the account that is already known for the same provider, with its
policy and managed settings freshness, when the lookup fails. Session
removals still clear the account, and a failed lookup before any account
is known still reports a missing token.

commit.message:
github: add shared-process hosting and anonymous-read IPC (#339281)

* github: extract shared request infrastructure

Separate the GitHub engine's request types, queue, scheduler, cooldown storage, response readers, and caller waiters from domain policy. Retain explicit-credential bootstrap and policy-driven control-read infrastructure without migrating existing Copilot consumers. All production Agent Host code, authentication and Copilot wiring remain unchanged from main so the refactor can land before the release branch.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: isolate control reads and cover shared request helpers

Scope buffered control coalescing to the quota account as well as the caller's credential/representation key. Add direct response-reader, header-parser and cooldown-state coverage, moving the generic inactive-account timer test to the shared-state suite. Correct the stale documentation claim about the deferred Copilot migration.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: add direct host fetchers and shared-process hosting

Port the single-attempt browser and Node executors from #338848 under platform/github. Initialize direct host networking and prepare opt-in shared-process GitHub hosting without migrating desktop callers or Copilot traffic. This slice is stacked on #339208.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: replace fetch services with request helpers

Keep shared-process hosting and anonymous-read IPC in this PR. Move direct networking to platform/request createFetch helpers, remove custom 421 handling and response adaptation, and retain the runtime fetch behavior. Reuse the existing Agent Host proxy fetch without changing Copilot networking.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: isolate shared-process hosting from fetch work

Keep the shared GitHub engine and typed anonymous-read IPC in this PR. Restore existing workbench, Agent Host and native networking; defer createFetch helpers and proxy integration to a stacked investigation PR.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: Add compact layout density to the Agents window (#339353)

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Bring `window.density.layout` to the Agents window, independently of the
editor-window Modern UI setting.

- Make Compact panels meet edge-to-edge, retaining visible single
separators and continuous connected-tab outlines.
- Keep tab/action-area horizontal padding consistent between densities.
- Use a 44px title bar in Default and 35px in Compact; preserve control
sizes, update auxiliary layouts and notification offsets, and improve
native macOS/right-hand action spacing.
- Keep density-menu changes local to the Agents window and accurately
display inherited User values. Preserve explicit empty array overrides
when editing inherited settings.
- Keep macOS traffic-light horizontal positioning fixed across
densities, while preserving OS-version-specific vertical centering and
zoom behavior.
- Ensure built-in themes provide visible Agents panel borders.

## Before / after

Captured in the same 1440 × 900 Chromium viewport with Dark 2026, the
desktop Agents layout, a Search editor and the bottom panel open.
Authentication, filesystem and terminal use the existing test mocks; no
live agent requests or user workspace data are involved. Before is the
branch's main merge-base (`3bf9306bd0d`); after is the final branch.

| Before | After — Default | After — Compact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: main, 35px title bar and floating panel
gaps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aca23716-0404-45be-ac71-d6362b3c8fee)
| ![After: Default, 44px title bar and visible panel
borders](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0ae3923-da42-4887-b4d2-8629c6ab8b59)
| ![After: Compact, 35px title bar and zero gaps between
panels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b796465-71cb-4a00-a48e-9ab3c3a80375)
|

## How to test

1. Open the Agents window and use **View > Layout Density** (also
available from the title-bar context menu).
2. Switch between Default and Compact without reloading. Default has
floating gaps and a taller title bar; Compact has no inter-panel gaps.
Tab outlines and action sizes should stay intact.
3. Change `window.density.layout` in User and Agents Window Settings.
Verify the Agents override wins, User settings stay unchanged, and
removing the override restores inheritance after reload.
4. Clear an inherited array setting in Agents Window Settings. An
explicit `[]` must persist; **Reset Setting** must restore inheritance.
5. Check panels and connected tabs in the built-in dark, light and
high-contrast themes.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- The focused Chromium command below — 452 passed, 1 existing
native-only frosted-glass test skipped.
- `npm run test-node -- --run
src/vs/sessions/test/node/builtinThemeBorders.test.ts --reporter dot` —
passed; checks all 19 built-in color themes and their inherited border
values.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Before/after DOM measurements — Default title bar 44px; Compact 35px,
with 0px horizontal/vertical inter-panel gaps and 0px outer grid
gutters.
- Isolated source-method probe of the renderer/native traffic-light
positioning path — passed for pre-Tahoe and Tahoe+, at zoom factors 0.8,
1 and 1.25.

<details>
<summary>Exact focused browser test command</summary>

```sh
npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --reporter dot \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/agentsPartCard.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/workbench.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/titlebarPart.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/layoutActions.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatCompositeBar.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/editorPart.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/test/browser/editor.contribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/services/configuration/test/browser/configurationService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts \
```

commit.message:
chat: Fail requests whose selected model is unavailable (#339307)

* chat: Fail requests whose selected model is unavailable

A selected model the extension host couldn't resolve silently fell back to the default (Auto) model, so requests were answered and billed by a different model than the one shown in the picker. Fail the request instead.

Also re-register BYOK providers when a Copilot token arrives after a failed mint, since they previously stayed unregistered until the next identity change, and make the unregister log say why.

Fixes #339239

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Reject stale-account tokens and tool model fallback

A Copilot token fetch that finished after an account switch on the same provider was adopted for the new account, which the BYOK token listener could then use to re-enable providers under the wrong account's policy. Check the account identity after the fetch, like the existing provider and enterprise URI checks.

Model-backed tool invocations now use the same strict model resolution as chat requests instead of falling back to the default model.

Fixes #339303

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agent host: restore Copilot managed-settings diagnostics (#339354)


## Summary

Fix the Copilot snapshot in **Developer: Policy Diagnostics**, which
currently fails with:

```text
Copilot runtime SDK does not expose getManagedSettings()
```

The bundled runtime no longer exports that function. Use the supported
sessionless `client.rpc.managedSettings.resolve()` API instead. The
current SDK/runtime bundle already supports it, so no dependency upgrade
is needed.

- Resolve through the existing host SDK client, forwarding the current
GitHub token and `vscode-agent-host` client identity while retaining the
configured proxy and enterprise endpoint.
- Preserve the account identity, resolved settings, per-source layers,
and runtime diagnostics, including source failures and cached-policy
fallback warnings.
- Retain bounded startup/query deadlines, prevent a late query after
startup times out, and reject results when authentication changes during
resolution. A diagnostics timeout does not stop the shared runtime.
- Remove the obsolete native-export check and temporary process-wide
proxy environment changes.
- Re-enable the previously gated provider diagnostics test, remove its
known-issue entry, and add a model-free end-to-end test for fetched
server policy.
- Document the sessionless scope and the isolated mock-server workflow.

## Scope

This changes diagnostics, not policy enforcement, harness selection, or
existing conversations. It creates no chat session, executes no policy
helper, and does not include session-local client-injected settings.

Normal runtime cache behavior is unchanged. The report preserves
cache/source warnings, but a returned snapshot alone is not proof of a
fresh server fetch or end-to-end enforcement.

## Validation

- Core compilation, targeted hygiene, and whitespace checks passed.
- 508 focused tests passed, with one existing pending test. Coverage
includes token/client identity, proxy and enterprise endpoint
configuration, signed-out resolution, account changes, source warnings,
startup/query timeouts, and shared-client reuse.
- The formerly gated diagnostics test passed against the real bundled
runtime in strict replay.
- A new registered end-to-end test uses the real host/runtime and replay
proxy to verify an actual server-policy request, account identity,
server policy in both the source layer and effective settings, the
resolved bypass restriction, and no model traffic.
- Manual testing in an isolated Code OSS window verified signed-in
device-policy resolution, then a mocked server policy alongside the
existing device policy. The report showed `source: "mixed"`,
`serverManaged: true`, the expected permissions in both locations,
`bypassPermissionsDisabled: true`, and no diagnostics warnings. The
proxy log independently confirmed a successful policy fetch.

The manual server override was cleared afterward. No real device or
enterprise policies, global proxy settings, or certificates were
changed.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

commit.message:
mcp: fix customization migration in multi-root workspaces (#339333)

* mcp: fix customization migration in multi-root workspaces

- Same-named `.vscode/mcp.json` servers in other workspace folders are
  never registered because the client resolves duplicate names by
  precedence, so the migration plan never saw the shadowed entries and a
  session scoped to a shadowed folder was offered nothing. Shadowed
  servers are now assessed with their resolved configuration so every
  folder's entries can be offered.
- Each workspace folder migrates into its own `.mcp.json`, so a matching
  server name in another folder cannot overwrite anything. The cross-root
  conflict guard rejected these migrations and asked users to rename
  servers; it is removed, and conflicts within the same destination are
  still rejected.
- Removing the only remaining property of a JSON object left a dangling
  trailing comma. Migrating every server out of a `.vscode/mcp.json` that
  ends with a trailing comma produced invalid JSON, failed verification,
  and was reported as a rollback failure. `setProperty` now removes that
  comma, as it already did for arrays.
- The disabled state of migrated servers was keyed by the session's root
  order rather than the workspace folder index that identifies root
  `.mcp.json` servers, so it could be applied to another folder's server.

Fixes #337097
Fixes #335884

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: keep same-named server precedence during partial migration

- The session receives the client-forwarded `.vscode/mcp.json` server
  ahead of root `.mcp.json` servers. Migrating only the folder whose
  server takes precedence let a shadowed same-named server in another
  folder take over and silently change the session's configuration.
  Shadowed servers now migrate first, and the server shadowing them only
  migrates once they all have; otherwise it is rejected with guidance to
  migrate them together.
- The settings sync test asserted the invalid `{ , }` output that
  `setProperty` produced when removing the only property before a
  trailing comma, which the previous commit fixed.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Unify sandbox settings and managed policy presentation (#339058)

* Unify sandbox settings and managed policy presentation

Unify cross-platform sandbox enablement, expose Agent Host sandbox controls, and forward resolved defaults without duplicating SDK fallbacks. Improve settings labels, discoverability, and ordering, and decouple managed policy presentation from the Settings editor.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep upcoming sandbox deprecation warnings visible

Enable developer tool access by default, remove local harness wording, and stabilize the Git overlay integration test fixture.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address sandbox policy review feedback

Remove legacy session policy metadata and cover replacement and clearing. Clarify sandbox network settings and document all policy restrictions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Reconcile restored sandbox settings and persist applied state (#339205)

Resolve saved sandbox choices against current managed policy before notifying providers. Persist confirmed enablement rather than pending or rejected choices, with restore and persistence regression tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Revert "Reconcile restored sandbox settings and persist applied state (#339205)"

This reverts commit cf13d88e79df00d3f973868f2397e3b06e6b1046. The persistence changes are maintained separately in #339206.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Organize sandbox settings and add Copilot user-configured paths

Group network and developer-tool settings, migrate the outbound setting, and add shared Copilot filesystem permissions without legacy fallback. Warn about per-OS filesystem settings and update descriptions, policy data, documentation, and regression tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix sandbox attachment path expectation for simulated Windows hosts

Normalize expected attachment paths for the target host rather than the CI runner OS. Fixes Linux and macOS Electron unit failures in #339058.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix sandbox readiness after settings merge

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix sandbox policy diagnostics Markdown expectation

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Keep an attached shell's tool call terminal live after an async call
returns and keep appending its partial output. Point the shell's
background work entry at that terminal, settle it on shell_completed,
and show the command and live output in the Background Shells details.

* Update the read-shell E2E snapshot for background shell terminals

The async shell call now completes with a terminal block, because its
output keeps streaming after the call returns.

* Settle background shell terminals from read results and every task read

When the agent polls a background shell with read_bash, the runtime puts the
exit code in the read result and sends no shell_completed notification, so
settle the shell from read, write, and stop results.

The task-list fallback now counts any read that started after the call went
to the background, including reads that a newer read superseded, so a shell
that exits before it is ever listed still settles.

Clear the background shell output view through the xterm write queue instead
of reset(), so output that xterm is still parsing can't land after the clear.

* Expose background shell output to screen readers

Addresses review comment 4162451160. The Background Shells details drew the
output only in a detached xterm, inside a div that had a name but no role,
so screen readers couldn't review the streamed lines.

The output is now a focusable region named for its command, with the
Terminal Chat Output hint. Open Accessible View shows the command, its
status, and the output without ANSI escapes, and closing it returns focus to
the output, or to the chat input once the picker has closed.

* Show only the live terminal in background shell details

While a background shell's output is shown, its details now hold just the
command, its status, and the terminal. The badge, shell ID, and start time
stay in the row's description.

The terminal also keeps a fixed height of 10 rows instead of growing with
the output. The details are pinned above the chat input, so each new row
pushed the command header up. Lines now fill the terminal from the top, then
scroll.

commit.message:
agentHost: add E2E coverage for managed OTel policy changes (#339315)

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Refs [#339219](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/339219).
Upstream fix:
[github/copilot-agent-runtime#24069](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/24069).
Its CI build containing head `a611759fb2777e411520ba981e9e897dfc2d12e9`
passes the regression below; newer upstream commits are not covered by
this result.

Adds replayable tests for actual user-message capture across sessions
and managed telemetry policy changes, with unchanged-policy and
explicit-restart controls. Registers the OTel suite in the standard E2E
runner. Both telemetry test leases clear inherited OTLP TLS
certificate/key settings only in their child environments.

The no-restart regression reproduces `Managed telemetry conflicts with
the already selected OTel configuration` verbatim on the bundled
runtime. It remains gated by `AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1`, preserving
successful-turn and policy-B telemetry assertions. This PR adds
coverage, not a production fix.

## Validation

`npm run compile-client`: **passed**. Targeted ESLint, hygiene, and `git
diff --check`: **passed**.

```bash
./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotOtelAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts
```

macOS, bundled SDK `1.0.16` / runtime `1.0.90`: **4 passing, 1
intentionally pending**, both normally and with all six
generic/trace-specific OTLP certificate/key variables inherited.

```bash
AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotOtelAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'new sessions honor changed managed telemetry without restarting'
```

After pushing TLS isolation
(`1ad64a30c70df5dabf96cfaf54b8b8e8784b24eb`):
- Bundled runtime: **fails with the exact original conflict**, even with
inherited TLS settings isolated.
- Upstream CI runtime: **passes** with the same assertions/fixtures and
all six TLS variables injected. Full suite with the known issue enabled:
**5 passing**; additional focused repetition: **1 passing**.
- Candidate: macOS arm64 native artifact `11235778322` from [CI run
37024837646](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/actions/runs/37024837646).
Build metadata identifies merge
`f1617f3ee247cf9a1d6abc27aab1d158580353c9`, containing PR head
`a611759fb2777e411520ba981e9e897dfc2d12e9`. Both the launcher and its
native library came from that artifact; the VS Code host and SDK wrapper
were unchanged.
- Candidate selection used a temporary AHP `runtimePath` configuration
hook, removed after validation. The fix is not yet bundled into this PR.

Earlier full local run, `npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --jobs 2`: OTel
passed; other suites failed on signing-dependent Git fixture setup.

Before merge: complete the required focused/repeated cross-platform
Azure validation for the updated head. No all-platform claim is made for
the upstream candidate.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

Separate the GitHub engine's request types, queue, scheduler, cooldown storage, response readers, and caller waiters from domain policy. Retain explicit-credential bootstrap and policy-driven control-read infrastructure without migrating existing Copilot consumers. Scope buffered control coalescing to the quota account as well as the caller's credential/representation key. Add direct response-reader, header-parser and cooldown-state coverage, moving the generic inactive-account timer test to the shared-state suite. Correct the stale documentation claim about the deferred Copilot migration.

commit.message:
github: distinguish GraphQL throttling from quota exhaustion (#339203)

* github: distinguish GraphQL throttling from quota exhaustion

Treat RATE_LIMIT as primary exhaustion without turning operation-specific RATE_LIMITED errors into an account-wide hourly cooldown. Preserve authoritative quota and Retry-After feedback, and cover error mapping, telemetry, partial results, and mutation no-replay.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* github: validate GraphQL Retry-After before overriding quota reset

Reject malformed numeric retry hints on GraphQL feedback paths so they cannot release an exhausted quota early. Preserve decimal delay-seconds and HTTP-date support without changing REST parsing. Add deterministic header, payload, and healthy-quota regressions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: preserve enterprise controls during Agent Host migration (#339023) The Local harness is being deprecated in favor of Agent Host, backed by the Copilot SDK. Rollout has started, but some existing VS Code enterprise policies need translation into the SDK's Unified Managed Settings so enterprise controls remain intact during the transition. ## What this PR does - **Enables supported legacy policy conversion by default.** Removes the separate bridge opt-in, `chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings`. When rollout or explicit selection chooses Copilot Agent Host, supported restrictions carry over automatically. Native terminal restrictions, including global user settings, still require approval under Allow All/assisted approval. - **Adds applied-policy readiness diagnostics.** Run **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** from the Command Palette to see conversion/enforcement coverage, source, impact, and remaining gaps. Separates unsupported requirements from source/path-dependent coverage needing verification; excludes unconfigured policies and preserves existing diagnostic sections. Policy gaps appear in diagnostics but do not block Agent Host rollout. Existing rollout behavior is unchanged, and supported policy restrictions remain enforced. Scope: Copilot Agent Host on this machine, not certification of remote hosts or other providers. Refs #332011, #337536, #337537. ## Accepted gaps (report-only) Accepted for this PR's rollout posture, not reclassified as enforced or treated as individual administrator consent. Source/path-dependent findings may already be enforced by runtime-native settings. OTel is implemented; its entries concern remaining forwarding, precedence, and runtime coverage. Its policies also reference `github.copilot.chat.otel.enabled`, `github.copilot.chat.otel.exporterType`, `github.copilot.chat.otel.captureIdentity`, and `github.copilot.chat.otel.headers`. **Merged fixes:** [#339144](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339144) closes the legacy macOS/Linux `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` gap allowing direct session Off overrides; it is omitted below. Host identity capture is also fixed by [#339045](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339045). Both fixes are merged into `main`; this is not a claim of release availability. Sandbox lifecycle validation remains open: distinguish policy still loading from confirmed withdrawal, and verify loss/reapplication of the last client's requirement across disconnect-grace expiry. The separate sandbox auto-approval gap remains below. | Policy / setting | Remaining impact | |---|---| | `ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval` / `chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval` | Bypass is disabled for excluded tools, but per-tool confirmation is not guaranteed through other approval paths. | | `ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove` / `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove` | Native shell asks are covered; custom-terminal coverage is incomplete (`chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled`). | | `ChatAgentSandboxAllowAutoApprove` / `chat.agent.sandbox.allowAutoApprove` | Active sandboxed commands may auto-approve without an equivalent blanket shell ask. Activation includes `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows`. | | `ChatMCP` / `chat.mcp.access` | Independent runtime discovery can escape workbench access filtering. | | `ChatAllowedMcpServers` / `chat.mcp.allowedServers`
`ChatDeniedMcpServers` / `chat.mcp.deniedServers`
`ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly` / `chat.mcp.allowManagedServersOnly` | VS Code-only restrictions do not reach every forwarded, discovered, or built-in server path. | | `McpEnterpriseManagedAuthIdp` / `mcp.enterpriseManagedAuth.idp` | Forwarded authentication lacks Local's enterprise IdP lookup; SSO may fail. | | `ChatPluginsEnabled` / `chat.plugins.enabled`
`ChatEnabledPlugins` / `chat.plugins.enabledPlugins` | Independent discovery and customization paths can bypass disablement or required-plugin decisions. | | `ChatExtraMarketplaces` / `chat.plugins.extraMarketplaces`
`ChatStrictMarketplaces` / `chat.plugins.strictMarketplaces` | Runtime-owned operations lack VS Code-only values; strict lists do not disable installed plugins. | | `ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization` / `chat.customizations.strictPluginOnlyCustomization` | Independent discovery, instructions, and selective lockdown lack equivalent coverage. | | `ChatHooks` / `chat.useHooks`
`ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly` / `chat.hooks.allowManagedOnly` | The Local switch does not disable runtime file hooks; managed-only file-hook/SDK-callback coverage is incomplete or unverified. | | `ChatAgentMode` / `chat.agent.enabled` | Agent Host targets can remain available when agent mode is disabled. | | `CopilotOtelEnabled` / `chat.agentHost.otel.enabled` | Separate destinations/recorders can override disablement. | | `CopilotOtelProtocol` / `chat.agentHost.otel.exporterType` | Inherited OTLP configuration can override exporter selection. | | `CopilotOtelCaptureIdentity` / `chat.agentHost.otel.captureIdentity` | Host identity capture is fixed ([#339045](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339045)); runtime account attribution awaits upstream merge, a bundled runtime roll, and end-to-end verification. No additional VS Code account-identity wiring is expected. | | `CopilotOtelHeaders` / `chat.agentHost.otel.headers` | Missing host forwarding can break authenticated export. | | `ChatAgentNetworkFilter` / `chat.agent.networkFilter`
`ChatAgentAllowedNetworkDomains` / `chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains`
`ChatAgentDeniedNetworkDomains` / `chat.agent.deniedNetworkDomains` | Legacy allowlists are not mandatory boundaries on native runtime URL/shell paths; supported URL denies and shared VS Code filtering remain. Domain `limitTo` integration is accepted follow-up work, not a landing prerequisite. | *🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

Normalize VS Code and copilotd metadata behind host-neutral helpers and recognize the advertised session/model configuration keys. Preserve compatible outgoing metadata, retries, steering display records, and context usage across restoration.

Keep generated declarations pinned without vendoring schemas, and add shared compatibility and real-handler wire regression coverage.

commit.message:
agentHost: cap BYOK tools at 128 and warn when tools are dropped (#339184)

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

BYOK turns in Copilot harness (Agent Host / Copilot SDK) sessions fail
when more than 128 tools are enabled. OpenAI-compatible providers reject
the request.

- **Every tool is forwarded.** Runtime tool search is never enabled for
BYOK models. The launcher checks bare model ids (`claude-*`, `gpt-5-4`),
but BYOK selections are vendor-qualified (`anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`).
- **Turning tool search on isn't a fix.** In a probe against the bundled
runtime, Claude and custom models still sent every tool. gpt-5.4+ sent a
native `{ type: 'tool_search' }` tool, which the BYOK proxy rejects
(`Unsupported tools[0] type 'tool_search'`).
- **Neither does generic tool search yet.** The runtime has an
undocumented `GENERIC_CLIENT_TOOL_SEARCH` flag. In the probe it only
added a `generic_tool_search` tool and deferred nothing, so it doesn't
help BYOK yet.
- **The local harness avoids this** with virtual `activate_*` tool
groups. The Copilot harness has no equivalent.

## Change

- **Cap in the BYOK proxy** (`byokLmProxyService.ts`,
`byokResponsesTranslation.ts`):
  - Requests are trimmed to 128 tools.
- Tools the conversation already called are kept first, so their calls
stay valid. The remaining slots follow the runtime's order, which lists
built-ins first.
- Kept tools stay in their original order, so the request looks the same
from turn to turn.
  - The request is still sent. The run is never blocked.
- The Agent Host log gets a warning with the counts. Names of dropped
tools go to the trace log.
- **Warning in the chat:**
- The proxy fires `onDidCapTools` with the session id from the bearer
token. `CopilotAgent` sends it to that session.
- The session adds a `SystemNotification` to the active turn, with a new
`ByokToolLimitExceeded` kind and warning severity.
- It's shown once per dropped-tool count, so it doesn't repeat every
model call.
- Text: "The model only supports 128 tools, 114 tools were not provided
to the model."
- **Configure Tools link:** the workbench adapter appends a link that
opens Chat Customizations on the Tools section.
  - Only that one command is allowed to run from this message.
- Markdown in the host's text is escaped, so the host can't inject a
command link.
- The host sends plain text, so clients that don't know the new kind
still show readable text.
- **The BYOK warning stays visible:** `IChatWarningMessage` gets an
opt-in `keepVisibleWhenCollapsed` flag. The completed-response
disclosure keeps flagged warnings out of "Completed N steps", and only
the BYOK warning sets it. All other warnings collapse as before.
- **Host text can't inject command links:** angle brackets are escaped
too, so `<command:…>` autolinks and raw `<a href>` in the host text stay
plain text.
- **Accessible View:** `getChatResponsePlaintextParts` now includes
`warning` parts as "Warning: {text}", with links shown as their labels.
This applies to every warning, so they also show up in transcript Find.

## Notes for reviewers

- This is a stopgap that keeps BYOK runs working. The proper fix is
runtime tool search for custom providers. That needs SDK work: the
generic flag adds a search tool but defers nothing today.
- `IByokLmProxyService` gains `onDidCapTools`. `CopilotAgent` gains an
`IByokLmProxyService` constructor dependency, and the test subclasses
are updated for it.

## Testing

Unit tests added/updated:
- `capBridgeTools`: under the limit, trimming the end of the list,
keeping already-called tools, and the default limit.
- Proxy: a 200-tool request succeeds, the model gets 128 tools, and one
event fires with the right session id.
- Session: warning content and metadata, dedup by dropped count, no
warning without an active turn.
- Agent: cap events go only to the matching session.
- Adapter: renders as a warning with the trusted Configure Tools link
and escapes host markdown.
- Renderer: a flagged warning stays outside the collapsed steps and
isn't counted, while an unflagged warning is still collapsed. This test
fails without the fix.
- Adapter: host autolinks and HTML stay plain text, and the rendered
warning's only link is Configure Tools. This test fails without the fix.
- Accessible View: warnings and their link text are included.

Commands run:
- `./scripts/test.sh
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokLmProxyService.test.ts
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`:
passed (106)
- `./scripts/test.sh
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts …`:
passed (791, with the proxy and translation suites)
- `./scripts/test.sh
src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts`:
passed (188)
- `./scripts/test.sh
src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts
src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts`:
passed (610)
- `./scripts/test.sh
src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`: the new test
passes. 12 tests fail, the same 12 that fail on a clean `main` checkout
(external chat discovery, state-file resolution, `collectDebugLogs`).
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in changed files. The remaining
errors come from the local environment (missing electron types, and an
installed SDK that's older than the bump).

Manual check: in a BYOK session with 242 tools, the turn completes, the
warning stays visible above "Completed 2 steps", and the link opens
Customizations → Tools.

commit.message:
agentHost: preserve legacy policy-required sandboxing (#339144)

Prevent a per-session Off selection from overriding the legacy VS Code
`ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` policy in Copilot Agent Host on
macOS/Linux.

The policy already locked the global `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled`
setting, and sandboxing remained enabled for sessions following that
setting. However, forwarding preserved only the resolved `on` value, not
the fact that it was mandatory. Agent Host therefore treated the policy
like a personal preference, allowing a session-level Off selection to
override it.

## Scope

- **Affected:** Copilot Agent Host sessions on macOS/Linux governed by
the legacy VS Code `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` policy, when a session
selects or already has an Off override.
- **Not a general sandbox failure:** the sandbox implementation itself
and the legacy Local harness are not changed. Runtime-managed
`sandbox.enabled: true` already has enforcement and session controls
from [#338172](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338172); that is
a separate policy path.
- Personal sandbox preferences remain overridable. Windows continues to
use its separate `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows` setting.

## Change

- Forward the legacy policy requirement separately from editable root
settings. The host aggregates connection-owned contributions
restrictively, so settings edits or another client cannot clear an
active requirement.
- Combine that requirement with the host's existing runtime policy
restrictions. Reconnect restores the contribution before authentication
and session replay; withdrawal or disconnect-grace expiry removes only
the owning client's contribution.
- Enforce the requirement in session configuration, not just the UI, and
publish the effective policy to the existing session controls.
- Apply policy arrival and withdrawal to running sessions, including
their peer chats and subagents. Preserve permitted SDK-approved bypasses
without weakening runtime restrictions.

No SDK or runtime change is required. This addresses the legacy
sandbox-enable gap described in
[#339023](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339023), not its
other policy-parity gaps.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*
