agentHost: preserve legacy policy-required sandboxing (#339144)

Prevent a per-session Off selection from overriding the legacy VS Code
`ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` policy in Copilot Agent Host on
macOS/Linux.

The policy already locked the global `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled`
setting, and sandboxing remained enabled for sessions following that
setting. However, forwarding preserved only the resolved `on` value, not
the fact that it was mandatory. Agent Host therefore treated the policy
like a personal preference, allowing a session-level Off selection to
override it.

## Scope

- **Affected:** Copilot Agent Host sessions on macOS/Linux governed by
the legacy VS Code `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` policy, when a session
selects or already has an Off override.
- **Not a general sandbox failure:** the sandbox implementation itself
and the legacy Local harness are not changed. Runtime-managed
`sandbox.enabled: true` already has enforcement and session controls
from [#338172](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338172); that is
a separate policy path.
- Personal sandbox preferences remain overridable. Windows continues to
use its separate `chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows` setting.

## Change

- Forward the legacy policy requirement separately from editable root
settings. The host aggregates connection-owned contributions
restrictively, so settings edits or another client cannot clear an
active requirement.
- Combine that requirement with the host's existing runtime policy
restrictions. Reconnect restores the contribution before authentication
and session replay; withdrawal or disconnect-grace expiry removes only
the owning client's contribution.
- Enforce the requirement in session configuration, not just the UI, and
publish the effective policy to the existing session controls.
- Apply policy arrival and withdrawal to running sessions, including
their peer chats and subagents. Preserve permitted SDK-approved bypasses
without weakening runtime restrictions.

No SDK or runtime change is required. This addresses the legacy
sandbox-enable gap described in
[#339023](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339023), not its
other policy-parity gaps.

commit.message:
agentHost: cap BYOK tools at 128 and warn when tools are dropped

BYOK models in Copilot SDK sessions never get runtime tool search: the session launcher gates it on bare model ids, and the runtime's native tool_search type is not supported by the BYOK proxy. Every enabled tool was forwarded, so sessions with more than 128 tools failed against OpenAI-compatible providers.

The BYOK proxy now trims requests to 128 tools, keeping tools the conversation already called and then the runtime's order (built-ins first). The turn continues, and the affected session shows a warning with a link to the Tools page in Chat Customizations. Completed-response disclosures no longer fold warnings into the collapsed steps.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
automations: add customization selection and save progress (#339176)

* automations: add customization selection and save progress

Adds a way to select the customizations that an automation syncs, and shows progress while the
agent host syncs them.

- Adds an "Advanced" section to the automation dialog with a checkbox list of customizations.
  A saved customization that changed locally shows an "Outdated" pill. Saving the automation
  updates it.
- Keeps the automation dialog open while the agent host saves the change. Shows a progress bar
  and a status, and shows errors in the dialog.
- Adds getCustomizationChoices and customizationIds to the automation store contract.
- Uses file plugins at their original paths when a local window saves the automation, so the
  local agent host does not copy them.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

* automations: address review feedback on customization selection

- Uses a host-controlled allowlist to decide which file plugins the agent host uses in place,
  instead of trusting the client ID. A client cannot make the host load an arbitrary host path.
- Restores the MessagePort transport check for local agent host clients.
- Waits for the customization choices to load before the dialog saves, so the save always
  includes the selection.
- Reloads the customization choices when the workspace isolation changes.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

* agentHost: mark host-local automation plugins with a dedicated scheme

Replaces the allowlist of trusted host plugin directories with a URI scheme. A `file:` plugin URI
now always names a client resource, so a host path cannot be confused with a client path.

- Adds the `vscode-agent-host-file:` scheme for plugin URIs that name a directory on the agent
  host's own disk. The plugin manager uses these directories in place.
- Gives automation run sessions their captured and local in-place plugins with this scheme.
- Removes trustHostPluginDirectory and the in-place rule for paths under hostPluginsPath.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

chat: Fix tabbed model picker for Free and Student plans (#339130)

* Fix tabbed model picker for Free and Student plans

Plans that only get Auto now see Auto's routing tiers with the models they lack grouped under an "Upgrade for More Models" heading, and the Copilot tab no longer disappears behind BYOK providers when Copilot relays nothing selectable.

When the Copilot SDK lists no models, as it does for Free and Student accounts, the agent host now offers Auto with its routing profiles, mirroring the Copilot CLI integration. Model validation still fails open for that otherwise-empty catalog.

HydraFusion is now offered to Student plans only as an upgrade, the same as Free.

Fixes #338792

commit.message:
Add initial workspace context to Copilot Agent Host chats (#337342)

* Add bounded initial workspace context for Copilot Agent Host

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Format workspace context regression tests

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Make workspace snapshot test headings platform independent

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Scope virtual timers to the workspace context timeout test

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Snapshot the worktree a Copilot turn actually runs in

The first-turn workspace snapshot read session state, which still names the
picked folder when a worktree session sends its first message: the worktree
is created in resolveWorkingDirectoryBeforeSend, but state only picks up its
path after the provider materializes. The snapshot therefore listed the
original checkout and showed its absolute path while the agent worked in the
worktree.

Pass the resolved working directories, the same ones handed to the agent's
sendMessage, to outgoing-turn contributions and build the snapshot from them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep the workspace snapshot to first turns and off the TTFT path

Only the first turn of a new conversation gets the snapshot: the default chat
or a user-created peer chat with no completed turns. Forks and side chats
already inherit the source chat's history, and tool-spawned chats receive a
focused task from the chat that delegated them.

Start enumerating when the first turn is accepted so the file list overlaps
working-directory, model and attachment resolution instead of adding to time
to first token. The warm-up is skipped while a worktree is pending, because
the worktree does not exist yet. The send now waits at most one second (was
two) and keeps the roots that are ready instead of dropping the whole
snapshot when one root is slow.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address workspace snapshot review findings

- Prepare the rendered snapshot for a worktree session as soon as the
  worktree exists (onDidChangeWorkingDirectoryPending) instead of when the
  outgoing-turn contribution runs, so creating it overlaps the checkpoint,
  model selection and attachment resolution.
- Isolate failures per root: a root that cannot be listed is logged and
  omitted, and the healthy roots are still sent.
- Tie preparation to the turn: it is stopped when the send stops waiting,
  the turn ends, or the preparation is replaced. The new uncached
  AgentHostWorkspaceFiles.enumerate stops its ripgrep process on
  cancellation and never starts a queued scan that was cancelled. The cached
  getFiles used by file completions is unchanged.
- Skip bare repositories and directories inside .git before scanning.
- Build the tree from path segments instead of URIs; at the 50,000-file cap
  this drops the synchronous build from about 360ms to about 37ms.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Never wait for the workspace snapshot on send, and release it with its chat

- The first send now includes only roots whose tree is already rendered for
  the directories the turn runs in, and omits roots still being listed,
  instead of waiting up to a second per root. Preparation still starts when
  the turn is accepted, or when a first-send worktree is created.
- If a session's worktree already exists when its first turn is accepted,
  the default chat prepares in the worktree, as the send path does.
- Stop preparation when a chat is removed (SessionChatRemoved) or its session
  is removed (onDidRemoveSession), not only on turn end.
- Recognize a linked worktree's admin directory (HEAD, gitdir, and a
  commondir naming a repository with objects/) even when its common
  directory is not named .git, and test it with a real linked worktree.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Build the workspace snapshot without blocking, for every waiting chat

- Build the tree in batches of 2,000 paths that yield to the event loop and
  stop once preparation is cancelled, so a large root cannot hold up the
  provider send. Sorted children are cached so rendering sorts each
  directory once.
- Track every first-turn chat waiting for a session's worktree instead of
  only the last one, and prepare or release each independently.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Make the initial workspace snapshot reliable, bounded, and observable

Evals showed the first model request leaves ~0.7s after the turn starts, and
13-14% of sessions dropped the snapshot because a full ripgrep enumeration
had not finished. Drops were logged only at trace, so misses could not be
diagnosed.

- Walk directories breadth first through IFileService, reading only the
  directories whose names fit the 2,000-character budget, instead of
  enumerating every file with ripgrep. A cold send-time walk takes 2-29ms on
  real repositories, including a 36k-file one that took ~0.8s to enumerate.
- Wait up to one second at send for roots still being prepared, and start
  preparation at send when the turn skipped ChatTurnStarted or its
  directories changed, instead of dropping the snapshot.
- Like the classic Copilot Chat workspace structure, skip hidden entries and
  a short list of dependency and build folders, and do not apply
  .gitignore, which emptied the tree for projects kept under ignored folders
  such as vendor/.
- Log every first send at info with the outcome of each root, and report
  agentHost.workspaceSnapshot telemetry with included, pending, empty, and
  unreadable root counts and the wait time.
- Revert the uncached enumerate added to AgentHostWorkspaceFiles, which is
  no longer used, so the expected ripgrep cancellation no longer logs a
  warning.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Do not add a second workspace snapshot to an unloaded restored chat

send_message can start a turn on a restored peer chat before its history is
loaded. Its merged session state then reports no turns, so the chat looked
new and could receive another snapshot on top of the one already in its
provider conversation. Treat a chat as new only when its chat state is
loaded and has no turns, matching classic Copilot Chat, where history is
always loaded before a request runs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Start the workspace snapshot for host-started first turns too

create_session, send_message, automations, and other
AgentHostTurnService.startTurnMessage paths dispatch ChatTurnStarted as a
server action, so onDidApplyClientAction never saw them and preparation only
started in onOutgoingTurn, putting the whole walk on time to first token.

Start preparation from onDidDispatchAction, which sees client and server
actions once each, skip rejected actions, and drop onDidApplyClientAction so
client turns are not seen twice. A new AgentSideEffects test starts a first
turn through AgentHostTurnService and checks the snapshot was already being
prepared when the outgoing-turn contribution ran.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Consume the workspace snapshot only when its turn reaches the provider

The snapshot was marked consumed in onOutgoingTurn and any turn in chat
history made the chat ineligible. A first turn that never reached Copilot,
such as a local /rename or a turn cancelled at the final pre-dispatch
checks, therefore suppressed the snapshot for the next turn that did, and
agentHost.workspaceSnapshot reported a send that never happened.

- AgentHostTurnTracker fires onDidDispatchTurn from markSendDispatched,
  after the final cancellation checks.
- The contribution consumes, logs, and reports the snapshot only on that
  event. A tracked first turn that ends without it is remembered as
  undispatched, so it does not count as provider history.
- A restored chat with history, or a chat whose history is not loaded yet,
  is still never treated as new.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Guard workspace snapshot state by turn and run before queue drain

- A cancelled turn's send can keep unwinding while the next turn starts.
  onOutgoingTurn now acts only for the chat's active turn and rechecks after
  its wait, so a stale send can no longer overwrite the next turn's tracked
  turn or dispose its preparation.
- The contribution now has order 175, so its onTurnEnd runs before
  QueueDrainContribution (200). A provider turn queued behind a local command
  is started from queue drain's onTurnEnd and now sees the local command as
  undispatched, so its preparation starts at dispatch instead of at send.
  Outgoing instruction order is unchanged, and the order no longer collides
  with other contributions.

Tests cover a second turn starting while the cancelled first send is still
waiting, and a provider turn queued behind /rename through the real send
path; both fail without their fix.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Detect first-turn ends from terminal state actions, not onTurnEnd

A cancelled local command such as a long-running !command fires no turn end
when it is cancelled: its turn was never tracked, so the only turn end comes
from the command's completion, possibly after a replacement turn started.
The replacement turn then saw the cancelled command as provider history and
lost its snapshot, and the late turn end released the replacement turn's
preparation and tracked turn unconditionally.

Observe a tracked first turn's end from its terminal state action
(ChatTurnComplete, ChatTurnCancelled, or ChatError) through
onDidDispatchAction, which runs as the state changes, and act only when the
action's turn id matches the tracked turn. Stale ends for an old turn are
ignored, and the contribution no longer implements onTurnEnd.

A new AgentSideEffects test pauses a real !command, cancels it, starts a
provider turn that prepares and waits before dispatch, then completes the
old command; the provider turn is sent with its snapshot and reported once.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: drop content-excluded paths from the workspace snapshot

The contribution now hands the provider a structured snapshot. The Copilot
provider checks every listed path with the SDK's contentExclusion.checkPaths
once its session exists, drops excluded entries with everything below them,
and omits the snapshot when the policy can't be evaluated.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: check snapshot roots for content exclusion and count the snapshot as sent only on submission

- Each snapshot root carries its path, which is checked with its entries; an
  excluded root is dropped entirely.
- The Copilot session reports delivery from its user-prompt-submitted hook,
  so a send abandoned during the content exclusion check leaves the snapshot
  for the next turn instead of consuming it.
- agentHost.workspaceSnapshot reports what reached the model after exclusion,
  plus the exclusion outcome and excluded path count.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: skip the snapshot's content exclusion check when the account doesn't use it

Like Copilot Chat, only check content exclusion when the Copilot token enables
it (copilotIgnoreEnabled) or that can't be determined. Otherwise a new
session's runtime may still be fetching rules, which delays the first turn and
can drop the snapshot for every user.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: gate the workspace snapshot behind a setting and keep its content exclusion check off the send path

- Add `chat.agentHost.experimental.workspaceSnapshot` (off by default, experiment-controlled) and skip all snapshot work while it is disabled.
- Start the content exclusion check when the send starts and wait for it only just before the prompt is submitted, so it overlaps the rest of the send preparation.
- Report how long the check took and how long the send waited for it in `agentHost.workspaceSnapshot`.
- Keep no more entries of a directory than the size budget could list.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: rename the workspace snapshot setting to chat.experimental.workspaceSnapshot

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: send the workspace snapshot without a content exclusion check

The check ran before the first turn started, when the SDK session has no content exclusion service yet, so it always reported the policy as unavailable and the snapshot was dropped for every account with content exclusion enabled.

- Render the snapshot into the host instructions directly; it lists file names only, never contents.
- Reduce the snapshot contract to rendered lines and a delivery callback.
- Remove the content exclusion fields from `agentHost.workspaceSnapshot`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: correct the workspace snapshot order comment

The contribution's order only sequences its hooks; the provider renders the
snapshot after every host instruction. Also drop a duplicated test JSDoc.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: send the workspace snapshot as a plain host instruction

The contribution now returns the snapshot as an ordinary host instruction
instead of a structured value the provider renders and reports back on.
This removes the provider-side changes. The snapshot counts as sent when
the host hands the turn to the provider, so a turn that fails after that
point is not retried with it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: cover the workspace snapshot's instruction order and bound its commondir read

Adds a built-in sequence test for an enabled Copilot first turn, so the
snapshot stays between the Markdown plan and chat surface instructions.
The Git-storage check now reads a linked worktree's commondir pointer
with a 4 KB limit, and the docs say that it reads it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

is created in resolveWorkingDirectoryBeforeSend, but state only picks up its
path after the provider materializes. The snapshot therefore listed the
original checkout and showed its absolute path while the agent worked in the
worktree.

Pass the resolved working directories, the same ones handed to the agent's
sendMessage, to outgoing-turn contributions and build the snapshot from them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep the workspace snapshot to first turns and off the TTFT path

Only the first turn of a new conversation gets the snapshot: the default chat
or a user-created peer chat with no completed turns. Forks and side chats
already inherit the source chat's history, and tool-spawned chats receive a
focused task from the chat that delegated them.

Start enumerating when the first turn is accepted so the file list overlaps
working-directory, model and attachment resolution instead of adding to time
to first token. The warm-up is skipped while a worktree is pending, because
the worktree does not exist yet. The send now waits at most one second (was
two) and keeps the roots that are ready instead of dropping the whole
snapshot when one root is slow.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address workspace snapshot review findings

- Prepare the rendered snapshot for a worktree session as soon as the
  worktree exists (onDidChangeWorkingDirectoryPending) instead of when the
  outgoing-turn contribution runs, so creating it overlaps the checkpoint,
  model selection and attachment resolution.
- Isolate failures per root: a root that cannot be listed is logged and
  omitted, and the healthy roots are still sent.
- Tie preparation to the turn: it is stopped when the send stops waiting,
  the turn ends, or the preparation is replaced. The new uncached
  AgentHostWorkspaceFiles.enumerate stops its ripgrep process on
  cancellation and never starts a queued scan that was cancelled. The cached
  getFiles used by file completions is unchanged.
- Skip bare repositories and directories inside .git before scanning.
- Build the tree from path segments instead of URIs; at the 50,000-file cap
  this drops the synchronous build from about 360ms to about 37ms.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Never wait for the workspace snapshot on send, and release it with its chat

- The first send now includes only roots whose tree is already rendered for
  the directories the turn runs in, and omits roots still being listed,
  instead of waiting up to a second per root. Preparation still starts when
  the turn is accepted, or when a first-send worktree is created.
- If a session's worktree already exists when its first turn is accepted,
  the default chat prepares in the worktree, as the send path does.
- Stop preparation when a chat is removed (SessionChatRemoved) or its session
  is removed (onDidRemoveSession), not only on turn end.
- Recognize a linked worktree's admin directory (HEAD, gitdir, and a
  commondir naming a repository with objects/) even when its common
  directory is not named .git, and test it with a real linked worktree.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Build the workspace snapshot without blocking, for every waiting chat

- Build the tree in batches of 2,000 paths that yield to the event loop and
  stop once preparation is cancelled, so a large root cannot hold up the
  provider send. Sorted children are cached so rendering sorts each
  directory once.
- Track every first-turn chat waiting for a session's worktree instead of
  only the last one, and prepare or release each independently.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Make the initial workspace snapshot reliable, bounded, and observable

Evals showed the first model request leaves ~0.7s after the turn starts, and
13-14% of sessions dropped the snapshot because a full ripgrep enumeration
had not finished. Drops were logged only at trace, so misses could not be
diagnosed.

- Walk directories breadth first through IFileService, reading only the
  directories whose names fit the 2,000-character budget, instead of
  enumerating every file with ripgrep. A cold send-time walk takes 2-29ms on
  real repositories, including a 36k-file one that took ~0.8s to enumerate.
- Wait up to one second at send for roots still being prepared, and start
  preparation at send when the turn skipped ChatTurnStarted or its
  directories changed, instead of dropping the snapshot.
- Like the classic Copilot Chat workspace structure, skip hidden entries and
  a short list of dependency and build folders, and do not apply
  .gitignore, which emptied the tree for projects kept under ignored folders
  such as vendor/.
- Log every first send at info with the outcome of each root, and report
  agentHost.workspaceSnapshot telemetry with included, pending, empty, and
  unreadable root counts and the wait time.
- Revert the uncached enumerate added to AgentHostWorkspaceFiles, which is
  no longer used, so the expected ripgrep cancellation no longer logs a
  warning.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

send_message can start a turn on a restored peer chat before its history is
loaded. Its merged session state then reports no turns, so the chat looked
new and could receive another snapshot on top of the one already in its
provider conversation. Treat a chat as new only when its chat state is
loaded and has no turns, matching classic Copilot Chat, where history is
always loaded before a request runs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Start the workspace snapshot for host-started first turns too

create_session, send_message, automations, and other
AgentHostTurnService.startTurnMessage paths dispatch ChatTurnStarted as a
server action, so onDidApplyClientAction never saw them and preparation only
started in onOutgoingTurn, putting the whole walk on time to first token.

Start preparation from onDidDispatchAction, which sees client and server
actions once each, skip rejected actions, and drop onDidApplyClientAction so
client turns are not seen twice. A new AgentSideEffects test starts a first
turn through AgentHostTurnService and checks the snapshot was already being
prepared when the outgoing-turn contribution ran.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Consume the workspace snapshot only when its turn reaches the provider

The snapshot was marked consumed in onOutgoingTurn and any turn in chat
history made the chat ineligible. A first turn that never reached Copilot,
such as a local /rename or a turn cancelled at the final pre-dispatch
checks, therefore suppressed the snapshot for the next turn that did, and
agentHost.workspaceSnapshot reported a send that never happened.

- AgentHostTurnTracker fires onDidDispatchTurn from markSendDispatched,
  after the final cancellation checks.
- The contribution consumes, logs, and reports the snapshot only on that
  event. A tracked first turn that ends without it is remembered as
  undispatched, so it does not count as provider history.
- A restored chat with history, or a chat whose history is not loaded yet,
  is still never treated as new.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Guard workspace snapshot state by turn and run before queue drain

- A cancelled turn's send can keep unwinding while the next turn starts.
  onOutgoingTurn now acts only for the chat's active turn and rechecks after
  its wait, so a stale send can no longer overwrite the next turn's tracked
  turn or dispose its preparation.
- The contribution now has order 175, so its onTurnEnd runs before
  QueueDrainContribution (200). A provider turn queued behind a local command
  is started from queue drain's onTurnEnd and now sees the local command as
  undispatched, so its preparation starts at dispatch instead of at send.
  Outgoing instruction order is unchanged, and the order no longer collides
  with other contributions.

Tests cover a second turn starting while the cancelled first send is still
waiting, and a provider turn queued behind /rename through the real send
path; both fail without their fix.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Detect first-turn ends from terminal state actions, not onTurnEnd

A cancelled local command such as a long-running !command fires no turn end
when it is cancelled: its turn was never tracked, so the only turn end comes
from the command's completion, possibly after a replacement turn started.
The replacement turn then saw the cancelled command as provider history and
lost its snapshot, and the late turn end released the replacement turn's
preparation and tracked turn unconditionally.

Observe a tracked first turn's end from its terminal state action
(ChatTurnComplete, ChatTurnCancelled, or ChatError) through
onDidDispatchAction, which runs as the state changes, and act only when the
action's turn id matches the tracked turn. Stale ends for an old turn are
ignored, and the contribution no longer implements onTurnEnd.

A new AgentSideEffects test pauses a real !command, cancels it, starts a
provider turn that prepares and waits before dispatch, then completes the
old command; the provider turn is sent with its snapshot and reported once.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: drop content-excluded paths from the workspace snapshot

The contribution now hands the provider a structured snapshot. The Copilot
provider checks every listed path with the SDK's contentExclusion.checkPaths
once its session exists, drops excluded entries with everything below them,
and omits the snapshot when the policy can't be evaluated.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: check snapshot roots for content exclusion and count the snapshot as sent only on submission

- Each snapshot root carries its path, which is checked with its entries; an
  excluded root is dropped entirely.
- The Copilot session reports delivery from its user-prompt-submitted hook,
  so a send abandoned during the content exclusion check leaves the snapshot
  for the next turn instead of consuming it.
- agentHost.workspaceSnapshot reports what reached the model after exclusion,
  plus the exclusion outcome and excluded path count.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: skip the snapshot's content exclusion check when the account doesn't use it

Like Copilot Chat, only check content exclusion when the Copilot token enables
it (copilotIgnoreEnabled) or that can't be determined. Otherwise a new
session's runtime may still be fetching rules, which delays the first turn and
can drop the snapshot for every user.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: gate the workspace snapshot behind a setting and keep its content exclusion check off the send path

- Add `chat.agentHost.experimental.workspaceSnapshot` (off by default, experiment-controlled) and skip all snapshot work while it is disabled.
- Start the content exclusion check when the send starts and wait for it only just before the prompt is submitted, so it overlaps the rest of the send preparation.
- Report how long the check took and how long the send waited for it in `agentHost.workspaceSnapshot`.
- Keep no more entries of a directory than the size budget could list.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: rename the workspace snapshot setting to chat.experimental.workspaceSnapshot

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: send the workspace snapshot without a content exclusion check

The check ran before the first turn started, when the SDK session has no content exclusion service yet, so it always reported the policy as unavailable and the snapshot was dropped for every account with content exclusion enabled.

- Render the snapshot into the host instructions directly; it lists file names only, never contents.
- Reduce the snapshot contract to rendered lines and a delivery callback.
- Remove the content exclusion fields from `agentHost.workspaceSnapshot`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: correct the workspace snapshot order comment

The contribution's order only sequences its hooks; the provider renders the
snapshot after every host instruction. Also drop a duplicated test JSDoc.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: send the workspace snapshot as a plain host instruction

The contribution now returns the snapshot as an ordinary host instruction
instead of a structured value the provider renders and reports back on.
This removes the provider-side changes. The snapshot counts as sent when
the host hands the turn to the provider, so a turn that fails after that
point is not retried with it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: cover the workspace snapshot's instruction order and bound its commondir read

Adds a built-in sequence test for an enabled Copilot first turn, so the
snapshot stays between the Markdown plan and chat surface instructions.
The Git-storage check now reads a linked worktree's commondir pointer
with a 4 KB limit, and the docs say that it reads it.

commit.message:
Publish chat background work and show background shells above the chat input (#338723)

* Publish chat background work and show background shells

Publish Copilot's running and waiting shells and running background subagents as AHP chat background work, and project the shells onto the Agents window's Background Shells pill.

* Publish only background shells as background work

Follow the protocol change that starts background work with shells only. The provider still skips kinds it doesn't render, since newer hosts can send more.

* Stop publishing background shell status

Follow the protocol change that drops status from background work. Every listed shell is unfinished, and Copilot never reports a shell as idle. The pill now shows the attached or detached mode and elapsed time.

* Ignore background work in the read shell E2E snapshot

The async shell is now published as background work from a separate task-list read, so its timing against the tool calls isn't part of this scenario.

* Drop terminal from the background shell work protocol copy

Follow the protocol change that removes the unused terminal field. Nothing in VS Code set or read it.

* Show background shells in the editor window's chat

Move the Background Shells pill control and the background work projection into the workbench so the editor window's Agent Host chat input can show the same pill as the Agents window. Share the pill's accessibility help between both windows.

* Agent Host: reconcile background work after a Copilot client restart

Addresses review feedback on stale shells after a client restart or crash. A session that replaced another started with an empty baseline, so shells the new runtime no longer reported stayed listed. The host now passes the chat's current background work when a watch attaches, and the session removes entries missing from its first read.

* Agent Host: keep reading background work after an abort

Addresses review feedback on the abort race. Aborting a turn bumped the task status revision without queuing a read, so a read in flight was discarded and the detached shell poll could stop for good, since detached shells report no exit on their own. The session now reads again once the abort settles.

* Sync background work protocol with AHP

Match microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482: background shells can link their terminal, and background subagents are their own kind that points at the subagent's chat. The Background Shells pill still shows shells only.

* Publish background subagents as background work

Running background agents are published with their chat. Idle ones have already reported back, so they're left out. Shells don't set a terminal yet; that waits for output streaming.

* Key background shell rows by the protocol id

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338723#discussion_r4136322435.
Rows used Copilot's shell ID from _meta as their identity, which the protocol doesn't guarantee is unique. Key rows by the entry id instead, and show Copilot's shell ID separately, only when the agent reports one.

* Keep background work out of the retained subagent E2E snapshot

Running background subagents are now published as background work. Those actions come from a separate task-list read, so their timing against the subagent's tool calls isn't part of this scenario, and CI's snapshot comparison failed on every platform. Ignore them here, as the read-shell scenario already does.

* Remove a stray E2E snapshot artifact

A failing local run left this .actual file next to the retained background subagent snapshot, and it was committed by mistake. Hygiene rejects it, and the test runner logs when it deletes it, which fails the no-console-output check.

* Sync the background work docs with AHP

Match microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482 at d513c6fb, which says background work lists only active work.

* Show only Detached on background shells

Attached is the common case, so an unlabeled shell reads as attached and only detached shells carry a label, matching the GitHub app.

* Sync the AHP protocol with microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482

Take agent-host-protocol at c53aef24, the head of #482 after merging main, so this PR and #482 can merge back to back. That also brings in chat move and reorder from #484: reject moveChat with InvalidParams, since clients may only move chats that advertise movable: true and this host never does.

* Sync the shorter background work description from AHP

Take agent-host-protocol at ab694bfd, the head of microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482. The only change is the shortened backgroundWork doc text from its review.

* Read background shells from chat state instead of chat summaries

microsoft/agent-host-protocol#482 dropped ChatSummary.backgroundWork, so
session subscribers no longer receive every chat's background work. The
Agents window pill now reads ChatState.backgroundWork through the active
session's chat subscription, like the editor window already did, and the
state manager no longer mirrors the list into chat summaries.

Syncs the protocol to microsoft/agent-host-protocol@dc9ff6b0.

commit.message:
Mark virtual tool groups as used when they are activated (#338812)

Activating a virtual tool group never updated the group's own
lastUsedOnTurn, so a just-activated group ranked as least recently used.
When the activation pushed the tool count over HARD_TOOL_LIMIT, the trim
collapsed that same group before the request was sent, and the model
could never reach the tools it was told were activated.

commit.message:
chat: preserve reasoning across turns and custom providers (#338874)

* chat: preserve earlier-turn reasoning for opted-in models

Honor preserved-thinking capabilities in both Copilot and extension-contributed endpoints. Enable Kimi K3 by default and support per-model opt-in or opt-out while retaining same-model and Messages API safeguards.

Fixes #338820. Verified with red-green request serialization tests and 607 targeted tests.

* chat: carry reasoning protocol capabilities through model API

Declare the selected provider API and adaptive-thinking mode across language-model registration and selection. Unknown protocols no longer bypass the Messages safeguard, and extension-contributed endpoints honor family aliases when choosing the preserved-thinking default.

pull_requests.title: copilot: dedup ADO auth-change events before rechecking repo status
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #320570

The ADO auth-change handler in `CodeSearchChunkSearch` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/node/codeSearch/codeSearchChunkSearch.ts`) re-fetched repo authorization status — an HTTP `semanticsearchstatus` request per tracked repo — on every `onDidAdoAuthenticationChange` event, including no-op silent token refreshes (e.g. triggered by window focus changes) that don't actually change the session identity. The existing GitHub auth handler already guards against this with a session-id + identity dedup; the ADO handler did not.

This splits the previously combined `Event.any(onDidAdoAuthenticationChange, onDidChangeIndexState)` listener into two independent listeners:
- The auth-change listener now dedups on session id + `authenticationSessionIdentityEquals` (mirroring the GitHub path), so no-op token refreshes no longer trigger a refetch.
- The index-state-change listener is left completely unguarded, so a real index-state notification can never be suppressed by the auth dedup.

Also promotes `anyAdoSession` from `BaseAuthenticationService` onto the `IAuthenticationService` interface (needed to read current session state from the dedup check), with two unrelated `IAuthenticationService` test mocks updated for interface compliance.

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] agentHost: forward tool-result images to BYOK models
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #339830 from `main`.

Fixes #339595
Fixes #339439

## Problem

In agent-host sessions, a BYOK (OpenAI-compatible) model never received images returned by tools such as `view`. It only received the text receipt `Viewed image file successfully.`

## Root cause

There were two problems:

1. **Vision capability never reached the runtime.** `synthesizeByokSessionConfig` registered BYOK models with token limits only. The renderer already reports `supportsVision`, but it wasn't passed on, so the Copilot runtime treated every BYOK model as text-only. It replaced tool-result images with the text receipt before the request reached the BYOK proxy. I confirmed this by running the SDK runtime against a stub `/responses` server. Without the capability, `function_call_output.output` is the plain string. With `capabilities.supports.vision: true`, it's an `[input_text, input_image]` array.
2. **The BYOK LM bridge had no image channel for tool outputs.** Once vision is declared, the array output was passed through untyped, and the renderer wrapped it in a text part.

## Changes

- `copilotSessionLauncher.ts`: forward `supportsVision` as `capabilities.supports.vision` on each BYOK `ProviderModelConfig`.
- `agentHostByokLm.ts`: add an optional `images` field to the two tool-output bridge items. `output` stays text, so a renderer that doesn't know the new field still gets today's text result.
- `byokResponsesTranslation.ts`: split array tool outputs into text plus images, reusing the existing data-URL and MIME validation from user messages.
- `agentHostByokLmHandler.ts`: forward the images as `data` parts inside the LM API `tool_result`, the same shape the in-extension path produces.

## How to test

1. Turn on `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`.
2. Add an OpenAI-compatible BYOK model that supports images (e.g. `gpt-4o`), with `"vision": true` and `"toolCalling": true`.
3. Put an image containing text the model can't guess (e.g. `ZEBRA-7341`) in the workspace.
4. In an agent-host session with that model, ask: *"Use the view tool to open probe.png and tell me exactly what text it contains. If you didn't receive image pixels, say so."*
   - Before this change: the model says it only got "Viewed image file successfully."
   - After this change: the model reads the text.
5. With `"vision": false`, the model should still get the text receipt and the turn should finish cleanly.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokLmProxyService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostByokLmHandler.test.ts`: passed, 145 tests.
- New tests use the exact payload captured from the runtime, plus a renderer `tool_result` mapping test. The launcher snapshot test now covers `supportsVision`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: reports 20 errors, the same 20 as without this change. They come from the locally installed `@github/copilot-sdk` (1.0.16) being older than the version pinned in `package.json`. None are in files this PR touches.

pull_requests.title: Keep contributed tool sets whose members register late
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Related to #329320

## Problem

On VS Code Web, Agent mode never gives the model Copilot's `read_file` tool (`copilot_readFile`). The agent falls back to `cat` in the terminal and can't open tool output that was saved to a file (anything over about 8 KB). The same request works on VS Code Desktop.

In the attached debug logs, every Copilot tool in the `read`, `web`, `vscode` and `execute` sets is missing, and the `web` set doesn't appear in the tool picker. Copilot tools in `edit` and `search` reach the model.

## Cause

When core registers a contributed tool set, it looks up its member tools. If some were found, the set was created and later members were added as they registered. If none were found, the set was skipped and never recovered.

Tool lookup goes through `isPermitted`, which depends on `chat.agent.enabled`, so members can be unresolvable while the window starts up. `edit` and `search` each contain an always-permitted core tool (`rename`, `usages`), so they survived. The other sets had no such tool and were lost. I couldn't confirm why the timing is different on web; a late-arriving account policy or remote extension host are the likely candidates.

pull_requests.title: sessions: Open cloud sandbox sessions without waking the environment
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

Opening a cloud sandbox session in the Agents Window dialed the sandbox before anything rendered. A dormant environment sat behind a Mission Control compute resume on every click, and when the resume failed (deleted environment) the open rejected outright, so the persisted-history fallback from #329292 was unreachable.

The cause is #334863: it added an on-demand connect to the shared `RemoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.prepareSessionForOpen`, and `SessionsService` awaits that hook on open and runs it on restore. The sandbox provider inherited it, so every open became a wake.

A second gap sat behind that one. After the user presses **Connect** in the banner, the chat on screen stayed bound to the read-only history stand-in: the content provider was replaced under the same session type, but nothing reloaded the chat. The composer reappeared while the model's `isReadOnly` stayed `true`, so sends were silently rejected until the session was re-opened.

## Changes

- **`CloudSandboxSessionsProvider`** opts out of `prepareSessionForOpen`. Opening or restoring a sandbox session never dials it; `CloudSandboxSessionContribution` activation reads the environment's state and connects only to an online environment, otherwise serving Mission Control history read-only with the connection banner offering the connect action. Waking a dormant environment is always a user action (no auto-wake).
- **Agents Window `ChatView`** reloads a bound chat when its session type's content provider is unregistered and then registered again. It saves view state, releases the model, waits for the model store to actually dispose it (bounded by `REPLACED_PROVIDER_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS`), then runs the normal load. A newer load supersedes a pending reload; a provider that merely goes away leaves the transcript on screen. The same path recovers a remote host that reconnected with a new client id.
- Specs: one paragraph each in `REMOTE_AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md` (open never wakes) and `SESSIONS.md` (chat view ↔ provider replacement contract).

## How to test

1. Enable cloud sandboxes in the Agents Window and open a sandbox session whose environment is offline.
   - Expected: the transcript renders immediately from history, read-only, with the **"Environment offline." [Connect]** banner. No `/connect` request is issued (check the Agent Host / Cloud Sandbox log).
2. Press **Connect**.
   - Expected: "Connecting…" banner while the transcript stays visible; once the connection lands the chat reloads briefly at the same scroll position, the banner clears, and a message can be sent to the live sandbox.
3. If the connect fails, the read-only transcript stays and the banner offers **Retry**.
4. Reload the window with that session active: the environment is not woken on restore.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatGroupsView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts` — 744 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing
- New tests: `CloudSandboxSessionsProvider opening` (fails without the override: 2 dials; passes with it: 0) and three `ChatView` provider-replacement tests (reload after release without double-clear, newer load supersedes, timeout fallback)
- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- `npx eslint` on the changed TypeScript files — clean
- Not run: manual end-to-end against a live sandbox.

## Notes for reviewers

- The post-Connect reload is one brief transcript re-render, coinciding with the banner clearing. Rebinding the same `ChatModel` to the new provided session would avoid it but means making `ChatServiceImpl.loadRemoteSession`'s wiring re-runnable for every contributed session type; deliberately out of scope here.
- The Editor window has the same stale-model gap after Connect; this PR only addresses the Agents Window flow.

pull_requests.title: Fix send button overflow in chat input toolbar for narrow widths
Fix UTF-8 encoding of MCP resource URI template values
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339843

Non-ASCII MCP resource-template values currently produce percent-encoded UTF-16 code units: `café` becomes `caf%E9`, and an emoji becomes two surrogate escapes. Encode valid Unicode strings as UTF-8 while retaining the existing ASCII punctuation escaping. Count prefix lengths by Unicode code point so a supplementary character remains intact. This follows [RFC 6570 §3.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6570.html#section-3.2.1).

The two added tests cover accented/CJK/supplementary characters, punctuation, and supplementary-character prefixes; all 26 existing tests, including control-character zero-padding, remain unchanged.

Validation:
- Actual-source targeted transpilation followed by `node test/unit/node/index.js --run src/vs/base/test/common/uriTemplate.test.ts`: 29 passing (28 URI-template tests plus the runner's error check); the two additions fail before the fix. Node 24.19.0 on Linux.
- Repository ESLint on both changed files and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Independent actual-source checks: 192 Unicode cases pass; 3,120 ASCII scalar and 32 string-composite controls remain unchanged.

No Electron/UI or live MCP-server test was run. Malformed lone-surrogate inputs now throw `URIError`, as reserved expansion already does; the encoder also string-coerces non-string array elements. Existing reserved-percent and composite-operator behavior is otherwise outside this fix.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and an independent review.

pull_requests.title: chat: Show only the selected harness's Copilot models in Manage Models
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #326538

## Problem

The Manage Models (Language Models) editor can show several groups that are all labelled **Copilot**. Copilot models come from:

- the regular Copilot provider (`copilot`)
- the Copilot CLI extension (`copilotcli`)
- each agent host harness. The Copilot CLI agent host groups its models under `copilotcli`; the Claude and Codex agent hosts group theirs under `copilot`, reaching them through the Copilot subscription (Claude via its `copilot` transport, Codex via `vscode-proxy`).

Each of these lists only works in its own harness, but they all appear together with the same label.

## Change

Manage Models now scopes the "Copilot" lists to the harness it was opened for:

- If the harness publishes its own Copilot models (models with `targetChatSessionType` equal to the harness), only that list is shown.
- Otherwise, only the regular Copilot models are shown.
- Models from other providers (BYOK, Ollama, OpenRouter, a harness's non-Copilot groups, …) are unaffected.

How the editor learns the harness:

- The model picker's **Manage Models...** action passes the harness it picks models for: `ChatInputPart.modelTargetSessionType` in the chat input, or the current model's target in the Agents window picker.
- Other entry points (Command Palette, account menu, notifications) fall back to the last focused chat's harness, then to the active customization harness.

Scope is limited to the Manage Models editor. The Chat Customizations editor's Models section and the model picker contents are unchanged.

## How to test

1. Make sure Copilot models from more than one harness are registered (e.g. local, Copilot CLI agent host, Claude/Codex agent hosts).
2. In a chat, select the **Local** harness, open the model picker and choose **Manage Models...**. Only the regular **Copilot** group is listed; other providers are unchanged.
3. Switch the chat to the **Copilot CLI** agent host harness and open **Manage Models...** again. Only the agent host's Copilot group is listed.
4. Repeat with the **Claude** and **Codex** agent host harnesses. Each shows only its own Copilot group.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "ChatModelsViewModel|ChatModelsWidget|modelPicker|ModelPicker|ChatInputPart"`: passed, 372 tests, including a new `ChatModelsViewModel` test covering all four Copilot sources plus a non-Copilot harness group.
- `npx eslint` on the changed files: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in the changed files. It fails only on errors that already exist in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/*` (`proxyCa`), which this change doesn't touch.
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- Manual steps 2–4 above have not been run yet.

pull_requests.title: nes: latch quota-triggered Copilot token refreshes
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #331579

Repeated NES quota errors can leave the legacy quota flags unchanged, causing the client to reset and mint a Copilot token on every failed request.

- Latch quota-triggered refreshes per account, endpoint, and model across completions and HTTP/WebSocket chat. Preserve known-exhausted guards and coalesce concurrent refreshes.
- Keep the latch across token rotations and elapsed time. A newer successful request rearms its scope; a five-minute backstop bounds failed refreshes and rapid recovery/failure cycles.
- Track request ordering so an older success cannot discard a newer quota failure or rearm its latch. Use GitHub account/issuer identity, snapshot static-session IDs separately.
- Stop successful requests from invalidating tokens based on unrelated legacy quota flags. Make the explicit `github.copilot.refreshToken` command force renewal so plan upgrades still refresh cached entitlement metadata.
- Add regression tests and forward the request context through the simulation fetcher.

Upgrades the root and remote-server `@github/copilot-sdk` dependency from `1.0.17-preview.4` to `1.0.17-preview.5`, with the SDK-bundled runtime pin updated to `1.0.92-5`. Both lockfiles were regenerated by running `npm install` from the repository root, and their changes are confined to the SDK and its platform packages.

This is a follow-up to merged #339423, based on current main rather than extending the old PR.

### SDK compatibility

Preview.5 adds `AccountAuthInfo`, a credential-free provider-owned account that exposes `login` directly and does not have `copilotUser`. Update connector account matching to read that login through the SDK's discriminant instead of assuming a Copilot-user payload. Parameterize the existing launcher test for token-callback and provider-owned accounts, including a different-login account that must not be selected. The initial SDK compilation error is resolved without casts or narrowed production types.

No E2E assertions, gates, fixtures, prompt baselines, or AHP baselines were changed.

### Validation

- `npm install` — passed in the repository root. Root/remote SDK and runtime pins were checked against their installed packages.
- `npm run compile-client` — passed with zero errors after handling the new authentication variant.
- `env -u COPILOT_HOME VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` — passed: 99 tests, including both connector account variants.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSessionLauncher.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` — passed.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/{providerIntegration/*,e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E,e2e/providers/codexAgentHostLive}.integrationTest.js'` — clean repeat passed: 70 tests and 6 existing skips. The initial run hit the unchanged Codex plugin-MCP advertisement failure; that exact test passed an isolated retry, and the entire batch then passed without changes.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 npm run test-agent-host-e2e` — initial attempt passed conformance, Claude, Codex, Copilot, and all five OTel scenarios, but the managed-settings entrypoint timed out during startup. Its complete isolated entrypoint passed an unchanged retry.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --jobs 2` — clean full strict replay repeat passed: all six entrypoints (conformance, Claude, Codex, Copilot, Copilot OTel, Copilot managed-settings diagnostics), 842 passing and 107 existing skips.
- `git diff --check` and commit hygiene — passed.

[GitHub Code OSS run 37341675492](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37341675492) passed on commit `d4bb3c96cbc`, including Windows/Linux/macOS Electron smoke and integration jobs.

[Azure packaged validation 480756](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480756) passed packaged Electron smoke and integration tests on Windows, Linux, and macOS. Downloaded integration-task logs confirm all six Agent Host E2E entrypoints actually ran and passed on each platform. Publishing and release are disabled.

The overall Azure build initially failed because the Windows Unit Tests job exceeded its 50-minute job limit during post-test Component Governance. Retried only that canceled Windows job, which reused its successful test checkpoints and completed finalization. **Build 480756 is now succeeded** on `d4bb3c96cbc`, with no code, assertion, or job-timeout changes. Checkpoint reuse is not counted as another independent test execution.

All build/test CI checks are green; the draft/review-policy `VS Code PR Check` remains pending. This does not resolve the separately documented live approve-only concern below.

### Remaining live approve-only concern

Keep this PR in draft. Preview.5 still attempts implementation after selecting `exit_only` (“Approve Plan Only”) in the existing planning scenario: **3/3 local live recording checks failed** the unchanged no-pending-confirmation assertion. These were local real-model checks, not CI replay failures:

```bash
AGENT_HOST_REPLAY_RECORD=1 VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts \
  --grep 'planning-mode session-state writes are auto-approved in default mode'
```

Original fixture bytes were restored after every check; no failed recording was accepted. The previously investigated plan-exit notice/approval semantics are not fixed by this bump. Green deterministic replay uses recorded assistant responses and must not be treated as evidence that the live model respects approve-only.

Runtime provenance: [`cli-1.0.92-5`](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/commit/6d9037e403e4fac0cc65be349f6ab0d9c9351564).

pull_requests.title: Updated MCP
pull_requests.body:
## Description

Fixes an issue where MCP migration items in the **Agent Customizations → Migrations** dashboard could only be selected by clicking directly on the checkbox.

Previously, clicking elsewhere on a migration item row provided hover/focus feedback but did not select the item. The selection count remained at `0` and the **Migrate** button stayed disabled.

### Root Cause

The migration tree is configured with:

```ts
openOnSingleClick: true
```

As a result, every single click on a tree item triggered `onDidOpen`.

The `onDidOpen` handler unconditionally called `openMigrationItem()`, which opened the migration item's details instead of toggling its selection state.

The checkbox itself handled selection correctly because it stopped event propagation, which made selection work only when clicking directly on the checkbox.

### Fix

Updated the `tree.onDidOpen` handler in `customizationMigrationDashboard.ts` to distinguish between single-click selection and item activation.

For a normal single click:

- Toggle the migration item's selected state.
- Update the checkbox.
- Update the group selection count.
- Enable/disable the **Migrate** button accordingly.

For double-click, keyboard activation, or items requiring manual review:

- Preserve the existing behavior of opening the migration item details.

The distinction is made using `event.editorOptions` and `event.sideBySide`.

### Result

Migration items can now be selected by clicking anywhere on the row, making the selection behavior consistent with the expected tree interaction.

Double-clicking or using keyboard activation continues to open the item details, and items requiring manual review continue to open their details on single click.

## Testing

Tested the Agent Customizations → Migrations dashboard by:

1. Opening the migration dashboard with migration items available.
2. Clicking different areas of a migration item row.
3. Verifying that a single click toggles the checkbox.
4. Verifying that the selected item count updates correctly.
5. Verifying that the **Migrate** button reflects the selection state.
6. Verifying that clicking the checkbox directly still works.
7. Verifying that double-clicking opens the migration item details.
8. Verifying that keyboard activation continues to open the details.
9. Verifying that items with `manualReviewReason` continue to open their details as expected.

## Related Issue

Fixes  #339177

pull_requests.title: agentHost: forward tool-result images to BYOK models
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339595
Fixes #339439

## Problem

In agent-host sessions, a BYOK (OpenAI-compatible) model never received images returned by tools such as `view`. It only received the text receipt `Viewed image file successfully.`

## Root cause

There were two problems:

1. **Vision capability never reached the runtime.** `synthesizeByokSessionConfig` registered BYOK models with token limits only. The renderer already reports `supportsVision`, but it wasn't passed on, so the Copilot runtime treated every BYOK model as text-only. It replaced tool-result images with the text receipt before the request reached the BYOK proxy. I confirmed this by running the SDK runtime against a stub `/responses` server. Without the capability, `function_call_output.output` is the plain string. With `capabilities.supports.vision: true`, it's an `[input_text, input_image]` array.
2. **The BYOK LM bridge had no image channel for tool outputs.** Once vision is declared, the array output was passed through untyped, and the renderer wrapped it in a text part.

## Changes

- `copilotSessionLauncher.ts`: forward `supportsVision` as `capabilities.supports.vision` on each BYOK `ProviderModelConfig`.
- `agentHostByokLm.ts`: add an optional `images` field to the two tool-output bridge items. `output` stays text, so a renderer that doesn't know the new field still gets today's text result.
- `byokResponsesTranslation.ts`: split array tool outputs into text plus images, reusing the existing data-URL and MIME validation from user messages.
- `agentHostByokLmHandler.ts`: forward the images as `data` parts inside the LM API `tool_result`, the same shape the in-extension path produces.

## How to test

1. Turn on `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`.
2. Add an OpenAI-compatible BYOK model that supports images (e.g. `gpt-4o`), with `"vision": true` and `"toolCalling": true`.
3. Put an image containing text the model can't guess (e.g. `ZEBRA-7341`) in the workspace.
4. In an agent-host session with that model, ask: *"Use the view tool to open probe.png and tell me exactly what text it contains. If you didn't receive image pixels, say so."*
   - Before this change: the model says it only got "Viewed image file successfully."
   - After this change: the model reads the text.
5. With `"vision": false`, the model should still get the text receipt and the turn should finish cleanly.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokResponsesTranslation.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/byokLmProxyService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostByokLmHandler.test.ts`: passed, 145 tests.
- New tests use the exact payload captured from the runtime, plus a renderer `tool_result` mapping test. The launcher snapshot test now covers `supportsVision`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: reports 20 errors, the same 20 as without this change. They come from the locally installed `@github/copilot-sdk` (1.0.16) being older than the version pinned in `package.json`. None are in files this PR touches.
