pull_requests.title: explorer: coalesce parent refreshes during bulk moves
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #339610.

Moving 32 files between expanded Explorer folders repeatedly refreshed the same parents. This coalesces **multi-file MOVE view refreshes** using the existing working-copy lifecycle, without deferring model mutations. Completion joins asynchronous handlers and the final refreshes, including undo/redo and partial failure.

| Matched Windows fixture | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Expanded operation, median of 15 samples | 2,110.4 ms | **238.3 ms** |
| Exact painted tree, separate 5 samples | 3,100.9 ms | **333.1 ms** |
| Parent refreshes / tree passes through quiescence | 64 / 64 | **2 / 2** |

Three fresh windows pass the original one-second expectation. Additional checks verify exact disk/model/tree entries, painted completion, drag, undo/redo, cut/paste, expansion, and selection/focus. No timer, collapse, setting, or whole-tree refresh is added. Collapsed-parent timings are diagnostic controls, never fixed-experience results.

![Measured data comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/comparison.png)

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: original expanded-folder drag recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/before.gif) | ![After: original expanded-folder drag recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/after.gif) |

Four-second original UI excerpts, with startup removed and the completed frame held. This is asynchronous latency, not a renderer-blocking or memory claim.

<details>
<summary>Root cause, lifecycle boundaries, and compatibility</summary>

The [per-file MOVE handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/24a41178148f72f49e4ac0756ddb3b5347429a91/src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/explorerService.ts#L413) refreshed both parents for each file. Separate coverage confirms 64 parent refreshes and 64 logical tree passes for 32 moves. Repeated Explorer filtering/rendering is the verified cost; no independent claim is made about the generic intersecting-refresh queue.

The fix reuses [working-copy operation completion](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/24a41178148f72f49e4ac0756ddb3b5347429a91/src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/common/workingCopyFileService.ts#L413), which also wraps undo/redo. Correlation IDs isolate overlapping batches, URI identity matches actual move events, and refreshes are keyed by model item so overlapping workspace roots remain distinct. Recursive refresh requirements are merged, not downgraded.

The completion participant joins the asynchronous file-event handlers before flushing. Both success and failure flush completed mutations, every parent refresh is attempted, and pending state is released in `finally` or disposal. File-operation errors still propagate; event/view errors use the existing unexpected-error reporting channel.

Sixteen new tests cover immediate model changes, coalescing, asynchronous continuations, final-render completion, nested/concurrent and matching overlapping batches, late events, partial failure, actual bulk-edit cancellation boundaries, single-file responsiveness, case-insensitive URI identity, distinct same-URI model parents, folder descendants/rename/nesting, copy/delete/external changes, refresh failure, and disposal before/during flushing.

The actual UI run covers a 32-file drag, keyboard undo/redo and cut/paste. All current disk and model names and actual tree children are checked; rendered viewport entries are separately verified. Both parent folders stay expanded. Unmoved selection/focus is asserted; post-action selection/focus matches the baseline.

Scope: local Windows fixture, not a universal zero-regression claim. Copy/delete and external watcher paths are not batched. This does not close the external Python watcher report #165271 or make a cache/LRU, initial-expansion, or memory claim.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Measurements, controls, and exact executed validation</summary>

Baseline: `24a41178148f72f49e4ac0756ddb3b5347429a91`; fixed: `19ad8071e6989a74ab0697bf62c14ca9c0e9f2c8`. Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev / Electron 43.7.5, Windows x64. The fixture contains 1,024 ordinary local TS files totaling 23,552 bytes; each operation moves 32 between sibling folders.

Per revision: three fresh primary windows, one warmup plus five measured samples per expanded/collapsed arm. The stronger supplementary run uses one additional fresh window and one warmup plus five exact-painted samples. Profiled samples are excluded from timing medians. Counts extend through empty refresh queues, no pending file-event scheduler/backlog, and 600 ms of quiescence. Quiescent elapsed time includes the existing watcher delay and observation interval; it is not confused with visible completion.

[All controlled samples, controls, completion boundaries and counts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/metrics.json).

Commands below retain the executed arguments; `$repo`, `$proof`, and `$swarm` replace only machine-local checkout, evidence, and Bug Swarm installation prefixes. Every heavy command ran through `with-perf-lock.ps1 -Owner w4-explorer-fix -FilePath <executable> -ArgumentList <arguments>`. Owned windows closed before releasing the lease.

| Check | Executed command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh baseline/fixed output | `npm.cmd run transpile-client` | Passed on both revisions |
| New tests against baseline product output | `.\build\node_modules\.bin\esbuild.cmd src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerService.test.ts --outfile=out\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerService.test.js --format=esm --sourcemap=external --tsconfig=src\tsconfig.json` | Passed; only the test module was refreshed |
| Failing-before regressions | `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerService.test.ts --grep "updates every model entry\|joins asynchronous operation continuations"` | Expected: 2 failed; per-file refreshes and completion before rendering |
| Baseline timing | `node "$swarm\scripts\run-scenario.mjs" --scenario "$proof\before\bulk-move-scenario.cjs" --checkout "$repo" --isolation w4-explorer-fix --repeat 3` | Expected performance failure 3/3; all exact-name checks passed |
| Fixed timing | `node "$swarm\scripts\run-scenario.mjs" --scenario "$proof\after\bulk-move-scenario.cjs" --checkout "$repo" --isolation w4-explorer-fix --repeat 3` | Passed 3/3; expanded medians below 1,000 ms |
| Baseline stricter tree/display check | `node "$swarm\scripts\run-scenario.mjs" --scenario "$proof\before\supplementary.cjs" --checkout "$repo" --isolation w4-explorer-fix --repeat 1` | Functional checks passed; expected exact-painted threshold failure at 3,100.9 ms |
| Fixed stricter tree/display check | `node "$swarm\scripts\run-scenario.mjs" --scenario "$proof\after\supplementary.cjs" --checkout "$repo" --isolation w4-explorer-fix --repeat 1` | Passed; 333.1 ms exact-painted median; 2 parent refreshes through quiescence |
| Client type check | `npm.cmd run typecheck-client` | Passed |
| Related unit suites | `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerService.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerModel.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerView.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerFileNestingTrie.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\fileActions.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\bulkEdit\test\browser\bulkFileEdits.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\services\workingCopy\test\browser\workingCopyFileService.test.ts --run src\vs\base\test\browser\ui\tree\asyncDataTree.test.ts` | 174 passed; existing `is fast` nesting benchmark remains skipped |
| Targeted lint | `npx.cmd --no-install eslint src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\browser\explorerService.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerService.test.ts` | Passed |
| Repository formatter | `node build\lib\formatter.ts --verify src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\browser\explorerService.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerService.test.ts` | Passed |

The original scenario's input and one-second assertion are unchanged. A source-row readiness wait was added identically to both copies after a setup race, and both revisions were rerun. The supplementary drag's viewport setup was likewise repaired on both sides without weakening any state/timing assertion.

Not run: installed Insiders (pending update left untouched), macOS/Linux, remote providers, or a screen reader. CI and human review remain separate from these local results.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Portable reproduction and manual checks</summary>

Download the [primary scenario](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/bulk-move-scenario.cjs) and [supplementary scenario](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/supplementary.cjs) into the same folder. They create disposable synthetic workspaces and never use repository files as inputs.

From a built checkout, the standard scenario runner can reproduce the primary case:

```powershell
node test\scenario\out\runScenario.js --dev <downloaded-folder>\bulk-move-scenario.cjs
```

The primary scenario uses platform-neutral path handling; the supplementary keyboard gestures are Windows-specific. Only Windows was executed. To reproduce the isolated validation above, use Bug Swarm's `run-scenario.mjs` with `--checkout <checkout> --isolation <unique-name> --repeat 3`. Do not overlap performance runs.

Manual check: open a folder with 1,024 small files in `source` and an empty sibling `destination`. Keep the parents expanded, select 32 source files, and drag them to the destination. Check the resulting entries, undo, redo, then cut/paste them back. The final names and expansion should remain correct without seconds of repeated updates.

</details>

<sub>Found and fixed by Bug Swarm. Draft, assigned to karthiknadig, for human review.</sub>

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

## Summary

Cloud Sandbox archive operations currently update only the local session cache, so the owning Mission Control task remains unarchived and other clients continue listing it. This completes the cross-client work left open by [#337163](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337163), following the task ownership used for deletion in [#339042](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339042).

- Send archive/unarchive requests to the owning Mission Control task without connecting to or waking the sandbox. Serialize mutations and change local state only after success.
- Query both archived and non-archived tasks, retain archived sessions and their history, and reconcile task archive flags in both Agents and Editor windows, including connected environments.
- Preserve AHP behavior for additional sessions sharing the environment. Cancel stale account work and invalidate discovery responses started before a successful mutation.
- Add cross-client round-trip, offline restoration, request rejection, ordering, and shared remote-provider regression tests. Update the provider ownership documentation.

## Validation

## Manual Verification

Live Mission Control mutation testing and UI end-to-end verification were not run; no live cloud sessions were modified. Archive endpoint paths and the task-list archive filter were checked against the existing Copilot API client and Mission Control OpenAPI contract.

To verify with two updated clients signed into the same account: archive a Cloud Sandbox session in one client, refresh discovery in the other, and confirm it is excluded from the non-archived list but available through the archive filter. Unarchive it and refresh the first client to confirm it returns. Repeat with a disconnected sandbox and an already-connected sandbox.

pull_requests.title: sessions: Fix empty cloud sandbox resume views
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Fix two client paths that can leave a resumed Copilot Cloud sandbox showing an empty conversation even after its live connection succeeds:

- Session activation now joins an explicit wake already in progress, including one that starts during the environment lookup, rather than opening an offline-history stand-in while the sandbox is waking. Failed wakes still fall back to persisted history, and merely opening a dormant environment still does not wake it.
- Mission Control history replay honors the host-announced default chat and, when none was announced, uses an unambiguous sole recorded chat instead of seeding an empty `<session>/chat`. Recorded catalogues identifying another chat or a tool, side, or fork origin prevent that inference. Multiple conversations remain separate.

Add regression coverage for successful and failed pending wakes, a wake racing the environment lookup, opaque recorded chat URIs, explicit empty defaults, ambiguous histories, and peer-chat catalogue metadata.

This replay path is used for Mission Control offline cloud history, not ordinary live VS Code agent-host restoration. Shared protocol reducers and live host session restoration are unchanged.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed. The first run caught missing required display names in two new test connection options; those were fixed and compilation was rerun successfully.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/taskEventReplay.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 158 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/taskEventReplay.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/taskEventReplay.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionContribution.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Commit-time hygiene checks — passed.
- The initial resume/default-chat regression tests failed against the previous implementation; the peer-chat guard tests also failed before the guard was added.

## Manual verification

Not yet verified against a live cloud sandbox. Resume a dormant sandbox and open its conversation while the wake is in progress; once connected, the existing transcript should load rather than remain on an empty offline-history view. Opening a dormant sandbox without explicitly resuming it should still display read-only persisted history without waking it.

When recordings omit both the default pointer and distinguishing catalogue metadata, the sole-chat inference cannot prove that no unrecorded peer exists. Explicit defaults and available catalogue evidence remain authoritative.

Related: #337780 and #339574. No separate tracking issue was provided.

## Scope

Desktop, supported local Copilot SDK/Agent Host sessions only. Standard extension-backed Copilot Chat, web/remote canvas rendering, and native canvas hosting in auxiliary windows are not included. Unsupported cross-window moves/direct opens are rejected explicitly.

pull_requests.title: Fix diff editor showing unchanged regions as partially revealed
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339566

When `diffEditor.hideUnchangedRegions.enabled` is on, unchanged regions can show up partially or fully expanded when a diff is opened or when the setting is turned on. They only collapse once the setting is toggled off and on again, which resets all regions.

### Causes

1. **Region state changes while the feature is off.** Cursor changes call `ensure{Original,Modified}LineIsVisible` even while unchanged regions are not hidden, which reveals lines of the invisible regions. The same goes for the state transfer when the diff is recomputed. Once the setting is turned on, those regions show up expanded. The state is also persisted in the editor view state.
2. **Restored cursors reveal lines.** `TextDiffEditor.setInput` awaits the diff before `setModel` + `restoreViewState`. So the regions already exist when the cursor states are restored, and the restored cursors reveal lines. This is unnecessary because the view state already contains which lines are revealed (`modelState`).
3. **Stale serialized state.** `restoreSerializedState` applied a saved hidden range to the first region that intersects it, or even just touches it (`LineRange.intersect` returns an empty range). Diff view states are keyed by the original/modified URI pair, which is stable for SCM diffs. If the diff changed since, a saved range from another region gets applied and reveals arbitrary lines.
4. `UnchangedRegion.showOriginalLine` computed the reveal amount incorrectly (`bottom - top`, ignoring already-revealed lines), unlike `showModifiedLine`. Revealing a line in the original editor could leave it hidden or reveal far too much.

### Changes

- While unchanged regions are not hidden, nothing changes their state. This covers revealing lines, transferring revealed lines on diff updates, and restoring the serialized state. All regions are therefore collapsed once the setting is turned on, consistent with the existing reset when it is turned off.
- Cursor changes with source `restoreState` don't reveal lines.
- The serialized state also stores each region's range, and only regions that did not change are restored. States serialized by older versions are ignored.
- `showOriginalLine` now mirrors `showModifiedLine`.

### Tests

New tests in `diffEditorWidget.test.ts`, all of which fail without the fix:

- One per scenario, replaying the `TextDiffEditor.setInput` sequence (create view model → wait for diff → set model → restore view state).
- Moving the cursor into a hidden part of the original editor, with different line numbers on the two sides (`showOriginalLine`).

Verification:

- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium-msedge --runGlob "vs/editor/**/*.test.js"`: 5439 passing
- `npm run monaco-compile-check` passes; typecheck and eslint report no errors in the changed files
- Manually in `scripts/code-web` (steps from the issue): before, both regions stay fully expanded after enabling the setting. After, they are collapsed ("56 hidden lines" / "57 hidden lines").

Note: #336765 also changes `UnchangedRegion.showOriginalLine` (keeping the old formula), so whichever of the two PRs is merged second will have a small conflict there. I'm happy to resolve it on this side if this PR goes in second.

pull_requests.title: Fix original side of diff editor not wrapping after inline view
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #199341

While the diff editor renders inline, `DiffEditorEditors` forces `wordWrapOverride2: 'off'` on the hidden original editor. It renders inline when it is narrower than `renderSideBySideInlineBreakpoint` with `useInlineViewWhenSpaceIsLimited`, or before its first layout. Nothing undoes this when switching back to side-by-side, because only `wordWrapOverride1` is set again. `ToggleWordWrapController` re-applies its state only when `wrappingInfo` changes, and it doesn't change here because wrapping stays off.

Result: with `editor.wordWrap: "on"`, the original side stops wrapping after the diff editor was narrow once, e.g. after resizing the window or opening a side bar or chat. It stays that way until word wrap is toggled off and on again.

Related (#199341): toggling word wrap while the diff editor renders inline doesn't update the hidden original editor, so both sides disagree once it is side-by-side again.

### Changes

- `DiffEditorEditors` remembers the original editor's `wordWrapOverride2` when switching to the inline view and restores it when switching back.
- `ToggleWordWrapAction` also stores the toggled state for the hidden original editor of an inline diff editor.
- `ToggleWordWrapController` re-applies its state whenever its editor can be toggled again (the original editor of an inline diff editor being shown again), even if no word wrap option changed.

### Tests

- `diffEditorWidget.test.ts` (both fail without the `DiffEditorEditors` change):
  - the original editor wraps again after an inline round trip and after being created at zero width;
  - a custom `wordWrapOverride2` survives the round trip.
- New `toggleWordWrap.test.ts` uses the real controller and action: toggling word wrap on, and toggling it back, while the diff editor renders inline must apply to both sides once side-by-side. Both fail without either of the two `toggleWordWrap.ts` changes.
- All editor tests (5436) and `vs/workbench/contrib/codeEditor` tests pass; `npm run monaco-compile-check` passes; typecheck and eslint report no errors in the changed files.
- Manually in `scripts/code-web` with `editor.wordWrap: "on"`, window 1600 → 1000 → 1600 px wide:
  - before: the original side renders 14 rows for 14 lines (no wrapping);
  - after: both sides wrap.

## Purpose

Apply the resolved Copilot Agent Host sandbox network policy to integrated browser tools.

The integrated browser runs outside the Copilot runtime sandbox. Thus, VS Code must apply the session restrictions to browser requests.

## Changes

- Send resolved network restrictions only with integrated browser client tool calls.
- Pass these restrictions to Chromium and Playwright.
- Block network requests when the session does not permit outbound access.
- Apply the allowed and denied domain lists when outbound access is permitted. Denied domains take priority.
- An empty allowed domain list adds no sandbox domain restriction. It does not permit outbound access.
- Require restricted tools to use isolated agent pages for the same session.
- Check page ownership for page lists, browser actions, and screenshots.
- Keep the existing Playwright checks for blocked page URLs.

This change does not add sandbox network filtering to the fetch-page tool. Calls without valid session restriction data keep the existing behavior.

## Settings

Rename the domain settings:

| Old ID | New ID |
| --- | --- |
| `chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains` | `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains` |
| `chat.agent.deniedNetworkDomains` | `chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains` |

Both settings now appear under Sandbox Network. In a search for `sandbox`, they follow User-Configured Paths.

Move saved values to the new IDs. Include application settings. Do not replace a value that is already set with a new ID.

Keep the enterprise policy names unchanged. Update setting references, terminal messages, and the generated policy data.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: tell HydraFusion phase chats apart from subagents in telemetry
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #339326

HydraFusion phase chats open through a synthetic `subagent_started` signal, so telemetry counted each phase as a subagent turn with no model.

- Adds `subagentKind` (`task` | `fusionPhase`) to the events that can report a subagent chat: `agentHost.turnCompleted`, `turnFailed`, `turnHung`, `hungTurnCompleted`, `requestTokenUsage`, `toolInvoked`, `toolCallStalled`, `stalledToolCallCompleted`, `askQuestionsToolInvoked` and `todoStoreOperation`. It is set only when `isSubagentSession` is true and defaults to `task`.
- Phase chat turn and tool-call events now report the phase's model.
- A subagent launched inside a phase now reports the root turn as `parentTurnId` instead of the phase chat's turn.

`isSubagentSession` stays `true` for phase chats; filter on `subagentKind == 'task'` to exclude them.

Not changed: `agentHost.executionModeChanged`, `agentHost.userMessageSent`, `toolCallDetails` and `chat.toolApproval`. They are reported for the root session or for user-sent messages and never report a subagent chat, so there is nothing to classify.

The cancelled turns without `subagentTaskModelSource` mentioned in the issue are `search_code_subagent` children, tracked in #339564.

**Testing**

- Live HydraFusion run in a Code OSS dev build with `--log trace`: phase chat events in `agentHostTelemetry.log` carry `subagentKind: fusionPhase` and the phase model; a `task` subagent launched inside the phase reports the root turn as `parentTurnId`; root turns carry no `subagentKind`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/platform/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js"`: 10021 passing, 13 failing. The 13 are in `copilotAgent.test.ts` and fail the same way without this change.

auto_merge.commit_title: agentHost: tell HydraFusion phase chats apart from subagents in telemetry (#339560)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* agentHost: tell HydraFusion phase chats apart from subagents in telemetry

Each HydraFusion phase opens a child chat through a synthetic
subagent_started signal, so the host reported every phase as a subagent
turn with no model and no task model source. That inflated subagent
launch counts and lowered the share of subagents with a known model.

Add a bounded subagentKind property (task | fusionPhase) to the events
that decide isSubagentSession per chat, and report the phase's model on
the phase chat's turn and tool-call events.

Fixes #339326

pull_requests.title: Find terminal profiles at the login shell path when it's not on PATH
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #195768

On macOS and Linux, a terminal profile with a bare path (the default `fish`, `zsh`, `bash`, … entries) is only looked up on the PATH of the resolved shell environment. That environment comes from running `$SHELL` as a login shell, and when resolution fails or times out, the lookup falls back to the pty host's own PATH. For VS Code launched from the macOS Dock, that's launchd's `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`. So a Homebrew fish at `/opt/homebrew/bin/fish` that is the user's login shell can disappear from the profile list. An explicit `terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.osx: "fish"` then can't match it and silently falls back to `$SHELL`, which in a Dock-launched app can still be the old shell after `chsh`.

Approach described on the issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/195768#issuecomment-5974827626

### Change
`src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProfiles.ts`:
- `getValidatedProfile` (Unix only): when a profile's path is a bare name equal to the basename of the user's login shell, that login shell's absolute path is added as an extra candidate **after** the PATH lookup. It's validated like any absolute path (exists check), so nothing changes when the shell is on PATH, and other bare names (e.g. `tmux`) are unaffected.
- New `getLoginShells`: `$SHELL` from the resolved environment and from the process, plus `os.userInfo().shell`, which reads the user database and so is current even when the session's `$SHELL` predates `chsh`. Only absolute paths are kept, de-duplicated. It's passed down through `detectAvailableUnixProfiles` → `transformToTerminalProfiles` → `getValidatedProfile`. `detectAvailableProfiles` takes an optional `testLoginShells` for tests, like the existing `testPwshSourcePaths`.
- `validateProfilePaths` (all platforms): when a bare name isn't found on PATH, the recursive call now passes `env`, `overrideName` and `isAutoDetected` like the other two recursive calls do. Previously they were dropped, which would have stripped them from a profile resolved through the login-shell candidate. This also affects any profile with a path array whose bare first entry isn't on PATH (e.g. `["pwsh.exe", "C:\\tools\\pwsh.exe"]` on Windows): its `env` and `overrideName` are now kept instead of silently dropped. The built-in default profiles set neither.

A profile found this way shows its full path in the profile picker (`fish, /opt/homebrew/bin/fish -l`), like other absolute-path profiles. Unchanged: profile defaults, how the default follows `$SHELL` when `defaultProfile` is unset, and shell environment resolution.

### How to test
macOS with fish from Homebrew (`brew install fish`), Code - OSS launched the way the Dock does (no `VSCODE_CLI`, launchd PATH):
```sh
env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" TMPDIR="$TMPDIR" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin SHELL=/opt/homebrew/bin/fish \
  XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/xdg-nobrew NODE_ENV=development VSCODE_DEV=1 \
  "./.build/electron/Code - OSS.app/Contents/MacOS/Code - OSS" . --user-data-dir=/tmp/udd
```
with `/tmp/xdg-nobrew/fish/config.fish` containing `set -gx PATH /usr/bin /bin /usr/sbin /sbin`, so the resolved shell env has no `/opt/homebrew/bin`, and `"terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.osx": "fish"` in the profile's settings.

1. Open a terminal. Before: fish starts without `-l` (generated fallback profile), and **Terminal: Select Default Profile** has no `fish` entry. After: `fish -l` from the `fish` profile, and the picker lists `fish, /opt/homebrew/bin/fish -l`.
2. Same with `SHELL=/bin/zsh` in the command above while the account's login shell is fish (`chsh -s /opt/homebrew/bin/fish`), i.e. a stale `$SHELL`, and a zsh config whose PATH lacks `/opt/homebrew/bin`. Before: zsh, silently. After: `fish -l`.
3. Regression: launched normally (fish on PATH), the picker still shows `fish, fish -l` and fish starts as before.

Results from my runs (dev build, Dock-style launch, `defaultProfile.osx: "fish"`):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `$SHELL`=fish, shell env resolution times out | `fish` (no `-l`), fish missing from picker | `fish -l` |
| `$SHELL`=fish, resolved PATH without Homebrew | fish missing from picker | `fish -l`, fish in picker |
| login shell fish, stale `$SHELL`=zsh, resolution times out | zsh | `fish -l` |
| login shell fish, stale `$SHELL`=zsh, zsh PATH without Homebrew | zsh | `fish -l` |
| fish on PATH (normal) | `fish -l` | unchanged |

Automated: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/node/terminalProfiles.test.ts` › `should find a bare-name profile at the login shell path when it is not on PATH` (fails without this change; it also fails if only the `validateProfilePaths` change is reverted). All terminal unit tests pass locally. Linux uses the same code path, verified only through the unit test. On Windows the only change is the `validateProfilePaths` fix above. The login-shell candidate is Unix only.

pull_requests.title: tasks: Release custom callbacks when providers are disposed
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #339537

**Five cycles x 2 MiB synthetic callback payload:** after successful discovery and provider disposal, each of three fresh windows retained **10 MiB before and 0 bytes after** GC.

| Additional retention after five cycles | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Distinct task identities | 5 copies / 10 MiB | 0 copies / 0 B |
| No-discovery control | 0 B | 0 B |
| Same-ID discovery control | 0 B growth | 0 B growth |

All providers are unregistered; discovery is empty, with no active tasks or terminals. The memory probe never executes callbacks.

Scopes cached callbacks to their provider while preserving startup/active/direct executions and other owners. Late results cannot reinsert disposed callbacks. **Startup review addressed:** the same main-thread/API cases pass at the base, fail on the initial PR, and pass at `93080fb8`; final memory remains zero in three new windows. This does **not** fix the failed promises/pending RPCs addressed by #338231.

[Comparison card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/4265d04bc6fd3ed1b34f22f30883176d9d1fe9c1/task-callback-retention-339537/comparison.png) | [Raw metrics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/4265d04bc6fd3ed1b34f22f30883176d9d1fe9c1/task-callback-retention-339537/metrics.json)

**Before**

![Before: five additional callback payloads retain 10 MiB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/4265d04bc6fd3ed1b34f22f30883176d9d1fe9c1/task-callback-retention-339537/before.gif)

**After**

![After: all five cycles retain zero callback payloads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/4265d04bc6fd3ed1b34f22f30883176d9d1fe9c1/task-callback-retention-339537/after.gif)

Four-second **measured-data replays**, not real-time playback. Payload size is synthetic, not a typical task/frequency estimate. External memory and weakly observed native-backed bytes agree; `arrayBuffers` stayed zero and is not evidence. Installed Insiders comparison remains unverified; its pending update was left untouched.

<details>
<summary>Ownership and lifecycle compatibility</summary>

[Provider disposal](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0817aaa824590067854c361e77eb973a08b3cf48/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTask.ts#L452-L462) removed the handler but not [successfully cached callbacks](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0817aaa824590067854c361e77eb973a08b3cf48/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTask.ts#L672-L680). [Completion cleanup](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0817aaa824590067854c361e77eb973a08b3cf48/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTask.ts#L721-L745) only handled non-provider entries.

The existing native snapshot independently identifies `ExtHostTask -> _providedCustomExecutions2 -> CustomExecution -> callback closure -> Buffer -> ArrayBuffer -> native JSArrayBufferData`. It was captured on the preserved hunt baseline; these affected sources are unchanged at this PR's fresh `0817aaa8` base. The repeated fixed measurements use external memory and weak observations, not another large snapshot.

The ownership index keeps the latest callback per owner and restores another live owner on collisions. Registration disposal removes only that owner's references after the main thread replies. A typed internal startup notification is sent before resolving the definition; ordered IPC delivers it before the unregister reply, even when extension-host disposal happened first. Startup reservations survive provider cleanup, then transfer to the active lifetime until the matching end event. An end during resolution suppresses late delivery; an end during asynchronous callback creation closes the unused PTY. Direct execution still retains the last-started callback for rerun and prunes older direct entries. No public API, timeout, cache cap, or failed-provider/task-ID promise handling was added; unregister failures are explicitly logged.

| Behavior | Verification |
| --- | --- |
| Successful discovery and resolution release on disposal | Node and worker unit tests; real API memory probe |
| Repeated discovery, same IDs, re-registration | Node and worker unit tests; both memory controls |
| Other providers, colliding IDs, shared callback objects | Node and worker unit tests, both disposal orders |
| Late discovery, resolution, and task-ID replies after disposal | Node and worker unit tests; old replies cannot replace a new owner |
| Running callback survives disposal and releases at completion | Node and worker unit tests, including asynchronous callback creation |
| Main-thread start while provider disposal precedes variable resolution or IPC delivery | Three focused tests pass at `0817aaa8`, fail at `4ff52438` (no callback/PTY), pass at `93080fb8` |
| Real workbench Run Task disposal before the extension host observes start | New API test passes at base, times out at initial PR, passes at final head; exact output, fully resolved workspace folder and completion verified |
| End/cancellation or resolution failure during startup; callback rejects or returns late | Main-thread and node/worker tests; no late attachment/start or retained execution after end |
| Delayed unregister reply and newer same-ID registration | Node/worker tests preserve the newer owner |
| Newly provided callback remains usable with an already-running same-ID task | Node and worker compatibility tests; original lookup precedence preserved |
| Original extension-held `Task` executes after registration disposal | Real `vscode.tasks.executeTask` API test passed **before and after**, with exact terminal output and task end |
| Disposal during actual execution | Real API test passed **before and after**, including empty discovery, output, and completion |
| Fetched task already requested before disposal | Node and worker tests preserve its callback until start |
| Direct tasks and provider/direct identity collisions | Node and worker tests, including rerun retention and subsequent pruning |
| Existing task behavior | Existing real API tests for fetch/execute, terminal output flush, task groups, process events, and back-to-back tasks pass |

Unregistering a provider does not mutate a `Task` or its `CustomExecution` held by an extension. The node fetched-handle path still uses its existing main-thread re-resolution contract.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact validation commands and results</summary>

Working directory: `Q:\GIT\vscode.worktrees\perf-fixes-5be74984`. Final builds, tests, and measurements ran serially through `with-perf-lock.ps1`, owner `fix-tasks-startup` (original proof owner `fix-tasks`). No dependency installation was needed.

| Command | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run transpile-client` | Passed; refreshed all baseline client/extension-host output before measuring |
| `npm run gulp compile-client compile-extension:vscode-api-tests` | Passed on final source; zero compilation errors |
| `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\node\extHostTask.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\browser\mainThreadTask.test.ts` | **58 passes**: original 44 lifecycle tests, 13 added startup/protocol/lifetime tests, and runner self-test |
| `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\browser\mainThreadTask.test.ts --grep "main-thread startup (preserves callbacks\|survives disposal)"` | Same final assertions: **3 pass at base; 3 fail at initial PR; 3 pass at final head** |
| `scripts\test-integration.bat --suite api-folder --grep "main-thread startup"` | Same real API test: **1 pass at base; 1 fails by timeout at initial PR**; passes on final head within full suite |
| `scripts\test-integration.bat --suite api-folder --grep "vscode API - tasks"` | Final: **9 passing, 1 pre-existing skip**. Original eight API tests retained. Actual Mocha results inspected, not just launcher exit status |
| `npx --no-install eslint --max-warnings 0 src\vs\workbench\api\common\extHostTask.ts src\vs\workbench\api\browser\mainThreadTask.ts src\vs\workbench\api\common\extHost.protocol.ts src\vs\workbench\api\node\extHostTask.ts src\vs\workbench\api\test\node\extHostTask.test.ts src\vs\workbench\api\test\browser\mainThreadTask.test.ts extensions\vscode-api-tests\src\singlefolder-tests\workspace.tasks.test.ts` | Passed; zero warnings/errors |
| `git diff --check` and `git diff --cached --check` | Passed |

Startup comparisons temporarily transpiled the three task modules from pinned revisions into the isolated worktree output and restored them in `finally`; the test code/assertions were unchanged. No source/branch switch. The real API test invokes **Run Task**, not `tasks.executeTask`, and disposes the provider in `onDidOpenTerminal` before either the callback or `onDidStartTask`.

Exact canonical before command:

```powershell
node C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\skills\bug-swarm\scripts\run-scenario.mjs --scenario C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\session-state\5be74984-e914-4843-8a16-9065f861cc4a\files\perf-swarm-wave2-fixes\tasks\task-provider-retention.cjs --checkout Q:\GIT\vscode.worktrees\perf-fixes-5be74984 --isolation w2-fix-tasks --repeat 3 --gif C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\session-state\5be74984-e914-4843-8a16-9065f861cc4a\files\perf-swarm-wave2-fixes\tasks\before-full.gif
```

Result on `0817aaa8`: **failed 3/3 at the unchanged RELEASE assertion**, exactly 10,485,760 external bytes and five additional live payloads in each window. All setup, empty-discovery, active-state, and control checks passed.

Exact canonical after command:

```powershell
node C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\skills\bug-swarm\scripts\run-scenario.mjs --scenario C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\session-state\5be74984-e914-4843-8a16-9065f861cc4a\files\perf-swarm-wave2-fixes\tasks\task-provider-retention.cjs --checkout Q:\GIT\vscode.worktrees\perf-fixes-5be74984 --isolation w2-fix-tasks-startup --repeat 3 --gif C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\session-state\5be74984-e914-4843-8a16-9065f861cc4a\files\perf-swarm-wave2-fixes\tasks\startup-after-full.gif
```

Result on final `93080fb8` source: **passed 3/3 new windows**. All 45 after-samples have zero live payloads; additional external/native-backed bytes are zero. Both controls remain zero. The unchanged threshold is less than 1 MiB total growth. `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` was removed and `TERMINAL_HUNT_CAPTURE_HEAP=0` for UI runs.

The source/output hashes, unchanged input hashes, and all raw per-cycle counters are published with the proof. All three public images returned HTTP 200 with matching SHA-256 and correct PNG/GIF signatures and media types; both GIFs are 1200 x 660, four seconds, under 110 KB.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Portable automated repro</summary>

Download the [evidence folder](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/tree/4265d04bc6fd3ed1b34f22f30883176d9d1fe9c1/task-callback-retention-339537), preserving the `repro` layout. Its [README](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/4265d04bc6fd3ed1b34f22f30883176d9d1fe9c1/task-callback-retention-339537/README.md) documents the runner and signals.

The unchanged [scenario](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/4265d04bc6fd3ed1b34f22f30883176d9d1fe9c1/task-callback-retention-339537/repro/task-provider-retention.cjs) launches the [development extension](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/4265d04bc6fd3ed1b34f22f30883176d9d1fe9c1/task-callback-retention-339537/repro/extension/extension.cjs) in its disposable workspace. pull_requests.title: Show lazy variable evaluation errors in the Variables view
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334940

A failed Variables request for a lazy variable rejects before the view model emits its refresh event, leaving the displayed value unchanged. Handle the failure in the expression model and display the adapter's error message. Preserve the lazy hint and variable reference so evaluation can be retried.

Only the latest lazy evaluation may update the expression, so an older request cannot overwrite a newer success or failure.

Tests cover rendered error display, successful retry, automatic expansion retaining sibling variables, an empty response retaining the existing value, and out-of-order success/failure completions. The error-display and sibling-preservation regressions fail against the original implementation.

pull_requests.title: languageDetection: stop discarding ranked model results
pull_requests.body:
Several smaller fixes to language detection, plus the service's first unit tests. The main one is a ranking bug: when the model's top two guesses were close in confidence, the result was silently thrown away.

**Scope, to avoid confusion with #339544:** this PR does **not** fix detection failing outright. That's a separate problem, fixed in #339544: the neural model never runs in packaged builds. The two PRs are independent as code and either can merge first. But the ranking changes below operate on the neural model's output, so in packaged builds they have no visible effect until #339544 lands. Until then, the model produces nothing to rank.

## The ranking bug

`detectLanguagesImpl` collected candidate languages into a `possibleLanguages` array but yielded that array from only one of its three exit paths: the one taken when a confidence gap of at least `expectedRelativeConfidence` (0.2) opened up. The `else` branch's `return` and the natural end of the loop both dropped the array.

So a runaway winner worked. A C++ program the model rates 0.9999 is followed by a large gap, which takes the one path that yields. But when the top results were close, nothing was reported at all: a moderate leader with a close runner-up (`rs` 0.35, `go` 0.19), a gradual fall-off, or several plausible candidates with no gap between them. That made the documented 0.2 accept bar meaningless in practice.

The ranking is now a pure generator, `rankModelResults`, that yields each result as soon as it's accepted and stops at the first clear drop-off. `adjustLanguageConfidence` now returns a copy instead of mutating its argument, so a result can be evaluated more than once without the correction compounding.

Two more cases reported nothing even though a language cleared its bar. Both were caught in review and are fixed in a follow-up commit:

- **Corrections can reorder the model's ranking, but the code stopped at the raw leader.** With `rs` 0.19 and `js` 0.18, JavaScript is corrected to 0.23 and should win, but it was never considered. Candidates are now sorted by corrected confidence.
- **A candidate below its own bar ended the search.** With per-language bars, that's wrong: a strict `sql` 0.49 hid an ordinary `go` 0.48. Such a candidate is now skipped instead.

The drop-off is still measured between *consecutive* candidates, skipped ones included. So `ini` 0.48 followed by `rs` 0.21 reports nothing: the model clearly prefers ini, and a distant runner-up isn't more plausible just because ini missed its stricter bar.

## A strict-language bar that can actually be met

`bat`, `ini`, `makefile`, `sql`, `csv` and `toml` had 0.5 subtracted from their score. Against a 0.2 accept bar, that required 0.7 raw confidence, so in practice they were never detected. They now have an explicit threshold of 0.5. That's still a much higher bar than other languages get, but it can be reached. The intent of #131912 (these languages' simple or ambiguous syntax caused wrong guesses) is preserved.

## Smaller fixes

- **Auto Detect in the language picker now says when it fails** ("Unable to detect editor language") instead of looking as if it did nothing.
- **The regexp model's load failure is logged again.** The `console.warn` had been commented out, which made that failure completely silent.
- **The picker caps the first line** passed to `guessLanguageIdByFilepathOrFirstLine` at `ModelConstants.FIRST_LINE_DETECTION_LENGTH_LIMIT`. The other two call sites, in `textEditorModel.ts` and `textResourceEditor.ts`, already did, so pasting a very long single-line document no longer runs first-line matching against all of it.

## Testing

- **18 new unit tests** in `languageDetection/test/browser/languageDetectionWebWorker.test.ts` cover the ranking and the confidence corrections. They test runaway winners, close races, gradual fall-off, the strict-language bar, reordering by correction, skipping a strict candidate that misses its bar, and non-mutation. They pass in Chromium via `test/unit/browser`, and they're the first tests this service has had. Three of the four tests added in review fail without the follow-up fix; the fourth pins down the drop-off behaviour that both versions share.
- **Type-checked and lint-clean.** A scoped `tsc` run over the changed files and their ~780 transitive imports under `src/tsconfig.json`'s `strict` settings passes, and `eslint` passes.
- **Not covered by the unit tests:** the picker notification and the first-line cap.

Fixes #339536.

For **944,000 bytes / 16,000 paragraphs / 32,000 added source lines**, median production-handler time improves as follows:

| Fresh window | Before | After | No-marker control, before / after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 921.4 ms | 142.1 ms | 43.7 / 42.2 ms |
| 2 | 711.3 ms | 142.5 ms | 41.3 / 42.3 ms |
| 3 | 724.2 ms | 144.9 ms | 43.9 / 41.2 ms |

Reuse the source-line scan, avoid duplicate class writes, and clear old diff decorations before DOM reconciliation. Exact paragraph text and every added marker remain unchanged.

**Component probe:** real built-in preview, synthetic valid line-change metadata; **not full diff-opening latency**. One warmup plus five measured samples per size/mode. All 15 large after-samples are below 200 ms.

![Three-window comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/ab9c1a11fae1551d31a0f0898dea3582ea4da6a3/markdown-line-marking-339536/comparison.png)

**After** — same scale, same checks:

![After measurements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/ab9c1a11fae1551d31a0f0898dea3582ea4da6a3/markdown-line-marking-339536/after.gif)

16 targeted tests and six real preview/diff/navigation checks pass. Markdown compilation, preview type-checking, and lint pass. Installed Insiders comparison is unavailable because its shared installation has a pending update.

<details>
<summary>Root cause, compatibility, and scope</summary>

[markChangedLines](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4/extensions/markdown-language-features/preview-src/index.ts#L444) calls [getElementsForSourceLine](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4/extensions/markdown-language-features/preview-src/scroll-sync.ts#L87) once per changed line. Each lookup started at element zero: O(changed lines × mapped elements). The bulk caller was introduced by [7e3a9f816579](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7e3a9f816579567186b3b29c5d10f4fdeae894e1).

The document-version-scoped map now keeps a cursor for nondecreasing queries. Backward queries restart, so arbitrary query order retains legacy semantics; DOM entries themselves need not be sorted. First exact duplicate, surrounding-element selection, body sentinel, fractional/non-finite queries, and nested/code element identity are preserved. No sorting, copied input, per-line index, or additional retained document is introduced; the cache adds one small wrapper and two scalar fields.

The cursor-only candidate still measured 234–239 ms. A local diagnostic CPU profile of that candidate's real loaded bundle showed decoration-induced DOM reconciliation work. Clearing preview-only classes/gutters/indicators before reconciliation avoids comparing them as source changes; the existing post-reconciliation clearing remains to handle incoming predecorated HTML. Adjacent lines mapping to the same element only write its classes once. Parser, highlighting, scroll visibility scans, and diff generation are unchanged.

Seven focused mapping tests include an operation-count regression and 256 mapping/query-order comparisons. The six-step real-window smoke verifies:

- Exact ordinary text, nested lists, multiline paragraphs and fenced code, plus a hash of the actually loaded preview bundle.
- Added/deleted markers against the legacy oracle, unordered/duplicate changes, incoming predecorated HTML, empty documents, undefined/empty changes, and map refresh.
- Source-selection scrolling forward/backward and exact source navigation with double-click explicitly enabled.
- Real inline and side-by-side diffs: all source text and separately rendered tooltip text, markers, modification gutters, deletion indicators, and inner highlights.
- Bidirectional diff scrolling, a labeled keyboard-activated anchor, and Ctrl+Home.
- A real document edit restoring original content and clearing all diff classes, indicators, gutters, and highlights.

Scroll smoke gestures wait for 250 ms of scroll/resize quiescence to allow the existing 100/200 ms feedback-suppression timers to expire. This is settled-gesture coverage, not a rapid-scroll race or universal no-regression claim. The earlier unisolated full-diff timing and sub-threshold normal-scroll hypothesis are not part of this fix.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Exact validation commands and results</summary>

Commands ran in the exclusive fix worktree, based on `6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4`; final source commit is `47cf6ef3570078b80cee82628c999de0217cb47c`. No original checkout rebuild, dependency installation, or other finding's fix is included.

The legacy scan was extracted unchanged to make it directly testable. |

pull_requests.title: Fix neural language detection in packaged builds: load the model's webpack chunks as ES modules
pull_requests.body:
Neural language detection has never worked in a packaged build. It fails on every call, silently, before the model is ever read. This PR makes it work, and makes that class of failure visible in the log from now on.

## What goes wrong

`@vscode/vscode-languagedetection@1.0.23` lazily loads its TensorFlow CPU backend as a separate webpack chunk (`dist/lib/979.js`), and the bundle was built with only webpack's CommonJS chunk-loading strategy:

```js
r.u = e => e + ".js";
r.f.require = (e,t) => { a[e] || (chunk => {/* register */})(require("./" + r.u(e))) };
// ModelOperations.loadModel():
await r.e(979).then(r.bind(r, 4979));
if (!await setBackend("cpu")) { throw new Error("Unable to set backend to CPU."); }
```

We run the detector in an ESM module worker, which has neither `require` nor `importScripts`. So `runModel` throws `ReferenceError: require is not defined` before it looks at the model, and `detectLanguagesImpl` catches that with a bare `console.warn`. From the outside, a total failure is indistinguishable from "this document has no detectable language."

## Why the obvious fix doesn't work

Supplying a `require` that fetches the chunk and evaluates it fails too. The workbench runs under Trusted Types, which forbids the `Function` constructor. Unlike `script.src`, that can't be unblocked by a policy, because the constructor does not accept `TrustedScript`, so `'unsafe-eval'` in the CSP makes no difference. This is the verbatim result of trying it in a real build:

```
EvalError: Evaluating a string as JavaScript violates this document's Trusted Type assignment
requirements.
    at new Function (<anonymous>)
    at globalThis.require (…/out/vs/workbench/services/languageDetection/browser/languageDetectionWebWorkerMain.js)
    at r.f.require (…/node_modules.asar/@vscode/vscode-languagedetection/dist/lib/index.js:2:702535)
    at r.e (…/index.js:2:702049)
    at n.loadModel (…/index.js:2:705059)
```
```
This document requires 'TrustedScript' assignment. The action has been blocked.
The JavaScript Function constructor does not accept TrustedString arguments.
```

## The fix

**Commit 1** loads the chunks as real ES modules ahead of time, then gives webpack a synchronous `require` that only serves what is already loaded. No string is ever evaluated. None of the rules in `tsec.exemptions.json` apply, and no new exemption is needed.

- **Chunk ids** are read back out of the bundle (`/\.e\((?<chunkId>\d+)\)/g`) rather than hard-coded, because they change between versions of the package. A false positive is harmless, since that "chunk" just fails to import and is skipped.
- **The chunk is CommonJS** and assigns to a bare `exports`, so `module`/`exports` are defined on the global scope only for the duration of each `import()`.
- **Ordering matters.** The pre-load has to run *after* the bundle is imported. The bundle's UMD header prefers CommonJS over AMD when it sees a global `module`/`exports`, but by that point the bundle is already imported, and `import()` caches, so it is never re-executed.
- **`getModelOperations` now caches its promise rather than its result.** Because of that global-scope window, two overlapping detection requests could each install their own holder, leaving one to record an empty `exports`. Webpack would then register an empty object, and `runModel` would throw. Overlap is routine: every notebook cell status bar requests detection on its own, and the editor status path fires without awaiting.

**Commit 2** routes the neural detector's failures through a new `$logMessage` on `LanguageDetectionWorkerHost` to `ILogService`, so they land in the window log instead of the worker console. This silence is why the bug survived. The only way it was eventually diagnosed was by temporarily re-throwing these errors so they reached a notification.

**Load failures now latch, and each failure is logged once** (follow-up commits, from review). The `_loadFailed` latch only covered `getModelOperations`, but `ModelOperations` loads the model lazily inside its first `runModel` call, and `loadModel` is private. So load failures went unlatched, including a broken chunk preload, which is exactly this PR's area: they were retried and logged on every throttled edit. Now:

- A `runModel` failure before any successful run counts as a load failure and is latched. The latch logs the reason the one time it trips; previously it tripped silently, usually on paste, before the user ever chose **Auto Detect**.
- After a success, failures are input-specific. They are logged without latching, so detection recovers.
- Each distinct failure message is logged only once.

## Why this went unnoticed

Microsoft's builds mask the failure. The `vscode-regexp-languagedetection` fallback is added by the release pipeline and isn't in any `package.json` in this repo, so when the neural path fails, the regexp model answers instead. Builds without that fallback get no detection at all. VSCodium, for example, fails 100% of the time. A from-source build of this repo has no fallback either, because the regexp package is absent from `node_modules`.

The model itself was always fine. Running it directly in Node on two sample programs gives **`cpp` 0.9999** for a 4.5 KB C++ program and **`py` 1.0000** for a 5.5 KB Python one.

## Longer term

This is a consumer-side fix that works with the published package. The durable fix belongs in [microsoft/vscode-languagedetection](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languagedetection): build it with a chunk-loading strategy a module worker can use (`output.chunkLoading: 'import'`), or disable code splitting for the backend. Once that ships, `preloadModelChunks` can be deleted.

## Testing

I want to be precise about what has and hasn't been verified:

- **Verified in a real product build.** An equivalent of this change, applied to an installed VSCodium, fixes detection. Pasting the C++ and Python samples into untitled editors and choosing **Auto Detect** gives C++ and Python, where before it gave nothing.
- **Type-checked and lint-clean.** A scoped `tsc` run over the changed files and their ~510 transitive imports under `src/tsconfig.json`'s `strict` settings passes, and `eslint` passes on the service directory.
- **No unit tests.** Nothing in this change can be exercised without loading the real model in a worker. That includes the latch and the log deduplication.
- **Not yet done: an end-to-end run of this exact TypeScript from source.** The product-build verification used a hand-applied equivalent, which did not include the promise caching, the logging change, or the load-failure latch.

Possibly related: #216776 reports the same symptom (new files stay Plain Text) in stock VS Code 1.90.2. It was closed as `info-needed` without diagnostics, so I can't confirm it has this cause.

pull_requests.title: fix(editor): add undo stop between typed open char and auto-closed chars of multi-character pairs
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for using Markdown! -->

### Description

Fixes #338693

When a language defines an auto-closing pair with a multi-character open
sequence (e.g. `{ open: 'begin', close: 'end' }`), typing the last
character of the open sequence inserted both the character and the
auto-closed close characters in a single undo group — a single undo
removed both `n` and `end`.

This change executes the typed character and the auto-closed close
characters as two separate edit operations with an undo stop between
them:

- an undo now first removes only the auto-closed `end`,
- a further undo removes the typed `n`.

Single-character pairs (e.g. `(`) are intentionally not affected and
still undo as one unit, so the well-known `()` behavior is preserved.
Composition (IME) input is also unchanged, as the close characters are
inserted on composition end where the open text is already present.

### Implementation notes

- `EditOperationResult` gains an optional second command batch that
  `CursorsController._executeEditOperation` executes after pushing an
  undo stop.
- A new `AutoClosingCloseCharInsertCommand` inserts the close characters
  right after the typed open character, keeps the cursor between open
  and close, and reports the same auto-closed character ranges as the
  existing `TypeWithAutoClosingCommand`, so overtype/skip and
  highlighting behavior is unchanged.

### Testing

Added two tests to `cursor.test.ts`:

- Typing `begin` with `{ open: 'begin', close: 'end' }` produces
  `beginend`; the first undo removes only `end` (cursor at `begin|`),
  the second undo removes `n` (cursor at `begi|`).
- Typing `(` still produces `()`, and a single undo removes both.

- The first test fails without the fix and passes with it; the second
  documents the preserved single-character behavior.
- The full `cursor.test.ts` suite (259 tests) and
  `cursorMoveCommand.test.ts` still pass.

pull_requests.title: fix(editor): place cursor between open and close when auto-closing pairs span lines
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for using Markdown! -->

### Description

Fixes #338692

Auto-closing pairs whose close starts with a line break (e.g.
`{ open: 'begin', close: '\nend' }`) placed the cursor on the line of
the close instead of between the open and the close: typing `begin`
inserted the newline and `end`, but the cursor ended up on the second
line before `end`.

**Cursor position** — the cursor position and the auto-closed character
ranges were derived from plain column arithmetic on the end of the
inserted range, which does not account for line breaks. This change
derives the cursor position from the start of the inserted text and
walks character offsets (counting line breaks as a single character)
when computing the auto-closed character ranges.

**onEnter rules** — as requested in the issue, the enter action is now
applied to the line introduced by the close character: the language's
`onEnterRules` are evaluated for the position behind the open character
(including the still-pending open character in the before text) and the
resulting indentation/append text is prepended to the rest of the close
character. Without a matching rule the current line indentation is
kept; `autoIndent: none` leaves the close untouched, `keep` preserves
the current indentation, and `IndentOutdent` falls back to the raw
close since its extra inserted line does not apply to auto-closed
characters.

**Line break counting** — line breaks in the close character are
counted as a single character (CRLF included) when walking the
auto-closed character ranges, matching how the model stores inserted
line breaks.

### Testing

Added three tests to `cursor.test.ts`:

- Typing `begin` with `{ open: 'begin', close: '\nend' }` produces
  `begin` / `end` on two lines with the cursor at the end of the first
  line (behind the open), not on the line of the close.
- With an `onEnterRules` entry matching the open (indent action), the
  close line is indented accordingly (`    end` with `tabSize: 4`,
  `insertSpaces`).
- All existing single-line auto-closing behavior is unchanged.

- The first two tests fail without the respective parts of the fix and
  pass with it.
- The full `cursor.test.ts` suite (259 tests) still passes.
- The touched files type-check cleanly under the repository's strict
  TypeScript settings.

pull_requests.title: fix(editor): complete auto-closing pairs whose open ends with a tab when typing Tab
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for using Markdown! -->

### Description

Fixes #338697

When a language defines an auto-closing pair whose open sequence ends
with a tab (e.g. `{ open: 'begin\t', close: 'end' }`), pressing Tab did
not complete the pair: the tab key was handled by the tab/indent
command, which never goes through the auto closing type operation, so
the close counterpart was not inserted.

This change runs the tab key through the auto closing pair lookup when
the tab key would insert a literal tab character (`insertSpaces`
disabled). The lookup runs before the whitespace-only indentation fast
path, so pairs whose open is a single tab (e.g. `{ open: '\t', close:
'end' }`) also complete on empty or whitespace-only lines. If the pair
matches, it is closed and the cursor is placed between the open and the
close, just like for any other auto-closing character.

### Testing

Added three tests to `cursor.test.ts`:

- Typing `begin` and then Tab with `{ open: 'begin\t', close: 'end' }`
  produces `begin\tend` with the cursor between the open and the close.
- Tab on an empty line with `{ open: '\t', close: 'end' }` completes the
  pair (`\tend`, cursor between open and close).
- With `insertSpaces` enabled, Tab inserts spaces to the next tab stop
  and does **not** complete the pair (no behavior change).

- The first two tests fail without the fix and pass with it.
- The full `cursor.test.ts` suite (260 tests) still passes, and the
  touched files type-check cleanly.

pull_requests.title: fix(debug): only remove stop details up to the continued event
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for using Markdown! -->

### Description

Fixes #339076

When the debugger continued a thread, the `onDidContinued` handler
removed **all** recorded stopped details for that thread. If a new stop
event arrived between the `continued` event and the (asynchronous)
cleanup, that newer stop was removed as well, making e.g. the call stack
pause header disappear.

This change tracks a monotonically increasing sequence number for each
recorded stop. When a `continued` event is received, the sequence number
at that moment is captured synchronously, and the asynchronous cleanup
only removes stops with a sequence number up to that value — newer stops
are preserved.

An `invalidated` event reprocesses existing stop details through
`handleStop`; the replayed stops now keep their original sequences so a
pending continued cleanup still recognizes (and removes) them instead of
mistaking the replayed stale stop for a newer one.

### Testing

Added tests to `debugSession.test.ts` (suite "DebugSession - stopped
details") using a fake raw debug session:

- A stop recorded after a `continued` event survives the cleanup, while
  stops recorded before it are removed.
- A stop replayed by an `invalidated` event while the continued cleanup
  is pending is still removed (regression test for the re-sequencing
  edge; fails against the previous behavior).
- Stops on other threads are not affected by the cleanup.

- The key tests fail without the fix and pass with it.
- The existing `debugSession.test.ts` suite (24 tests) still passes, and
  the touched files type-check cleanly.

pull_requests.title: fix: mark task terminals with TaskTerminalType so the shell executeCommand guard applies
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for using Markdown! -->

### Description

Fixes #338610

Terminals created for `CustomExecution` tasks were created without a
`type`, which made
`mainThreadTerminalShellIntegration.instanceSupportsExecuteCommandApi`
treat them as regular interactive terminals. As a result, extension
authors could call `Terminal.shell.executeCommand` on task terminals,
bypassing the guard that restricts the API to proper terminal types.

This change passes `TaskTerminalType` when the terminal service creates
the terminal for a `CustomExecution` task, so task terminals are
identified consistently and the `executeCommand` guard applies to them.

### Testing

Added `terminalTaskSystem.test.ts` which constructs a
`TerminalTaskSystem` with a mocked `ITerminalService` and verifies that
the terminal created for a `CustomExecution` task is configured with
`type: TaskTerminalType`.

- The new test fails without the fix (`type` is `undefined`) and passes
  with it.
- The test and the touched files type-check cleanly under the
  repository's strict TypeScript settings (the mocks use the real
  `ICreateTerminalOptions`/`Event<ITaskEvent>`/`Promise<void>`
  signatures).

Fixes #339535.

Disposes marker view state **before** clearing the resource index used to find it, then invalidates the sorted-resource cache. This stops obsolete diagnostic copies accumulating across hidden updates and prevents hidden views from returning stale resources.

| Measured result | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Current diagnostics | 2,000 | 2,000 |
| Obsolete view models after seven cycles | 13,976 | **0** |
| Post-GC growth, MiB/cycle | 19.66-19.77 | **0.13-0.14** |
| Visible-update control, MiB/cycle | 0.043-0.044 | 0.033-0.046 |
| States after explicit clear | 0 | 0 |

![Measured Problems retention comparison: unchanged diagnostic count, zero obsolete models after the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8e11412294982e1ec8e2f64ea08764ee729ee465/problems-retention-339535/comparison.png)

Same 2,000-diagnostic fixture on 500 URIs; three fresh Windows Dev windows per side. Heap figures are ranges of warmed per-window medians. The unchanged repro passes **3/3**; **53 focused tests**, compilation, formatting, and lint pass. Live tree/table hidden-state cleanup, text, filtering, keyboard navigation, and accessible labels are verified.

Synthetic provider, not language-server latency. Installed Insiders was not launched because its shared installation has a pending update.

<details>
<summary>Before and after: short recorded-data replays</summary>

These 4.51-second cycle plots replay exact recorded samples from window 1 of 3, **not elapsed-action playback**. Both use identical scales and subtract the first warmup cycle from each plotted heap sample. The complete raw measurements, including warmup and controls, are published.

### Before

![Before: 13,976 obsolete models accumulate; recorded-data replay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8e11412294982e1ec8e2f64ea08764ee729ee465/problems-retention-339535/before.gif)

### After

![After: exactly 2,000 current models and zero obsolete models; recorded-data replay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8e11412294982e1ec8e2f64ea08764ee729ee465/problems-retention-339535/after.gif)

[Raw samples, metrics, reproducible proof renderer, and provenance](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/tree/8e11412294982e1ec8e2f64ea08764ee729ee465/problems-retention-339535).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Root cause, portable reproduction, and exact validation results</summary>

### Root cause and scope

[Visibility cleanup](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4/src/vs/workbench/contrib/markers/browser/markersView.ts#L558-L570) unsubscribes model notifications, resets the resource model, then enumerates that model to remove view state. If a single-resource update invalidated the sorted cache, that enumeration is empty. Reopening adds new marker identities to the still-populated state maps.

The fix keeps removal and reset in one ordered teardown callback. Reset invalidates the sorted-resource cache before notifying listeners, so `getAllResourceMarkers()` is empty while hidden. It preserves view mode, multiline settings, filtering, ordinary resource updates, and final disposal. Tests cover populated and invalidated caches in both tree and table modes, repeated hidden updates, displayed diagnostic text, replacement/removal, and disposal.

This order dates to `7723f2548c26655be9f282ba7a317c9192073c05`; it is not claimed as a recent regression. The affected files are identical between the preserved hunter build `dcb81648f8a8f1863d2577f8fec98e805e5f95a0` and the fresh baseline `6fad7188e7dbf7db564e5e4a85960eb2bf69bdf4`. The table above uses the fresh baseline, not the slightly different earlier hunter heap readings.

### Portable scenario

[Download the unchanged standalone scenario](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8e11412294982e1ec8e2f64ea08764ee729ee465/problems-retention-339535/problems-retention.scenario.cjs) and follow the [source-checkout reproduction instructions](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/8e11412294982e1ec8e2f64ea08764ee729ee465/problems-retention-339535/README.md#portable-reproduction). No private paths or external fixtures are needed. It creates its workspace, uses Node built-ins, resolves modules from the actual dev workbench, and writes raw JSON measurements.

The measured input is 2,000 diagnostics, 500 logical URIs, four markers per URI, 77-character messages, and 1,478,001 serialized bytes. Only messages change while hidden; resource/range/count shape is fixed. The scenario's SHA-256 is `0c4d6b74100faa4fd538b61d32733cbd558d655008e6c4fe2295d29c9d9d6f2f`. Published bytes match both measured runs exactly.

The source field in this preserved scenario contains a historical investigation link; #339535 is the issue this PR resolves. Plain hide/show alone is not claimed to leak.

### Executed validation

Commands below ran from `Q:\GIT\vscode.worktrees\perf-fixes-5be74984`, under the shared measurement lease with owners `fix-problems` and `fix-problems-cache-*`. These variables identify the exact machine-local paths used; the portable download above does not depend on them:

| Regression tests on unfixed baseline | `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\markers\test\browser\markersView.test.ts --grep MarkersView` | 4 expected retention failures; 4 controls passed |

Related: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9678

- Route public Dev Container sample reads through the owning host's leased `IGitHubAnonymousClient.getFile(...)`: resolve repository `HEAD` with one REST API request, then download raw content pinned to that commit. Downloads omit credentials and API-identification headers, enforce the existing 1 MiB byte limit and pinned-origin redirect boundary, and track raw-host throttling separately from the REST API quota. Both operations use the local governed engine, caller-selected attribution/priority and a shared deadline. `GitHubCancellation` (`AbortSignal | CancellationToken`) is normalized inside the client. Custom API hosts must configure their raw base explicitly; JSON API reads remain confined to `apiBaseUri`.

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

Adds regression coverage for restored messages moving below newer local messages during passive history refreshes and for response-subscription retention during historical replacements. No separate tracking issue was filed; this originated from investigation of a reported Cloud sandbox transcript.

### Upstream integration

[#339458](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339458) landed on `main` while this PR was in progress. The merge retains its per-turn replacement, indexed insertion, and keyed response-listener cleanup instead of maintaining a second production implementation. The remaining diff against `main` is test-only.

The specific Cloud trigger is session-level context usage moving from a restored response to a newly completed response. The underlying ordering bug is shared passive-history reconciliation, not transport reordering.

### Coverage

- Context-usage migration from a cancelled restored turn to a newly completed turn, including model, displayed, and serialized order.
- Historical prompt replacement with local IDs present or absent in replayed history.
- Omitted local IDs: refresh an older response after an external turn has already been appended, or refresh it together with a new unanchored external turn. Preserve local model/view identities, unchanged external requests, draft state, and append behavior.
- Historical insertion around hidden requests and interleaved local/external turns, repeated refreshes, and removal.
- Response subscriptions remain bounded across 25 same-ID historical replacements, are released on removal and tail promotion, and are cleaned up on teardown while retaining session-cost updates.
- Indexed insertion validation and operation-log roundtrips.

### Validation

Both omitted-local-ID regressions failed against the previous compiled PR implementation with `[historical, external, local]` instead of `[historical, local, external]`. The response-subscription regression also failed: 25 replacements left 26 subscription disposables retained. All three pass with the upstream implementation.

- `npm run transpile-client` - passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatService/chatService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/model/chatModel.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/model/chatViewModel.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/model/chatSessionOperationLog.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widgetHosts/viewPane/chatContextUsageWidget.test.ts` - passed, 630 tests.
