pull_requests.title: Start restored terminals at their current size
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #174486

## Summary

After VS Code restarts, a persistent terminal's shell is respawned at the size the terminal had when the previous session was saved. The terminal's current size only reaches the shell as a SIGWINCH after startup, so anything that reads the size while the shell starts (`$COLUMNS`, `stty size`, prompts that draw full-width lines, the `typeset -p COLUMNS` in the original report) can see the old size. This PR sends the current size to a restored process before it starts.

## Root cause

A restored terminal's process is recreated in the pty host using the size from its saved replay event ([`ptyService.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7622a529314a4abcefd7ca9e3d7344bc9ccba9e/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L294-L295)). It isn't spawned until the window attaches to it and calls `start()`. Two things kept it at the old size:

1. `TerminalProcessManager.createProcess` receives the terminal's current `cols`/`rows`, but on the attach path it goes straight to `start()` without sending them ([`terminalProcessManager.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7622a529314a4abcefd7ca9e3d7344bc9ccba9e/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts#L340-L419)). The first resize is sent only after the process reports ready.
2. Even a resize sent earlier would have been dropped: `TerminalProcess.resize` ignores calls until the pty is spawned ([`terminalProcess.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7622a529314a4abcefd7ca9e3d7344bc9ccba9e/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProcess.ts#L546)).

## Change

- **`TerminalProcessManager.createProcess`:** when attaching to a local persistent process, call `resize(cols, rows)` before `start()`. Remote terminals are excluded: `RemotePty` holds resizes until `start()` has resolved, so the early resize would arrive after the shell had spawned.
- **`TerminalProcess.resize`:** if the pty hasn't been spawned yet, record the size in the spawn options so `start()` spawns at it. The ≥1 clamp now applies to both branches.
- **`PersistentTerminalProcess`:** the same attach path is used to reattach to a process that's already running (window reload, moving a terminal to another window). That early resize is ignored between `attach()` and `start()` when the process is running, so it keeps its size until its replay is done, as before. Only the pty host knows whether the process has been spawned.
- **`BasePty.handleReplay`:** the early resize has no pixel size, and `LocalPty` dedupes on cols/rows, so the terminal's next resize, which carries the pixel size added in #295820, was dropped. `BasePty` now forgets the last size once a replay is done. This also ensures that a running process, which ignored the early resize, is resized after its replay. Every attach ends in a replay, so the next resize always reaches the pty, as it did with a fresh pty before.
- **Tests:**
  - `terminalProcessManager.test.ts`: an attached local process is resized before it starts; a newly launched process and an attached remote process aren't.
  - `localPty.test.ts`: the size is sent again after a replay.

The `TerminalProcess` and `PersistentTerminalProcess` changes have no unit tests, because they would need a real pty (node-pty). I verified them in the dev build (below).

I described the approach on the issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/174486#issuecomment-5973287909

## How to test

1. Use a shell whose rc file prints its size at startup and on resize, e.g. a profile running `bash --rcfile <file> -i` with:
   ```sh
   echo "STARTUP $(stty size)"
   trap 'echo "WINCH $(stty size)"' WINCH
   ```
2. Open a terminal with that profile in the panel, and another in the editor area.
3. Quit VS Code (Cmd+Q / File > Exit) so the terminals are restored on the next start, which is the default `terminal.integrated.persistentSessionReviveProcess: onExit`.
4. Change something that changes the terminal's size, e.g. `terminal.integrated.fontSize` from 12 to 16.
5. Start VS Code again.
   - **Expected:** the restored shells print `STARTUP` with their current size.
   - **Before this PR:** they printed the previous session's size, followed by a `WINCH`. On `main` it's a race, so it doesn't happen every time.
6. Reload the window (`Developer: Reload Window`) with the shell still running. It should behave as before, with no extra resize before the history is replayed.

Automated:

```
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalProcessManager.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/electron-browser/localPty.test.ts
```

`attach › resizes an attached process to the terminal size before starting it`, `attach › does not resize an attached remote process before starting it` and `LocalPty resize › sends the size again after a replay` fail without the corresponding change.

## Validation

Tested in a dev build on macOS with the probe shell above: a full quit, font size 12 → 16, then a relaunch on the same profile. The pixel size was read with `TIOCGWINSZ`.

| scenario | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| restored terminal in the panel | `STARTUP 16x108` → `WINCH 12x79` (racy) | `STARTUP 12x79` (sometimes 12x78 → 12x79) |
| restored terminal in the editor area | `STARTUP 57x108` | `STARTUP 42x79` |
| restored terminal in a hidden panel | 80x30 a few ms after start, correct once shown | 80x30 from the start, correct once shown |
| window reload with a running shell | two `WINCH 12x79` after replay (the pixel size briefly drops to 0) | no `WINCH`; size and pixel size kept |
| pixel size after restore | `751x228 px` | `751x228 px` |
| layout unchanged between sessions | usually exact | usually exact; sometimes a few columns narrow for 25–110 ms (see below) |

The restored history renders correctly in all cases. All 2435 terminal unit tests pass (`--grep "Terminal|PtyHost|XtermSerializer|LocalPty"`), and so do hygiene, eslint, the layers check and typecheck.

Limitations and things worth knowing:
- **Remote isn't fixed, and behaves as before.** `RemotePty` holds resizes until `start()` has resolved (`_startBarrier`), so a restored remote shell still starts at the saved size. Changing that barrier is a separate question, so I left it out; it could be a follow-up.
- **Windows (conpty) isn't tested.** A restored conpty process is now spawned at the current size rather than the saved one. The viewport-clearing padding added after the restored history ([`postRestoreMessage`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/d7622a529314a4abcefd7ca9e3d7344bc9ccba9e/src/vs/platform/terminal/node/ptyService.ts#L271-L279)) is still computed from the saved row count. When the terminal has more rows than last session, the replayed viewport could pull in some scrollback and the cursor might not end up at the top-left before conpty's inherit-cursor query. Shrinking looks benign.
- **When the layout didn't change between sessions,** the shell now starts at the terminal's first size estimate, the same one a new terminal is created with. It can be a few columns smaller than the final layout until the layout settles. The saved size on `main` can be off in the same way when the previous session saved before its layout settled.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: native Mission Control environments
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Expose VS Code's existing native Agent Host utility process as an opt-in user-local Mission Control environment over Azure Web PubSub. Local sessions continue using local IPC; remote clients use the same native session state and protocol handler. No separate daemon is launched.

**Native GitHub stack 339625:** `main` → [#339492](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339492) → this PR. Merge the URI prerequisite first. GitHub stack metadata is registered, not merely represented by the base branch.

- Register, heartbeat, withdraw and recover the environment using trusted local credentials, canonical-owner checks and a stable random profile-local compute identity.
- Enforce signed control, sealed identity/MCP authentication, lane/client-ID binding, passive access, relay workspace/resource grants, and host-management/root-configuration restrictions.
- Discover/connect to existing user-local environments with cached-first inventory and background refresh; retain the existing managed-sandbox flow.
- Mirror authoritative AHP actions and selected genuine SDK metadata with bounded spools, durable acknowledgements and signed retained backfill. Native titles and activity update MC's task catalog.
- Support the opt-in path in built desktop products as well as source builds, retaining the existing default-off experimental setting keys.
- Use product display names, ordinary Mission Control class/management names, and a scoped DI-backed native adapter. Node implementation lives under `node/missionControl/`.
- Consume negotiated standard session URIs from the prerequisite without global provider aliases or historical URI/storage rewriting.

No separate VS Code issue is linked; this is the user-local environment integration. Environment-management UX alongside SSH/dev tunnels is a separate follow-up.

## Security scope and remaining qualification

Remote owner access includes sessions, tools and granted workspace resources. MC stores mirrored conversation content; credential sealing is not conversation E2EE.

Mandatory handshake binding, per-client/session credential sponsorship, OS containment, response-part ID continuity and full durable AHP restart/history baselines remain accepted deferrals. Unbound sealed tokens remain replayable, active credentials use the existing shared native provider store, and path grants do not claim OS confinement.

The code-linked security matrix is `src/vs/platform/agentHost/MISSION_CONTROL_SECURITY_REQUIREMENTS.md`. Only outstanding work is listed in `MISSION_CONTROL_PRODUCTION_GAPS.md`; operation/configuration is described in `MISSION_CONTROL.md`.

Signed-package opt-in/crypto loading, managed-sandbox live compatibility, enterprise network qualification and longer real-service renewal/soak verification are not claimed complete. No review requirement or release/privacy approval is overridden by this PR.

## How to exercise

1. Sign in to GitHub in a desktop window and leave `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControlFakeEndpoint` empty.
2. Enable `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControl.enabled`, using the default trusted HTTPS endpoint.
3. Wait for `Mission Control ready; environmentId=...` in the Agent Host log.
4. Create/use a native session normally over local IPC.
5. From a separate matching-owner client, discover the environment, authenticate through the relay and list/open/drive that same session. In another VS Code instance, use **Connect to Mission Control Environment...**.
6. Verify task title/activity, disconnect/reconnect, and owner withdrawal. Offline user-local attachment does not provision replacement compute.

The local test-endpoint setting is only for a trusted loopback HTTP integration-test server; the local GitHub credential is sent there if explicitly configured.

## Validation

Current product-cleanup head: `7c6725d9cf1`. Local validation:

- `npm run transpile-client` — **passed**.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — **passed**.
- `npm run test-node -- --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/{missionControl*,protocolServerHandler,agentHostAuthenticationService}.test.js'` — **303 passed**.
- `env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/missionControlEnvironmentActions.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHost.contribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/accessibility/chatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts` — **166 passed**, including built-environment discovery/connection and AI-disabled gating.
- `node --test build/lib/test/agentHostDependencies.test.ts` — **2 passed**, including runtime package traversal through moved modules.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — **passed**.
- `node_modules/.bin/eslint src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/*.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/{agentHostMain,agentHostManagementService}.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/electron-browser/localAgentHostService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/{missionControl*,protocolServerHandler}.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/{remoteAgentHost.contribution,cloudSandboxAgentHostService,missionControlEnvironmentActions}.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/missionControlAgentHostContribution.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHost.contribution.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/{missionControlEnvironmentActions,cloudSandboxAgentHostService}.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatAccessibilityHelp.ts` — **passed**.
- `git diff --cached --check` and normal commit hooks — **passed**.
- Documentation file/line/heading links — **passed**.

The parent stack integration at `5092cc38c51` passed **2,510 Node and 1,578 Electron/browser tests**. [Code OSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37240718187) passed all 21 jobs on that head, with CodeQL, Component Fixtures, chat-lib, Telemetry, Monaco, dependency and license checks also green. Those CI results are not represented as results for the newer cleanup head; replacement CI is pending.

Real two-instance evidence establishes isolated native hosts, absence of fresh sessions from the viewer's ambient host, actual Azure WPS routing, remote turns, stable naming/configuration separation, and recovery after deliberate socket interruption. The bounded connection ran 14 minutes 37 seconds before interruption and recovered in about 3.4 seconds with the same client ID. It does not establish full token-expiry soak or diagnose the Copilot app's reported disconnections.

(Written by Copilot)

pull_requests.title: agentHost: one Codex thread restart at a time, none under a claimed turn
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339511

Before a Codex session's first turn, several paths can restart its thread at once — the pre-turn restart in `_sendMessage`, `_ensureCurrentLaunchBeforeTurn`, customization reconciliation, `_changeAgent` and the MCP auth reconnect. Overlapping restarts each started a thread; the turn ran on one while another was persisted as the session's thread, so the conversation was lost on resume. A send could also read the thread while it was cleared ("no backing thread"), or have it replaced after the turn was claimed.

**Changes** (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/codexAgent.ts`)

- `ICodexSession.threadRestart`: the latest thread restart requested for the session and not yet settled.
- `_restartThreadWithCurrentTools` chains a session's restarts through `threadRestart`: each request records itself immediately and waits for the one before it. If a turn has by then been claimed (`currentTurnId`) or sent (`firstTurnSent`), it marks the session for reload instead of replacing the thread; otherwise it runs the existing restart, renamed `_restartThreadNow`. A successful restart persists its replacement thread itself (`_persistMaterializedSession`), so every caller is covered — including `_reconnectSessionsForMcpAuth`, which never persisted it — and the callers' own persistence right after the restart is removed.
- New `_ensureSettledThreadConnection`: waits until no restart is pending, then returns the thread's connection, looping if a restart was requested meanwhile. `_sendMessage` uses it after the resume step and right before both turn claims (`thread/compact/start` and `turn/start`), with no `await` between it and the claim.

Each restart is recorded at request time, not when it starts running, for two reasons: a restart queued behind another stays visible to a waiting send, so the send cannot claim its turn between the two; and a restart requested between the send's last check and its claim checks `currentTurnId` only after an `await`, so it sees the claim and reloads instead.

**Tests** (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexPrewarmEviction.test.ts`)

A `createThreadRestartRace` helper drives a prewarmed session over the wire with that file's peer harness, holding back the first `thread/unsubscribe` and `turn/start`:

- *pre-turn thread restarts run one at a time and reload once the turn is claimed* — without the change it fails: `thread-1` is unsubscribed twice, two thread starts overlap, `turn/start` runs on `thread-3`, then a further restart unsubscribes `thread-3` under the running turn and the session persists `thread-4`.
- *a turn waiting out a thread restart also waits out a restart requested after it* — covers a restart queued behind the one a send is waiting on; a version that only waits for the restart in flight lets the turn run on `thread-2` while the queued restart persists `thread-3`.

- *an MCP auth restart under a claimed prewarm persists the replacement thread its turn runs on* — drives `handleAuthenticationToken` while a send that has claimed the prewarm waits; without the persistence in the restart, the turn runs on `thread-2` while the session's persisted thread is still `thread-1`.

With the change all three pass, and so do all Codex node unit tests (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/*.test.ts`).

**Behaviour to note**

- A failed restart now fails the send waiting on it (`CodexResumeFailed` / `CodexTurnError`) instead of the send failing later with "no backing thread".

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pull_requests.title: agentHost: hosts declare their default model explicitly, and the chat input uses it
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339509

**Changes**

- A namespaced `vscode.defaultModel` model `_meta` key (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/meta/agentModelDefaultMeta.ts`, following the `common/meta` layout) marks the model an agent runs when a session selects none; it is read with a strict `=== true` check. The protocol itself is unchanged.
- `AgentHostLanguageModelProvider.provideLanguageModelChatInfo` declares `isDefaultForLocation: { [ChatAgentLocation.Chat]: true }` for the first enabled model carrying the key and `{}` for all others. When no model carries it, no default is declared — the previous behaviour, so a host that does not send the key is unaffected.
- Codex marks the first model of the list it publishes, which is the model `CodexAgent._defaultModel()` runs when no model is sent. Claude and the Copilot CLI pass no model to their SDKs in that case and let the SDK resolve one from settings and policy, so they mark nothing.
- A model scoped to one session type (`targetChatSessionType`) is no default outside that session, so the two places that read "any model that is the Chat default" now skip such models, as `McpSamplingService._getDefaultModels` already does:
  - `chatSetupProviders.ts`: `SetupAgent.whenLanguageModelReady` (so an agent host's default cannot satisfy readiness for a request before the default agent's own models arrive), and the `languageModelDefaultCount` in `computeDiagnosticInfo`;
  - `mcpCommands.ts`: *Configure Sampling Models* no longer preselects agent-host models for a server with no saved configuration.

**Why**

Codex runs `models[0]` of the list it publishes when a session has no model (`CodexAgent._defaultModel`), but every agent-host model was published with an empty `isDefaultForLocation`, so the chat input fell back to the first non-BYOK model of a pool sorted by name (`ChatInputModelSelectionController._defaultModel`, `ChatInputPart.getModelsForSessionType`). A session's first turn ran on Codex's default and later turns on that other model — Codex compacted the context to switch, and the turn failed when the account could not use it. The protocol defines no order or default flag for `AgentInfo.models`, so the default is declared explicitly in `_meta` rather than inferred from position. With the Codex default declared, the chat input and the Agents window both select the model Codex would run anyway.

Only `Chat` is declared: agent-host models are offered only in session pools (`filterModelsForSession`), and inline chat's default lookup is per location, so it is unaffected.

**Tests**

- `agentHostLanguageModelProvider.test.ts`: *declares only the model the host marks as its default, wherever it is listed* — a marked model that is not first, an unmarked list (no default) and non-`true` values. It fails before the change and passes after.
- `agentMetaReaders.test.ts`: *agent model default meta* round-trips the marker and ignores other values.
- `codexModelRefresh.test.ts`: *marks the model a session runs without a selection as the default* checks the marked model is the one `_defaultModel()` returns; two existing Codex `_meta` snapshots now include the key.

With the change, the provider, `agentHostByokLmHandler`, `agentHostChatContribution`, `chatContextUsageWidget`, `chatInputModelUtils`, `chatInputModelSelectionController`, `agentMetaReaders`, `metadataCompatibility` and all Codex node tests pass. `mcpCommands.test.ts`: *Configure Sampling Models preselects only defaults that are not scoped to a session type* covers the MCP guard; `SetupAgent.whenLanguageModelReady` has no existing test harness, and its guard is not covered by a new test.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pull_requests.body: Fixes #339506 Agent-host chat session contributions now carry their own welcome, so an empty agent-host chat no longer falls back to the generic coding-agent welcome ("Delegate to @agent-host-codex", "…will be forwarded to the … coding agent where work is completed in the background"). **Changes** - `agentHostChatContribution.ts`: `AgentHostContribution._registerAgent` registers with `welcomeTitle` = the agent's display name and `welcomeMessage` = "{0} runs on this machine." - `remoteAgentHostChatContribution.ts`: `RemoteAgentHostContribution._registerAgent` registers with `welcomeTitle` = its existing `displayName` (`Agent [Host]`) and `welcomeMessage` = "{0} runs on {1}." with the agent and host labels. - The names in the message go through a new `escapeMarkdownText` in `base/common/htmlContent.ts`, which backslash-escapes every ASCII punctuation character, since `ChatWidget` renders `welcomeMessage` as Markdown (HTML off) and host labels are user-configured. `escapeMarkdownSyntaxTokens` leaves HTML tags (dropped by the renderer) and a leading `>` (a blockquote) in place, and `MarkdownString.appendText` still autolinks URLs, `www.` hosts and email addresses, decodes entities and turns spaces into ` `. `chatWidget.ts` is unchanged: these contributions now supply the welcome text through the same fields extension-contributed session types already use. `editorCloudSandboxContribution.ts` is left as is: its session type is named "GitHub Sandbox", not an internal id, and its work does run in the cloud. **Tests** - `agentHostChatContribution.test.ts`: *local agent contribution provides its own welcome instead of the delegation fallback* (including the markdown escaping). - `remoteAgentHost.contribution.test.ts`: the existing test's harness moves into a `registerAgent` helper, unchanged; the new *provides its own welcome instead of the delegation fallback* expects `Codex [build_box]` / `Codex runs on build\_box.`. - `htmlContent.test.ts`: *escapeMarkdownText escapes every ASCII punctuation character and nothing else*. The contribution tests use labels with HTML (`…`) and a leading `>`. Both new contribution tests fail without the source change (`welcomeTitle` / `welcomeMessage` are `undefined`) and pass with it; both files pass in full. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

pull_requests.title: agentHost: remove dropped remote hosts before rebuilding host names
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339504

`RemoteAgentHostService._reconcileConnections` now removes the connections no longer exposed by a factory **before** it rebuilds the name map, instead of after. The loop itself is unchanged; only its position and comment move.

**Why**

Each `_removeConnection` fires `onDidChangeConnections`, and listeners read `connections`, which names entries from `_names`. When one reconcile dropped two or more connected hosts, `_names` had already been rebuilt without them, so the first removal's event reported the hosts still waiting to be removed under their address (and without their `operatingSystem`). `RemoteAgentHostContribution` treats a name change as a reason to tear down and re-register all of that host's agents, so it re-registered them under the address and disposed them again on the next event.

Neither the moved loop nor `_removeConnection` reads the rebuilt names, tokens or formatters, and the rename detection only looks at addresses that are still desired, so it is unaffected.

**Test**

`remoteAgentHostService.test.ts`: *keeps the names of remaining connections while removing several entries at once* connects two named hosts, waits for their dials to settle, removes both entries in one configuration change, and records `connections` at every `onDidChangeConnections`.

Without the fix the first snapshot is `[{ address: 'host2:8080', name: 'host2:8080' }]` and the test fails; with it the snapshots are `[[{ address: 'host2:8080', name: 'Host 2' }], []]`. pull_requests.title: Keep terminal editors working after moving them to another editor group
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #183268

## Summary

If you move a terminal editor to another editor group (with `View: Move Editor into Right Group` and the other move commands, by dragging its tab to another group, or with `View: Move Editor into New Window`), terminal keybindings that send a sequence to the active terminal stop working. Examples are Cmd+Backspace and Cmd+←/→ on macOS, and Ctrl+Backspace on Windows/Linux. The keypress is swallowed until the terminal loses focus and gets it back. The issue title says Mac, but this happens on every platform.

The cause is that `TerminalEditorService` treats the source half of a move as a real close and stops tracking the terminal. This PR makes it ignore that close.

## Root cause

An editor moves across groups in two steps in [`EditorGroupView.doMoveOrCopyEditorAcrossGroups`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/45373f06ff77cc97a7754a376548d8937fb3af54/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorGroupView.ts#L1503-L1507). The editor first opens in the target group, then closes in the source group with `EditorCloseContext.MOVE`. The `TerminalEditorInput` and its terminal instance are the same objects throughout.

`TerminalEditorService`'s [`onDidCloseEditor` handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/45373f06ff77cc97a7754a376548d8937fb3af54/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalEditorService.ts#L94-L108) didn't look at the close context. On a move it:

1. called `_removeInstance`, which drops the terminal from `instances`, deletes its `_editorInputs` entry and disposes its focus, dispose and capability listeners;
2. called `setActiveInstance(undefined)`, because the moved terminal was the active one.

Next the target group activates the editor, and [`onDidActiveEditorChange`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/45373f06ff77cc97a7754a376548d8937fb3af54/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalEditorService.ts#L63-L76) calls `setActiveInstance(instance)`. The instance is no longer in `instances`, so the index is `-1` and `activeInstance` stays `undefined`. As a result:

- `ITerminalService.activeInstance` is `undefined` while a terminal editor is focused, so `workbench.action.terminal.sendSequence` (which all of these keybindings use) has no target and does nothing.
- The terminal only comes back later through the ["unknown editor" path in `onDidVisibleEditorsChange`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/45373f06ff77cc97a7754a376548d8937fb3af54/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalEditorService.ts#L77-L92). That path only pushes the instance back into `instances`. It doesn't re-register its listeners, so `onDidFocusInstance`, `onDidDisposeInstance` and `onDidChangeInstanceCapability` stay silent for that terminal afterwards.

## Change

- **`terminalEditorService.ts`:** the `onDidCloseEditor` handler returns early when `e.context === EditorCloseContext.MOVE`, because the terminal is still open in the editor area.
  - The terminal stays in `instances` and keeps its input mapping and listeners.
  - The existing `onDidActiveEditorChange` handler then re-parents it to the new group (`setGroup`) and makes it active, as it already does for any activation.
  - I also updated the handler's comment. It previously listed "dragging and dropping to another editor" as a case where the terminal should be removed.
- **New `terminalEditorService.test.ts`:** this is the first test suite for `TerminalEditorService`. It registers a terminal through the real `resolveResource` path and drives the service through its `IEditorService` events:
  - `keeps a terminal editor tracked and active when it moves to another group`: a MOVE close followed by activation in the target group. It fails without this change (`{ instances: [], activeInstance: undefined }`).
  - `removes a terminal editor when it is closed`: a normal close still removes the terminal, which guards the existing behavior.

I outlined this approach on the issue before starting: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/183268#issuecomment-5971059792

### What's unchanged

| scenario | how it's handled |
|---|---|
| Closing a terminal editor (Cmd/Ctrl+W, close button) | close context is not `MOVE`, so the terminal is removed as before |
| Moving a terminal editor to the terminal panel | [`moveToTerminalView`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/45373f06ff77cc97a7754a376548d8937fb3af54/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalService.ts#L826) removes it explicitly through `detachInstance` |
| Dragging a terminal editor to another VS Code window | [`onDidRequestDetach`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/45373f06ff77cc97a7754a376548d8937fb3af54/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalService.ts#L296) → `detachInstance` |
| An editor that fails to open in the target group | it closes with a non-`MOVE` context, so it's removed as before |
| Terminal editors created by splitting an editor | still picked up by the `onDidVisibleEditorsChange` path, which this PR doesn't touch |

## How to test

1. Run `Terminal: Create New Terminal in Editor Area` twice.
2. Type some text in the active terminal (e.g. `echo hello world`), but don't press Enter.
3. Run `View: Move Editor into Right Group`.
4. Without clicking anywhere, press **Cmd+Backspace** on macOS (**Ctrl+Backspace** on Windows/Linux).
   - **Expected:** the line (macOS) or the previous word (Windows/Linux) is deleted.
   - **Before this PR:** nothing happens until you focus something else and come back to the terminal.
5. Repeat step 4 after each of these moves:
   - moving the terminal back with `View: Move Editor into Left Group`;
   - dragging a terminal editor's tab into another group;
   - running `View: Move Editor into New Window`.
6. Regression checks:
   - Cmd/Ctrl+W on a terminal editor still kills the terminal.
   - `Terminal: Move Terminal into Panel`, or dragging a terminal editor onto the terminal panel, still moves it there without leaving a copy in the editor area.

Automated:

```
./scripts/test.sh --grep "Workbench - TerminalEditorService"
```

## Validation

- **New suite:** the move test fails with the product change reverted and passes with it.
- **Existing terminal tests:** all of the terminal browser unit tests pass.
- **Checks:** hygiene, eslint, `valid-layers-check` and `typecheck-client` pass.
- **Manual testing:** done in a dev build on macOS, using the steps above.
  - Cmd+Backspace works after moving right, moving back left and dragging the tab to a new group.
  - After `Move Editor into New Window`, the terminal stays tracked and renders and runs in the new window.
  - Closing that window still closes the terminal, as before.
  - Moving to the panel and closing with Cmd+W behave as before.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Stabilize sessionless managed-settings diagnostics E2E
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Stabilizes the macOS ARM64 managed-settings diagnostics E2E failure tracked in microsoft/vscode-engineering#4080. This does not address that issue's separate Windows compile-cache failure.

Authentication schedules Copilot runtime startup asynchronously. Immediately requesting diagnostics races startup against the production 4.5-second overall deadline, which includes both startup and policy resolution.

- Subscribe to root state before authentication and wait for the authenticated provider's model catalog, establishing a completed sessionless runtime RPC before probing policy.
- Preserve every existing policy/error assertion and fresh server-policy fetch, and explicitly assert that no sessions were created.
- Retain runtime logs on test failure.
- Add unit coverage proving startup still consumes the overall diagnostics deadline, and document the readiness boundary.

Production implementation and the 4.5-second overall / 3.5-second query deadlines are unchanged. No timeout increases, skips, assertion relaxation, model recording, or recovery-branch changes are included.

## Reproduction

Using main at `7f20cdad`, the exact startup error was reproduced with a temporary runtime-launch delay of 4.7 seconds (zero policy requests). A 4.0-second launch delay plus an 800 ms loopback policy-response delay reproduced the overall timeout during querying. With the readiness barrier, both scenarios passed twice with the same delays. All temporary fault-injection hooks were removed.

Natural intermittency was not reproduced locally. The retained failing CI artifacts omit the diagnostics process's timing logs, so the underlying reason for slow CI startup is not established; this change corrects the demonstrated test-readiness race.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client` - passed, zero compilation errors.
- `npm run hygiene` - passed.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --grep 'managed settings|sessionless managed'` - passed, 9 tests.
- `INTEGRATION_TEST_ELECTRON_PATH="<isolated Electron executable>" ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotManagedSettingsAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts` - passed, 2 tests, strict tokenless replay.
- [Azure pipeline 111, build 480304](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480304), source `6a7573aa32486ef15bdec077b62eb193956b2502` - succeeded on macOS ARM64. Electron integration task/log 910 passed; all six Agent Host E2E suites passed with six parallel workers. The exact diagnostics test passed in 5.303 seconds including readiness setup; the managed-settings suite took 12.5 seconds overall. Publishing/release were disabled.

One packaged macOS ARM64 CI execution is verified; repeat CI and Windows/Linux/macOS x64 validation are not yet completed. A local full-suite run had separate failures outside diagnostics, including Claude/Codex workspace-completion assertions reproduced in isolation; the packaged Azure full E2E run passed.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Restore peer chats lost after session refresh
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #339409.

### What changed

- Revert #339074 in full, including its Codex continuation UI, model/account plumbing, telemetry, and supporting storage APIs. This intentionally removes the entire feature, not just the URI-resolution change.
- Restore fragment-free backend session resolution. Selecting a peer chat must not register its chat fragment as a separate backend session.
- Automatically recover erased peer-chat membership for verified affected local Copilot CLI sessions, retaining original chat URIs, surviving transcripts, and provider continuation metadata.
- Remove verified phantom registrations without deleting their shared backing storage, and refresh recovered list projections before the first session-list response, including after a restart.

### Why

The fragment-bearing resolution introduced by #339074 can register a phantom session separately from its real parent, while both use the same path-based local database. The phantom writes an empty peer-chat mirror; subsequent legacy reconciliation can erase the parent's authoritative membership. Reverting prevents the corruption, but does not repair membership already lost.

### Recovery safety and limitations

- Recovery requires a restore-created phantom, a matching registered parent, and surviving selected-chat backing metadata. Additional candidates require affirmative parent membership evidence; healthy catalogues are not scavenged.
- Respect explicit deletions, authoritative ownership elsewhere, and concurrent membership changes. Do not rewrite child transcripts or chat-local provider metadata, and do not create missing child databases.
- Persist the pre-recovery membership and a completion marker. Interrupted recovery uses frozen candidates; completed recovery does not resurrect later removals.
- Preserve existing order and archive state. Missing peers are appended deterministically and restored as active because their original order/archive flags cannot be reconstructed.
- Legacy directory names are only recovery evidence, not authoritative current ownership; this does not require redesigning stable chat identities or chat moves.

### Validation

- `npm run compile` - passed.
- `npm run hygiene` - passed (12,895 files checked).
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostPeerChatStore.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostDatabase.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSessionRegistry.test.ts` - passed: 792 passing, 16 pending.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - passed.
- Previously validated recovery against 91 isolated SQLite backup copies: 23 affected peers recovered; healthy catalogues, 86 child databases, and 110 foreign membership rows unchanged. No manual changes to live storage.
- Verified recovery in the installed build, including preserved author/reviewer transcripts. Regression tests cover first-list visibility for live, cold, and already-completed recovery; the new cold projection tests failed on the pre-fix implementation.

CI build [480291](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480291) hit an intermittent macOS managed-settings diagnostics timeout also reproduced on main in builds [480293](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480293) and [480122](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480122). That failure is being investigated separately.

Build [480297](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480297) is still running on the temporary integration-test recovery-bypass commit. The bypass has been reverted; that build is not validation of the current head. Recovery remains enabled in tests. A full cross-platform CI run on the current head has not yet completed.

To test manually, start the fixed build against an isolated copy of affected storage with a verified restore-created fragment registration and an empty peer-chat mirror. The initial list should show recovered peers without opening the parent; opening a recovered peer should load its original transcript. Refresh/restart should retain membership without duplicating it, and subsequent intentional removals should stay removed.

pull_requests.title: fix(terminal): avoid hanging safeDisposeTerminal after process exit
pull_requests.body:
## Problem

`TerminalService.safeDisposeTerminal()` waits for the terminal's `onExit`
event before resolving its Promise.

A Task terminal that exits with a non-zero code can intentionally remain
open so the user can inspect its output. In that lifecycle, `onExit` has
already fired and will not fire again.

If the user subsequently kills that terminal, `safeDisposeTerminal()`
could therefore leave its returned Promise pending indefinitely.

## Fix

Detect the already-exited lifecycle state using `instance.exitCode`.

When the terminal is already disposed or its process has already exited,
dispose it directly instead of waiting for another `onExit` event.

Live terminals retain the existing `onExit` waiting behavior.

## Validation

- Regression reproduced before the fix: Promise remained `pending`
- Regression passes after the fix: Promise becomes `settled`
- 219 terminal-related tests passing
- 0 failing tests
- ESLint clean
- `git diff --check` clean
- Regression was also validated against a real `TerminalInstance`

The change is limited to:
- `terminalService.ts`
- `terminalService.test.ts`

pull_requests.title: notebook: avoid quadratic carriage-return stream normalization
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Normalizes ordinary carriage-return progress output without rescanning the entire stream repeatedly. The same **164 KB batch** drops from **1.30 seconds to 2.2 ms**, with identical output.

| Measured operation | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| 41 KB progress batch | 80.6 ms | 0.6 ms |
| 82 KB progress batch | 315.8 ms | 1.1 ms |
| 164 KB progress batch | 1,296.6 ms | 2.2 ms |

![Recorded before and after measurements for Notebook stdout - remove the 1.3-second stall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8a50bfd61d53df3579025ef6b9f0e58ab1fbbd95/brief-performance-proof/notebook-proof.png)

**Proof scope:** Legacy dollar-text lines keep the old path. Component probe, not live-kernel execution. 68 notebook tests and 299,593 baseline compatibility comparisons passed. Legacy dollar-text behavior is intentionally preserved; those affected streams retain the old path and cost.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction clips (startup removed), implementation, and full validation commands</summary>

The clips below are brief measured-result excerpts. The comparison above is the primary performance proof; clip duration is not a benchmark.

Fixes a source-derived notebook stdout performance defect found by the performance swarm. No matching open issue or fix PR was found, and no new issue was filed. Related implementation history: #160946 (stream compression) and #188998 (compression-flag reporting, preserved here).

## Root cause

`NotebookCellOutputTextModel.appendData` normalizes terminal-style stdout before publishing the output change. `fixCarriageReturn` repeatedly searches and replaces against the entire accumulated string, consuming one carriage-return-bearing line at a time.

A batch of 4,000 ordinary progress records:

```text
Task 00000: running\rTask 00000: complete\n
Task 00001: running\rTask 00001: complete\n
...
```

is only **164,000 bytes**, but normalization blocks the renderer for about **1.3 seconds**. Doubling the input from 1,000 to 2,000 to 4,000 records produced roughly four times the runtime at each step.

## Change

For ordinary streams, process each logical line once. Walk its carriage-return segments backward and keep only the suffix not overwritten by a later segment. This preserves shorter overwrites without repeatedly rebuilding the whole stream.

- Preserve a pending final carriage return for the next append.
- Preserve CRLF, consecutive returns, Unicode line boundaries, UTF-16 overwrite behavior, and existing backspace processing.
- Keep output compression flags, version invalidation, and data-change events unchanged.
- Do not change notebook rendering, execution, or provider APIs.

### Explicit compatibility boundary

The old replacement-string algorithm has observable dollar-text quirks: for example, `$$\r\r` becomes `$`. This PR deliberately preserves them instead of combining a behavior change with the performance fix.

If a carriage-return-bearing line contains `$`, the existing algorithm is retained for that stream. Such inputs retain their previous complexity. Dollar text on an unaffected line does **not** disable the optimized path. The new tests cover both cases.

## Before / after

Same scenario, actual production output model inside Code OSS, exact output checks, one warm-up and five measured samples per size:

| Progress records | Appended bytes | Before median | After median |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,000 | 41,000 | 80.6 ms | 0.6 ms |
| 2,000 | 82,000 | 315.8 ms | 1.1 ms |
| 4,000 | 164,000 | **1,296.6 ms** | **2.2 ms** |

For the 164 KB case, the same **84,010 output bytes**, version, and event count are verified. The already-normalized same-output control takes 0.2-0.3 ms.

The unchanged scenario fails the 200 ms renderer budget before the fix and passes **3/3** in fresh fixed windows. The three after-run medians are **2.2, 2.3, and 2.0 ms**, with worst samples at or below 2.6 ms.

### Before

![Before: 164 KB of notebook progress output blocks the renderer for about 1.3 seconds - measured-result excerpt, startup removed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8a50bfd61d53df3579025ef6b9f0e58ab1fbbd95/brief-performance-proof/notebook-before-short.gif)

### After

![After: identical notebook output normalizes in about 2.2 milliseconds - measured-result excerpt, startup removed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8a50bfd61d53df3579025ef6b9f0e58ab1fbbd95/brief-performance-proof/notebook-after-short.gif)

[Scenario](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/87412d0bd3c7e89f875e8aeb74f5b4fd0eb6a95c/notebook-stream-normalization/stream.scenario.cjs) · [Scenario implementation](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/87412d0bd3c7e89f875e8aeb74f5b4fd0eb6a95c/notebook-stream-normalization/renderer-probe.cjs) · [Before data](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/87412d0bd3c7e89f875e8aeb74f5b4fd0eb6a95c/notebook-stream-normalization/before.json) · [After run 1](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/87412d0bd3c7e89f875e8aeb74f5b4fd0eb6a95c/notebook-stream-normalization/after-1.json) · [Run 2](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/87412d0bd3c7e89f875e8aeb74f5b4fd0eb6a95c/notebook-stream-normalization/after-2.json) · [Run 3](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/87412d0bd3c7e89f875e8aeb74f5b4fd0eb6a95c/notebook-stream-normalization/after-3.json)

Windows 11 x64, AMD EPYC 7763 (32 logical processors), 128 GiB RAM, Node 24.20.0, Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev. Timings exclude input construction and assertions. Benchmarks were run sequentially under the shared measurement lease, without concurrent builds.

Baseline: `dcb81648f8a8f1863d2577f8fec98e805e5f95a0`. Fixed: `709ff28acde959947531c9aa8ac16ced1ba9b663`, based on `253b7648aa69de1a651a327370098f3814b8922f`. The relevant normalization and output-model code is identical between the baseline and the fix's parent.

## Regression coverage

- Existing notebook common and text-model suites: **68 tests passed**.
- New exact-output cases cover short/long overwrites, pending and consecutive returns, CRLF, backspace ordering, Unicode line separators, UTF-16 boundaries, and legacy dollar behavior.
- Every semantic case is also tested at every possible byte-buffer split, including inside UTF-8 sequences.
- Thousands of carriage-return segments on a single line preserve the uncovered suffix correctly.
- A 4,000-record append through the actual notebook text model preserves one output item, one data-change event, the output version, and invalidation of append-only history.
- An additional [compatibility checker](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/87412d0bd3c7e89f875e8aeb74f5b4fd0eb6a95c/notebook-stream-normalization/notebook-stream-compat.mjs) exhaustively compared **299,593 inputs** of length 0-6 over `a`, `b`, CR, LF, backspace, `$`, U+2028, and U+2029 against the unchanged implementation. Both output text and `didCompression` matched.

## Validation commands and results

From the fix checkout:

```powershell
npm run compile-client
# PASSED: full client/extension compilation and type-check, zero errors.

.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\notebook\test\browser\notebookCommon.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\notebook\test\browser\notebookTextModel.test.ts --reporter dot
# PASSED: 68 tests. Executed through the shared measurement lease.

npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\notebook\common\notebookCommon.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\notebook\test\browser\notebookCommon.test.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\notebook\test\browser\notebookTextModel.test.ts
# PASSED: all three changed files.

node 'C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\session-state\5be74984-e914-4843-8a16-9065f861cc4a\files\notebook-stream-compat.mjs'
# PASSED: 299593 fixed-versus-baseline output and compression-flag comparisons.

git diff --check
# PASSED.
```

Exact before/after scenario commands, with local path aliases:

```powershell
$lock = 'C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\session-state\5be74984-e914-4843-8a16-9065f861cc4a\files\perf-swarm-high-impact\with-perf-lock.ps1'
$runner = 'C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\skills\bug-swarm\scripts\run-scenario.mjs'
$scenario = 'C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\session-state\5be74984-e914-4843-8a16-9065f861cc4a\files\perf-swarm-high-impact\editor-notebook\stream.scenario.cjs'
$evidence = 'C:\Users\kanadig\.copilot\session-state\5be74984-e914-4843-8a16-9065f861cc4a\files\notebook-stream-fix'

& $lock -Owner notebook-stream-before -FilePath node -ArgumentList @($runner, '--scenario', $scenario, '--checkout', 'Q:\GIT\vscode', '--isolation', 'fix-nb-stream-before', '--gif', "$evidence\before.gif")
# EXPECTED FAILURE at the latency budget; setup, exact-output and control checks pass.

& $lock -Owner notebook-stream-after -FilePath node -ArgumentList @($runner, '--scenario', $scenario, '--checkout', 'Q:\GIT\vscode.worktrees\perf-fixes-5be74984', '--isolation', 'fix-nb-stream-after', '--repeat', '3', '--gif', "$evidence\after.gif")
# PASSED 3/3; exact-output and control checks pass in every window.
```

### Limits

These are production-component renderer measurements, not a live Jupyter kernel or end-to-end notebook-opening benchmark. No shipped-build comparison, macOS/Linux UI runs, full repository suite, or OOM test was performed. Dollar-bearing overwritten lines intentionally keep the legacy path; backspace normalization is unchanged.

</details>

pull_requests.title: chat: preserve transcript order when refreshing history
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Refreshing an older response could move it below a newer locally sent message. The history merger removed and rebuilt the changed suffix, kept local requests in place, and appended the rebuilt turns at the end. Even an elapsed-time or usage update could change the visible conversation order.

- Match history turns by request ID and replace changed restored turns in their existing model/view position.
- Insert newly loaded history before its next known turn, preserving unchanged and locally created request/response objects.
- Keep drafts and the existing deferral while a response is streaming; repeated snapshots do not duplicate requests.
- Dispose superseded response listeners and refresh last-request state and session cost after history removals.
- Add regressions using the real chat service, model, and view model for metadata/content updates, older history, local echoes, missing IDs, streaming, and removals.

This is independent of the authentication-recovery changes in #339454. It does not change the protocol client, authentication, or host-side persistence.

## Validation

- Confirmed the ordering regressions fail before the fix: `[README, hi]` becomes `[hi, README]` despite correctly ordered incoming history.
- Reproduced and fixed both review-found removal edge cases; follow-up review found no remaining blocking issues.
- 319 related tests pass in Electron.
- 318 browser-applicable tests pass in each of Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
- Targeted TypeScript diagnostics, ESLint, whitespace checks, and pre-commit hygiene pass.
- The maintainer reported that the earlier combined history/authentication test snapshot no longer reproduced the issue. The final removal-only corrections have automated validation, not a second manual retest.

## Manual verification

Open a restored remote chat, send and complete a new message, then trigger a history refresh (for example, return after switching apps). Confirm earlier turns remain above the newer message, response text stays visible, and the unsent draft is preserved. Also load older history and verify it is inserted before the existing turns without duplication.

A turn also missing from another client's history is not proof of a display-order bug; this PR does not claim to repair missing host-side history.

* chat: preserve transcript order when refreshing history

Reconcile refreshed history by request identity and replace changed turns in their existing model and view positions instead of appending them after local messages. Preserve drafts, local responses, and streaming deferral while supporting older history insertion.

Dispose superseded response listeners and publish removals after updating the request list so last-request state and session cost remain current. Add real service/model/view regressions for ordering, identity, streaming, and history removals.

* chat: match ID-less history before reusing request IDs

Replace positional fallback with unique request-content matching in both the previous and incoming history. Preserve provider IDs, avoid assigning ambiguous duplicates another turn's local identity, and keep identical history refreshes as no-ops.

Cover ID-less history prepends, removals, and one-to-many and many-to-one ambiguous matches with real model/view regressions.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: restore authentication on transport reconnect
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #339229. The transport can now reconnect, but the client still assumed that a remembered client ID meant authentication survived on the replacement connection. A host that requires authentication again can reject later requests with `AuthRequired`, while local authentication caching prevents a new authentication request from being sent.

- Restore required or previously established authentication for replay and snapshot reconnects, not only fresh initialization.
- Defer protected subscriptions reported missing before authentication, and restore subscriptions omitted from handshake snapshots after authentication.
- Keep recovery in progress and queued actions buffered until authentication and subscription restoration settle.
- Preserve errors for resources that remain missing or forbidden after authentication; keep the existing behavior for connections without authentication.
- Add six regressions covering cached/resolved credentials, replay/snapshot recovery, traffic ordering, response continuity through turn completion, and terminal subscription failures.

## Validation

- Four new regressions reproduced the old behavior before the fix: readiness was reported too early and protected subscriptions were marked unavailable.
- 321 related protocol-client, sandbox service, credential, and telemetry tests pass in Electron.
- 122 sandbox service/credential/telemetry tests pass in each of Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. The protocol-client suite is Electron-only and was excluded by the browser runner.
- Targeted TypeScript diagnostics, ESLint, whitespace checks, and pre-commit hygiene pass.
- Independent read-only review found no blocking issues.

## Manual verification pending

On mobile, open a sandbox chat, send a message, switch to another app, return, and send a follow-up. Verify recovery authenticates before messages are released and that responses remain visible after completion.

The supplied logs establish the post-reconnect authentication failure. They do not identify the chat-state update that removed an earlier streamed reply, so this PR does not claim that the separate disappearing-response symptom is conclusively resolved. Live mobile validation remains pending. The separately reported regular-tunnel recovery issue is also outside this fix.

auto_merge.commit_title: agentHost: restore authentication on transport reconnect (#339454)
auto_merge.commit_message:
Re-establish authentication on replacement transports even when reconnect resumes an existing client. Restore protected subscriptions after authentication before reporting readiness or draining queued actions.

Add regression coverage for replay and snapshot recovery with cached or resolved credentials, response continuity, and genuinely unavailable subscriptions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

pull_requests.title: splitview: avoid intermediate layouts when distributing views
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Stops rendering an intermediate editor width that is immediately discarded. The existing editor is laid out **once instead of twice**, with the same final dimensions. This is a modest optimization, not a large end-to-end speedup.

| Measured operation | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Existing-editor layouts | 2 | 1 |
| Layout-method time | 9.6 ms | 7.2 ms |

![Recorded before and after measurements for Editor split - one final layout, not two](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8a50bfd61d53df3579025ef6b9f0e58ab1fbbd95/brief-performance-proof/split-proof.png)

**Proof scope:** Modest measured benefit. This is layout-method time, not total editor-opening time. 137 SplitView, grid, and editor-group tests passed; final sizes and constraints are covered.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction clips (startup removed), implementation, and full validation commands</summary>

The clips below are brief measured-result excerpts. The comparison above is the primary performance proof; clip duration is not a benchmark.

Fixes #164200.

## Root cause and change

When adding or removing a view with distributed sizing, `SplitView` first calls `relayout`, then `distributeViewSizes`, which calls `relayout` again. Automatic sizing takes the same path when the views are already evenly distributed. Both sizes reach the existing editors, so they render an intermediate width that is immediately discarded.

Preserve the first constraint-solving pass, but defer its view layout and proportion notifications until distribution computes the final sizes. This is deliberately not a change to the distribution algorithm: removing the first sizing pass entirely would change final sizes when minimum/maximum constraints apply.

The same fix covers distributed removal. Numeric sizing, split sizing, explicit `skipLayout`, and the default split-sizing setting retain their behavior.

## Before / after

Real workbench split-right commands against a small synthetic text file. One warm-up, five measured split/close cycles per run. Instrumentation forwards every `CodeEditorWidget.layout` call to the original implementation and only records its dimensions and duration.

| Existing editor during a split | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Layout calls per split | 2 | 1 |
| Width sequence | 1046.4 → 633 | 633 |
| Final width | 633 | 633 |
| Median summed layout-method time | 9.6 ms | 7.2 ms |

The identical scenario fails before and passes **3/3** after: **15 measured splits**, each with exactly one original-editor layout at its final width.

A direct production `SplitView` control also verifies final-size equivalence:

- `Auto(0)` and `Distribute`: first-view sizes **980 → 600** before, **600** after.
- `Split(0)`: **600** both before and after.
- Every case ends with view sizes **600 / 600**.

### Before

![Before: every editor split lays out a discarded intermediate width - measured-result excerpt, startup removed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8a50bfd61d53df3579025ef6b9f0e58ab1fbbd95/brief-performance-proof/split-before-short.gif)

### After

![After: every editor split lays out the final width exactly once - measured-result excerpt, startup removed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8a50bfd61d53df3579025ef6b9f0e58ab1fbbd95/brief-performance-proof/split-after-short.gif)

[Scenario](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/a71b9b705c5eba8d6016565d4338eb3f5c2435a9/splitview-164200/split-layout.scenario.cjs) · [Before measurements](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/a71b9b705c5eba8d6016565d4338eb3f5c2435a9/splitview-164200/split-before-results.json) · [After measurements](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/a71b9b705c5eba8d6016565d4338eb3f5c2435a9/splitview-164200/split-after-results.json)

Windows 11 x64, AMD EPYC 7763, 32 logical processors, 128 GiB RAM, Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev. These are method timings, not end-to-end split latency. The reported Markdown-webview cost was not benchmarked. The table uses the final saved after-run measurements; the GIF records the first passing after run.

pull_requests.title: Agent host: show skill argument-hint as inline placeholder
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #339445

In agent-host chat sessions, a skill's `argument-hint` frontmatter wasn't shown as inline placeholder text after `/skill `, while runtime commands like `/review` and local chat prompts/skills already show theirs. The hint was dropped at every layer of the agent-host skill path. Restoring it makes skills consistent with commands.

## Changes

- **Skill metadata:**
  - `parseSkillFile` now reads `argument-hint` (trimmed; a blank value is ignored).
  - Plugin and Claude skills carry the hint through `readSkills` and `toParsedSkill`.
  - Copilot discovery prefers the SDK-reported `ServerSkill.argumentHint` and falls back to the frontmatter.
  - The hint lives in a namespaced `_meta` key, `vscode.skill.argumentHint`, on `SkillCustomization`, with a typed reader and writer in `common/meta`. The synced protocol types are unchanged. Hosts that don't publish the key behave exactly as before.
- **Completions:** skill completion `_meta` gains an optional `argumentHint`, alongside the existing command `argumentHint`.
- **Rendering:** the Agents window placeholder and the workbench `InputEditorCommandArgumentHint` now accept agent-host skill references as well as commands. They still show the hint only while the command or skill is the sole input followed by one space.

## Testing

1. Create `~/.copilot/skills/design-prep/SKILL.md` with `argument-hint: "<problem and repo> [offline]"` and `user-invocable: true`.
2. In an Agents window Copilot CLI session, type `/design-prep ` and accept the completion. The hint appears as grey placeholder text.
3. Type any character. The hint disappears.
4. Check that `/review ` still shows its hint.
5. Check that a skill without `argument-hint` shows no placeholder.
6. Check that a skill installed from a plugin with an `argument-hint` shows its hint.

Unit tests cover the parser, the `_meta` reader and writer, Copilot discovery (SDK hint and frontmatter fallback), the completion provider, and both renderers. Lint and the layers check are clean for the changed files.

Caveats:
- I verified this with unit tests only, not in a running Agents window.
- Codex skills and legacy `commands/*.md` files are out of scope.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: persist passive flags before publishing updates
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

## Summary

Independent Windows Agent Host stabilization work, based on main. This does not include or update the Node-hook/spellchecker changes in [#339430](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339430).

- Await passive read/archive catalog synchronization before publishing the root summary notification. Previously the host published the flag after writing legacy session metadata, while the authoritative central catalog update remained queued. A bounded shutdown could exit before that queued update completed, and the first listing after restart returned the old flag.
- Make unexpected synchronization failures reject the action rather than publish a success-shaped notification. Existing durable pending snapshots and shutdown replay remain in place for central-write failures.
- Serialize legacy flag values with their durable catalog receipt in the existing per-session snapshot transaction. A rejected snapshot write must not leave the rejected flag in legacy persistence. Preserve legacy-only fallback and clearing automatic-archive metadata on unarchive.
- Update the unit test to enforce the stronger publication boundary using a deterministic blocked queue and a dirty-write barrier, including the catalog value at publication. Preserve the E2E's exact immediate-restart assertions and all providers.
- Include underlying filesystem errors in temporary-directory cleanup failures. This is diagnostic coverage for the independent Codex cleanup failure, not yet a claimed cleanup root-cause fix.
- Retain existing host trace diagnostics for every provider, including restarted hosts, so subsequent slow-restore failures identify the blocked restore stage rather than only reporting the final timeout.

Clients retain optimistic local updates; the host's root summary notification now waits for catalog synchronization instead of exposing a flag whose durability depends on later background work.

## Evidence and ownership

The preserved [Windows attempt 1](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37078430948/job/111073417451) lost Codex read state after restart; [attempt 2](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37078430948/job/111081529317) lost Claude read state. In attempt 2 the host published archived/read status 97 at 00:45:23.285Z, started shutdown at 00:45:23.735Z, timed out at 00:45:28.243Z, and the restarted listing returned archived/unread status 65. The corrected boundary prevents that restart from beginning in response to a notification while the catalog update is still queued. The exact work consuming the original shutdown budget is not yet established.

The archive E2E was added by Rob on September 2 in 2583f029c67a ([#333922](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333922)). The premature-publication window was introduced when central catalog authority and asynchronous passive synchronization were added by Sandeep on September 16 in 8ec3108ced2a ([#332410](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/332410)). This identifies the ordering change, not a proven timing-exposure commit for these particular CI runs.

Codex directory cleanup also failed in unrelated PR builds. Preserved descendant logs show shutdown completing, but the suite report dropped the nested filesystem errors. Ownership remains unclassified until independent CI exposes the failing operation and path.

Original-head [Windows attempt 3](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37078430948/job/111103171499) passed archive/read restoration and Claude checkpoints, but failed Codex `peer chat catalog and transcript survive a host restart` and directory cleanup. The AHP trace shows session subscribe id 3 at 02:22:06.925Z, a 20-second client response timeout, teardown issuing duplicate subscribe id 4 at 02:22:30.728Z, and id 4 returning a restored snapshot at 02:22:38.144Z. The original request then received a superseded-subscription error at 02:22:38.145Z. This was slow restoration, not evidence that the peer transcript was absent. Codex finished app-server initialization around 02:22:13.077Z, but the info-level logs do not identify which remaining restore stage consumed the delay. The new trace-enabled diagnostics are intentionally not presented as a restore-timeout fix; no timeout, assertion, provider, or Windows coverage is changed. The peer-persistence test was added by Rob on August 4 in f30e956db592 ([#328733](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328733)); a causal introducing commit for this delay remains unknown.

The separate Claude checkpoint failure was a real shell-command failure, not evidence of lost historical bytes: the preserved AHP tool result reports `success: false`, exit 127, and `/usr/bin/bash: line 1: node: command not found`. It is outside this persistence/cleanup change.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`: passed.
- Deterministic pre-fix regression, `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --grep 'waits for catalog synchronization before publishing'`: failed as expected because publication occurred while the catalog queue was blocked.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts`: passed on the final head, 667 passing / 16 existing pending.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostCatalogSyncService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostCatalogReconciliationService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostShutdown.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostE2EServerLease.test.ts --grep 'passive|read/archive|un-loaded session|AgentHostCatalogSync|AgentHostCatalogReconciliation|AgentHost.*shutdown|Agent Host E2E server lease'`: passed on the final head, 84 passing.
- `npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --grep 'archiving a never-restored session|provider checkpoints: historical'`: passed for every provider, strict replay, no fixture updates.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/harness/agentHostE2ETestHarness.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check` and commit hygiene: passed.
- `npm run test-agent-host-e2e`: first complete strict replay passed, 840 passing / 109 existing pending. The final-head unguarded local run encountered five timeouts while macOS suspended the machine: four separate host logs stop at 19:30:44 PDT and resume at 19:47:49, matching `pmset`'s 1,026-second system sleep; the remaining timeout matches a later 159-second system sleep. These local failures are classified as infrastructure using the OS and host timestamps, not merely because another run passed. `caffeinate -is npm run test-agent-host-e2e` on the unchanged final head passed in 290.7 seconds, **840 passing / 109 existing pending**, with process-scoped OS sleep prevention and unchanged timeouts, assertions, fixtures, and complete provider coverage.
- First independent [Code OSS run 37089034427](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37089034427) and [Azure definition 111 build 480125](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480125) both passed at `21a8541458f`, including Windows, Linux, and macOS Electron integration tests and complete provider coverage. Codex cleanup did not reproduce in either execution; this is not proof that cleanup is correct.
- Exact final-head (`ebe9a9e81cc`) [Code OSS run 37091195909](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37091195909): **fully green**, including Windows, Linux, and macOS Electron integration tests and all six Agent Host suite entrypoints. Every provider's immediate-restart archive/read assertion passes on Windows.
- Exact final-head [Azure build 480127](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=480127): **Windows x64 and Linux x64 Electron integration tests passed**. The overall build failed because macOS passed conformance, Claude, Codex, Copilot, and Copilot OTel, but the separate managed-settings diagnostics test failed: `fetched server policy appears in sessionless diagnostics and channel layers` expected no diagnostic error and received `Copilot runtime diagnostics exceeded 4.5 seconds while starting the Copilot runtime.` This sessionless startup path does not exercise passive session flag mutations. Its ownership is not established, and no timeout, assertion, or unrelated policy/runtime behavior is changed here. Azure CI currently runs macOS ARM64 tests even with the macOS x64 build flag selected; no claim of macOS x64 CI validation is made.
- Trace-enabled latest head `b7dc7a58205`: `npm run transpile-client`, focused ESLint, `git diff --check`, commit hygiene, `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostE2EServerLease.test.ts` (7 passing), and `caffeinate -is npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --grep 'peer chat catalog and transcript survive a host restart|archiving a never-restored session'` (every provider passed) all passed.
- `caffeinate -is npm run test-agent-host-e2e` on `b7dc7a58205`: **840 passing / 109 existing pending**, all six entrypoints passed, 302.4 seconds.
- Latest-head [independent Code OSS run 37093841714](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37093841714): **fully green**, including Windows, Linux, and macOS Electron. Codex's peer-catalog/transcript restart test passed on Windows with the original response budget and assertions.

- This PR remains draft because the persistence fix is causally established, but the newly reported Codex restore delay and directory-removal failures still lack a proven root cause. Neither reproduced in the latest diagnostic execution, and cleanup did not reproduce in any of the six independent Windows Code OSS/Azure executions. These passes are not used to declare those failures harmless or fixed. The trace and raw filesystem-error improvements preserve the evidence needed on their next occurrence. The previous macOS diagnostics startup failure is also not claimed fixed by this passing validation.

pull_requests.title: agent Host: Reduce repeated scans when discovering external Copilot sessions
pull_requests.body:
## Problem
Addresses the reopened repro in #337848.

#338145 reduced SDK catalog scans when Agent Host fills in missing metadata for sessions it already knows about. It did not change background discovery of sessions created in the standalone Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, or legacy VS Code extension host.

The new repro identifies that discovery path: it repeatedly scanned roughly 5,000 SDK sessions to recheck a small set of candidates, including hundreds with unchanged incomplete metadata.

This PR reduces those background scans and waits for metadata changes where appropriate, while retaining a limited faster discovery path for newly created or newly ready sessions.

## What changes

- **Keep new sessions responsive.** Newly created or newly ready sessions can  trigger up to four discovery scans, spaced at least five seconds apart.  Existing history does not receive this fast-scan allowance.
- **Slow down repeated background work.** Other candidates can trigger a scan  no sooner than one minute after the previous successful scan. Persistent  failures gradually back off to hourly retries.
- **Wait for meaningful changes.** Sessions with incomplete markers or missing  working-directory/client metadata wait for their metadata files to change  rather than being retried indefinitely.
- **Preserve recovery.** File watchers and bounded background probes detect  later updates. Metadata written during a scan triggers a confirming retry  when needed, rather than leaving the session stuck waiting.

Legacy sessions with missing working directories still retry, since recreatinga deleted worktree does not necessarily change the watched metadata files.

This reduces how often discovery lists the full SDK catalog; it does not remove bulk listings or change the runtime's filesystem parallelism. Slow SDK calls and overflow probing can still delay when a new session appears.

## Validation

Unit tests (clear `COPILOT_HOME` if it is set in your shell, otherwise the agent tests read the real `~/.copilot/session-state`):

    npm run transpile-client
    scripts\test.bat --runGlob "**/agentHost/test/node/{copilotAgent,copilotChatDiscovery}.test.js"

Result: 518 passing.

New tests:
- an unresolved new session gets fast scans at 0/5/10/15/20 s, then falls back to 60 s;
- candidate retries back off past one minute (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 24 min);
- 160 ready, unlisted overflow sessions scan only at 0/60/120 s;
- metadata completed during a listing doesn't leave an overflow candidate waiting forever;
- recent sessions missing `cwd`/`clientName` list once, then publish after `workspace.yaml` changes.

Manual: with a large `~/.copilot/session-state`, check `agenthost.log`. `[CopilotDiscovery] Scan N started` should appear at most about once a minute when idle. There should be no repeated `failed to classify … Incomplete Copilot session marker` warnings. A new `copilot` CLI session should appear within a few seconds.

pull_requests.title: github: add cloud automations, tasks and environments domains
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
