pull_requests.title: Don't treat a failed GitHub session lookup as a sign-out
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9871

- Keep the current default account when refreshing it fails because the GitHub session lookup throws, for example `Canceled` while an extension host restart re-registers the authentication provider. Previously the error was handled like a sign-out.
- Keep the account's policy data and managed settings freshness with it, so a satisfied `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` gate stays satisfied instead of blocking AI and asking a signed-in user to "Sign in to continue".
- Only applies when an account is already known for the same authentication provider. Session removals still clear the account, "no matching session" is unchanged, and a failed lookup before any account is known still reports a missing token.
- Recovery uses the existing refresh triggers: the provider re-registering, window focus, and the account data poll.
- Add a regression test for a failed lookup with a satisfied refresh gate, and a test that the startup case still blocks with `noToken`.

Not in this PR: closing the gate's modal when the gate recovers, and offering **Retry** instead of **Sign In** when a session exists.

## How to test

Automated:

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/test/browser/defaultAccount.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/policies/test/browser/accountPolicyService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/policies/test/browser/accountPolicyGateContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/policies/test/browser/multiplexPolicyService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputModeValidation.test.ts`: 134 passing.
- Negative control: with the new branch disabled in the compiled output, `a failed session lookup keeps the signed-in account and satisfied refresh gate` fails with `account: undefined` and `failure: 'noToken'`.
- ESLint on both changed files: clean. `npm run typecheck-client`: no new errors compared to `main`.

Manual:

1. Sign in, then serve these managed settings with `npm run mock-policy-server` and run **Developer: Sync Account Policy**:
   `{ "forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": true, "telemetry": { "enabled": true, "endpoint": "http://localhost:4319" } }`
2. Run **Developer: Reload Window**. Copilot restarts the extension host to apply the telemetry policy (`[OTel] ... Restarting the extension host`).
3. If an account refresh lands during that restart, the window log shows `Attempt N to get sessions failed: Canceled`. Before this change, when all three attempts failed, the account was cleared and the "Sign in to continue" modal appeared. With this change the log shows `Keeping the current default account after the session lookup failed`, AI stays available, and no modal appears.

The race is timing dependent. Pausing the restarted extension host for a few seconds and running **Developer: Sync Account Policy** during the pause makes it reliable. I reproduced the bug this way on Insiders 1.141 (`de892dd1f99`) and checked the fix on a Code OSS build of this branch (below).

### Before / after

Both runs use the same Code OSS build of this branch, with the fix disabled in the compiled output for "before". `npm run mock-policy-server` served entitlements and `{ "forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": true }`. Copilot isn't built in this setup, so I restarted the extension host with **Developer: Restart Extension Host**, paused the new extension host for 10 seconds, and ran **Developer: Sync Account Policy** during the pause. The "Extension host did not start in 10 seconds" toast comes from that pause. Screenshots are cropped to the dialog and the window log.

**Before:** the lookup fails, the gate restricts AI, and the modal opens. The gate recovers when the extension host resumes (`state=inactive` at 14:27:20), but the modal stays open.

![Before: the "Sign in to continue" modal over the window log, which shows the failed lookup and the gate going from restricted to inactive](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/356b6a30-d667-4bcf-89cc-8ff27aef9ae7)

**After:** the lookup fails the same way (three `Canceled` attempts), then the log shows `Keeping the current default account after the session lookup failed`. The gate doesn't change and no modal opens. **Developer: Sync Account Policy** reports success because the kept account's managed settings are still fresh.

![After: no modal; the window log shows the failed lookups followed by "Keeping the current default account after the session lookup failed"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c29d3289-8b71-4ffb-a663-57c6ec36115d)

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Treating only session removals as a sign-out comes from the existing [`onDidChangeSessions` handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f1a93acac97b1eb31e725dc93e2b3e8829938905/src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/browser/defaultAccount.ts#L454-L476) ("only removal-only events represent an immediate sign-out").
- Keeping accepted policy through a transient failure follows the [managed settings fetch failure handling](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f1a93acac97b1eb31e725dc93e2b3e8829938905/src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/browser/defaultAccount.ts#L1252-L1254) from #337583 and the [same-scope refresh](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f1a93acac97b1eb31e725dc93e2b3e8829938905/src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/browser/defaultAccount.ts#L1198) from #338836.
- Recovery relies on the existing [provider re-registration refresh](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f1a93acac97b1eb31e725dc93e2b3e8829938905/src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/browser/defaultAccount.ts#L488-L495).
- The tests follow [`sign-out closes a satisfied native refresh gate`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f1a93acac97b1eb31e725dc93e2b3e8829938905/src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/test/browser/defaultAccount.test.ts#L1083) and [`reconciles a replacement without a signed-out gap and preserves removal-only behavior`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/f1a93acac97b1eb31e725dc93e2b3e8829938905/src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/test/browser/defaultAccount.test.ts#L1391).

pull_requests.title: fix: task provider counter bug
pull_requests.body:
This PR is needed for https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338231.
In task provider, there is some logic to check how many tasks are pending. The count gets increases when a new task list is being queried and decreased when the task list query finishes. When the task list query takes longer than 5 seconds, its marked as timed out and the count decreases also. This creates is a bug / edge case where when the task list query resolves after for example 6 seconds, the count accidentally decreases twice (once by timeout and once by the task list query resolving). The pr changes and moves the counting logic slightly to make a late task list query resolve decrease the count by only once.

pull_requests.title: sessions: Add guided model comparison setup for bakeoff
pull_requests.body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12239fbb-1659-4401-a1a8-db06ca736ee4



<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

A focused alternative to [eli/abo-redesign](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/eli/abo-redesign), keeping the guided Compare Agents experience without its subagent refactor, replacement results surface, or shared extension-host model-resolution changes.

### Guided comparison setup

- Replace the setup dialog with an experimental workflow inside the tabbed model picker: **Attempts -> optional Judge -> optional Synthesizer**.
- Run 2-10 distinct fixed models once each, or one fixed model 2-10 times. Auto/routing models are excluded.
- **Done** saves the setup in the composer; **Run N Attempts** launches it. Back/Next navigation preserves selections, and unavailable models invalidate the saved setup.
- Freeze the draft's workspace, branch, agent harness, execution mode, approval permissions, attachments, and supported model configuration into every participant. Permission and mode remain independent, so Interactive, Autopilot, and Plan drafts retain their selected approval level.
- Each selected model uses its effective saved or schema-default thinking/reasoning configuration. This picker does not currently expose per-role thinking-level overrides.
- Show the token warning immediately when hovering **Run N Attempts**.

### Attempts, Judge, and synthesis

- Keep the existing comparison grid and results surface. Attempts launch concurrently in isolated worktrees with stable participant identities.
- Add the default-on, opt-out setting `sessions.chat.compareAgents.openInGrid`. When enabled, open the grid before discarding the original draft so automatic draft creation cannot cancel navigation; when disabled, attempts start in the background.
- Make Judge and Synthesizer independently optional: attempts can run without review, and review can run without synthesis.
- Keep full Judge and synthesis instructions inline for reliable tool references. Present only their initial main-chat requests as collapsed **Judge Instructions** / **Synthesis Instructions** disclosures; the complete prompt remains available when expanded, copied, searched, edited, or read through Accessible View.
- Preserve recommended synthesis and optional additional instructions. Remove Custom Synthesis decisions, questions, per-attempt choices, and their tool/schema contracts.
- Ignore obsolete persisted custom-decision data while retaining additional instructions and existing synthesis participants. Legacy unversioned comparisons retain their previous Judge fallback; new comparisons do not infer one.

### Comparison group lifecycle

- Use the standard comparison-group **Mark All as Done** action and confirmation instead of a custom archive control.
- Automatically retire and remove only the generated comparison group after all of its participant sessions are archived.
- Make bulk Undo recreate that comparison group and restore membership without moving sessions that the user independently restored or assigned to another group.
- Leave ordinary and manually created groups unchanged, including unrelated empty groups.

### Scope

- Shared model-picker workflow and chat-request disclosure hooks are optional and inert for ordinary chat/model-picker callers.
- No subagent refactor, replacement results surface, custom-synthesis UI, or shared extension-host model-resolution workaround is included.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, enable `sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled` and `chat.experimentalModelPicker`.
2. Start a new Agent Host draft in a Git repository with at least one commit and a remote, using an agent that supports worktrees.
3. Select Interactive, Autopilot, or Plan and an approval-permission level. Open the model picker and activate **Compare Models**.
4. Select one model and adjust **Number of Runs**, or choose 2-10 distinct models. Confirm each selected model inherits its existing saved/default thinking level; changing thinking levels within this picker is not supported in this PR.
5. Optionally select a Judge and Synthesizer, use Back/Next to verify choices persist, choose **Done**, then hover and activate **Run N Attempts**.
6. Verify every participant inherits the draft's execution mode and approval permissions. With `sessions.chat.compareAgents.openInGrid` enabled, verify attempts open together; disable it and verify a new comparison starts without automatic navigation.
7. With a Judge, verify its full inline instructions are initially collapsed and review remains available. With a Synthesizer, verify recommended synthesis and additional instructions remain, but custom decision questions do not.
8. Use **Mark All as Done** on the comparison group. Verify the generated group is removed only after every participant is archived, then use Undo and verify the group and eligible membership return. Confirm an ordinary manual group is unaffected.

## Validation

- `npm run compile` - passed after rebasing onto main.
- Main focused regression suites - **882 passing, 1 pending**.
- Execution-mode and permission inheritance suites - **15 passing** across Interactive, Autopilot, and Plan with all three Copilot approval levels.
- Additional shared-boundary review suites - **346 passing** for ordinary model-picker behavior, normal input, chat list rendering, session-group archive actions, comparison summaries, and provider permission handling.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - passed.
- Targeted TypeScript type checking - passed.
- ESLint and repository formatter checks - passed for changed TypeScript files.
- `node build/stylelint.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chat.css` and targeted comparison CSS validation - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- Rendered and inspected light, dark, and high-contrast component fixtures, including eight Judge/synthesis disclosure fixtures with explicit collapsed-state assertions.
- Manually verified an existing four-attempt comparison in a 2x2 Code OSS grid and keyboard expansion/collapse with Enter and Space.
- A complete paid live-provider Judge/synthesis run was not performed.

<details>
<summary>Main focused regression command</summary>

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionComparisonService.test.ts
```

</details>

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

pull_requests.title: agent Host: Reduce redundant Git work in AH sessions
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Reduce Git overhead in Agent Host session preparation and checkpoint capture, particularly on Windows:

- **Skip unnecessary reviewed-ref deletion.** Enumerate existing refs and avoid deletion when none match. Add an optional strict lookup mode to distinguish an empty result from a failed lookup, preserving known-ref cleanup when enumeration fails.
- **Read branches concurrently.** Resolve the current and default branches in parallel after repository and HEAD validation, retaining existing fallbacks and retry behavior.
- **Deduplicate checkpoint captures by checkout root.** Process each checkout once per successful baseline, turn-start, or turn-end capture. Preserve retries after failures, fresh snapshots on later turns, and separate linked worktrees.

Adds regression coverage for concurrency, ref enumeration, duplicate captures, and failure recovery.

No changes to session identity, provider-startup ordering, checkpoint-before-mutation guarantees.

## Performance evidence
| Change in this PR | Performance evidence | Measurement scope |
|---|---|---|
| Skip reviewed-ref deletion when no refs exist | Windows: **222 → 174 ms**, saving **~49 ms** | Awaited idle-draft disposal, not total first-progress time |
| Read current and default branches concurrently | Windows: **182 → 139 ms**, saving **~43 ms** | Branch discovery; real-host runs also showed **~40–50 ms** less affected new-session preparation |
| Deduplicate checkpoint captures by checkout root | **63–399 ms saved on Windows**, **7–48 ms on Linux** | Turn-start checkpoint capture with an existing baseline, for multiple folders sharing one checkout |
| Same checkpoint deduplication change, measured through the real host | **1.7–2.1 s faster** new-session progress; **1.6–1.9 s faster** follow-ups | Send-to-first-meaningful protocol progress with three folders sharing one dirty checkout; new sessions run on a warm host |

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostCheckpointService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostReviewService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\shared\worktreeIsolation.test.ts` — **98 tests passed**.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Real-Git Windows/Linux probes verified captured trees, unchanged real indexes, and separate linked-worktree captures.
- Regression negative control confirmed that the original implementation fails the new duplicate-capture test.

pull_requests.title: extensions: keep update checks on polling cadence
pull_requests.body:
Do not reschedule the full installed-extension update check when an extension's auto-update delay expires. Clarify that delay expiry makes an update eligible rather than guaranteeing its installation time.

Addresses #339362 by keeping the UTD check cadence regular, not rescheduling to align immediately when an extension exits quarantine.  

Prior to that PR, the maximum delay for an auto-update was max(Cadence).  With that change and the alignment of 12-hr quarantine and 12-hr cadence, the maximum became max(Quarantine) - which would always be less than 2*max(Cadence).  The changes in this PR can cause the maximum delay between publish and auto-update to increase to max(Quarantine+Cadence), which could be as much as double, but maintains both the quarantine and the distributed rollout.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: avoid OTel file-export test batching race
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

Follow-up to #339315. Linux builds [479847](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=479847) and [479862](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=479862) exported Agent Host spans but failed to observe the required SDK spans within the file-export test's ten-second polling budget. The managed-policy tests passed.

### What changes

Set `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY=100` only in the file-export test's child environment. This keeps native SDK batching comfortably within the existing polling budget. Assertions, timeout, fixtures, managed-policy tests, and production configuration are unchanged.

### User impact and diagnosis

Users can encounter the same batching delay: completed spans are exported asynchronously, so traces may not appear immediately. The bundled SDK's first batch can take roughly ten seconds. That delay is not, by itself, evidence of dropped telemetry or a failed agent turn.

The test also waits only ten seconds, leaving essentially no scheduling margin. Polling is not the problem; racing the first batch with an equally short deadline is. Successful baseline runs took about eleven seconds overall, and captured span timestamps showed roughly ten seconds between span completion and file observation.

A deliberately slower inherited batch interval reproduces the same host-spans-only assertion failure; the child-only override makes that reproducer pass. This establishes a concrete failure mechanism, but official Azure validation is still needed before attributing both original CI failures conclusively to it.

### Validation

All commands below ran with the current bundled SDK `1.0.17-preview.0` / runtime `1.0.92-0`.

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `npx eslint src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotOtelAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY=10000 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotOtelAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'provider turn exports SDK spans'` — failed before the fix with missing SDK spans; passed after the fix in 611 ms on macOS.

Further container runs encountered dynamic-import failures before tests executed; those are not counted as passes.

Three Linux x64-only Azure CI repetitions were queued using the Azure DevOps CLI, all pinned to `6a2261b615a9f6997539e30d9c5883b03bc8c0ae` on `rwoll/fix-otel-file-export-ci`:

The same cases are now integration tests in `extensions/github/src/test/github.test.ts`, run locally in VS Code; the github suite isn't in `.vscode-test.js` or `scripts/test-integration.sh`, so CI type-checks and lints them but doesn't run them. tsc, eslint and the hygiene check pass.

## Scope

This changes diagnostics, not policy enforcement, harness selection, or existing conversations. It creates no chat session, executes no policy helper, and does not include session-local client-injected settings.

Normal runtime cache behavior is unchanged. The report preserves cache/source warnings, but a returned snapshot alone is not proof of a fresh server fetch or end-to-end enforcement.

pull_requests.title: Simplify background shell reconciliation
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follow-up to #339220.

- Replace shell task-read counters with a snapshot of shell IDs and their originating tool calls, captured before requesting the task list. Reconcile only the same executions, leaving shells started or replaced during the request untouched.
- Keep the shared task-list request, SDK task types, and running/idle filtering in the session. The terminal helper reconciles captured executions synchronously, without owning the request or returning unrelated tasks.
- Preserve reconciliation before the stale-publication guard. Superseded responses can still settle shells without publishing stale background work.
- Move shell-helper completion handling before result-content construction, outside the PTY-rendering block.
- Keep this to two implementation files and two test files. Synchronous helper tests cover shell-ID reuse and prior completion; gated session tests cover capture-before-read and running/idle filtering. No UI, SDK, protocol, or settings changes.

### Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --reporter dot`: 834 passing.

2. Repeat with `read_bash` waiting for completion. Verify the terminal exits with the reported exit code and the shell leaves the background list.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Capture-before-await and execution-identity checks follow the existing [subagent activity-revision snapshot](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/dcb81648f8a8f1863d2577f8fec98e805e5f95a0/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L1947-L1976).

pull_requests.title: chat: Enrich reference previews and add pill context copying
pull_requests.body:
GitHub issues and PRs recorded as References currently show only their URLs on hover. This adds rich previews and useful list titles without changing the authored-artifact versus related-reference categorization introduced in #337923.

### Changes

- Share on-demand GitHub metadata resolution between Agents and editor chat. Opening References prefetches core metadata for the first five eligible entries; subsequent visible rows resolve as the list scrolls. PR checks are requested when their detailed hover is opened. References do not gain background polling or invoke a model.
- Show explicit loading text, use resolved titles in the list, and show the URL fallback only after resolution fails. Preserve pending hover intent while asynchronous metadata replaces rows, including image references.
- Offer existing copy actions alongside removal in single-item pill context menus, including URL, full-path, and relative-path copying. Copy does not require removal support; collections retain per-row actions. Document the interaction in accessibility help.
- Consolidate reference fixtures into Single, Collections, and Mixed. They use the real pill/dropdown/hover interactions and safe in-memory actions; headless captures show PR, long-title issue, and commit previews rather than resting pills alone.

### Testing

1. In Component Explorer, open `sessions/chatReferences/Single`. Hover a PR or issue; right-click it or press Shift+F10 and copy its URL. Right-click the file pill and try Copy Path and Copy Relative Path. The fixture status line reports the copied value.
2. Open Collections. Open the PR and issue dropdowns and hover different rows. Only one detail card should appear. Remove an item and verify the collection becomes a single pill. Collection-level context menus should not offer an ambiguous per-item copy action.
3. Open Mixed. GitHub references should gain their titles and rich previews while remaining in References. Enter the image row immediately after opening the dropdown: its preview should still appear when pending metadata completes. Check the website, settings, ADO, file, and commit actions.
4. With a signed-in GitHub account, repeat with real reference-only issues/PRs in Agents and editor chat. Verify only the initial eligible batch is prefetched, scrolling resolves further visible entries, and reopening a resolved hover reuses metadata. Check the failed-request fallback and loading presentation on retry.
5. Verify authored items remain dedicated pills and reference-only items are not promoted. Hiding AI features should continue to hide the existing chat surfaces; this adds no new setting or independent entry point.

Local validation passed: client compilation, the focused reference/menu/accessibility unit suites, targeted lint, and headless interaction checks. Expanded Dark/Light fixture captures were error-free and byte-identical after remounting.

### Visual evidence

The [Screenshots & Tests report](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339342#issuecomment-5958803939) contains the component-fixture comparison.

pull_requests.title: mcp: fix customization migration in multi-root workspaces
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

- Same-named `.vscode/mcp.json` servers in other workspace folders are never registered because the client resolves duplicate names by precedence, so the migration plan never saw the shadowed entries and a session scoped to a shadowed folder was offered nothing. Shadowed servers are now assessed with their resolved configuration so every folder's entries can be offered.
- Each workspace folder migrates into its own `.mcp.json`, so a matching server name in another folder cannot overwrite anything. The cross-root conflict guard rejected these migrations and asked users to rename servers; it is removed, and conflicts within the same destination are still rejected.
- Removing the only remaining property of a JSON object left a dangling trailing comma. Migrating every server out of a `.vscode/mcp.json` that ends with a trailing comma produced invalid JSON, failed verification, and was reported as a rollback failure. `setProperty` now removes that comma, as it already did for arrays.
- The disabled state of migrated servers was keyed by the session's root order rather than the workspace folder index that identifies root `.mcp.json` servers, so it could be applied to another folder's server.

Fixes #337097
Fixes #335884

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

### How to test

Automated:

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/common/jsonEdit.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/mcpServerCustomizationMigration.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMigrationServiceImpl.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMigration.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostMcpServerSupport.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts`: passed (207 passing).

Manual:

1. Set `chat.customizations.mcpServerMigration.enabled`, `chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled`, and `"chat.mcp.access": "all"`.
2. Open a multi-root workspace where two folders define the same server names in `.vscode/mcp.json`, with a trailing comma after the last entry.
3. Start a new Copilot CLI Agent Host session and open **Chat: Open Customizations** → **Migrations** → **Migrate MCP Servers**.
4. Every folder's servers are offered. Migrating moves each into its own folder's `.mcp.json` and removes it from `.vscode/mcp.json`, without a cross-root conflict or rollback error.

pull_requests.title: fix: guard multi-diff item clearBinding against re-entrant disposal (fixes #339312)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary The multi-diff editor throws `BugIndicatingError: Cannot unbind a diff editor template from a different item` when a `ManagedVirtualizedItem` disposes a binding. Clearing a binding synchronously disposes the diff editor, which fires editor model-change events that drive the item's own `autorun`; that autorun re-enters `_clearBinding()` and disposes the same binding a second time, so `unbind()` finds `_viewModel` already cleared (`undefined !== item`) and throws. Impact: unhandled error surfaced to telemetry when closing/switching multi-diff editors (e.g. the Agent Sessions diff view) on all platforms. Fixes microsoft/vscode#339312 Recommended reviewer: ``@hediet`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`10de1b93436`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/10de1b93436) | | Author | ``@hediet`` | | PR | n/a | | Message | Refactor multi-diff virtualized scrolling | | Why | This change introduced the `ManagedVirtualizedItem` lifecycle where `_clearBinding()` disposes a binding whose `dispose()` synchronously re-enters the same item's `autorun` via editor events; the clear path has no re-entrancy guard, so the nested dispose runs against already-cleared state. Subsequent commits (`98e228b47bc`, `519f5fa46f0`) refined the same lifecycle but kept the re-entrant clear path. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Autorun as ManagedVirtualizedItem.autorun participant Clear as _clearBinding() participant Binding as DiffEditorItemBinding.dispose() participant Unbind as DiffEditorItemTemplate.unbind()/setItem() participant Editor as DiffEditor events Autorun->>Clear: item hidden, not kept alive Note over Clear: ⚠️ Root cause:
no re-entrancy guard Clear->>Binding: binding.dispose() Binding->>Unbind: _template.unbind(item) (before super.dispose) Note over Unbind: setItem(undefined)
_viewModel = undefined
editor.setDiffModel(null) Unbind->>Editor: synchronous model-change event Editor->>Autorun: re-enters autorun Autorun->>Clear: _clearBinding() again Clear->>Binding: binding.dispose() again Binding->>Unbind: unbind(item) Note over Unbind: 💥 _viewModel (undefined) !== item
Cannot unbind a diff editor template from a different item ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/diffEditorItemTemplate.ts` | crash site | L539 (from stack): `throw new BugIndicatingError('Cannot unbind a diff editor template from a different item')` | | `src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/diffEditorItemTemplate.ts` | re-entrant trigger | L592-L593: `dispose()` calls `this._template.unbind(this.item)` before `super.dispose()`, so `currentBinding`/`_store` are still live; `unbind` → `setItem(undefined)` fires editor events synchronously | | `src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/virtualizedItemManager.ts` | root cause (producer) | L228-L247: `_clearBinding()` disposes the binding with no guard; the autorun at L149-L155 re-enters it during that synchronous dispose | ### Repro Steps This is a timing-dependent re-entrancy, reproduced by closing/hiding a multi-diff item whose diff editor fires a synchronous model-change event during disposal. 1. Open a multi-diff editor (e.g. a source-control / Agent Sessions diff view) with at least one visible diff item that has loaded its diff model. 2. Trigger disposal of a bound, visible item — close the editor, switch the active editor, or scroll the item out while it is being cleared. 3. During `_clearBinding()`, `binding.dispose()` → `unbind()` → `setItem(undefined)` → `editor.setDiffModel(null)` fires an editor event that re-enters the item's `autorun`, calling `_clearBinding()` a second time on the same binding. 4. The nested `unbind()` sees `_viewModel === undefined`, `undefined !== item`, and throws `BugIndicatingError`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/browser/widget/multiDiffEditor/virtualizedItemManager.ts`, `ManagedVirtualizedItem._clearBinding()`: add an `_isClearingBinding` guard flag. On entry, if a clear is already in progress the method returns immediately; otherwise it sets the flag, performs the unbind/dispose/reset sequence inside a `try`, and resets the flag in `finally`. This fixes the bug at the data producer — the clear path that initiates the re-entrant disposal — rather than at the crash site. The outer `_clearBinding()` invocation still completes the full clear atomically (it sets `_templateReference` to `undefined` and disposes the reference after the binding dispose returns), so the nested call being a no-op does not leave the item half-cleared. The throw inside `unbind()` is preserved as a genuine invariant check for other callers; it is simply no longer reached on this re-entrant path because the duplicate dispose never starts. **Why this is correct**: the guard makes the unsupported "dispose during dispose" ordering unrepresentable at the producer, which is the lifecycle-fix priority (reorder/serialize the producer's state mutations), instead of teaching the consumer `unbind()` to tolerate inconsistent state. No `logService.error` or telemetry path is removed, and no `try/catch` swallows the error. **Alternatives considered**: - Guard inside `unbind()` / `DiffEditorItemBinding.dispose()` by comparing `_viewModel` and returning early — rejected: that is a crash-site guard that silently tolerates double-dispose and would mask the same re-entrancy for every other binding type, hiding the producer bug. - Defer `editor.setDiffModel(null)` to a microtask so events do not fire synchronously — rejected: broader behavioral change to editor teardown timing with higher regression risk than serializing the clear. ### Recommended Owner ``@hediet`` — author of the multi-diff virtualization refactor (`10de1b93436`) and the follow-up lifecycle fixes; active `microsoft/vscode` core team member (write access, multiple commits in the last 90 days).

pull_requests.title: fix: guard webview find against disposed frame subtree (fixes #339314)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary `WebviewMainService.getFrameByName` (electron-main) reads `getWebContents(id).mainFrame.framesInSubtree.find(...)` unconditionally. When a find / stop-find IPC request is handled against a webContents whose render frame has already been torn down (window closed, navigated away, or detached editor window disposed), `mainFrame.framesInSubtree` is `undefined`, so `.find(...)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')` in the main process. This new-in-1.140.0 bucket affects 566 users / 736 hits across Mac, Windows, and Linux. Fixes microsoft/vscode#339314 Recommended reviewer: ``@dmitrivMS`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`9cc2a44b`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9cc2a44bf20ac6f4badef53bc9f33dfdb5803378) | | Author | ``@dmitrivMS`` | | PR | #337403 | | Message | webview: Fix find in detached editor windows (#337403) | | Why | The commit reworked `getFrameByName` to resolve the frame via the shared `getWebContents(id)` helper and routes stop-find/find requests through auxiliary web-contents IDs (detached editor windows) as well as main window IDs. This widened the set of webContents the find path runs against — including auxiliary/detached contents that can be disposed between request and handling — so `mainFrame.framesInSubtree` can now be `undefined` at the dereference, which the prior window-only path did not expose. Verified ancestor of shipped commit `07f806f9` (first appears in `1.140.0~389`, matching the "new in 1.140.0" anomaly). | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Renderer as Webview (renderer) participant IPC as ipcMain / ChannelServer participant Service as WebviewMainService participant Electron as Electron WebContents Renderer->>IPC: stopFindInFrame(id, frameName) IPC->>Service: call stopFindInFrame Service->>Service: getFrameByName(id, frameName) Note over Electron: ⚠️ Root cause:
render frame already disposed,
framesInSubtree is undefined Service->>Electron: getWebContents(id).mainFrame.framesInSubtree Note over Service: 💥 TypeError: Cannot read
properties of undefined (reading 'find') ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/platform/webview/electron-main/webviewMainService.ts` | crash site & fix | L96 (from stack): `getWebContents(id).mainFrame.framesInSubtree.find(...)` dereferences `undefined` when the webContents' render frame is disposed | ### Repro Steps The error is a timing-dependent race on the main process; it fires when a stop-find/find reply is handled after the target render frame is gone: 1. Open a webview-backed editor (e.g. Markdown preview, Simple Browser, or a detached editor window) and start Find (Cmd/Ctrl+F) inside it. 2. Close the webview / window (or navigate it away) while a find or stop-find request is in flight. 3. The in-flight `stopFindInFrame` / `findInFrame` IPC call reaches `getFrameByName`, whose `webContents.mainFrame.framesInSubtree` is now `undefined`, throwing the `TypeError`. - Detached editor windows (added in #337403) increase the likelihood because stop-find is now routed through auxiliary web-contents IDs that are disposed independently of the main window. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `webviewMainService.ts` → `getFrameByName()`: the producer of the invalid state is Electron's render-frame disposal, which lives outside `microsoft/vscode` and cannot be reordered or awaited, so a consumer-side guard at this external boundary is the correct fix. `getFrameByName` now returns `WebFrameMain | undefined`: it checks `contents.isDestroyed()` and `contents.mainFrame?.framesInSubtree` before calling `.find(...)`, returning `undefined` when the frame subtree is gone. The two callers (`findInFrame`, `stopFindInFrame`) already treat a missing frame as a no-op, so they early-return on `undefined`. This mirrors the existing disposed-frame guards already in this codebase: the `contents.isDestroyed()` check in `setIgnoreMenuShortcuts` (same file) and the `frame.isDestroyed()` guard in `app.ts`'s `isSafeFrame`. The genuine `Unknown frame` throw is deliberately preserved for the live-frame case (a real frame subtree that does not contain the named frame), so the error-telemetry pipeline still surfaces that distinct, actionable condition — only the disposed-webContents undefined read is suppressed. **Alternatives considered**: adding `?.`/`try/catch` directly at the crash-site `.find(...)` was rejected because it would also swallow the meaningful `Unknown frame` signal and does not express *why* the value is absent; guarding explicitly on `isDestroyed()` / missing subtree keeps the disposed-frame no-op distinct from the live-frame "frame not found" error. ### Recommended Owner ``@dmitrivMS`` — author of the culprit commit #337403 and an active `microsoft/vscode` team member (238 commits in the last 90 days), who owns the webview find-in-frame routing changed by that PR.

pull_requests.title: fix: guard terminal scroll operations before renderer is attached (fixes #339313)
pull_requests.body:
### Summary `TerminalInstance.sendText()` (reached via `runCommand`) calls `this.xterm?.scrollToBottom()`, which forwards to `XtermTerminal.scrollToBottom()` → bundled xterm.js `scrollToBottom` → `scrollLines` → `get dimensions`. When this runs against a terminal whose renderer has not been initialized yet (the xterm instance exists but `attachToElement`/`raw.open()` has not run, so the render service and its `dimensions` object do not exist), xterm.js throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'dimensions')`. 389 users / 448 hits across Windows, Mac, and Linux on 1.140.0. Fixes microsoft/vscode#339313 Recommended reviewer: ``@meganrogge`` ### Culprit Commit No single culprit commit — this is a **pre-existing latent race** that surfaced as a new stable bucket in 1.140.0. The entry path `sendText → scrollToBottom` (`terminalInstance.ts` line, authored 2022) and the `XtermTerminal.scrollToBottom` wrapper (authored 2021) both long predate the baseline, and `git blame` on the throwing call sites points to commits years older than the regression window. The anomaly is a timing/re-bucketing shift (bundled xterm.js scroll internals), not a logic change in a commit within the 1.139.1→1.140.0 range. | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — pre-existing | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | The crash path exists since 2021–2022; no commit in the regression window changes the triggering logic. Treated as a pre-existing boundary race. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller as runCommand / sendText participant Inst as TerminalInstance participant Xterm as XtermTerminal participant Raw as xterm.js (bundled) Caller->>Inst: sendText(text, shouldExecute) Inst->>Xterm: this.xterm?.scrollToBottom() Note over Xterm: ⚠️ Boundary: renderer not
yet initialized (no attachToElement) Xterm->>Raw: this.raw.scrollToBottom() Raw->>Raw: scrollLines() -> get dimensions Note over Raw: 💥 TypeError: Cannot read
properties of undefined (reading 'dimensions') ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `node_modules/@xterm/xterm/lib/xterm.js` | crash site | `get dimensions` (from stack) — bundled third-party, unmodifiable | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/xterm/xtermTerminal.ts` | boundary / fix site | L767-L768: `scrollToBottom(): void { this.raw.scrollToBottom(); }` delegates straight into xterm.js with no attach guard | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts` | trigger | L1422: `this.xterm?.scrollToBottom();` inside `sendText`, which can run before the instance is attached to the DOM | ### Repro Steps This is a timing-dependent race, so it is non-deterministic: 1. Trigger `sendText`/`runCommand` on a `TerminalInstance` whose xterm object has been created but not yet attached to the DOM (`attachToElement` / `raw.open()` not yet called) — e.g. programmatic command execution against a backgrounded or just-created terminal, or a restart that re-creates the xterm before re-attaching. 2. `sendText` reaches `this.xterm?.scrollToBottom()`. 3. xterm.js walks `scrollToBottom → scrollLines → get dimensions` and dereferences the render service's `dimensions`, which is `undefined` because the renderer was never opened. 4. `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'dimensions')` is thrown. Increase likelihood by executing commands against terminals immediately on creation or during a restart, before layout/attach completes. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/xterm/xtermTerminal.ts`): Add an early-return guard `if (!this._attached) { return; }` to the renderer-delegating scroll wrappers (`scrollToBottom`, `scrollUpLine`, `scrollDownLine`, `scrollUpPage`, `scrollDownPage`, `scrollToTop`). `_attached` is set only after `attachToElement` runs `this.raw.open(container)` — the exact point at which xterm.js constructs its render service and the `dimensions` object the throwing code reads. The producer of the violating value is bundled third-party xterm.js, which cannot be modified in this repo, so the fix is placed at VS Code's own boundary wrapper and gated on the real lifecycle signal (`_attached`) rather than suppressing the symptom at the crash site. Scrolling a terminal that has no renderer yet is a no-op anyway, so the guard changes no user-visible behavior. The guard is not a `try/catch` and does not touch any `logService.error` path. **Alternatives considered**: - Wrapping the `scrollToBottom` call in `terminalInstance.sendText` in `try/catch` — rejected because it hides the error from telemetry instead of preventing the invalid lifecycle call, and would mask other legitimate failures. - Optional-chaining into xterm.js internals (`this.raw.scrollToBottom?.()`) — rejected because the method is always callable; the undefined value is deep inside xterm.js's render service, unreachable from the wrapper, so chaining would not prevent the throw. ### Recommended Owner ``@meganrogge`` — terminal area owner; authored the `sendText → scrollToBottom` call path and is an active core maintainer with write access (commits within the last 90 days).

pull_requests.body:

## Summary

Fixes a regression introduced by #339034: client-side schema filtering dropped settings-derived worktree configuration because the host marks these properties `readOnly`. In particular, `git.worktreeSymlinkFolders` stopped reaching the host, so folders such as `node_modules` were no longer symlinked into new worktrees.

- Ignore `readOnly` in session config validation/filtering and in the pre-send settings refresh. Pickers still honor `readOnly` for UI editability; advertised-key, enum, and session-mutability checks remain unchanged.
- Restore forwarding of branch prefixes, included files, symlink folders, branch tracking, and the create-new-branch option.
- Match the provider test schema to the real host and cover creation, resolution, folder-settings refresh/clearing, programmatic worktree configuration, and read-only mutable values such as shell initialization scripts.
- Update workbench tests to expect read-only values to remain in resolution and completion payloads.

pull_requests.title: chat: preserve request-start context on terminal telemetry
pull_requests.body:
## Why

Comparing Local (extension-host) and Agent Host request failure rates currently requires joining the workbench's terminal outcomes to provider telemetry to recover SKU and BYOK context. Requests that fail before a model response can be lost from that join, biasing the comparison.

This adds request-start context to `interactiveSessionProviderInvoked`, so supported outcomes can be grouped by the workbench's Copilot SKU and selected model source without depending on a model-response event.

Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9798.

## What changes for reporting

| Example | Before | With this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A known Copilot selection fails before a model response | A query requiring provider telemetry can drop the failure | The outcome carries the known request-start SKU and `selectedModelSource=copilot` |
| A selected BYOK model disappears during the request | The completion-time model lookup can be empty | `selectedModelSource=byok` remains available |
| The user's entitlement changes during a request | Joining to later account state can misattribute the request | `requestStartCopilotSku` retains the workbench entitlement known at request start |
| No model or entitlement is resolved when the request starts | Missing data can be mistaken for first-party/default usage | Source is explicitly `unknown`; absent SKU remains absent |

The presence of `selectedModelSource` identifies enriched rows; its explicit `unknown` value is distinct from absence on older events.

The source is a bounded selection category (`copilot`, `byok`, `other`, `unknown`), not the actual model/provider chosen by Auto, HydraFusion, or a fallback. Host Copilot models use the registered session provider; BYOK bridge metadata takes precedence. Custom vendor names and bridge identifiers are not added to telemetry.

Known non-Copilot session providers are `other`; unresolved session providers remain `unknown`. A model's picker restriction to a session type does not by itself make its provider unknown. Neither `other` nor `unknown` establishes non-BYOK credentials.

## Compatibility and scope

Existing queries keep the same event names, row counts, IDs, results, and legacy `model` lookup semantics. This is additive enrichment, not deduplication at the producer. A failed invocation followed by a retry still emits the existing outcomes.

The SKU belongs to the workbench account, not necessarily the remote host's credential. Missing context is never backfilled from later state. The change does not add execution IDs, retry provenance, accepted-start coverage, or the planned distinction between internal errors and user-facing interruptions.

The checked-in contract document describes the fields, examples, and rollout/query limitations.

## Manual verification

Exercised the initial implementation in an isolated, authenticated Windows Code OSS profile with development logging-only telemetry (before the review follow-ups for empty BYOK identifiers, removal of the redundant context-version field, and known non-Copilot provider classification):

- Local and Copilot Agent Host success and cancellation.
- Local Retry, plus a catalog-known BYOK request and Retry against a loopback endpoint returning HTTP 400 before any successful model response.
- A real Claude Agent Host completion classified as `unknown` in the initial implementation. The review follow-up now classifies registered non-Copilot providers as `other`, covered by focused tests rather than a repeat of this live scenario.
- Model/session switching, reload and history restoration, and file create/edit/save/reopen.

The final run produced eight outcomes across eight distinct requests: four successes, two cancellations, and two `errorWithOutput` outcomes. All eight carried the populated `requestStartCopilotSku`; selected-model source matched each case. Reload/history navigation added no duplicate outcomes.

An initial run used stale emitted JavaScript; those thirteen rows were discarded as validation evidence. The scenarios above were repeated after transpilation and reload. Opening the Copilot dashboard resolved the initially unavailable workbench entitlement without injecting a SKU.

Limitations: this validates local logging, not production ingestion or deployed scorecard schemas. The observed Copilot AH UI had no equivalent Retry button; no same-ID AH resume was claimed as a live test. Unrelated runtime observations included a diff-editor disposed-model error, a ResizeObserver-loop warning, and a restored mode-picker mismatch; none was established as caused by this telemetry-only change.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: log sandbox connection failures and milestones
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Add concise, ordinary `ILogService` records to diagnose cloud sandbox startup timeouts and HTTP connection failures without requiring the connection diagnostics buffer or AHP payload logging.

- Log validated `X-GitHub-Request-Id` values, environment/session/client IDs, HTTP status, elapsed time, and retry guidance for failed connect/reconnect requests. Preserve status and pacing while excluding response bodies and arbitrary headers.
- Record relay readiness, the first publish acknowledgment and host frame, AHP initialization identity/completion, and connection failure stages. Closing summaries include outstanding acknowledgments and receive/error counts without credentials or payloads.
- Bound repeated recoverable warnings while always logging failures that close the relay. Add regression coverage and document the log correlation workflow.

Timeout, retry, and reconnect behavior remains unchanged. This improves troubleshooting; it does not fix the underlying sandbox startup failure or change the startup watchdog.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed, zero compilation errors.
- Targeted unit tests — passed, **365 tests**:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts
```

- Targeted ESLint — passed, eight changed TypeScript files:

pull_requests.title: docs: add CI artifact testing skill
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #339239
Fixes #339287
Fixes #339303

If the extension host couldn't find the selected model (e.g. a BYOK / custom endpoint model), the request silently fell back to the default model (Auto), so a different model answered and billed it while the picker still showed the user's choice.

- **Core:** if the selected model can't be found, chat requests and model-backed tool invocations now fail with an error instead of falling back. Requests with no model selected still use the default.
- **BYOK:** providers come back when a Copilot token arrives after a failed fetch. Before, they stayed unregistered until the next account change or reload. The unregister log now says whether policy or a missing token caused it.
- **Auth:** a Copilot token fetch that finishes after you switch to another account on the same provider is now rejected instead of being used for the new account, so the BYOK listener can't apply the wrong account's policy.

Related: #326554 (providers in another extension host now show an error instead of being rerouted).

pull_requests.body: ## Summary Fix a phone new-session composer regression exposed when Compare Agents made the existing harness picker reachable with only one available harness. ### What broke and why Compare Agents adds `Run and Compare Agents...` inside the existing harness picker; it does not add a standalone lane action. To keep that action reachable when only one harness is available, the existing harness picker remains active instead of becoming disabled. This exposed the `Copilot` harness chip alongside the repository, worktree, and branch controls. The phone composer intentionally keeps those controls expanded and lets the lane scroll horizontally. The intrinsically sized lane could become wider than the phone viewport while still being centered and clipped. On an actual phone this caused: - the leading repository and trailing harness controls to be cut off - the repository separator to render as an unexplained empty square - desktop responsive compaction to collapse the separate `Manual permissions` control in some setting combinations The existing screenshots did not catch this because several "phone" fixtures only used a phone-sized viewport while explicitly disabling `IChatPhoneInputPresenter`. They therefore rendered desktop-style controls rather than the real phone composition. ### What changed - keep standard phone control lanes at their natural width and horizontally scrollable - disable desktop picker compaction for phone scroll lanes and restore expanded controls - hide the repository separator on phone - constrain the experimental workspace/worktree/branch/harness tray to the composer width - keep the phone picker search focus on its rounded field - align the send action with the other composer actions - keep welcome phrases grouped with the centered new-session hero - preserve the standard active-chat phone composer, with Local and permissions in the secondary toolbar - run every phone screenshot fixture through the real phone presenter and phone context - use a deterministic welcome phrase so the blocking screenshot is stable The final diff was audited after removing superseded active-composer logic, unused fixture customization hooks, and formatting-only changes. pull_requests.title: agentHost: Add controllable inter-session messages
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Fixes #335540.

This adds explicit same-host inter-session message control to the Agent Host `send_message` tool:

- `send` with `delivery: "queue"` creates a separate turn, starting immediately when idle or waiting while the target is busy.
- `send` with `delivery: "steer"` updates an active target turn and is handed to the provider immediately.
- `replace` and `cancel` operate on an owned queued message while it is still pending, using a stable host-generated `messageId` and optimistic `expectedRevision`.
- `get_session_context` reports messages sent by the calling chat, including their delivery mode, lifecycle status, ID, and revision.

Steering is reported as `processing` and cannot be replaced or cancelled after dispatch because providers do not offer reliable retraction. Queued mutations require exact source-chat ownership and revision matching. User edits invalidate agent mutation ownership so a stale agent cannot overwrite them.

The queue-drain contribution now observes server-dispatched pending-message actions, allowing agent-generated steering to reach the provider without forwarding client steering twice. Provider steering cleanup only synchronizes pending state and cannot start queued work after the user stops a turn.

The atomic mutation contract is intentionally limited to chats on the same Agent Host. Pending messages remain in-memory across a full host restart.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionServerTools.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/chatContributions.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSideEffects.test.ts` — 469 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionServerTools.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/chatContributions.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts --grep 'steers explicitly|returns only pending messages|does not consume queued work|round-trips queued agent provenance'` — 4 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <8 touched TypeScript source/test files>` — passed.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts` — 24 passing in strict replay.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Manual Code OSS validation verified real-provider steering consumption, queued delivery and draining, pending replacement with revision increment, pending cancellation, processing cancellation refusal, and idle steering rejection.

An additional combined unit run completed with 1,039 passing and two unrelated local-environment failures in attachment tests whose expected `/home/test-user` path differed from the macOS home path.

pull_requests.title: tasks: set Task terminal type on CustomExecution launch config
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338610

### Cause
When launching a `CustomExecution` task, `TerminalTaskSystem._createTerminal` constructed the terminal launch configuration with `isFeatureTerminal: true`, but omitted `type: TaskTerminalType` (`'Task'`), unlike `Shell` and `Process` tasks.

Because `MainThreadTerminalShellIntegration` checks `instance.shellLaunchConfig.type !== 'Task'` to determine whether a terminal supports the `executeCommand` API, `CustomExecution` task terminals were reported as supporting it, bypassing the guard introduced in #275667 / #275782 and allowing command text to be sent as input into the task terminal.

### Solution
Set `type: TaskTerminalType` on the `CustomExecution` launch configuration in `terminalTaskSystem.ts`, matching `Shell` and `Process` tasks. Added regression tests verifying that task terminals notify the extension host that `executeCommand` is unsupported, and that `InternalTerminalShellIntegration.executeCommand` throws accordingly.

pull_requests.title: git: clear blame state when focusing editor outside repository
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #314754

### Cause
When switching focus to an editor whose document does not belong to a Git repository, `GitBlameController._updateTextEditorBlameInformation` returned early without clearing `this.textEditorBlameInformation`. In parallel, `GitBlameEditorDecoration._onDidChangeActiveTextEditor` cleared decorations on visible editors that were not active.

When refocusing the Git-tracked editor on the same line, `_updateTextEditorBlameInformation` computed the blame and assigned it to `this.textEditorBlameInformation`. Because `this._textEditorBlameInformation` was never reset when focus switched away, `isResourceBlameInformationEqual` evaluated to `true`, suppressing `this._onDidChangeBlameInformation.fire()`. As a result, inline decorations were not redrawn on the refocused editor until the selection changed.

### Changes
In `extensions/git/src/blame.ts`:
- Reset `this.textEditorBlameInformation = undefined` when the active editor lacks `diffInformation`, lacks a repository / `HEAD` commit, or when blame cannot be retrieved.
- Check if the editor is still the active editor after awaiting `_getBlameInformation`.

### Verification Steps
1. Open a Git-tracked file with inline blame enabled (`git.blame.editorDecoration.enabled: true`).

pull_requests.title: test: Align Node unit test timeouts with Electron
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

The Node test entry point creates its own Mocha instance, so the `--timeout=5000` passed to the outer Mocha CLI did not configure the tests it runs. They instead inherited Mocha's 2-second default.

- Match the Electron runner's defaults: 5 seconds locally and 30 seconds in Azure/GitHub CI.
- Forward explicit `--timeout` / `-t` options to the actual runner, including `0` to disable timeouts.
- Remove the npm script's fixed timeout so it does not override the CI default.
- Document the defaults and overrides. Explicit suite/test timeouts remain unchanged.

Motivated by the 2-second bootstrap timeout in [build 479318](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=479318). This fixes the shared runner configuration rather than adding individual timeout overrides.

On Windows with the repository's downloaded Node binary:

- `& '.\.build\node\v24.20.0\win32-x64\node.exe' node_modules\mocha\bin\mocha.js test\unit\node\index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit --run src\vs\base\test\common\async.test.ts` — **passed: 148 tests, 2 pending**.
- `& '.\.build\node\v24.20.0\win32-x64\node.exe' --check test\unit\node\index.js` — **passed**.

pull_requests.title: github: extract governed discovery and model control service
pull_requests.body:
**Hold for the next milestone: do not merge until the release branch has been created.**

This is the deferred Copilot portion split out of #339208. It is a sibling of HTTP follow-up #339227, not a prerequisite for it.

```text
main
  └─ #339208 GitHub/common infrastructure
       ├─ #339227 HTTP quota fixes — can land before the release branch
       └─ this PR: Copilot extraction — held until the next milestone
```

## Scope

- Move the existing Agent Host Copilot API implementation into `platform/github/common/copilotApiService.ts`, with a thin Agent Host binding and direct consumer imports.
- Route `/copilot_internal/user` through an explicit-credential GitHub bootstrap client, without an extra `/user` lookup, account selection or dependency on accepted-token publication.
- Govern CAPI model reads separately from GitHub quota: bounded admission/body/waiter limits, independent cancellation, credential-specific coalescing, cooldowns and one transient GET retry.
- Preserve existing inference/streaming behavior and Copilot protocol headers/errors.
- Preserve the reviewed authentication-lifecycle fixes: rejected/superseded unpublished credentials discard cached discovery, captured metadata and active model reads without disturbing a credential still retained elsewhere.
- Preserve explicit malformed-JSON errors, domain-local cooldown policy and the author's confirmed host/account quota-sharing decision.

The reusable types, queue, scheduler, cooldown storage, response readers, waiter ownership and control transport are already in #339208. This PR contains the service extraction, hosting/authentication integration, related tests, SDK typing/Monaco scope adjustments and migration documentation.

## Release and integration order

1. Land #339208 independently; its production Agent Host/Copilot implementation and wiring are unchanged from main.
2. Land #339227 independently.
3. After branching for the next milestone, rebase this PR onto main with the landed HTTP fixes before merging or rolling out governed Copilot discovery.

The two Copilot-specific HTTP regression cases are preserved in the old full-stack backup and were rerun with both siblings applied. Carry them into this PR when rebasing after #339227 lands; the pure sibling does not include the HTTP policy or failing/skipped cross-slice tests.

## Validation

Head `1c0140a5c7646536c148dc0a7d790e58f548f00e`, based on common refactor `0206b410044151e1131ca524d0657c45a3237cfe` and main `6acefc10230a19be05f3da88a428e069a6860a3c`:

- Full product compilation, Monaco compilation, dependency-layer checks and scoped hygiene passed.
- 167 focused Copilot/host/bootstrap/helper tests and 20 authentication/replay tests passed independently of the HTTP sibling.
- Combined refactor + HTTP + Copilot validation passed 948 tests, including both original cross-slice regressions. The combined GitHub implementation/tests and Copilot auth/binding match the previously reviewed full snapshot exactly.
- Copilot/auth implementation and focused tests are unchanged from reviewed follow-up `929ab9cb469cf83b6f7d66d147fd3c084cb1bd42`. Earlier model reviews and Code OSS recordings remain historical evidence, not new runs on this split.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678. Previous review discussion is retained on #339208; original full heads are preserved on `agents/github-refactor-before-release-split` and `agents/github-http-before-release-split`.

pull_requests.body:
**Fixes:** #339191

**Description of the proposed changes:**
This PR fixes a bug in the MCP registry where server configurations were being erroneously dropped when switching between local and remote extension hosts. 

Previously, `registerCollection` only checked the server `id` when determining if a configuration already existed, leading to registration collisions between hosts. This patch updates the collision check to evaluate both `id` and `remoteAuthority` (`c.id === collection.id && c.remoteAuthority === collection.remoteAuthority`), allowing the registry to correctly persist configurations across different hosts.

**How to test them:**
1. **Unit Tests (Added):** Run the test suite for `mcpRegistry.test.ts`. A new test explicitly verifies that the registry successfully stores multiple servers with the same ID as long as their `remoteAuthority` differs, and correctly prevents duplicates when both match.
2. **Manual Verification:** 
   * Launch the VS Code development build (`./scripts/code.sh`).
   * Trigger the `MCP: List Servers` command and select `+ Add Server`.
   * Create a basic `stdio` local command server.
   * Reload the window (`Developer: Reload Window`).
   * Run `MCP: List Servers` again. The local server configuration will successfully persist and populate in the dropdown UI without being dropped by the extension host.

pull_requests.title: Build a 64-bit Windows setup with Inno Setup 7
pull_requests.body:
Refs #339236

On Windows on Arm, the VS Code installer takes much longer than it needs to because the setup is an x86 executable, and x86 emulation there is much slower than x64 emulation. Inno Setup 7 can build a 64-bit setup through the new [`SetupArchitecture`](https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/index.php?topic=setup_setuparchitecture) directive, but it still builds an x86 setup by default.

This PR sets `SetupArchitecture=x64` in `code.iss`. VS Code only ships x64 and arm64 builds, and both can run an x64 setup, so no per-arch condition is needed.

### Why the version guard

VS Code gets ISCC from the [`innosetup`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/innosetup) npm package ([joaomoreno/node-innosetup-compiler](https://github.com/joaomoreno/node-innosetup-compiler)). It's currently at **6.4.1**, which is also the latest version published to npm. Inno Setup 6 doesn't know the directive and would fail the build, so it's wrapped in `#if Ver >= EncodeVer(7, 0, 0)`. That makes this PR safe to merge now. It changes nothing until `innosetup` is updated to 7.x, and then it takes effect without further changes. Git for Windows used the same approach in https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/pull/732.

### 64-bit safety of the Pascal Script

Git for Windows had to fix record layouts for Windows API calls when moving to a 64-bit setup, because pointers become 8 bytes wide. `code.iss` doesn't declare any records. Its only external import is `MultiByteToWideChar`, whose parameters are all either 32-bit integers or string types that Pascal Script passes as pointers, so it is ABI-correct on x64 without changes. The script also uses none of the features that Inno Setup 7 removed for 64-bit setups (`{sysnative}`, `EnableFsRedirection`, or loading 32-bit DLLs).

### Testing

I compiled the full `code.iss` with the same `/d` definitions that `gulpfile.vscode.win32.ts` passes (quality `stable`, so the Appx code paths are included) against a stub source directory. I checked the PE machine type of each resulting `VSCodeSetup.exe`:

| Compiler | arm64 user | arm64 system | x64 user | x64 system |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inno Setup 6.4.1 (current `innosetup` npm) | x86 | x86 | x86 | x86 |
| Inno Setup 7.1.0 | **x64** | **x64** | **x64** | **x64** |

All builds succeed. The only new compiler warnings with 7.1.0 are about obsolete `[LangOptions]` font directives in one of the bundled `i18n/Default.*.isl` files, and they don't relate to this change.

I haven't run these stub setups end to end (installing or updating), since that needs a real build. That's worth doing on the first Inno Setup 7 build, including an update from an existing 32-bit-setup install, which Inno Setup documents as supported.

### Follow-up needed

Publish `innosetup@7.x` and bump `package.json`/`package-lock.json`. That step activates this change.

pull_requests.title: Fix #338697: Auto-close counterpart when typing tab in opening pair
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #338697

### Description
When a language configuration defines an auto-closing pair where the opening counterpart ends in a tab character (e.g. {"open": "begin\t", "close": "end"}), pressing the Tab key in the editor after typing  egin did not trigger auto-closing because \TabOperation\ inserted a standard \ReplaceCommand\ without checking for auto-closing pairs.

### Changes
- In \TabOperation._replaceJumpToNextIndent\, check whether typing a tab completes an auto-closing pair open sequence using \AutoClosingOpenCharTypeOperation.getAutoClosingPairClose\ when \selection.isEmpty()\ and \insertsAutoWhitespace\ is true.
- If an auto-closing pair matches, return a \TypeWithAutoClosingCommand\, inserting the tab along with its closing counterpart and registering the auto-closed range.
- Added unit tests in \cursor.test.ts\ verifying auto-closing on Tab with both default indentation and \insertSpaces: true\.

The shared AHP client omitted the required root `channel` from `reconnect` requests. A host that validates the request rejects every retry, while reloading works because the initial `initialize` request already includes the field.

- Include `channel: ROOT_STATE_URI` and check the reconnect payload against the protocol's parameter type.

- Keep the existing success/failure/cancellation semantics and telemetry-level gate. No raw error messages, tokens, request bodies, or diagnostic identifiers are added to telemetry.

`firstFailureCode` is numeric and appears in `Measures`; `firstFailurePhase` describes a recovery step, not necessarily the exact failed RPC method.

Fixes two issues in a chat's Copilot session started while the turn-start checkpoint is captured (`prepareTurn`).

**1. A prepared turn could be sent without newly added plugins**

The turn that `prepareTurn` launched a session for checks its configuration using the plugin state already in memory, instead of waiting for syncs again. While a plugin sync is running, its plugins are marked `Loading` and left out of that state until the sync finishes. If a client added a plugin after preparation finished but before the message was sent, nothing looked different, so the first message went out without the new plugin's (or MCP server's) tools.

The fast path is now used only when nothing is still loading:
- no host or client plugin is in the `Loading` state;
- no workspace customization discovery refresh is pending;
- no workspace MCP discovery refresh is pending.

Otherwise the turn waits for the syncs, like any other send, and that wait can be cancelled. Changes that had already finished were caught before and still are.

**2. Stop couldn't release a preparation stuck on a plugin sync**

`_prepareTurn` waited for plugin syncs with `CancellationToken.None`, and Stop couldn't cancel it. If a sync stalled, the chat's queue stayed blocked after Stop, which held up later turns and other queued operations.

Preparation now goes through `_queueChatTurn`, like `sendMessage`, and passes its token to the sync wait. Stop releases the queue while the sync itself keeps running for other chats.

## Changes

- **`copilotAgent.ts`**:
  - `SessionPluginController.isSettled()`: true when no host or client plugin is loading and neither discovery refresh is pending.
  - `SessionDiscoveredEntry.isSettled`: tracks queued and running discovery refreshes.
  - `_refreshSessionConfiguration`: uses the in-memory fast path only when `launchedForTurn` and `isSettled()` are both true.
  - `_prepareTurn`: queued through `_queueChatTurn` (new operation `'prepareTurn'`), passes its token to `retryFailedClientSyncIfNeeded`, and checks for cancellation before launching the session.
- **`sessionMcpDiscovery.ts`**: `isSettled` on the per-root and per-session MCP discovery, tracking pending rescans and merges.

## Testing

New tests in `copilotAgent.test.ts`, both of which fail without this change:
- "the prepared turn awaits a plugin sync that started after its preparation"
- "Stop releases a preparation waiting on a plugin sync" (preparation is released and no session is created)

Validation:
- `npx tsc -p src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed. eslint is clean.
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob "**/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.js" --grep "prepared turn|prepareTurn|Stop releases a preparation"`: 4 passing (the 2 new tests plus the 2 existing prepared-turn tests).
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob "**/agentHost/test/node/**/*.test.js"`: 8123 passing, 12 failing. All 12 are in `CopilotAgent` (external chat discovery, state-file resolution, restore round-trip) and fail the same way on `main`.
