pull_requests.title: Stream attached background shell output in Agent Host chats
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follows: #338723

Streams attached background shell output using only what `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.16 already ships. There are no SDK, runtime, or AHP protocol changes.

SDK APIs this relies on, all received through `CopilotSession.on()` except the RPC:

- `tool.execution_partial_result` (`ToolExecutionPartialData.partialOutput`) is the live output. The runtime keeps sending it for a shell tool call after the call returns with `<command started in background with shellId: …>`, or another attached "still running" result.
- `system.notification` with `kind.type: "shell_completed"` (`shellId`, `exitCode`) reports the exit.
- `tool.execution_complete` text from `read_bash`/`write_bash` (`<shellId: … completed with exit code N>`) or a stop also reports the exit. When a read sees the exit, the runtime sends no `shell_completed`.
- `session.rpc.tasks.list()` is the fallback: a read that starts after the call went to the background and no longer lists the shell as running or idle means it exited.

Changes:

- Keep forwarding a shell call's `tool.execution_partial_result` after the call returns in the background. The Agent Host used to drop partial results once a call completed.
- Append that output to the call's AHP output terminal (`terminal/data`), creating it if nothing was printed yet. Point both the tool result's terminal block and `BackgroundShellWork.terminal` at it.
- Mark the terminal exited (`terminal/exited`, with the exit code when known) as soon as one of the signals above reports it. It stays subscribable until the session is disposed.
- Skip detached shells, which get no partial output.
- In a streaming shell's Background Shells details, show only the command, its status, and a read-only terminal that subscribes to `BackgroundShellWork.terminal` while the details are open. Once there's output, the terminal keeps a fixed 10 rows, so the details don't move as lines arrive.
- Make that output a focusable region. Open Accessible View shows the command, status, and output without ANSI escapes.

Limits: past about 10 KiB, each partial result carries only the tail of the output, so very fast output can skip lines. The tool call's status icon stays neutral after a background exit.

<details><summary>How to test</summary>

1. In a Copilot Agent Host chat, send: `Use your shell tool in async mode (do not detach) to run exactly: for i in $(seq 1 60); do echo "stream-step:$i"; sleep 1; done` and ask it to reply "started" without waiting.
2. Open **1 Background Shell** and press Right Arrow on the shell. Its terminal keeps adding `stream-step` lines, and so does the tool call's terminal.
3. Press Tab into the output, then Alt+F2 (Alt+Shift+F2 on Linux). The Accessible View shows it as text.
4. In a new chat, ask it to run `sleep 3; echo done` the same way, then `read_bash` that shell until it completes. The AHP log shows `terminal/exited` with `exitCode: 0`.

</details>

<details><summary>Validation</summary>

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npx eslint` on the 18 changed TypeScript files: passed.
- Unit tests on the 11 affected files: 1,338 passing, 11 pending. The test `background shell does not create an output-only terminal` is replaced by `background shell without early output gets an output-only terminal that streams until shell_completed`.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts` at e3dfcd3bc10: 233 passing, 26 pending. Later commits only change workbench UI. The `shell read helper remains a non-terminal tool` AHP snapshot gains the async call's `terminal` block.
- Manual, in Code OSS with the bundled 1.0.16 runtime at ae497582307: the details streamed live (`stream-step:50` to `stream-step:57` in about five seconds), and the tool call's terminal received all 60 lines. The accessible view hasn't been checked with a screen reader.

Unit test command:

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostStateManager.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentHost/agentHostBackgroundShells.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionBackgroundShellsControl.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/accessibility/chatBackgroundShellOutputAccessibleView.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentHost/agentHostSessionInputPills.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatInputPills.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/accessibility/chatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/sessionChatPills.test.ts
```

</details>

-----------------------------------------

<details><summary>Inspirations from</summary>

- `BackgroundShellWork.terminal` and its SHOULD come from [`BackgroundShellWork`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/channels-chat/state.ts#L237-L247).
- Reporting the exit on the terminal instead of the completed tool call follows [`ToolResultTerminalContent`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/channels-chat/state.ts#L1660-L1676) and [`ChatToolCallContentChangedAction`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/channels-chat/actions.ts#L343-L357), which only changes a running tool call.
- Reading the shell ID and exit code from result text follows [`parseCompletedShell`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L35-L45).
- Feeding the terminal after the call returns builds on [`NonPtyShellTerminalStreams.completeToolCall`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotNonPtyShellTerminals.ts#L191-L198), which already kept it unretired, and changes [`onToolPartialResult`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L8614-L8619), which dropped partial results for completed calls.
- The tool call keeps streaming without client changes because a non-PTY terminal stays attached until it settles in [`AgentHostSessionHandler`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts#L4921-L4931).
- Subscribing to the terminal and flattening its content follows [`AgentHostOutputChannel`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/agentHostOutputChannel.ts#L32-L41).
- The details view reuses `ChatTerminalToolProgressPart`'s [title](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L383-L388) and [output](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L1439-L1447) markup, [10-row limit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L78), [status decorations](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L218-L259), and [named output region](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L1585-L1604).
- The read-only terminal's options and column math come from [`DetachedTerminalCommandMirror`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/chatTerminalCommandMirror.ts#L610-L617) and [`computeChatTerminalMirrorCols`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/chatTerminalCommandMirror.ts#L139-L147).
- `ChatBackgroundShellOutputAccessibleView` follows [`ChatTerminalOutputAccessibleView`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/990fb5379d30f3de2c9551aecc10917767b17b0f/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/accessibility/chatTerminalOutputAccessibleView.ts#L14-L75).

</details>

auto_merge.commit_title: Stream attached background shell output in Agent Host chats (#339220)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* Stream background shell output in Agent Host chats

Keep an attached shell's tool call terminal live after an async call
returns and keep appending its partial output. Point the shell's
background work entry at that terminal, settle it on shell_completed,
and show the command and live output in the Background Shells details.

* Update the read-shell E2E snapshot for background shell terminals

The async shell call now completes with a terminal block, because its
output keeps streaming after the call returns.

* Settle background shell terminals from read results and every task read

When the agent polls a background shell with read_bash, the runtime puts the
exit code in the read result and sends no shell_completed notification, so
settle the shell from read, write, and stop results.

The task-list fallback now counts any read that started after the call went
to the background, including reads that a newer read superseded, so a shell
that exits before it is ever listed still settles.

Clear the background shell output view through the xterm write queue instead
of reset(), so output that xterm is still parsing can't land after the clear.

* Expose background shell output to screen readers

Addresses review comment 4162451160. The Background Shells details drew the
output only in a detached xterm, inside a div that had a name but no role,
so screen readers couldn't review the streamed lines.

The output is now a focusable region named for its command, with the
Terminal Chat Output hint. Open Accessible View shows the command, its
status, and the output without ANSI escapes, and closing it returns focus to
the output, or to the chat input once the picker has closed.

* Show only the live terminal in background shell details

While a background shell's output is shown, its details now hold just the
command, its status, and the terminal. The badge, shell ID, and start time
stay in the row's description.

The terminal also keeps a fixed height of 10 rows instead of growing with
the output. The details are pinned above the chat input, so each new row
pushed the command header up. Lines now fill the terminal from the top, then
scroll.

Disconnected cloud sandbox sessions expose Rename, but the inherited AHP-only implementation silently does nothing without a live connection.

Rename the owning Mission Control task using `PATCH /agents/tasks/{task_id}`, update the local title after success, and use the existing AHP rename once when already connected. Update the existing discovery inventory/cache and route default-chat rename through the same operation. Sessions not owned by the discovered task continue to use AHP.

Deliberately does not add pending-command storage, reconnect replay, or title reconciliation. The Tasks API updates the task record, not the host title, so a later connection after an offline rename can report the old host title. Host-reported titles remain authoritative.

## Summary

Cloud sandbox sessions should be automatically trusted like Codespaces, rather than prompting inconsistently when opening a session, mounting its folders, or sending a message.

- Add a disposable `registerTrustedAuthority(scheme, authority)` API to workspace trust. Registrations match an exact scheme and authority, participate in automatic/forced workspace trust, and do not persist user-granted folder trust.
- Have the shared sandbox contribution register each environment before publishing its provider, including cached/offline restoration in both Editor and Agents windows. Dispose the registration with its environment; workspace trust contains no sandbox address-prefix logic.
- Use the existing connection customization to exempt sandbox message sending from the local/window workspace-trust gate. Local folders and other remote hosts retain their existing trust checks.
- Cover registration lifetime, duplicate registrations, authority/scheme isolation, offline restoration, teardown, and message sending without granting local workspace trust. Document the provider-owned trust contract.

## Summary

pull_requests.title: github: distinguish GraphQL throttling from quota exhaustion
pull_requests.body:
Related https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9678

Addresses GitHub protocol-audit finding: an operation/resource-specific GraphQL `RATE_LIMITED` error must not exhaust the account's entire GraphQL quota.

Previously, an HTTP 200 response with `RATE_LIMITED`, 4,999 remaining points, and an hourly reset could force `remaining = 0` and delay unrelated GraphQL for an hour. Queries whose cost exceeds the remaining points can also return `RATE_LIMITED` while cheaper queries remain admissible.

- Treat `RATE_LIMIT` and valid zero-quota feedback as primary exhaustion; do not infer account-wide exhaustion from `RATE_LIMITED` alone, its message, or its path.
- Honor server reset and Retry-After feedback without shortening an existing cooldown. Merge partial quota feedback and reject malformed GraphQL quota numbers.
- Recognize both error types consistently in domain error mapping and existing rate-limit telemetry.
- Preserve HTTP 200 GraphQL errors and fail closed on partial domain results. Do not replay mutations or add an operation-local retry framework.

* github: distinguish GraphQL throttling from quota exhaustion

Treat RATE_LIMIT as primary exhaustion without turning operation-specific RATE_LIMITED errors into an account-wide hourly cooldown. Preserve authoritative quota and Retry-After feedback, and cover error mapping, telemetry, partial results, and mutation no-replay.

Reject malformed numeric retry hints on GraphQL feedback paths so they cannot release an exhausted quota early. Preserve decimal delay-seconds and HTTP-date support without changing REST parsing. Add deterministic header, payload, and healthy-quota regressions.

Related https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9678

Addresses a finding from the GitHub protocol audit: accepting a review-thread reply does not necessarily publish it when the viewer already has a pending review.

- Add an explicit `pending` reply outcome. Only a confirmed `SUBMITTED` comment produces `succeeded` or `reconciled` and permits coupled thread resolution.
- Retain comment state in mutation responses and paginated reconciliation reads. Missing or malformed state and duplicate operation-marker matches remain indeterminate, without blind write replay.
- Report pending/unconfirmed replies accurately in Agent Merge tool results, guidance, and transcript labels.
- Never submit, discard, or replace the user's pending review. Published reply-and-resolve behavior and intentional standalone thread resolution are preserved.
- After a confirmed pending reply, stop Agent Merge for that folder when the repair turn completes, is cancelled, or fails, and notify the user. Resuming requires explicit re-enablement. The current turn, other folders, and published/indeterminate reply behavior are preserved.

pull_requests.title: explorer: Make cancelling an inline rename a rebindable command
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #174877

Implements the approach from [alexdima's review on #178639](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/178639#pullrequestreview-1365175845): a command with a default Escape keybinding replaces the Escape handling hard-coded in the explorer's inline name input.

### Change

- `fileActions.contribution.ts`: `filesExplorer.cancelEdit`, bound to Escape when `filesExplorerFocus && explorerResourceIsEditing && inputFocus`. It cancels the edit the same way scrolling the input out of view already does (`editable.data.onFinish('', false)`).
- `files.ts`, `explorerView.ts`: a new `explorerResourceIsEditing` context key, set in `ExplorerView.setEditable`. Without the key, `filesExplorerFocus && inputFocus` would also match the explorer's find input, which renders inside the tree, where `list.closeFind` handles Escape at a lower weight.
- `explorerViewer.ts`: drops the `KeyCode.Escape` branch from the input's keydown listener.

### Validation

Real key events sent through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, with the binding from the issue (`escape` → `workbench.action.focusActiveEditorGroup`, `!inputFocus`):

- stable 1.138: Escape in the rename input cancels and also moves focus to the editor (the bug). Same for the New File input. Without the user binding, cancelling a rename keeps focus in the explorer.
- this branch: Escape cancels, focus stays in the explorer and the user binding doesn't run. A typed name is discarded, for rename and New File. A second Escape then runs the user binding.
- Escape still closes the explorer's find widget, and clicking away still commits a rename.
- With `-filesExplorer.cancelEdit` on Escape and `filesExplorer.cancelEdit` on `ctrl+g`, Escape leaves the input open and `ctrl+g` cancels it.
- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, eslint on the changed files, and the files contrib unit tests pass.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: parallelize message send and git checkpoint capture (experiment)
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

**What's slow today:** before the agent host sends your message to Copilot, it saves a snapshot of your workspace (a git checkpoint) so the agent's edits can be undone later. The message waits until that snapshot is finished. On Windows that takes 200–500 ms in a large repo, and it happens on every message, so the chat looks idle for that long before anything appears.

**What this PR changes:** the message is sent right away, and the snapshot is saved at the same time. The model can start thinking and responding immediately. The snapshot only has to be finished before anything changes the workspace, so every tool call (file edits, terminal commands, subagents) and every plugin hook command waits for it.

**Result:** on Windows, follow-up messages reach the model about 150–200 ms (around 30%) sooner, with the same undo and checkpoint guarantees as before.

It's off by default and behind the experiment setting `chat.agentHost.experimental.deferTurnStartCheckpoint`. Follow-up to #339053.

**Before:** the message waits for the snapshot

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant AH as Agent host
    participant Git as Checkpoint (git)
    participant CLI as Copilot runtime
    participant M as Model

    AH->>Git: capture turn-start checkpoint
    Git-->>AH: done (200–500 ms on Windows)
    AH->>CLI: send(turn)
    CLI->>M: first model request
    M-->>CLI: tool call
    CLI->>CLI: run tool
```

**After:** the message is sent while the snapshot is saved, and tools and hook commands wait for it

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant AH as Agent host
    participant Git as Checkpoint (git)
    participant CLI as Copilot runtime
    participant M as Model

    par
        AH->>Git: capture turn-start checkpoint
    and
        AH->>CLI: send(turn, turnStartBarrier)
        CLI->>M: first model request
    end
    Git-->>AH: done
    M-->>CLI: tool call
    CLI->>AH: tool and hook commands wait for turnStartBarrier
    note over AH,CLI: Also applies to plugin hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, ...)
    AH-->>CLI: barrier settled
    CLI->>CLI: run tool
```

## Changes

- **`agentSideEffects.ts`**: when the provider supports it (`IAgentChats.supportsTurnStartBarrier`):
  - creates a `turnStartBarrier` that settles with the checkpoint capture and hands it to both `prepareTurn` and `sendMessage`;
  - with the setting on, dispatch no longer waits for the capture;
  - the experiment trigger fires in both arms. It's generalized to `_reportExperimentTrigger(settingId)` and held until the assignment context is available.
- **`copilotAgent.ts`**: keeps the current barrier for each chat. A session that is still starting (before `send()`) reads it from there, so SessionStart hooks also wait.
- **`copilotAgentSession.ts`**: `_handlePreToolUse` waits for the barrier before any tool runs, and the runtime exposes `waitForTurnStartBarrier()` for hooks.
- **`copilotPluginConverters.ts`**: every plugin hook command (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, SessionEnd, ErrorOccurred) waits for the barrier before it runs. Hooks with no plugin commands don't wait.
- **`agentHostCheckpointService.ts`**:
  - `getBaselineCheckpoint` and `getTurnCheckpointPair` wait for any in-flight turn-start capture, so readers never see a missing baseline;
  - internal callers use a variant that doesn't wait, to avoid a deadlock.
- **Behavior change when deferred**: a failed capture is logged and the turn continues without a checkpoint, instead of failing the turn.
- **Telemetry**: `sendStageCheckpointMs` is left out whenever deferral is on and the provider supports the barrier, even if the capture already finished (documented in `OTEL.md`). `timeToProviderDispatch` shows the gain.

## Measurements

Setup:
- MSBench hello benchmark on Windows and Linux, using Insiders `ec2e580` with this change's bundle.
- 4 runs per arm, with the first turn and a follow-up turn measured separately.
- "VS Code repo" means the workspace was a checkout of the VS Code repo (about 19.6K files).
- Values are medians (off → on).

| Scenario | Checkpoint wait removed | Turn start → handoff to Copilot | Turn start → first model call | Time to first progress (UI) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Windows, small workspace, follow-up turn | 221 ms | 248 → 32 ms (**−87%**) | 444 → 296 ms (**−33%**) | 2290 → 2054 ms (**−10%**) |
| Windows, VS Code repo, follow-up turn\* | 403 ms | 464 → 50 ms (**−89%**) | 688 → 476 ms (**−31%**) | 2322 → 2284 ms (−2%) |
| Windows, VS Code repo, first turn | 512 ms | 1079 → 524 ms (**−51%**) | 1810 → 1704 ms (−6%) | 6008 → 6710 ms (+12%)† |
| Windows, small workspace, first turn | 60 ms | 469 → 364 ms (−22%) | 1076 → 1098 ms (+2%) | 4905 → 4880 ms (−1%) |
| Linux, VS Code repo, follow-up turn\* | 198 ms | 269 → 82 ms (**−70%**) | 418 → 281 ms (**−33%**) | 1944 → 2095 ms (+8%)† |
| Linux, VS Code repo, first turn | 96 ms | 644 → 415 ms (**−36%**) | 1694 → 1115 ms (**−34%**) | 6478 → 5514 ms (−15%)† |

\* Leaves out runs where `session.send()` was held for up to 1.3 s by a `github-mcp-server` auth retry loop. The benchmark has no GitHub MCP auth, and the loop happened in both arms. It's tracked on the runtime side in github/copilot-agent-runtime#24238.

† Within run-to-run noise. Time to first progress (UI) includes the model's own response time, which varies by about ±1 s between runs, so at n=4 differences under ~15% aren't meaningful. The "first model call" column is the reliable measure of this change, and the experiment will give the real UI number.

Notes:
- Windows follow-up turns are about 10× more common than first turns in production, so the follow-up rows are where most of the user-visible gain is.
- Time to first progress (UI) includes the model's own response time, so at n=4 only the Windows small-workspace follow-up shows a gain clearly above noise. The experiment will give the real number.
- With the checkpoint taken off the critical path, Copilot's own session setup accounts for most of the remaining first-turn time.

## How to test

1. Set `"chat.agentHost.experimental.deferTurnStartCheckpoint": true` and use an agent-host (Copilot CLI) session in a git workspace.
2. Send a message that edits a file, then a follow-up. In `agenthost.log`, `sendMessage called` / `session.send() returned` appear before `git write-tree` finishes.
3. Confirm the edit isn't applied until the capture finishes, and that checkpoint restore and undo still work.
4. Optionally, install a plugin with a `SessionStart` or `UserPromptSubmit` hook command and confirm it runs only after the capture finishes.

pull_requests.title: Show MCP server tools in Chat Customizations > Tools
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

The Tools page in Chat Customizations now lists the tools that MCP servers contribute, under **Connected Sources**. Each server has one toggle that enables or disables the whole server, and with it all of its tools.

## Changes

**Agent host: publish each server's tools (no AHP protocol change)**
- In Copilot CLI sessions the agent host, not VS Code, runs the MCP servers, and AHP's `McpServerCustomization` has no tool list. The host now gets each server's model-visible tools from the SDK's `rpc.mcp.listTools` and puts them in the customization's `_meta['agentHost.mcpServerTools']`. That is a namespaced extension, so other agent hosts aren't affected.
- Tools are refreshed when a server becomes Ready, on `tools_updated`, and on inventory loads. They're kept across state changes, so a stopped server still shows its last known tools.
- MCP servers nested in a container, such as VS Code's synced plugin container, can't take extra fields through the narrow `mcpServerStateChanged` action. Instead, `SessionPluginController` republishes the container when one of its servers' tools change.

**Tools page and counts**
- A new `mcpServerToolSets.ts` builds one tool set per MCP server. It prefers the tools reported by the active session and falls back to VS Code's local MCP cache. Servers that contribute no tools are hidden; disabled servers that have tools stay listed so they can be turned back on.
- A new shared `IAICustomizationToolsModel` (workbench layer) owns the MCP server tool sets and the enabled Tools count: built-in tools plus tools from enabled MCP servers. The Tools page, the Agents window overview and toolbar, and the navigation total all read it, so they always agree and don't each add up the parts.
- On every customization re-sync, such as after a toggle, the host briefly republishes the synced plugin container as Loading with no children. That made the server row and count flicker. The page now reuses the last tools the session reported while a server is temporarily missing; this memory is reset when the active session changes.

## How to test

1. Add a workspace `.vscode/mcp.json` with a stdio MCP server that exposes tools, and open a Copilot CLI (Agent Host) session.
2. Open Chat Customizations → **Tools**. The server should appear under **Connected Sources** with a count like `150/150`, and expanding it should list its tools.
3. Toggle the server off and on. The row should stay in place with no flicker. The count should switch between `0/N` and `N/N`, and the **Tools** badge should change by N.
4. An MCP server with no tools should not appear on the Tools page.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: no new errors in the changed files. Unrelated errors that already exist on `main` remain (`copilotSystemNotification.ts`, `copilotToolDisplay.ts`, `localTranscriptionService.ts`).
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "mcpServerToolSets|Customizations toolbar|toolsListWidget|AgentHostToolSetEnablement|McpCustomizationController|MCP server inventory|Agent host _meta readers"`: **162 passing**, after rebasing on `main`.
- A broader run with `--grep "...|CopilotAgent|Codex"`: 1843 passing, 12 failing. The same 12 fail without this change; they read this machine's real `~/.copilot/session-state`.
- `npx eslint` on all changed files: passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: no layer violations.
- `npx component-explorer render --fixture-id-regex "aiCustomizationManagementEditor/Tools|aiCustomizationShortcutsWidget"`: all 18 fixtures render.

issues.title: Agents: #339409 peer-chat recovery is undone when the phantom comes from a never-sent peer chat
issues.body:
Follow-up to #339409 / #339476.

The recovery in #339476 can restore a session's peer chats and then lose them again within a second. This happens when the phantom registration was created by a peer chat that never sent a message. The phantom is never unregistered, its restore erases the recovered catalogue, and the recovery is already marked `completed`, so it never runs again.

- VS Code Version: 1.141.0-insider, commit `ae1080a9ed1098a8b532c6cfd50977d784b29e6d` (contains #339476)
- OS Version: macOS
- Feature: Agents Window, local Agent Host / Copilot CLI, multi-chat sessions

## Steps to Reproduce

Session state before updating to a build that contains #339476 (all of it produced by the #339409 regression):

1. Parent session `copilotcli:/P` had 10 peer chats. One of them, `C0`, was created but **never sent a turn**.
2. Phantoms `copilotcli:/P#C0`, `copilotcli:/P#C1` and `copilotcli:/P#C2` were registered with `source = restore`. The parent's `peerChats` metadata had been erased to `[]`.
3. Update to the build above and launch.

## Expected

All recoverable peer chats are restored. Every phantom is unregistered so it cannot run the #339409 erase path again.

## Actual

```text
12:08:36.923 [info]    [AgentHostPeerChatStore] Recovered 8 peer chats affected by #339409 for copilotcli:/P
12:08:37.587 [warning] [AgentService] Skipping peer-chat catalog entry 0 that is not owned by copilotcli:/P#C0
   … entries 1-7 …
12:11:34.434 [info]    [AgentService] Restored session copilotcli:/P#C0 with 15 turns
```

- The two phantoms of chats that had sent turns (`C1`, `C2`) were unregistered. The phantom for `C0` stayed registered.
- About 0.7 s after recovery, the `C0` phantom was restored. It rejected all 8 entries and wrote `peerChats = []` to the parent again, so the sidebar again shows the parent with no peer chats.
- The parent's `agentHost.peerChatRecovery339409` marker already reads `{"recovered":[…8 chats…],"completed":true}`, so later launches never retry.
- Later in the same run, selecting the parent restored the phantom again (`Restored session copilotcli:/P#C0 with 15 turns`), followed by `Catalog synchronization for copilotcli:/P#C0 remains pending: acknowledgementSuperseded`. The phantom stays registered.

The other two affected sessions on this machine had only sent-to peer-chat phantoms. Both recovered correctly and stayed recovered.

## Root cause

In [`recoverChatSelectionCorruption`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ae1080a9ed1098a8b532c6cfd50977d784b29e6d/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostPeerChatStore.ts#L87), a selected phantom is verified only if its chat backing database has `agentHost.chatProviderData`:

```ts
if (!await backing.object.getMetadata(CHAT_PROVIDER_DATA_METADATA_KEY)) {
    continue;           // never reaches verifiedPhantomChatIds.push(chatId)
}
```

A peer chat that never sent a turn has no `agentHost.chatProviderData`: its backing DB has 0 rows in `turns`. An SDK session was created for it, but its storage has 0 turns too. As a result:

1. `C0` is not added to `verifiedPhantomChatIds`.
2. [`_recoverChatSelectionCorruption`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/ae1080a9ed1098a8b532c6cfd50977d784b29e6d/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L3357) unregisters only verified phantoms, so the `C0` phantom stays registered.
3. The recovery still completes, because the other phantoms were verified, and it writes `completed: true`.
4. Startup restores the remaining phantom. It hits the original #339409 path ("Skipping peer-chat catalog entry N that is not owned by …#C0") and erases the parent catalogue that was just recovered.

After that the session cannot recover by itself:
- `completed: true` blocks any further recovery.
- With the marker removed but the phantom still unverifiable, `if (verifiedPhantomChatIds.length === 0) return;` exits before doing anything. The `C0` phantom is now the only one left.

## Manual workaround (confirmed)

With VS Code quit:
1. Delete `agentHost.peerChatRecovery339409` from the parent's `session.db`.
2. Add `agentHost.chatProviderData` to the `C0` chat's backing `session.db`.

On the next launch, the recovery verified the `C0` phantom, logged `Recovered 8 peer chats…`, and unregistered the phantom. There were no further `not owned by` warnings, and the catalogue has stayed intact since.

## Suggested fix

Something along these lines:

- Verify a *selected* phantom from evidence that does not depend on the chat having sent a turn. For example: the backing chat dir resolves to the parent (the path check that already exists), plus the phantom's own `restore` registration.
- Or always unregister restore-created, fragment-bearing `copilotcli` registrations whose parent is registered. A fragment-bearing session URI is never valid once #339074 is reverted, and unregistering does not touch shared storage.
- Avoid writing `completed: true` while an unverified fragment phantom of the same parent is still registered, so a later launch can retry.

issues.body:
Testing #339183

Repro:
- Add a new chat to the middle row that already contains chats that are equally distributed
- Observe the newly added chat sometimes had more horizontal space, and resized the entire row vertically

Expectation:
- The new chat would resize to redistribute the space evenly and keep the row height

There's also some resizing on focus if the space is available, but it didn't _always_ resize on focus which was a bit confusing. I wouldn't do any resize on focus. However, I might suggest adding maximize on double click, and an easy way to minimize again.

issues.title: ChatGPT sidebar header controls become unclickable in Integrated Browser at wider viewport widths
issues.body:
Type: Bug Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.140.0 - OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (build 26200) Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open VS Code's Integrated Browser and navigate to `https://chatgpt.com/`. 2. Sign in with a ChatGPT Plus account. 3. Make the Integrated Browser editor area relatively wide. 4. Try clicking the controls at the top of the ChatGPT sidebar: - ChatGPT / Codex selector - Search button - Sidebar toggle button 5. The controls remain visible, but do not respond to mouse clicks. 6. Resize the Integrated Browser to a narrower width. 7. Try the same controls again. They become clickable. Additional observations: - The issue is dependent on the Integrated Browser viewport width. - Other parts of the ChatGPT page remain interactive. - The issue reproduces when signed in with a ChatGPT Plus account. - The issue does not reproduce when logged out. - The issue does not reproduce when signed in with a ChatGPT Free account. - Other ChatGPT plans have not been tested. - ChatGPT works normally in a regular desktop browser. - The issue still reproduces when VS Code is launched with `code --disable-extensions`. - The issue also reproduces in the latest VS Code Insiders build. This appears to depend on both the viewport width and the ChatGPT account state/plan. One possibility is that a UI element present for Plus accounts overlaps these sidebar controls or otherwise affects hit testing at certain responsive-layout widths, but I have not identified the exact cause. issues.title: MCP resource URI templates incorrectly encode non-ASCII variable values
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Reproduced against `main` at `3d5764c14dea123b0fd50fb61788328c33c076b8` on Linux with Node.js 22.22.1, using the actual `UriTemplate` source. This is a source-level reproduction, without extensions or a live MCP server session.

`UriTemplate` percent-encodes UTF-16 code units instead of UTF-8 bytes. This affects non-ASCII values entered for an MCP resource template: `mcpResourceQuickAccess.ts` collects the variable text and calls `resolveURI`, and `mcpServer.ts` resolves it through this helper.

To reproduce in the existing `UriTemplate` unit suite:

```ts
const template = UriTemplate.parse('resource://docs/{name}');
template.resolve({ name: 'café' });
// Actual:   resource://docs/caf%E9
// Expected: resource://docs/caf%C3%A9

template.resolve({ name: '中文' });
// Actual:   resource://docs/%4E2D%6587
// Expected: resource://docs/%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87

template.resolve({ name: '🚀' });
// Actual:   resource://docs/%D83D%DE80
// Expected: resource://docs/%F0%9F%9A%80
```

The accented and emoji results fail `decodeURIComponent`; the Chinese result decodes to different characters. Prefix expansion also counts UTF-16 units: `{name:1}` should retain the whole first emoji, rather than splitting its surrogate pair.

[RFC 6570](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6570.html#section-3.2.1) specifies UTF-8 percent-encoding and Unicode-character prefix lengths. The previous low-control padding fix in #323012 does not address these non-ASCII values.

A focused correction and regression tests are prepared: UTF-8 encoding while preserving ASCII punctuation escaping, plus code-point prefix slicing. I plan to submit the linked fix. AI assistance was used for the investigation; the reported outputs were reproduced against the actual source.

issues.title: Copilot agent host (Copilot CLI) sessions load no user or workspace instruction files on macOS
issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version:
- VS Code: 1.140.0 (commit 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74)
- OS: macOS 26.6.2
- Feature: agent mode, regular ole' honkin chat UI panel, both in 'Autopilot' mode and 'Interactive'
- Selected model: Sonnet 5.5
- Logs: couldn't find any major logs that I felt comfortable sharing. 

Custom instructions I have used for years are not included in the system prompt of agent host sessions. The editing UI still lists and edits them, and the Local agent still loads them. After the latest update, none of them reach the agent.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/prompts/general.md (or whatever filename of your choiuce) and fill with instructions.
2. Also create ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md with the same rule, and .github/copilot-instructions.md in the open workspace, just for good measure.
3. Start a new Copilot agent host session in that workspace and ask along the lines of "Do you see any custom instructions?"
4. Inspect the system.message event in ~/.copilot/session-state/<session file id thing>/events.jsonl and the agent host log.

None of them are seemingly getting to the agent, and this symptom started with the "new" experience (some popup about Copilot is different now; I dismissed it and promptly forget what it was talking about. whoops.)

## Notes

- Checked in new sessions started after the files were created, as well as existing sessions. No diff.
- The system.message in events.jsonl contains none of the text from any of the three files. 
- The agent host log shows the same customization every time, before and after the files existed: Resolved system message: mode=customize sections=[identity:replace, tool_instructions:append] +content(length 1178)
- The files are valid and the VS Code UI lists them. The same files worked in earlier versions.
- No setting in settings.json disables or relocates them.
- I can Cmd+P and `> Conf` and get to the UX to change my old instruction files. If this is expected to be discontinued, that UX shouldn't be there. But, I assume that's not what's happening seeing as the other copilot.md files are being ignored too.

issues.title: fix: guard stale ghost text screen reader rendering (fixes #339819)
issues.body:
### Summary While rendering ghost text (inline completions) for the screen reader, `GhostText.renderForScreenReader` builds a `TextEdit` whose replacement positions are taken from the cached ghost-text part columns. When the current editor line has become shorter than the cached ghost text expects (the document was edited during the deliberate `timeout(50)` + `waitForState` delay before the delayed screen-reader announcement), the line-capping step is a no-op and a replacement lands past the end of the capped text. `TextEdit.apply` then calls `rangeFromPositions(lastEditEnd, endPositionExclusive)` with `start > end`, which throws `BugIndicatingError: start must be before end`. Impact: an unhandled error is logged (921 users on stable 1.140.0) and the screen-reader announcement is lost; it does not crash the editor. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339819 Recommended reviewer: ``@hediet`` ### Culprit Commit Not identified — pre-existing. The `renderForScreenReader` capping logic (`cappedLineText = lineText.substr(0, lastPart.column - 1)`) dates back to the original ghost-text implementation (`7ec64f0dad5d`, 2021) and the `TextEdit`-based rendering (`a9cd99e83e03`, 2024); neither assumes `lineText` may be shorter than the cached part column. The issue itself records a prior occurrence (microsoft/vscode#287069) tracked since 1.97-era builds and anomaly hits in multiple releases, so this is a long-standing latent race re-bucketed for stable 1.140.0, not a new regression from a specific commit. | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — pre-existing | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | Capping logic never handled the case where the live line is shorter than the cached ghost-text columns; surfaced as a new stable bucket, not introduced by a recent change. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ctrl as inlineCompletionsController participant GT as GhostText.renderForScreenReader participant TE as TextEdit.apply participant RFP as rangeFromPositions Ctrl->>Ctrl: timeout(50) + waitForState (document may change) Note over Ctrl: Cached ghost text now stale
vs. current (shorter) line Ctrl->>GT: renderForScreenReader(lineText) Note over GT: ⚠️ Root cause:
substr cannot lengthen lineText;
lastPart.column-1 > lineText.length GT->>TE: applyToString(cappedLineText) TE->>RFP: rangeFromPositions(lastEditEnd, endPositionExclusive) Note over RFP: 💥 start > end

To increase likelihood: 1. Enable a screen reader (or `editor.accessibilitySupport: "on"`) and `editor.screenReaderAnnounceInlineSuggestion`. 2. Trigger an inline completion (ghost text) whose part column is near the end of a line. 3. Within the ~50ms announcement delay (`timeout(50)` + `waitForState` in `inlineCompletionsController`), delete characters on that line / replace the line with a shorter one (e.g. fast backspacing or an external edit) so the live line becomes shorter than the cached ghost-text column. 4. The delayed `renderForScreenReader` runs against the now-shorter line; the capped line is shorter than the last part's column and `TextEdit.apply` throws `start must be before end`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/model/ghostText.ts` → `renderForScreenReader()`: add a guard immediately after computing `lastPart`, before the capping/`TextEdit` construction. issues.body:
### Summary The editor throws `BugIndicatingError: Illegal value for lineNumber` from `TextModel.getLineMaxColumn` while measuring line widths for an inline-edit (NES) preview. During a synchronous `undo` the model shrinks, and the inline-edit width `derived` recomputes (it reads `editorObs.versionId`) while the edit's cached `displayRange` / `originalDisplayRange` still references the pre-undo line count. The shared helper `maxContentWidthInRange` then iterates those now-out-of-bounds line numbers against the current (shorter) model, hitting the line-count guard in `getLineMaxColumn`. Impact: a visible unhandled error affecting ~1,000 stable users on 1.140.0 whenever an inline edit is showing as the buffer shrinks underneath it. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339818 Recommended reviewer: ``@hediet`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not identified — pre-existing stale-range pattern | | Author | — | | PR | — | | Message | — | | Why | — | > No single regression commit was confirmed. The `maxContentWidthInRange` loop that dereferences stale line numbers dates to `f2c7116f8e19` (Feb 2025) and the `getWidthOfLine` call on line 42 to `461887743ad0` (Jan 2026); both predate the 1.140.0 window and pass the ancestry check against the shipped commit `07f806f9`. The bucket surfaced as a *new* stable anomaly in 1.140.0, but the throwing code path is pre-existing — the spike most plausibly reflects increased NES/inline-edit exposure rather than a change to this loop. Per the re-bucketing / pre-existing guidance, no speculative culprit is named; the owner is taken from the feature area. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Undo as TextModel undo participant Model as TextModel (content change) participant Derived as inlineEditsSideBySideView
_editorMaxContentWidthInRange participant Util as maxContentWidthInRange participant Crash as TextModel.getLineMaxColumn Undo->>Model: _applyUndo shrinks buffer Note over Model: line count decreases;
versionId increments Model->>Derived: synchronous layout cascade
recompute (reads versionId) Note over Derived: ⚠️ Root cause:
cached originalDisplayRange
still has pre-undo lines Derived->>Util: maxContentWidthInRange(editor, staleRange) Util->>Crash: getWidthOfLine(i) for out-of-bounds i Note over Crash: 💥 Illegal value for lineNumber ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts` | crash site | L900 (from stack): `throw new BugIndicatingError('Illegal value for lineNumber')` when `lineNumber > getLineCount()` | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/utils/utils.ts` | root cause | L41-L44: `for (let i = range.startLineNumber; i < range.endLineNumberExclusive; i++) { editor.getWidthOfLine(i, reader); }` iterates a range not reconciled with the current model | | `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/inlineEditsViews/inlineEditsSideBySideView.ts` | producer | L220-L227: `derived` keyed on `versionId` recomputes `maxContentWidthInRange(this._editorObs, originalDisplayRange, reader)` with the stale edit range after the model shrank | | `src/vs/editor/browser/observableCodeEditor.ts` | pass-through | L534-L539: `getWidthOfLine` forwards `lineNumber` to `editor.getWidthOfLine` | ### Repro Steps Non-deterministic timing-dependent race. To increase likelihood: 1. Enable inline suggestions / next-edit-suggestions (NES). 2. In a non-`file` scheme document (e.g. an untitled or notebook cell editor), trigger an inline edit preview whose `displayRange` extends to near the end of the buffer. 3. While the side-by-side inline-edit preview is visible, perform an `undo` (or any edit) that removes lines so the model becomes shorter than the preview's `displayRange`. 4. The synchronous content-change → layout cascade recomputes the width derived against the stale range, iterating a line number beyond the new line count and throwing `Illegal value for lineNumber`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/view/inlineEdits/utils/utils.ts` → `maxContentWidthInRange()`: before iterating, clamp the incoming `range` to the current model's line count (`model.getLineCount()`), reading the authoritative line count in the same atomic section that already reads the model. The loop and the subsequent `mapToLineArray(l => model.getLineContent(l))` now use the clamped range, so no line number outside `[1, lineCount]` is ever passed to `getWidthOfLine` / `getLineContent`. This is the stale-cached-identifier lifecycle pattern: the consumer holds a range captured against an older model version and re-reads it after the producer (the undo-driven content change) shrank the model. The sanctioned fix for that pattern is to re-resolve the stale reference against authoritative state in the same read section, which is exactly what this utility — the single reconciliation point every inline-edit width call site routes through — is positioned to do. It fixes where the range meets the model, not at the crash site: `getLineMaxColumn`'s guard is left intact so it keeps feeding the telemetry pipeline for genuinely illegal callers, and no `logService.error`/throw is removed or wrapped in try/catch. After this change, `utils.ts:41` cannot pass an out-of-bounds line number to `getWidthOfLine` because every iterated value is bounded by `model.getLineCount()` read immediately above the loop. **Alternatives considered**: - Guarding at the crash site in `getLineMaxColumn` (e.g. returning a fallback instead of throwing) — rejected: it masks the real bug for every caller and removes a legitimate invariant check that feeds error telemetry. - Fixing each producer (`inlineEditsSideBySideView`, `inlineEditsDeletionView`, `inlineEditsCustomView`, `longDistancePreviewEditor`) to re-clamp its edit range before calling the utility — rejected: six-plus call sites all funnel the same edit-derived ranges through this one helper, so reconciling once at the shared reconciliation point is both minimal and complete; duplicating the clamp at every caller would be error-prone and easy to miss on future call sites. ### Recommended Owner ``@hediet`` — Henning Dieterichs owns the inline-edits / NES rendering area, authored `maxContentWidthInRange` (`f2c7116f8e19`) and the side-by-side view that produces the stale range, and is highly active in `microsoft/vscode` (148 commits in the last 90 days). --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. issues.title: Bundled /create-* customization slash commands are not registered in Copilot SDK harness sessions
issues.body:
### Type: Bug

The bundled `/create-prompt`, `/create-instructions`, `/create-skill`, `/create-agent` and `/create-hook` slash commands are not available in Copilot SDK harness sessions (the agent-host sessions used by the Agents window / Copilot SDK harness). They are still available in regular Copilot Chat.

The skills are still shipped and still referenced by other built-in customizations, so this looks like a gap in how the harness builds its slash-command catalog rather than an intentional removal.

### Evidence that the commands still exist in the installed build

All paths below are inside the installed app at `/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app`.

The skill definitions are present and are all marked user-invocable (`disable-model-invocation: true`, no `user-invocable: false`):

```
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-agent/SKILL.md
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-hook/SKILL.md
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-instructions/SKILL.md
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-prompt/SKILL.md
extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/create-skill/SKILL.md
```

They are documented as a shipped feature in `extensions/copilot/changelog.md:73` (0.38):

> **Create agent customizations from chat** — New `/create-prompt`, `/create-instruction`, `/create-skill`, `/create-agent`, and `/create-hook` slash commands to generate customization files directly from a conversation.

Other bundled customizations actively depend on them:

- `extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/init/SKILL.md:48` tells the agent to recommend them:
  > Once finalized, propose related agent-customizations to create next (`/create-(agent|hook|instruction|prompt|skill) …`)
- `extensions/copilot/assets/prompts/skills/agent-customization/SKILL.md:3` hides itself *because* they are expected to exist:
  > `user-invocable: false # don't show as slash command, we have sepcialized create-agent, create-instructions, create-hook prompts for that`

### Current behavior

In a Copilot SDK harness session, the available skill catalog contains user-level skills (`~/.copilot/skills`) and plugin skills, but none of the bundled `create-*` skills — and `init` is missing as well. The `agent-customization` skill correctly stays hidden, so the net effect is that **no** built-in entry point for creating customization files is reachable from the harness.

Because `agent-customization` deliberately hides itself in favor of the `create-*` commands, the result is a discoverability dead end: `/init` recommends commands the user cannot invoke.

### Expected behavior

Bundled user-invocable skills shipped with the Copilot extension (`create-agent`, `create-hook`, `create-instructions`, `create-prompt`, `create-skill`, `init`) should be registered as slash commands in Copilot SDK harness sessions, the same way they are in Copilot Chat.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Agents window and start a session on the Copilot SDK harness.
2. Type `/` in the chat input.
3. Observe that `/create-agent`, `/create-hook`, `/create-instructions`, `/create-prompt`, `/create-skill` and `/init` are absent, while user-level and plugin skills are listed.
4. Start a regular Copilot Chat session and type `/` — the `create-*` commands are listed there.

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.140.0 (stable), commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`, 2026-09-30
- GitHub Copilot extension: 0.68.0
- `@github/copilot-sdk-darwin-arm64`: 1.0.15-preview.4
- OS: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64

### Notes

If this is intentional and the harness is meant to rely on natural-language requests instead, then `init/SKILL.md` and the `user-invocable: false` rationale in `agent-customization/SKILL.md` should be updated, since both currently point users at commands that do not exist in this surface.

issues.title: fix: register extension install commands in Agents window (fixes #339804)
issues.body:
### Summary The Agents (sessions) window throws `command 'workbench.extensions.installExtension' not found` whenever code paths that are shared with the main workbench try to install an extension. The sessions window loads chat UI contributions (via `chat.shared.contribution.js`) and the extension URL handler — both of which call `commandService.executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', ...)` — but it never loads `workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts`, the only place that registered that command. So the command is missing in the sessions window and `_tryExecuteCommand` rejects. Affected 25 users on the current build across Windows, Linux, and Mac. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339804 Recommended reviewer: ``@sandy081`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | not identified — pre-existing architectural gap | | Author | — | | PR | — | | Message | — | | Why | No single commit in the regression range introduced the defect. The producers (`chatAgentRecommendationActions.ts`, `aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts`, `extensionUrlHandler.ts`) and the command registration are both long-lived. The bucket became "new" because the sessions window progressively adopted the shared chat contribution that reaches these producers, while the extensions contribution that registers the command was never added to the sessions bundle. The fix therefore closes the registration gap rather than reverting a commit. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User (Agents window) participant Producer as Chat/URL contribution participant CmdSvc as CommandService participant Registry as CommandsRegistry Note over Registry: ⚠️ Root cause:
workbench extensions.contribution
not loaded in sessions window,
so installExtension is never registered User->>Producer: Trigger install (recommendation / customization / URL) Producer->>CmdSvc: executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', id) CmdSvc->>Registry: getCommand(id) Registry-->>CmdSvc: undefined Note over CmdSvc: 💥 Error thrown:
command 'workbench.extensions.installExtension' not found ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/services/commands/common/commandService.ts` | crash site | L93-L95 (from stack): `if (!command) { return Promise.reject(new Error(\`command '\$\{id}' not found\`)); }` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts` | root cause | L437-L582 (pre-change): the sole registration of `workbench.extensions.installExtension`, only loaded in the main workbench bundle, not in the sessions window. | | `src/vs/sessions/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts` | root cause | Sessions-window extensions contribution registered only a config setting and never registered the install/uninstall commands. | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatAgentRecommendationActions.ts` | producer | L89-L91: `await commandService.executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', recommendation.extensionId, ...)` — loaded in sessions via `chat.shared.contribution`. | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts` | producer | L471: `await accessor.get(ICommandService).executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', CHAT_CUSTOMIZATION_EXTENSION_ID, { enable: true })`. | | `src/vs/workbench/services/extensions/browser/extensionUrlHandler.ts` | producer | L276: `await this.commandService.executeCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension', extensionId, ...)` — loaded in sessions via `sessions.common.main.ts`. | ### Repro Steps 1. Open the Agents (sessions) window. 2. Invoke any flow that installs an extension from shared chat UI — e.g. click an "Install Chat Customization Extension" / agent-recommendation install action, or open a `vscode:extension/` URL that the extension URL handler resolves in that window. 3. The command dispatch reaches `CommandService._tryExecuteCommand`, which cannot find `workbench.extensions.installExtension`. 4. Observe the unhandled error `command 'workbench.extensions.installExtension' not found`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** - **New `src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensionsCommands.ts`**: extracted the `workbench.extensions.installExtension`, `workbench.extensions.uninstallExtension`, and `workbench.extensions.search` command registrations verbatim into a dedicated, idempotent `registerExtensionsCommands()` function. This module only touches `CommandsRegistry` and resolves its services lazily via the accessor, so it pulls in no editor panes or view containers and is safe to load in a lightweight window. This is the data-producer fix location: the command must exist wherever its producers run, so registration is made shareable rather than guarding each call site. - **`src/vs/workbench/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts`**: replaced the inlined registrations with a single `registerExtensionsCommands()` call and removed the now-unused imports. Behavior in the main workbench is unchanged — the same commands are registered through the shared module. - **`src/vs/sessions/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts`**: call `registerExtensionsCommands()` so the Agents window registers the same install/uninstall/search commands it already has services for (`IExtensionsWorkbenchService`, `IWorkbenchExtensionManagementService`, and `IExtensionGalleryService` are all registered in the sessions bundle). The command now resolves in that window instead of rejecting. This fixes the defect at its source — the missing registration — rather than suppressing the symptom at the crash site in `commandService.ts` (which must keep throwing for unknown commands so telemetry stays accurate). No `logService.error`/telemetry path is removed, and no `try/catch` masks the error. **Alternatives considered** - Guarding each producer with a "command exists?" check before calling — rejected: it scatters duplicated lifecycle checks across unrelated features and silently drops a capability the sessions window actually supports, rather than fixing the single missing registration. - Importing the whole workbench `extensions.contribution.ts` into the sessions window — rejected: it registers extension editor panes and view containers that do not belong in the Agents window and would bloat/alter that window's UI. **Why this fix**: after this change, `src/vs/sessions/contrib/extensions/browser/extensions.contribution.ts` calls `registerExtensionsCommands()` at load time, so `CommandsRegistry.getCommand('workbench.extensions.installExtension')` returns the handler in the Agents window and `commandService.ts:94` can no longer reject with "command not found". ### Recommended Owner ``@sandy081`` — owns extension management (dominant author of `extensions.contribution.ts`) and is actively working on the Agents/sessions window (agentHost) integration, making him the right owner for a fix that bridges both areas. --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. The changes have been pushed to the branch [`fix/sessions-install-extension-command-339804-1f04c4d3f37765d3`](https://github.com/vscodebot-pr/vscode/tree/fix/sessions-install-extension-command-339804-1f04c4d3f37765d3). > > **Original error:** ERR_API: [2026-10-05T15:21:52.672Z] create pull request in microsoft/vscode failed (attempt 1) Original error: Validation Failed: {"resource":"PullRequest","code":"custom","field":"fork_collab","message":"fork_collab Fork collab can't be granted by someone without permission"} - https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#create-a-pull-request Retryable: false Suggestion: This error cannot be resolved by retrying. Please check the error details and fix the underlying issue. issues.title: fix: wrap agent-host URIs with rootless paths (fixes #339802)
issues.body:
### Summary The Agent Host URI wrapper (`wrapAgentHostUri` in `agentHostUri.ts`) builds a `(redacted) URI that **always** carries a connection authority, but sets its path to `originalUri.path || '/'`. That expression only repairs an *empty* path; it does not repair a non-empty, **rootless** path (one that does not begin with `/`), as opaque URIs such as `untitled:Untitled-1` (path = `Untitled-1`) have. RFC 3986 requires an authority-bearing URI's path to be empty or begin with `/`, so `URI.from`/`_validateUri` throws `[UriError]: If a URI contains an authority component, then the path component must either be empty or begin with a slash`. The throw surfaces as an unhandled error while mapping session customization resources into client space (168 users, 742 hits on `429a4ec7`). Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339802 Recommended reviewer: @aeschli ### Culprit Commit No regression-range commit touched the failing code path. The bug is **pre-existing** in `wrapAgentHostUri`: the `originalUri.path || '/'` guard was written to cover empty paths only and never handled rootless opaque paths. The bucket is classified `new` because the surrounding customization-mapping feature (which first routes opaque URIs through this wrapper) reached the `429a4ec7` build, not because a commit in the range introduced the faulty line. | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | Not identified — pre-existing latent bug in `wrapAgentHostUri` | | Author | n/a | | PR | n/a | | Message | n/a | | Why | The path-validity guard at the producer only handled empty paths; a rootless path combined with the always-present agent-host authority violates RFC 3986. No range commit changed this line. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Pills as agentHostSessionInputPills participant Map as agentHostSessionCustomizations.mapHostUri participant Wrap as wrapAgentHostUri participant URI as URI.from / _validateUri Pills->>Map: map customization resource to client space Map->>Wrap: toAgentHostUri(originalUri, connectionAuthority) Note over Wrap: ⚠️ Root cause:

issues.title: fix: validate chat participant declaration regardless of when clause (fixes #339803)
issues.body:
### Summary `MainThreadChatAgents2.$registerAgent` throws `chatParticipant must be declared in package.json: copilot-cloud-agent` when an extension registers a chat participant whose chat-session contribution is declared in `package.json` but is currently gated off by its `when` clause. The declaration check used `getAllChatSessionContributions()`, which filters out any contribution whose `when` condition is not currently satisfied, so a *declared-but-disabled* participant was treated as *not declared* and the registration threw. Impact: an unhandled error is reported to telemetry (and registration fails) whenever the `copilot-cloud-agent` participant registers while `config.github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.enabled` is false. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#339803 Recommended reviewer: ``@joshspicer`` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`548e73f30b8`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/548e73f30b8015c51ba993a9d0085ff3aff537fe) | | Author | ``@joshspicer`` | | PR | #275918 | | Message | check chatSessionService in $registerAgent (#275918) | | Why | It added `const chatSessionRegistration = this._chatSessionService.getAllChatSessionContributions().find(...)` to gate the throw. `getAllChatSessionContributions()` filters by `_isContributionAvailable` (the `when` clause), so a contribution declared in package.json but disabled by its `when` condition is excluded, making the "declared in package.json" check fail and throw. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as Copilot extension participant EH as ExtHost participant MT as MainThreadChatAgents2.$registerAgent participant CS as ChatSessionsService Ext->>EH: register "copilot-cloud-agent" participant EH->>MT: $registerAgent(id="copilot-cloud-agent") MT->>CS: getAllChatSessionContributions() Note over CS: ⚠️ Root cause:
filters out contributions whose
`when` clause is currently false CS-->>MT: list WITHOUT copilot-cloud-agent Note over MT: 💥 Error thrown:
chatParticipant must be
declared in package.json ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadChatAgents2.ts` | crash site | L351 (from stack): `throw new Error(\`chatParticipant must be declared in package.json: \$\{id}\`)` | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadChatAgents2.ts` | root cause | L343: `const chatSessionRegistration = this._chatSessionService.getAllChatSessionContributions().find(...)` — availability-filtered lookup used as a declaration check | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatSessions/chatSessions.contribution.ts` | producer | L874-L878: `getAllChatSessionContributions()` applies `.filter(entry => this._isContributionAvailable(entry.contribution))` | ### Repro Steps 1. Ensure `github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.enabled` is set to `false` (so the `copilot-cloud-agent` chat-session contribution's `when` clause — `config.github.copilot.chat.cloudAgent.enabled` — evaluates to false). 2. Load the Copilot extension so it calls `vscode.chat.createChatParticipant`/registers the `copilot-cloud-agent` participant. 3. During `$registerAgent`, the declaration check calls `getAllChatSessionContributions()`, which omits the disabled contribution. 4. Observe the thrown error `chatParticipant must be declared in package.json: copilot-cloud-agent` reported to error telemetry. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatSessionsService.ts` + `.../chatSessions/chatSessions.contribution.ts`: add a new `isChatSessionContributionDeclared(chatSessionType)` method that reports whether a contribution (by primary `type` or `alternativeIds`) was *declared*, independent of its `when` clause. It consults `_contributions`/`_alternativeIdMap` directly rather than the availability-filtered `getAllChatSessionContributions()`. - `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadChatAgents2.ts`: replace the availability-filtered `getAllChatSessionContributions().find(...)` with `isChatSessionContributionDeclared(id)`. This fixes the check at the place where the wrong data source was consumed: the guard is meant to assert the participant is *declared in package.json*, which is a declaration fact, not a runtime-availability fact. A `when`-gated-off contribution is still declared, so registration must be allowed. - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/mockChatSessionsService.ts`: implement the new interface method in the mock. **Alternatives considered** - Add a `?.` / early-return guard at the `throw` crash site in `$registerAgent`: rejected because it suppresses the symptom at the crash site rather than correcting the declaration check that produced the wrong decision. - Make `getAllChatSessionContributions()` stop filtering by `when`: rejected because many other callers rely on it returning only currently-available contributions; changing it would regress those consumers. ### Recommended Owner ``@joshspicer`` — author of the culprit commit #275918, active in `microsoft/vscode` within the last 90 days. --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. issues.title: API: expose selected SCM resources to extension commands invoked by keybindings
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Feature request

Provide a supported way for an extension command invoked by a keyboard shortcut to obtain the currently selected file resources in the built-in Source Control Changes view, including multi-selection.

This request is about extension access to SCM resource selection. It does not request a global Ctrl+C override or an integration with a particular chat product.

## Problem and use case

I am developing a local extension that copies selected file references for use in a coding assistant. Users select several staged or unstaged files in the existing Source Control view, press Ctrl+C, then paste those references into the assistant.

The selection works when the command is invoked from `scm/resourceState/context`: the command receives the selected resource states. Invoking the same command through a keybinding does not supply those arguments. Falling back to the active editor URI is incorrect: in our test, seven SCM files were selected but only the active editor file path was copied.

The context-menu workaround works, but does not provide the requested keyboard workflow.

## Minimal reproduction

Register an extension command and contribute it to both a menu and a keybinding:

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "commands": [
      { "command": "example.inspectScmSelection", "title": "Inspect SCM Selection" }
    ],
    "menus": {
      "scm/resourceState/context": [
        { "command": "example.inspectScmSelection", "group": "navigation" }
      ]
    },
    "keybindings": [
      {
        "command": "example.inspectScmSelection",
        "key": "ctrl+alt+c",
        "when": "focusedView == workbench.scm && listFocus && !inputFocus"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```js
vscode.commands.registerCommand('example.inspectScmSelection', (...resources) => {
  const paths = resources.flat().map(resource => resource?.resourceUri?.toString());
  console.log('SCM command arguments:', resources, paths);
});
```

1. Open a Git workspace with several changed files.
2. Select multiple file rows under Staged Changes or Changes.
3. Invoke Inspect SCM Selection from a selected row's context menu: selected resources are supplied.
4. Invoke it with the keybinding while the SCM list has focus: the same selection is not supplied as command arguments.

## Requested capability

A supported query API or command returning selected SCM resource URIs would unblock this. An opt-in mechanism to forward resource context to keybinding commands could also address the use case. I am not requesting a change to existing command argument behavior by default.

Design considerations include selection versus focused item, staged and unstaged entries for the same URI, multiple repositories, tree-view folders, and empty selection. The implementation should not silently substitute the active editor URI for SCM selection.

## Existing implementation

The selection is already available internally in `SCMViewPane.getSelectedResources()`. `RepositoryPaneActionRunner.runAction()` reads that selection and supplies it to menu actions:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmViewPane.ts

SCM menu argument behavior is documented here:

https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/scm-provider#menus

## Related issues

- #24916: broader SCM keyboard-shortcut support. This request specifically concerns extension access to the current SCM multi-selection.
- #207066: Git staging shortcut and focus behavior; related discussion of SCM list context.
- #3553 and #316820: access to built-in Explorer selection; this request concerns the built-in SCM view.
- #72442 (closed as duplicate of #170248): keyboard commands on tree items. #170248 concerns focused items in extension-owned TreeViews, rather than querying built-in SCM selection.

If this SCM API request is already covered by an existing issue, please point me to the preferred tracking issue; I am happy to consolidate there.

## Environment

Observed locally on Windows, VS Code 1.139.1 (x64), commit 04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1, with a local helper extension and the built-in Git provider.

I would be interested in contributing an implementation once the desired scope and API shape are agreed on.

issues.title: Markdown Preview local file links fail in vscode-file provider with JSON parse error
issues.body:
## Description
Clicking relative Markdown Preview links to ordinary local `.txt` or `.ps1` files can fail with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` in VS Code's internal `vscode-file` text content provider.

## Reproduction
1. Open a workspace with non-empty `file_structure.txt` and `file_structure.ps1` files.
2. Add links such as `[map](./file_structure.txt)` and `[generator](./file_structure.ps1)` to Markdown.
3. Open Markdown Preview and click either link.

## Expected
The linked file opens as text in the editor.

## Actual
The window logs a JSON parse error in `provideTextContent` for a `vscode-file://vscode-app/...` URI. The files are valid and non-empty; adding `./` did not help.

## Environment
- VS Code 1.140.0
- Windows desktop
- Markdown Preview

## Workaround
Adding `workbench.editorAssociations` entries mapping `*.txt` and `*.ps1` to `default`, then reloading the window, allowed both links to open. This suggests an issue in the editor/provider routing; root cause is unconfirmed.

issues.title: Git: staging a file with unsaved edits silently stages stale on-disk content (commit/stash already prompt to save)
issues.body:
- VS Code version: 1.140.0
- OS version: Linux x64 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (WSL2, remote Ubuntu-24.04)

Type: Bug

**Summary**
Clicking the stage (+) button on a file that has unsaved edits runs `git add` against the file on disk, so the *old* content gets staged. The editor buffer still holds the new content, leaving the file in `MM` state (staged old + unstaged new). The user then reviews/commits content that differs from what the editor shows.

**Why this is a bug, not a feature request**
The Git extension already guards against this exact situation for **commit** and **stash**, but not for **stage**:

- commit — `git.promptToSaveFilesBeforeCommit` (enum `always|staged|never`, **default `always`**): dialog "…has unsaved changes which won't be included in the commit… Would you like to save it before committing?" → saves, then re-adds.
- stash — `git.promptToSaveFilesBeforeStash` (**default `always`**): same pattern.
- stage — **no equivalent check at all.**

So with default settings, committing a dirty file prompts, but staging the same dirty file silently stages stale content.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Edit a tracked file and do **not** save (keep the dirty dot).
2. In Source Control, click the `+` (Stage Changes) for that file.
3. Compare what got staged against what the editor shows — they differ.

Aggravating, very common setup (staging lands *before* the save):
- `files.autoSave: "onFocusChange"`
- While reviewing a diff, edit the current side, then click `+`.
- Leaving the editor triggers autosave, but the stage command runs against the pre-save disk content; staging completes first, autosave second → stale content staged, file ends in `MM`.
- Two independent async paths (blur→save vs click→`git add`) with no ordering guarantee.

**Expected**
Reuse the same prompt/behavior as commit and stash, ideally behind a new `git.promptToSaveFilesBeforeStage` with identical semantics (`always|staged|never`, default `always`).

To be explicit: I am **not** asking for a silent autosave before staging. Silently flushing a dirty buffer to disk is itself a data-loss risk; a prompt is the right shape and is already VS Code's chosen pattern for commit and stash.

**Actual**
Stale on-disk content is staged with no warning; user must notice the `MM` state and re-stage.

**Code path (main, Oct 2026, commit 16023148)**
- `extensions/git/src/commands.ts` — `@command('git.stage')` → `repository.add(resources)`
- `extensions/git/src/repository.ts` — `add()` → `this.repository.add(resources.map(r => r.fsPath))`
- `extensions/git/src/git.ts` — `add()` → `git add -A <paths>` (reads from disk)
- No dirty-document check anywhere on the stage path.
- Contrast: commit guard at `commands.ts` (uses `git.promptToSaveFilesBeforeCommit`), stash guard at `commands.ts` (uses `git.promptToSaveFilesBeforeStash`).
- Also affects `stageAll` / `stageFile` / `stageSelectedChanges`, which all funnel into `repository.add`.

**Proposed fix**
Factor out the existing dirty-document prompt (already used by commit/stash) into a shared helper and call it from the stage entry points, controlled by `git.promptToSaveFilesBeforeStage` (default `always`), matching commit/stash.

**Related**
- #190315, #104945, #114363, #107452 — history of the commit-side prompt.
