issues.title: Copilot SDK harness receives abap: documents as read-only snapshots while Local can edit them
issues.body:
Type: Bug ## Summary In the same VS Code installation, the Local chat harness can read and edit an ABAP document using its abap: URI, then activate it through ADT MCP. The Copilot SDK harness receives the document as a read-only attachment snapshot and does not appear to expose a capability for reading or editing the original abap: document. Providing the original URI explicitly did not resolve the problem. ## Environment - VS Code: 1.140.0 (user setup) - Commit: 07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74 - @github/copilot: 1.0.89-7 - @github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.15-preview.4 - OS: Windows 11 x64, build 26200 - ABAP document provided by the SAP ADT extension - ADT MCP server running and connected ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open an ABAP program through the SAP ADT extension. The document has an abap: URI, not a local filesystem path. Example URI, with identifying details replaced: abap:/repotree-v1//Local%20Objects%20($TMP)//Source%20Code%20Library/Programs//.prog.abap 2. Start a chat using the Local harness and attach the open document. 3. Ask the agent to modify the program. In my test, Local successfully read and edited the document. It then called ADT MCP activation, which returned: "Activation successful." 4. Start a chat using the Copilot SDK harness and attach the same document. 5. Ask the agent to modify it, and also provide the original abap: URI. ## Actual result In the Copilot SDK session, the attached document is represented by a read-only snapshot under: %APPDATA%\Code\agentSessionData\...\attachments\... The agent reports that it cannot read or edit the original abap: URI with its available tools. ADT MCP connectivity works: the agent successfully listed the configured SAP destination. The apparent problem is source-file access, not MCP connectivity. Observed difference: Local harness: - Reads the original abap: document - Modifies the document successfully - Activates successfully through ADT MCP Copilot SDK harness: - Receives a read-only attachment snapshot - Cannot access the original abap: document - Can still communicate with ADT MCP ## Expected result The Copilot SDK harness should be able to read and edit the original virtual document through the registered VS Code filesystem/document provider, as the Local harness does. If non-file URI editing is not supported, please document this limitation and indicate whether support is planned or any configuration is required. ## Questions - Does the Copilot SDK harness support documents with non-file URI schemes? - Is there a setting that enables access to VS Code virtual documents? - If this is an integration gap, should it be addressed in VS Code's Copilot harness or by the filesystem-provider extension? ## Evidence A screenshot of the successful Local session is attached. It shows: - Reading the document - Editing the ABAP source - Calling ADT MCP activation - "Activation successful." issues.title: Copilot Chat "Local" harness hangs on "Considering…" in VS Code for the Web on a custom HTTPS origin (GitHub login fails)
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No. Only built-in extensions are installed; the bug is in the built-in GitHub Copilot Chat extension (0.68.0), whose `bugs` URL points to this repo.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`), VS Code Server for the Web (`server-linux-x64-web`, `serve-local`), built-in Copilot Chat 0.68.0
- OS Version: server Linux x64 (Kubernetes pod); client macOS 27.0.1, Dia 154.0.8037.98 (Chromium-based, arm64)
- Copilot plan: Copilot Business

### Summary

The same VS Code for the Web server (same `--server-base-path`, same account) behaves differently depending on the browser origin:

| Origin | Extension GitHub auth | Local harness | Copilot harness (Agent Host) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http://localhost:13338/<base-path>/` (port-forward) | `Logged in as <user>` | answers | answers |
| `https://<custom-domain>/<base-path>/` (reverse proxy) | `GitHub login failed` | **hangs on "Considering…" forever** | answers |

On the custom origin, the extension host never gets a Copilot token source. A prompt sent with the **Local** harness never produces a request, and no error is shown. The **Copilot harness** (Agent Host) works in the same window: it receives the GitHub session over AHP (`authenticate`). So a valid GitHub session exists in the workbench, but the Copilot Chat extension's own GitHub login fails.

On the official build this is mostly hidden, because new chats default to the Copilot harness (presumably via the `chat.defaultToCopilotHarness` / `chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness` experiments). It surfaces as soon as the user picks **Local**. It always surfaces on downstream builds that ship without `tasConfig` (e.g. code-server), where those settings stay `false` and every chat hangs.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On a Linux host, start the VS Code Server for the Web (1.140.0) under a sub-path:
   `code-server serve-local --server-base-path=/@user/ws/apps/vscode-web/ --port 13338 --host 127.0.0.1 --accept-server-license-terms --without-connection-token`
2. Expose it through an HTTPS reverse proxy at `https://<custom-domain>/@user/ws/apps/vscode-web/`. In our setup this origin is shared with another web app (Coder's dashboard), which routes to VS Code by path.
3. Open that URL and sign in to GitHub with an account that has a Copilot seat.
4. Open a new chat, switch the harness picker to **Local**, and send `hello`. It stays on "Considering…" forever.
5. Port-forward the same server to `localhost:13338` and open `http://localhost:13338/@user/ws/apps/vscode-web/`. Sign in, open a new chat, pick **Local**, and send `hi`. It answers.

**Expected:** the Local harness works on any origin, or fails with a clear error.
**Actual:** on the custom origin, "Considering…" forever, with no request sent and no error.

### Logs

`GitHub Copilot Chat` output, custom origin:

```
[warning] [LanguageModelAccess] LanguageModel/Embeddings are not available without a Copilot token source
[info] [CopilotCLIModels] Skipping model fetch since there is no Copilot token source
[warning] Unable to fetch remote agents because user is not signed in.
[warning] GitHub login failed        (x5)
[info] Got Copilot token for <user>
[warning] [LanguageModelAccess] LanguageModel/Embeddings are not available without a Copilot token source
```

`GitHub Copilot Chat` output, `localhost` origin (same server, Local harness):

```
[info] Logged in as <user>
[info] Got Copilot token for <user>
[info] ccreq:<id>.copilotmd | success | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 | 889ms | [title]
[info] ccreq:<id>.copilotmd | success | gpt-6-luna | 2105ms | [panel/editAgent]
```

`agenthost.log`, custom origin with the default Copilot harness (works):

```
[info] [Copilot] Auth token updated
[info] [Copilot:<id>] sendMessage called: "hi" (0 attachments)
[info] [Copilot:<id>] Full message received: 19 chars
[info] [Copilot:<id>] Session idle
```

### Additional notes

- The base path is identical in both cases, so `--server-base-path` itself is not the trigger. Only the browser origin differs.
- The model picker is filled by the Agent Host, so the UI looks ready while the Local harness can't serve any request.
- Workaround: `"chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness": true` and `"chat.defaultToCopilotHarness": true`.
- Not tested: a dedicated domain serving only VS Code. I can't tell whether any custom origin is affected, or only one shared with another app.

### Asks

1. Make the Copilot Chat extension's GitHub login (and its Copilot token source) work when the web workbench runs on a custom HTTPS origin, as the Agent Host already does.
2. Fail fast with an actionable error (or fall back to the Copilot harness) when the Local harness has no token source, instead of hanging silently.
3. Clarify whether the Copilot harness becoming the default (today an experiment) is planned for builds without `tasConfig`.

### Related

#293987, #335403, #332129

Type: Feature Request Your recent changes to the Agent workflow in VS Code are making my work harder instead of easier. Previously, I could let the agent work, review the list of modified files, inspect the diffs, and then accept or reject the changes. That was simple, clear, and safe. Now the files are modified directly, the relevant settings are scattered across different places, permissions do not solve the same problem, and I have to look for workarounds just to regain a level of control that used to exist by default. For my development workflow, this is a regression. I do not want an agent to modify my files directly without giving me a clear review step where I can approve or reject the changes afterward. To be clear: these changes are making my work more complicated, wasting my time, and I am fed up with it. I am paying for a tool that is supposed to make my work easier, not for one that removes useful controls and forces me to adapt my workflow around product changes I did not ask for. If this is now the standard workflow, with no proper way to restore file-by-file review and approval, I do not see the point in continuing to pay for this product. issues.title: Copilot: Autopilot permissions auto-approve plans in Plan mode
issues.body:
## Description
When using the Plan agent in VS Code Copilot Chat with permissions set to Autopilot, Copilot proceeds directly to implementation without waiting for me to review and approve the plan. Autopilot appears to automatically approve the plan itself.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Select Plan mode in VS Code Copilot Chat.
2. Set permissions to Autopilot.
3. Submit a request that requires planning and implementation.
4. Observe that implementation starts without explicit plan approval.

## Expected behavior
Plan mode should stop after presenting the plan and wait for explicit approval. Autopilot may approve implementation actions once the plan is approved, but should not approve the plan itself.

## Actual behavior
Implementation starts without an explicit plan approval step when Autopilot permissions are enabled.

## Impact
This makes Plan mode unreliable as a review checkpoint. Permission approval and approval to move from planning into implementation should be separate decisions. I want to review the plan before any implementation begins.

issues.body:
## Type
Bug

## Summary

In VS Code 1.140.0, changing the selected model in an Agent Host chat silently clears the currently selected custom agent. Once the custom agent is cleared, its `tools:` allowlist is no longer applied and the session falls back to the full workspace/global tool registry.

This is provider-independent. I initially noticed it because a MiniMax BYOK provider has a 128-tool limit and began failing after the update, but the same tool-surface expansion occurs with another contributed BYOK provider (OpenCode / Space Bunny) after the custom agent is cleared.

## Environment

- VS Code: **1.140.0** (`07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`, x64)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 7.0.0-38-generic
- Agent Host / Copilot harness
- Custom agents defined in `.github/agents/*.agent.md`
- Example providers used during investigation:
  - `klarkxy.minimax-vscode-copilot` 2.6.0
  - `onesoftqwq.opencode-go-copilot-provider` 1.12.0

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create/select a custom agent with a restricted `tools:` list.
2. Start an Agent Host chat with that custom agent selected.
3. Verify the live tool surface is restricted to the custom agent's tools.
4. Change the selected model in the model picker.
5. Send another request / inspect Agent Host logs and tool surface.

## Actual behavior

On every model switch observed, the Agent Host log shows:

```text
[Copilot] Clearing custom agent selection
[Copilot] Changing model to: <vendor>/<model>

issues.title: [chat-perf] layoutDurationMs regressed 21–39% in 8 chat scenarios
issues.body:
### Summary
:rotating_light: New regression: `layoutDurationMs` increased by 21–39% in 8 chat scenarios (text-only, tool-terminal, large-codeblock, file-links, thinking-response, tool-read-file, mixed-content, tool-edit-file) in the latest nightly. This is a broad, abrupt jump not seen in the previous 6 runs, and is outside normal noise.

### Evidence
- **Current values vs baseline (mean ± stddev):**
  - text-only: 227.7ms ±10.2ms (was 170.8ms ±5.1ms, +33.3%)
  - tool-terminal: 322.3ms ±10.2ms (was 241.1ms ±13.3ms, +33.7%)
  - large-codeblock: 217.6ms ±9.1ms (was 169.2ms ±6.1ms, +28.6%)
  - file-links: 255.1ms ±3.6ms (was 205.5ms ±6.0ms, +24.1%)
  - thinking-response: 213.4ms ±10.6ms (was 154.0ms ±5.1ms, +38.6%)
  - tool-read-file: 273.8ms ±9.3ms (was 223.4ms ±6.3ms, +22.6%)
  - mixed-content: 170.3ms ±8.2ms (was 126.2ms ±4.3ms, +34.9%)
  - tool-edit-file: 193.7ms ±6.4ms (was 160.3ms ±6.9ms, +20.8%)
- **Prior 6 runs:**
  - All scenarios above were stable, with layoutDurationMs within 5–15ms of their baseline means and no upward drift.
  - This jump is abrupt and simultaneous across scenarios, not a gradual trend.
- **Suspect commits:**
  - Several recent merges touch chat/session layout and rendering, notably:
    - 5270ba6 (sessions: Stabilize docked side pane sizing)
    - 1f3057f (sessions: Preserve workbench-level pane sizing)
    - 4ccdb71 (sessions: Synchronize live last turn changes)
    - 38220ea (Improve agent feedback workflows and persistence)
    - 125f1cb (sessions: Add external session visibility banner)
  - These landed between the last good baseline and this regression. Of these, 5270ba6 and 1f3057f are most likely to affect layout performance across scenarios.

### Suggested action
- Bisect between the last good run and this one, focusing on the above session/layout-related commits.
- Profile layoutDurationMs in chat scenarios to pinpoint the cause.
- Revert or optimize the responsible change(s) to restore previous performance.

_No matching open issue or prior alert covers this specific multi-scenario layout regression._

issues.title: worktree disk-usage traversal causes high CPU load

labels.name: freeze-slow-crash-leak
labels.description: VS Code crashing, performance, freeze and memory leak issues

issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A (Agents window / Agent Host)
- VS Code Version: 1.141.0-insider (ae1080a9ed1098a8b532c6cfd50977d784b29e6d)
- OS Version: macOS 15.8.1 (24H32), Apple Silicon
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window with an active Agent Host session
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): N/A
- Logs: Captured an 11.38-second renderer CPU profile with `dbgjs` (8,497 samples).

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Enable `chat.agentHost.ahpJsonlLoggingEnabled`.
2. Open the Agents window and run an Agent Host session that produces sustained protocol traffic.
3. Observe the Agents renderer process in Process Explorer or Activity Monitor.

## Actual

The Agents renderer consumed approximately 274% CPU.

The CPU profile attributed:

- 3.67 seconds (32%) to garbage collection.
- 4.28 seconds (38%) to Chromium/V8 `(program)` work.
- 894 ms of self time to the MessagePort receive callback in `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.mp.ts`.
- Additional significant time to `postMessage`, JSON serialization, UTF-8 encoding, and Agent Host frame logging.

The sampled hot path for incoming frames was:

`MessagePort message` -> `AgentHostIpcChannelTransport._handleFrame` -> `_logFrame` -> `AhpJsonlLogger.log` -> `VSBuffer.fromString` -> UTF-8 `encode`

The profile also showed the corresponding outgoing IPC path spending time in `postMessage`.

`AhpJsonlLogger.log` copies/redacts each protocol message, serializes it, UTF-8 encodes it, queues it, and writes it. With sustained protocol traffic this creates substantial allocation and garbage-collection pressure in the renderer.

No customization telemetry functions appeared in the hot stacks.

## Expected

Agent Host diagnostic logging should not cause the Agents renderer to consume multiple CPU cores under normal protocol traffic. Logging should be bounded, sampled, batched, moved off the renderer, or otherwise avoid serializing and allocating for every frame on the renderer's hot path.

## Additional notes

Disabling `chat.agentHost.ahpJsonlLoggingEnabled` and restarting the Agent Host connection is an immediate mitigation.

issues.title: Test Plan Item: Managed Sandbox Settings Resolution
issues.body:
- [x] Mac OS @aeschli
- [ ] Windows - @digitarald 
- [ ] Linux @hawkticehurst 

Complexity: 4

Authors: @dileepyavan

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&assignees=dileepyavan)


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339645%0A%0A&assignees=dileepyavan)

---
### Test Surfaces

Complete the validation in both:

- **Editor Window** — Use the Chat view in the regular VS Code workbench.
- **Agents Window** — Use a Copilot Agent Host session in the Agents Window.

### Setup

1. Create `managed-settings.json` at the platform-specific location:

   | Platform | Location |
   |---|---|
   | Windows | `%ProgramFiles%\GitHubCopilot\managed-settings.json` |
   | macOS | `/Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json` |
   | Linux | `/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json` |

2. Start with the restrictive profile below:

   ```json
   {
     "sandbox": {
       "enabled": true,
       "allowBypass": false,
       "sandboxMcpServers": true,
       "sandboxLspServers": true,
       "allowDevToolAccess": false,
       "userPolicy": {
         "network": {
           "allowOutbound": false,
           "allowLocalNetwork": false
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

3. Completely reload/restart VS Code after every change to `managed-settings.json` so the file-based managed settings take effect.
4. Start a new Copilot Agent Host session with sandboxing enabled.
5. Configure at least one MCP server and one LSP server that can be invoked during testing.

### Expected Settings Resolution

Validate every managed sandbox setting against a conflicting user setting. Managed restrictions must win, while managed allowances must not make a stricter user preference more permissive.

| Managed setting | Conflicting user setting | Expected resolved value | Expected behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sandbox.enabled: true` | `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled: off` | Sandbox **On** | The session is sandboxed and the UI reflects the enforced state. |
| `sandbox.allowBypass: false` | `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands: true` | Bypass **Off** | Commands cannot leave the sandbox. |
| `sandbox.enabled: true`, with `sandbox.allowBypass` omitted | `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands: true` | Bypass **Off** | Requiring the sandbox without explicitly permitting bypass also disables bypass. |
| `sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowOutbound: false` | `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork: true` | Outbound network **Off** | External network requests are blocked. |
| `sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowLocalNetwork: false` | `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowLocalNetwork: true` | Local network **Off** | Requests to localhost and the local network are blocked. |
| `sandbox.allowDevToolAccess: false` | `chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.allowDevToolAccess: true` | Developer-tool access **Off** | Toolchain directories and caches are not granted automatically. |
| `sandbox.sandboxMcpServers: true` | `chat.agent.sandbox.mcpServers: false` | Sandbox MCP servers **On** | MCP servers run inside the sandbox. |
| `sandbox.sandboxLspServers: true` | `chat.agent.sandbox.lspServers: false` | Sandbox LSP servers **On** | LSP servers run inside the sandbox. |

Then invert each managed value and keep the user setting restrictive. Verify that permissive managed values do not override the user's stricter choice:

| Managed value | Restrictive user value | Expected resolved value |
|---|---|---|
| `sandbox.enabled: false` or omitted | `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled: on` | Sandbox **On** |
| `sandbox.allowBypass: true` | `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` | Bypass **Off** |
| `sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowOutbound: true` | `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork: false` | Outbound network **Off** |
| `sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowLocalNetwork: true` | `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowLocalNetwork: false` | Local network **Off** |
| `sandbox.allowDevToolAccess: true` | `chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.allowDevToolAccess: false` | Developer-tool access **Off** |
| `sandbox.sandboxMcpServers: false` or omitted | `chat.agent.sandbox.mcpServers: true` | Sandbox MCP servers **On** |
| `sandbox.sandboxLspServers: false` or omitted | `chat.agent.sandbox.lspServers: true` | Sandbox LSP servers **On** |

### Validate With `/sandbox policy`

For every row above:

- Reload VS Code after updating `managed-settings.json`.
- Start a new session and run `/sandbox policy` before executing a command.
- Verify the Markdown report shows the expected resolved value and its managed source.
- Verify all seven resolved fields are represented correctly: sandbox enablement, bypass, outbound network, local network, developer-tool access, MCP server sandboxing, and LSP server sandboxing.
- Change one value in `managed-settings.json`, reload VS Code, start a new session, and run `/sandbox policy` again. Verify the report reflects the new effective policy rather than the previous value.

### Validate Runtime Application

After confirming the report, run a command that exercises each resolved setting and verify runtime behavior matches `/sandbox policy`:

| Resolved control | Command or action to run | Expected restrictive result |
|---|---|---|
| Sandbox enabled | Run a normal terminal command and inspect the session sandbox state. | The command runs inside the sandbox. |
| Bypass disabled | Request a command outside the sandbox. | The bypass is rejected or unavailable; the sandbox remains enabled. |
| Outbound network disabled | Run an HTTPS request to an external domain. | The request is blocked. |
| Local network disabled | Start or target a localhost service, then request it from the sandbox. | The localhost/local-network request is blocked. |
| Developer-tool access disabled | Run a tool that depends on a user-level toolchain directory or cache not otherwise allowed. | Access is blocked unless separately permitted by filesystem policy. |
| MCP server sandboxing enabled | Invoke the configured MCP server. | The MCP server runs subject to the sandbox restrictions. |
| LSP server sandboxing enabled | Trigger the configured LSP server through an agent task. | The LSP server runs subject to the sandbox restrictions. |

Repeat with the permissive managed profile and restrictive user values. Verify the runtime still follows the stricter resolved user choice shown by `/sandbox policy`.

### Cross-Surface Validation

- Verify the Editor Window and Agents Window show the same resolved state for sessions using the same managed settings.
- Verify `/sandbox policy` reports the same effective values on both surfaces.
- Verify actual command enforcement matches the report on both surfaces.
- Verify removing `managed-settings.json`, restarting VS Code, and starting a new session removes the managed floor and restores the saved user settings.

### Reporting Problems

If any setting resolves incorrectly, `/sandbox policy` disagrees with actual command behavior, or the Editor Window and Agents Window differ:

- Run **Developer: Export Agent Host Debug Logs**.
- Share the exported Agent Host logs directly in Slack with the failure details, platform, the relevant `managed-settings.json` profile, the conflicting user setting, and the observed `/sandbox policy` result.
- Do not post credentials, tokens, or other secrets.

**Related PRs:** #339058, #339205, #339206, #339401, #339632

issues.body:

- [x] Linux @rzhao271

Complexity: 3

Authors: @dileepyavan

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&assignees=dileepyavan)


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339644%0A%0A&assignees=dileepyavan)

---
### Test Surfaces

Complete the scenarios independently in both:

- **Editor Window** — Open the Chat view in the regular VS Code workbench.
- **Agents Window** — Open a Copilot Agent Host session in the Agents Window.

### Default Scenario

For each test surface:

- Start a new Copilot Agent Host session.
- Open Settings, search for `sandbox`, and enable `chat.agent.sandbox.enabled`.
- Verify `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork` is enabled.
- Ask the agent to open an external website using an integrated browser tool.
- Verify the page loads and the agent can interact with it and capture a screenshot.
- Verify the browser page is isolated to the current agent session.

### Network Restrictions

- Disable `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowNetwork` and ask the agent to open an external website. Verify the request is blocked.
- Re-enable network access and add a domain to `chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains`. Verify requests to that domain are blocked.
- Set `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains` to one domain. Verify that domain loads and requests to other domains are blocked.
- Add the same domain to both the allowed and denied lists. Verify the denied list takes priority.
- Clear the allowed-domain list. Verify it adds no domain restriction, but does not independently enable outbound network access when `allowNetwork` is disabled.

### Page Isolation

- Open an integrated browser page directly as the user.
- Open another page from a different Agent Host session.
- From the current sandboxed session, list browser pages and attempt browser actions and screenshots.
- Verify the session can access only its own isolated agent pages.
- Verify user-owned pages and pages owned by another session are not listed or accessible.

### Settings Validation

- Search Settings for `sandbox` and verify the order is User-Configured Paths, Allowed Domains, and Denied Domains.
- If values exist under the previous network-domain setting IDs, verify they migrate to `chat.agent.sandbox.network.allowedDomains` and `chat.agent.sandbox.network.deniedDomains`.
- Verify an existing value under a new setting ID is not overwritten during migration.

### Scope

Use integrated browser tools for these scenarios. The fetch-page tool is not covered by these sandbox network restrictions.

**Related PR:** #339563

issues.title: Agent host (Copilot): most of the system prompt is re-written to the prompt cache in every session

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

issues.body:
In Copilot agent host sessions, most of the system prompt is written to the provider's prompt cache again in every new session, even when two sessions have the same tools, workspace and settings. One line that differs per session sits in the same cache block as about 20,000 characters of fixed instruction text.

This is a cost and latency inefficiency, not a correctness problem.

## What is sent

The system prompt goes out as two blocks, each with a cache breakpoint. The cut is right after `</environment_limitations>`.

| Block | Contents | Size | Same in every session? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | identity, code-change rules, tips, prohibited actions | 3,069 chars | Yes |
| 2 | environment section, all tool instructions, notifications, file-link rules, progress updates, session folder, commit trailer, closing lines | 23,180 chars | No |

Comparing the first request of two sessions, the tools and block 1 are identical. Block 2 differs in exactly one line:

```
Session folder: /root/.copilot/session-state/ddb0077a-2ad2-4ab7-b4df-cd598d9c6bcb
Session folder: /root/.copilot/session-state/ea14396a-8053-48f8-adec-f90613701dc8
```

A cache block is reused only when everything up to its breakpoint is identical, so block 2 can never be read from another session's cache.

## Measured

VS Code Insiders 1.141.0 (`678d0d87a0`), Copilot agent host session, Claude Opus 5.5, two sessions in identical containers, usage read from the first model request of each session through a logging proxy.

| | Cache read | Cache written |
|---|---|---|
| Session A, first request | 13,878 tokens | 8,520 tokens |
| Session B, first request | 13,878 tokens | 8,751 tokens |

For comparison, the same prompt text sent as one fixed block with the session folder section removed (through the `promptOverrideString` debug setting): the second session's first request read 21,666 tokens and wrote 802.

So each session pays for roughly 8,000 tokens of cache write that could be a cache read. Within a session the block is cached after the first request, so this is a one-time cost per session. It is a small share of a long session and a large share of a short one.

How much this matters outside a benchmark is not measured. Identical containers are the best case for sharing. Real sessions differ in workspace and tool set, so the benefit would mostly go to a user who opens several sessions in the same workspace within the cache lifetime.

## Where the fix would be

Only a handful of sections in block 2 actually vary: the environment section, the session folder, the commit trailer and the text the agent host appends. The rest, about 90% of the block by character count, is fixed for a given tool set. Ordering the fixed sections before the varying ones, with the cache breakpoint between them, would let them be shared.

The block layout is decided by the Copilot runtime, not by VS Code. The agent host does shape it indirectly: it sends its system message in `customize` mode with `identity` and `tool_instructions` overrides (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/prompts/`), and my understanding is that the runtime only uses its stable-sections-first layout for prompts that are not customized that way. So this likely needs a change on the runtime side, or a change in how the agent host contributes its sections. Filing here to track it from the VS Code side.

One thing to keep in mind for any fix: moving sections changes the order the model reads them in, so it should be checked for behavior and not treated as a pure cost change.

issues.title: Background shell output disappears from the Background Shells details while it streams

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Verification succeeded

labels.name: terminal
labels.description: General terminal issues that don't fall under another label

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

issues.body:
<!-- bug_report_template -->

Live output in the Background Shells details shows up and then disappears right after, leaving only the command. It keeps happening while the shell runs, so the output can't really be watched from the details.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In an Agent Host chat with Copilot, ask the agent to run a command in an attached background shell that prints for a while, for example `for i in $(seq 1 60); do printf 'hello\n'; sleep 1; done`.
2. Click the Background Shells pill above the chat input.
3. Open the shell's details.

**Actual:** The terminal in the details shows the output and then disappears right after, leaving only the command header. It gets torn down and rebuilt each time the row's elapsed time updates, which is about once a second during the command's first minute. The same command's terminal in the chat response keeps streaming normally.

**Expected:** The details keep showing the output as it streams, like the tool call's terminal in the chat does.

### What is breaking it

The live output in the details came with #339220. It broke a few hours later, when #339342 changed how dropdown pills cache their hovers:

- [`ChatDropdownPillActionViewItem`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1828c0f07d13581ea1bf58aec83c7416bb38003c/src/vs/workbench/browser/chatDropdownPill.ts#L117-L123) now keeps a hover per entry. Whenever the pill's entries update, it compares the cached entry with the new one and, if they differ, disposes the cached hover's `disposable`.
- [`sameResourceHover`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1828c0f07d13581ea1bf58aec83c7416bb38003c/src/vs/workbench/browser/chatDropdownPill.ts#L466-L474) includes `ariaDescription` in that comparison, and the cache [covers any entry](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1828c0f07d13581ea1bf58aec83c7416bb38003c/src/vs/workbench/browser/chatDropdownPill.ts#L391) whose hover uses the `chat-pill-location-hover-panel` class.
- Background shell rows [use that class](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/1828c0f07d13581ea1bf58aec83c7416bb38003c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/sessionBackgroundShellsControl.ts#L146-L154) for the panel width. Their description includes the elapsed time, which changes every second, and their hover `disposable` is what closes the live output terminal.

So every elapsed-time update looks like a different resource to the cache. The output terminal is closed, and the picker builds a new one in the details that are still open.

Seen on macOS in a Code OSS build from `main` after #339342. The code path is present at `1828c0f07d13581ea1bf58aec83c7416bb38003c`. Other platforms have not been tested.

issues.title: Agent host: SessionCustomizationDiscovery retries agents/skills discovery endlessly for sessions whose worktree was deleted
issues.body:
`SessionCustomizationDiscovery` keeps re-running `agents.discover` / `skills.discover` for sessions whose working directory (a git worktree) has since been deleted. Every call fails with `Invalid working directory`, the error is logged and swallowed, and the next file-change event triggers it again. Nothing ever stops it for that session.

Seen in VS Code Insiders 1.140.0 (commit `429a4ec703266abbd31f6886764e4127955bdc9d`), macOS arm64, with agent host Copilot sessions.

## What I see

Four sessions whose worktrees had been deleted (I checked that each path no longer exists on disk) produced **1,944** discovery errors in one ~3-hour `agenthost.log` (1,226 `agents.discover`, 718 `skills.discover`). Each path was retried about 417 times in 20 minutes:

| 10-min window | discovery errors |
|---|---|
| 13:40 | 20 |
| 13:50 | 44 |
| 14:00 | 861 |
| 14:10 | 803 |
| 14:20 | 12 |
| 14:40 | 200 |

The 14:00–14:20 spike matches a period when agent sessions were running many tools (`bash`, `apply_patch`, …) and so changing many files.

Verbatim from `agenthost.log`, showing multiple rounds per second for the same four paths:

```
2026-10-04 14:10:00.655 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/message-reordering-issue-logs-analysis
2026-10-04 14:10:00.663 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/session-child-chat-disappearance-issue
2026-10-04 14:10:00.665 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/merge-ahp-session-fix-with-prototype
2026-10-04 14:10:00.668 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode-engineering.worktrees/github-workflow-squid-troubleshooting
2026-10-04 14:10:01.069 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/session-child-chat-disappearance-issue
2026-10-04 14:10:01.202 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/message-reordering-issue-logs-analysis
2026-10-04 14:10:01.202 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/merge-ahp-session-fix-with-prototype
2026-10-04 14:10:01.212 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/session-child-chat-disappearance-issue
2026-10-04 14:10:01.215 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode-engineering.worktrees/github-workflow-squid-troubleshooting
2026-10-04 14:10:02.105 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode-engineering.worktrees/github-workflow-squid-troubleshooting
2026-10-04 14:10:02.105 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request skills.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/message-reordering-issue-logs-analysis
2026-10-04 14:10:02.108 [error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/merge-ahp-session-fix-with-prototype
```

The same thing happened on 2026-10-02 with a different set of deleted worktrees (about 340 errors in the single minute 12:50), for example:

```
[error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request agents.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/hooks-error-investigation-docs
[error] [SessionCustomizationDiscovery] Error during discovery: Request skills.discover failed with message: Invalid working directory, projectPaths: /Users/roblou/code/vscode.worktrees/log-investigation-issue-analysis
```

## Likely cause (from reading `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/sessionCustomizationDiscovery.ts`)

- `onDidFilesChange` → `_scheduleRefresh()` → `_onDidChange.fire()` runs straight away, with no debounce or coalescing, so a burst of file changes from an active agent turns into a burst of rediscoveries.
- `discover()` builds `projectPaths` from `_workingDirectories` without checking that they still exist, then catches the RPC error, logs it, and returns `[]`. There's no back-off, and the session isn't marked as having a missing working directory, so the next change event tries again.

## Why it matters

Each failing call is cheap on its own, but it's one more RPC to `copilot-runtime` on every file-change burst, for every such session. It also floods `agenthost.log`: here it was the largest error source and buried the other logs we were using to investigate high CPU in `copilot-runtime` (#337848).

## Suggestions

1. Debounce/coalesce `_scheduleRefresh`.
2. Skip discovery, or stop re-running it, when the session's working directory no longer exists. Resume it if the directory comes back, for example through a watcher on the parent folder.
3. Log the failure once per session instead of on every attempt.

- VS Code Version: 1.137.0
- OS Version: Linux x64

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Run VS Code via `code serve-web` and open and extension project like the [helloworld sample extension](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-extension-samples/tree/main/helloworld-sample)
2. F5 to run/debug the extension via the dev extension host
3. The extension doesn't load (for example, the "Hello world" command is not loaded)

This appears to be the result of #330308, specifically [the line adding additional conditions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/06a2bc84d0555f4c7ebd176809673e61fa49c6ff#diff-10a490793cdf946af52b08b20f65e837f9344c564486152f3479c1d802e065edR310) to running extension host options from a web payload. This makes sense from a security stance, but makes it impossible to debug extensions when running via `code serve-web`, complicating extension development.

issues.title: Test: Copilot plugin slash commands in Agent Host
issues.body:
Refs: #338982

- [x] anyOS @Giuspepe
- [ ] anyOS @dileepyavan

Complexity: 3

Authors: @aeschli

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339612%0A%0A&assignees=aeschli)

---

Copilot Agent Host sessions support `/plugin` commands for discovering and managing plugins through the Copilot SDK. Commands provide argument completion, formatted results, actionable errors, and progress while mutations run.

## Test setup

1. Open the Agents window.
2. Create a new session using the **Copilot CLI** provider.
3. Ensure GitHub Copilot authentication is active.

## Verify command completion

In a newly created chat, without first sending another request:

- Enter `/plugin ` and verify completion includes `list`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `enable`, `disable`, and `marketplace`.
- Accept `install` from completion and verify plugin suggestions open automatically.
- Verify install suggestions use qualified names such as `plugin@marketplace`.

## Verify marketplace commands

Run:

```text
/plugin marketplace list
```

Verify:

- Included and registered marketplaces are clearly separated.
- Marketplace names and sources are formatted as readable Markdown.

Run:

```text
/plugin marketplace browse awesome-copilot
```

Verify:

- Available plugins are shown as a readable list.
- Plugin names and descriptions are formatted consistently.
- Marketplace-name completion is offered after `/plugin marketplace browse `, `/plugin marketplace update `, and `/plugin marketplace remove `.
- Default and managed marketplaces are not offered for removal.

Run:

```text
/plugin marketplace update awesome-copilot
```

Verify the marketplace refresh succeeds and produces a clear result.

If you have a disposable marketplace repository available, also verify:

```text
/plugin marketplace add <repository>
/plugin marketplace remove <marketplace>
```

For a slow add or remove operation, verify progress is shown and then cleared when the operation completes.

## Verify plugin installation

Choose a plugin from the `awesome-copilot` marketplace that is not currently installed.

Run:

```text
/plugin install <plugin>@awesome-copilot
```

Verify:

- **Installing plugin…** appears while installation is running.
- The final response includes the canonical `plugin@marketplace` identity.
- The installed version is shown when available.
- The number of installed skills is shown.
- Any SDK post-install instructions or deprecation warnings are surfaced.
- `/plugin list` shows the installed plugin.
- Completion for update, disable, and uninstall uses the SDK-recognized plugin identity.

## Verify enable and disable

Run:

```text
/plugin disable <plugin>@awesome-copilot
/plugin list
```

Verify the plugin is reported as disabled.

Then run:

```text
/plugin enable <plugin>@awesome-copilot
/plugin list
```

Verify it is reported as enabled.

Also verify:

- Enable completion offers disabled plugins.
- Disable completion offers enabled plugins.
- Already-enabled and already-disabled operations produce clear guidance rather than silently succeeding.

## Verify update and uninstall

Run:

```text
/plugin update <plugin>@awesome-copilot
```

Verify the result clearly reports whether the plugin was updated and includes the new version when available.

Run:

```text
/plugin uninstall <plugin>@awesome-copilot
```

Verify:

- Progress is shown if the operation takes longer than the progress delay.
- The command reports successful removal.
- The plugin no longer appears in `/plugin list`.
- The plugin is no longer suggested for update, disable, or uninstall.

## Verify errors and recovery guidance

Verify friendly errors for:

- `/plugin install` without a source.
- `/plugin uninstall` without a plugin.
- `/plugin update` without a plugin.
- `/plugin enable` or `/plugin disable` without a plugin.
- Browsing a marketplace that does not exist.
- Installing from a repository that does not contain a valid `plugin.json`.
- Uninstalling or updating a plugin that is not installed.
- Using an ambiguous bare plugin name when the same name exists in multiple marketplaces.

Verify errors do not expose internal RPC details such as:

```text
(sendFailed) Request session.plugins...
```

## Verify accessibility and cancellation

- Verify progress and completion messages are announced by a screen reader.
- Start a slow plugin mutation and cancel the turn.
- Verify progress is cleared and does not reappear after cancellation.
- Start another turn and verify stale progress from the previous command is not shown.

issues.title: Renderer OOM during Copilot external ingest: unbounded file search returns millions of files
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. Post-crash extension-host inspection identifies a pending `GitHub.copilot-chat` file search and its external-ingest initialization call. Extension Bisect and Insiders have not been tested.

- VS Code: 1.140.0 Stable, commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`
- Local OS: macOS 27.0 (26A428), ARM64, 16 GiB RAM
- Electron: 43.7.3
- Remote: Linux container on an SSH host; VS Code Server uses the same commit
- Built-in Copilot Chat: 0.68.0
- Workspace: a large source tree with generated build output

## Problem

The remote workspace window repeatedly crashes with a renderer V8 out-of-memory failure shortly after opening it. Investigation strongly implicates Copilot external-ingest initialization enumerating the entire workspace with an effectively unlimited result count, then sending millions of file matches through the extension-host/renderer search RPC path.

Excluding build output is a practical mitigation, but background indexing should have bounded resource usage and should not take down the editor window when a large directory is not excluded.

## Observed reproduction conditions

1. Open a large source/build workspace in a remote container.
2. Have Copilot external ingest available and enabled.
3. Have build output excluded from `files.watcherExclude`, but not from `search.exclude` or `files.exclude`.
4. Allow background workspace initialization to run.

Three renderer crashes were observed, approximately 2–3 minutes after the respective renderer process started. A standalone synthetic reproduction has not been constructed.

## Sanitized crash and diagnostic evidence

Paths are replaced with `/workspace/PROJECT`. Dates, user identities, host addresses, container identifiers, remote URI authorities and process IDs are omitted. The excerpts below are extracted summaries, not complete raw logs.

### Renderer failures

```text
[crash 1] [error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: crashed, code: 5)
[crash 2] [error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: crashed, code: 5)
[crash 3] [error] CodeWindow: renderer process gone (reason: crashed, code: 5)

macOS crash report summary, common to all three:
  process: Code Helper (Renderer)
  architecture: ARM-64
  exception: EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP
  termination: SIGNAL, code 5
```

Code 5 alone was not used to diagnose OOM. Offline disassembly of the installed Electron framework at the common crash offsets identified the V8 OOM fatal-error path. The nearby code constructs the V8 OOM message and contains the allocation-failure diagnostics. The stripped crash reports' nearest exported symbol names are not reliable function attribution.

### Pending search identified in the surviving remote extension host

A temporary inspector session and an on-container heap snapshot showed suspended `_findFilesImpl` and `reconcileDbFiles` async frames. Extracted search metadata:

```text
extension: GitHub.copilot-chat
API: findFiles2
folder: /workspace/PROJECT
filePattern: **/*
maxResults: 9007199254740991  (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)
disregardExcludeSettings: false
disregardSearchExcludeSettings: false
external-ingest frame: ExternalIngestIndex.reconcileDbFiles
```

Parsing retained Buffer objects as VS Code RPC messages yielded:

```text
method: $handleFileMatch
single provider/session pair: 2 / 4
retained messages: 4,845
serialized message bytes: 1,310,327,224
file-result entries: 2,480,599
entries under /workspace/PROJECT/out/: 2,027,288

RPC-wide pending replies: 4,858
RPC-wide unacknowledged requests: 4,857
```

These are retained-message and result-entry counts, not a unique-file count or a measurement of renderer heap use. The snapshot was taken after the renderer had crashed, so some queue retention may be a consequence of the disconnect.

A remote extension-host memory sample was approximately 6.0 GB RSS, 0.20 GB JS heap used, and 1.31 GB ArrayBuffers. The RSS figure should not be interpreted as 6 GB of JavaScript objects. The container remained running, with `OOMKilled=false`, cgroup `oom_kill=0` and `memory.failcnt=0`.

A separate remote watcher warning was also present:

```text
[error] [File Watcher ('parcel')] Inotify limit reached (ENOSPC) (path: /workspace/PROJECT)
```

That is an additional resource issue; the large retained messages examined here were file-search results, not file-event notifications.

## Source path at the affected VS Code commit

The installed Copilot bundle matches the source at the version's commit:

- [ExternalIngestIndex initialization](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/extensions/copilot/src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/node/codeSearch/externalIngestIndex.ts#L306) awaits reconciliation.
- [reconcileDbFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/extensions/copilot/src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/node/codeSearch/externalIngestIndex.ts#L911) requests `**/*` with `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` and `CancellationToken.None`. Per-file `shouldTrackFile` filtering happens after the full search returns.
- [SearchOperation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadSearch.ts#L107) stores matches in a Map; [handleFindMatch](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadSearch.ts#L193) revives incoming URIs and adds matches; completion [materializes the result array](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74/src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadSearch.ts#L182).

Together, the pending call, unbounded source query and retained result messages strongly implicate this path. A live renderer allocation profile and an isolated before/after reproduction are still missing, so this report does not claim that every retained byte caused the renderer failure.

## Expected behavior / areas to investigate

- Bound background indexing's file enumeration and transport memory, or use an incremental/batched indexing API that does not retain the complete result set in the renderer.
- Apply relevant indexing eligibility filters before full result materialization where feasible.
- Propagate cancellation and provide backpressure/resource limits so an oversized background scan can stop or degrade gracefully.
- Keep the editor usable and report an indexing limit/error instead of crashing the renderer.

## Mitigation applied, not yet validated

The following settings have been added to the affected remote workspace. A fresh-window stability test after this change has not yet been performed.

```json
{
  "github.copilot.chat.workspace.codeSearchExternalIngest.enabled": false,
  "search.exclude": {
    "**/out/**": true,
    "**/.repo/**": true,
    "**/prebuilts/**": true
  }
}
```

The affected call respects search exclusions. Existing `files.watcherExclude` rules do not govern file-search results.

Related: #325919 describes renderer OOM from another unbounded file-search caller, the Sessions telemetry file-count path. This report concerns Copilot external-ingest reconciliation; it does not assume that the two triggers are identical.

## Privacy

Only sanitized excerpts and aggregate measurements are included. No raw heap snapshot, full crash archive, source-file contents, private repository URLs, credentials, encoded remote authorities or complete extension logs are attached. The temporary remote heap snapshot was deleted and the inspector port was closed after analysis.

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. Extensions and Git are disabled in the reproduction.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev, `678d0d87a02696c2b93c52cef30d579a3c7fb0e8`. The implicated Explorer/tree sources are unchanged on checked main `24a41178148f72f49e4ac0756ddb3b5347429a91`.
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise x64.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create sibling `source` and `destination` folders. Put 1,024 small TypeScript files in `source`, totaling 23,552 bytes; leave `destination` empty.
2. Expand the folders in Explorer, select 32 source files, and drag them to `destination`.
3. Observe the repeated Explorer updates while the move completes. Restore the files and repeat.
4. Compare the same 32-file operation with the parent folders collapsed. The controlled measurements invoke the same production Explorer bulk-edit entry point; separate real drag baselines verify the user action.

**Expected:** A bulk move should not repeatedly refresh and render the same parent folders for every file. The folders should remain expanded and show the exact moved files promptly.

**Observed:** Three fresh windows plus an independent fourth reproduction show approximately **1.9 seconds expanded versus 0.2 seconds collapsed**.

| Fresh window | Expanded median | Collapsed-parent control |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1,962.9 ms | 200.0 ms |
| 2 | 1,810.2 ms | 198.5 ms |
| 3 | 1,935.7 ms | 197.7 ms |
| Independent repeat | 1,896.4 ms | 203.4 ms |

One warmup plus five measured samples per arm. Every source/destination name is checked in both the live model and on disk; all checks pass. Real 32-file drag baselines take 2.31-2.45 seconds including automation.

### Cause and measurement boundary

[`ExplorerService.onDidRunOperation`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/24a41178148f72f49e4ac0756ddb3b5347429a91/src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/explorerService.ts#L413) refreshes both parents for each individual move. Separate precise coverage records **64 parent refreshes and 64 tree renders for one 32-file batch**. CPU profiles locate the repeated work in tree rendering and Explorer filtering; profiled samples are excluded from the timing table.

Primary timings measure the asynchronous bulk-edit operation, not a single renderer long task. The live model and file-event backlog must be stable for 600 ms before each sample. Control re-expansion is outside the primary timing. Collapsing folders is a diagnostic control, not the proposed fix.

### Scope

This is not an LRU/capacity proposal or memory-leak claim. It is distinct from #165271, whose external Python moves use file-watcher notifications rather than this Explorer-owned bulk-edit path. It also does not establish the five-second initial-expansion report #243608.

Installed Insiders comparison was not performed because its pending update was left untouched.

issues.body:
Type: Bug ## Description When using Ctrl+I (Inline Chat) to edit a Python file in a VS Code WSL workspace, Copilot generates a response successfully, but fails when applying the patch. The logs suggest the patch tool passes the Linux workspace path to a Windows-side file operation, where it is interpreted as a Windows path and cannot be found. ## Environment - OS: Windows 11 - Remote environment: WSL, Ubuntu 22.04 - VS Code: 1.140.0 - GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.68.0 - Workspace: opened in a VS Code window connected to WSL - File: `hello.py` in the workspace - Models observed: `mai-code-1.1-flash` and `gpt-6-luna` ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open the project in WSL using VS Code (`code .`). 2. Open `hello.py` from the workspace Explorer. 3. Use Ctrl+I to request a simple edit, such as adding `print("Hello, World!")` at the end of the file. 4. Allow Copilot to generate and apply the edit. ## Expected behavior Copilot applies the generated change to the open file in the WSL workspace. ## Actual behavior Copilot generates a response, but the edit is not applied. Inline Chat reports that the requested change could not be applied, then aborts after repeated attempts. ## Relevant log excerpts At one point, the patch tool rejected paths as non-absolute: `Invalid input path: home/.../hello.py. Be sure to use an absolute path.` On a later attempt, the path was treated as a Windows path and could not be found: `Healed error: Error: File not found: \home\...\hello.py, original error: Error: File not found: \home\...\hello.py` The logs then show: `Aborting inline chat edit: too many failed edit attempts` and, on the latest attempt: `[InlineChat], BAIL_OUT because of needsExitTool` ## Additional detail The GitHub Copilot Chat extension can be found via Extensions search, but it does not appear under either the Local - Installed or WSL: Ubuntu-22.04 - Installed groups. Its details page shows “Disable AI Features.” The extension installation location is therefore unclear. issues.title: Custom `LanguageModelChatProvider` with `imageInput: true` still blocks pasted images ("does not support images")

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
# Bug report: Custom `LanguageModelChatProvider` with `imageInput: true` still blocks pasted images ("does not support images")

## Summary

A BYOK model contributed via a custom `vscode.LanguageModelChatProvider` (not `chatLanguageModels.json`) that declares `capabilities.imageInput: true` is correctly recognized as vision-capable in VS Code's own *Manage Models* / model-info UI (shown with the "vision" badge), but pasting/attaching an image into Copilot Chat while that model is selected still shows a strikethrough attachment with a "`<model>` does not support images" tooltip, identical to what's shown for a model that does **not** declare image support.

## Environment

- VS Code: `1.140.0` (commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`), `x64`
- OS: Windows
- Extension: custom in-development extension implementing `vscode.LanguageModelChatProvider` directly (registered via `contributes.languageModelChatProviders`, vendor id `anythingllm`), not a `chatLanguageModels.json`-configured custom endpoint
- Reproduced in a fresh Extension Development Host (`--extensionDevelopmentPath`, `--disable-extensions`), launched via `F5`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Implement `provideLanguageModelChatInformation` to return a model with:
   ```ts
   capabilities: {
     toolCalling: true,
     imageInput: true,
   },
   ```
2. Launch the Extension Development Host (`F5`) and open Copilot Chat.
3. Select the custom model in the model picker.
4. Confirm the model shows vision/image support in the model-info UI (e.g. via *Manage Models*).
5. Paste an image (clipboard paste) into the chat input.

## Expected behavior

The image attachment is accepted (no strikethrough), consistent with the model's declared `imageInput: true` capability, and the image is forwarded to `provideLanguageModelChatResponse` as a `LanguageModelDataPart` in the user message's `content`.

## Actual behavior

The pasted image chip is shown with a strikethrough and the tooltip "`<model-name>` does not support images", exactly as if `imageInput` were `false`.

## Diagnostic evidence collected

- The extension's own output channel confirms `provideLanguageModelChatInformation` is being called and is returning the model with `imageInput: true` (logged capability counts / returned model count match expectations).
- VS Code's own *Manage Models* UI independently shows "vision" support for this same model — i.e. the capability **is** being read and surfaced correctly somewhere in VS Code's UI, just not enforced consistently by the chat input's attach/paste gating.
- Switching the active model selection to a different, built-in Copilot model (e.g. GPT-4o/GPT-5) in the **same** window immediately allows the same image to be pasted without a strikethrough. Switching back to the custom BYOK model reproduces the strikethrough again — this rules out a general Copilot/vision-entitlement problem and isolates it to this specific model/provider.

## What was ruled out

All of the following were tried live and made **no difference** to the outcome:

- Running the extension's own "refresh models" command (which fires `onDidChangeLanguageModelChatInformation` to force VS Code to re-query `provideLanguageModelChatInformation`).
- Starting a brand-new Copilot Chat conversation tab and reselecting the model there.
- Toggling the model off and back on in *Manage Models*.
- A full stop/restart of the Extension Development Host (not just a new chat tab — the whole process was killed and relaunched via `F5`).
- Confirming the user is signed in to GitHub/Copilot in that window (this was explicitly checked, since it's a known factor in related reports — see below).

## Related issues

These describe closely related symptoms for BYOK/custom-provider vision support, but neither is an exact match for this specific combination (capability correctly shown in the model-info UI, yet still blocked at paste time, persisting on 1.140.0 — well after the fixes referenced below):

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329560 — "BYOK model can not use vision in 1.132 version" (image data part missing from the message payload on custom endpoints/providers; fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329646, confirmed working by the reporter on a later release)
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/319255 — "Custom Endpoint vision attachments stop working when using BYOK without GitHub sign-in" (closed/resolved)
- A later comment on #329560 (2026-08-20) reports the issue "still occuring" in one specific BYOK usage mode even after the fix shipped, suggesting there may be more than one code path involved.

## Possible cause (speculative)

Given the capability is read correctly for display purposes (model-info/"Manage Models") but not honored by the chat input's paste-gating check, these two UI surfaces may be consulting different/desynced copies of the model's `LanguageModelChatInformation` (e.g. one freshly queried, one cached from an earlier resolution), or the paste-gating check may not yet have been updated to cover extension-registered `LanguageModelChatProvider`s the same way it covers `chatLanguageModels.json`-configured endpoints.

## Impact

Any extension that implements `vscode.LanguageModelChatProvider` directly and wants to support image input currently cannot do so reliably from the user's perspective, even though the documented API contract (`capabilities.imageInput: true`) is implemented correctly on the extension side.

issues.title: Agent sessions with BYOK models: tool-result images (e.g. `view` tool) are silently dropped before reaching the model — source-level root cause, regression shipped in 1.132.0

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: bundled (VS Code 1.140.0)
- VS Code Version: 1.140.0 (also source-verified on current `main`, commit `24a4117`)
- OS Version: Windows 10 (protocol-agnostic; reproduces on any OS)
- Feature: agent mode — tool result pipeline for BYOK (OpenAI-compatible) models
- Selected model: any BYOK vision-capable model via custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (verified via a local logging proxy against DeepSeek / StepFun / Mimo endpoints)
- Logs: outgoing request bodies captured at a local OpenAI-compatible proxy — the tool message contains only a 31-char text receipt, no image part (details below)
- Relates to #339439 (same symptom reported from a CLI agent session with black-box evidence; this report adds the source-level root cause and the git-verified regression window)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a BYOK provider with an OpenAI-compatible base URL, model declares image input support (a request-logging proxy makes the evidence visible).
2. Start an agent session with that model.
3. Ask the model to look at an image file — it invokes the `view` tool.
4. Inspect the outgoing request body: the tool result is only `"Viewed image file successfully."` — no image content part anywhere.
5. Contrast: attach the same image directly to the user prompt → the request contains a proper image part.

## Actual result

The model receives a 31-character text receipt instead of the image. It correctly reports it received no pixels. The image bytes exist in agent-host session state (base64 payload present), so the loss happens between the agent host and the model request.

## Expected result

Tool-result images are forwarded to the model as image content parts — as the legacy in-extension path still does, and as the Claude-bridge path does. If a model cannot consume images, degrade explicitly with a visible notice instead of silently sending a text receipt.

## Root cause (source-verified on `main` @ `24a4117`): the BYOK LM bridge has no image channel for tool results

The image survives deep into the pipeline — `handleClientToolCallComplete` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts` ~line 2910) correctly extracts `EmbeddedResource` blocks into `binaryResultsForLlm` — then hits **three consecutive drop points**:

1. **Bridge DTO has no image field** — `IByokLmFunctionCallOutputItem.output` is `string` only:
   `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostByokLm.ts` (~line 59)
   ```ts
   export interface IByokLmFunctionCallOutputItem {
       readonly type: 'function_call_output';
       readonly callId: string;
       readonly output: string;   // ← no image channel
   }
   ```
   Compare `IByokLmMessageItem.content: IByokLmContentPart[]` (text | image) — the user-message path *does* have an image channel.

2. **Responses→bridge translation takes text only** — `output: item.output ?? ''`:
   `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/byokResponsesTranslation.ts` (~line 179)

3. **Renderer-side conversion emits text-only LM parts** — `agentHostByokLmHandler.ts` (~line 289):
   ```ts
   case 'function_call_output':
   case 'custom_tool_call_output':
       return {
           role: ChatMessageRole.User,
           content: [{ type: 'tool_result', toolCallId: item.callId,
               value: [{ type: 'text', value: item.output }] }],  // ← no image branch
       };
   ```
   while the user-message conversion **in the same file** (`_toChatMessageParts`, ~line 313) has a full `image_url` branch — this asymmetry is exactly why attaching images to the prompt works while tool-result images do not.

**This is a capability regression of the agent-host bridge**, not a new-code typo:

- The legacy in-extension path still forwards tool-result images today (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts` ~line 514):
  ```ts
  input.push({ type: 'function_call_output', call_id: message.toolCallId, output: asText });
  if (asImages.length) {
      input.push({ role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'input_text', text: 'Image associated with the above tool call:' }, ...asImages] });
  }
  ```
- The Claude-bridge path converts them too (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/clientTools/claudeClientToolResult.ts` ~line 52). Only the OpenAI-compatible BYOK LM bridge lacks the channel.

## Regression window (git-verified)

- `26b7c6b` (2026-06-23): bridge born text-only ("agentHost: add opt-in BYOK language-model bridge") — opt-in, no user impact.
- `2c549ee` (2026-07-29): "Enable Agent Host migration settings by default" flips `chat.agentHost.enabled` to `true`.
- Verified by diffing the actual tag sources:
  - **1.131.0** (2026-07-27): default `!isWeb && product.quality !== 'stable'` → stable users on legacy path, tool-result images work.
  - **1.132.0** (2026-08-04): default `true` → stable users moved to the bridge → tool-result images dropped.
- **Last good stable: 1.131.x. First broken: 1.132.0.** Insiders affected earlier (~late June builds).
- On current `main` the `chat.agentHost.enabled` setting is gone (`agentHostEnablementService` enables the host unconditionally on desktop), so recent builds have **no configuration fallback**.

## Workaround

Attach the image directly to the user prompt instead of letting the model call `view`.

issues.title: Test: Send messages between chats
issues.body:
Refs: [#339298](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339298), [#335540](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335540)

- [x] anyOS @aiday-mar
- [ ] anyOS @amunger

Complexity: 4

Authors: @sandy081


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339594%0A%0A&assignees=sandy081)

---

The existing `send_message` tool has been enhanced to give agents more control over messages sent to another chat.

## What the tool supports

- **Queue:** send a message as a separate turn. It starts immediately if the receiving chat is idle; otherwise it waits. Multiple queued messages run in order.
- **Steer:** send a correction to the receiving chat's active turn, rather than queue a separate turn.
- **Replace:** change a message the sending chat queued while it is still pending, keeping its place in the queue.
- **Cancel:** remove a message the sending chat queued while it is still pending, without stopping the current task.

A message that has started processing can no longer be replaced or cancelled as a pending message. Already-delivered steering cannot be retracted. Sending is asynchronous: the tool does not wait for the receiving chat's reply.

## Set up

In the Agents Window, create a session on a workspace. In that session, send this prompt to create a peer chat:

> Create another chat in this session, in the same workspace, and say hi.

Open the main chat and the peer chat side by side. Use the first to send instructions and watch what happens in the second.

The following scenarios are suggestions. Feel free to follow your own scenarios to exercise these behaviors.

## Send work and queue a follow-up

In the first chat, ask:

> Use send_message to ask the other chat to wait for 30 seconds, then write the alphabet from a to z.

While the second chat is waiting, ask the first:

> After that, queue another message asking it to write the alphabet in reverse.

Check that the second chat receives the first request and runs the follow-up as a separate turn afterward, rather than interrupting the first request.

## Replace a queued message

Repeat the waiting task and queue the reverse-alphabet follow-up. Before it starts, tell the first chat:

> Replace that queued message: ask it to write a to u instead of the reverse alphabet.

Check that the pending message is replaced, not duplicated, and only the replacement runs in the original queue position.

## Cancel a queued message

Repeat with a fresh waiting task and queued follow-up, then tell the first chat:

> Cancel that queued follow-up.

Check that the follow-up disappears and never runs, while the current task continues.

For replacement and cancellation, expand the tool result to confirm the outcome rather than relying only on the agent's reply. If the follow-up has already started, it is too late to mutate it as a pending message; repeat with a fresh wait to exercise the pending case.

## Steer work already in progress

Start another waiting task that will write ten lines. While the second chat is working, tell the first:

> Use send_message to steer the other chat's current work: write fifteen lines instead of ten. Do not queue a separate follow-up.

Check that the correction reaches the current work rather than waiting as another queued turn. The second chat should take the correction into account before answering. Do not expect a running wait command to stop instantly.

Feel free to try your own scenarios, such as counting numbers, listing animal names or coordinating small disposable workspace tasks. Check that messages reach the intended chat, queued work stays in order, and the tool clearly reports when a message has already started and cannot be replaced or cancelled.

issues.title: Test: Read and last-modified state in Agents Window
issues.body:
Refs: [#339500](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339500), [#338969](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/338969)

- [ ] anyOS @justschen
- [x] anyOS @houghj16

Complexity: 3

Authors: @sandy081


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23339593%0A%0A&assignees=sandy081)

---

Each chat, including the main chat, shows its own read status and last-modified time.

## Set up

In the Agents Window, have different kinds of sessions available, including single-chat and multi-chat sessions. Include both new and existing sessions.

## Read one chat without reading another

Send prompts in different chats and switch away while they respond. Check that the chats show unread responses. Open one chat: it should become read without marking other chats read.

Repeat with the main chat and peers in a multi-chat session. Each chat should show its own read status independently. An unread peer must not make the main chat appear unread.

## Mark the whole session as read

With unread responses in the main chat and multiple peer chats, use Mark as Read on the session. Check that the main chat and all its peer chats become read, while chats in other sessions remain unchanged. This is a session-level action, not an action on individual chats. Also check it on a single-chat session.

## Keep last-modified times independent

Send prompts in different chats at distinguishable times. Check that each chat's last-modified time updates for its own conversation, not when another chat changes.

Repeat with the main chat and peers. The main chat must not inherit a peer's last-modified time, and peers must not inherit each other's times. Also check single-chat sessions.

## Leave and return

Switch between chats, reload the Agents Window, then restart after the conversations finish. Check that each chat retains its own read status and last-modified time. Include previously read existing chats: they should not unexpectedly become unread after reload or restart.

Keep testing focused on these two fields.
