issues.title: Expose the chat permission level (Default / Allow all / Autopilot) in agent hook input
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
### Problem

A `PreToolUse` hook can return `allow`, `deny` or `ask`. We verified on all three permission levels (Default, Allow all, Autopilot) that:
- a hook `allow` skips VS Code's own confirmation;
- a hook `ask` always shows a confirmation, even under Allow all and Autopilot.

That is a safe default, but a policy hook cannot adapt to the level the user chose, because the hook input (`timestamp`, `hook_event_name`, `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_use_id`, `cwd`) does not include it.

Our use case: a security hook asks for confirmation on operations that are risky but legitimate, such as a command outside a per-agent allowlist, and denies operations that must never run. Under Default, `ask` is what we want. Under Allow all or Autopilot, the user has explicitly chosen to skip confirmations, and the hook's `ask` prompts become the main source of interruptions. We would like to turn those `ask` into `allow` in these modes, while keeping every `deny`.

### Why the workaround is not safe

VS Code records the level for each request in the chat session file (`modeInfo.permissionLevel`). We tried reading it from the hook, but writes to that file are deferred and batched. We observed a request made under Allow all and the next request made under Default appended in a single write, after the second request had started. A hook reading the file during a request can therefore see a stale level. When the user switches from Allow all back to Default, the hook would relax its checks right after the user turned confirmations back on. Reading undocumented internal storage is also fragile across versions.

### Proposal

Add the effective permission level of the request to the common hook input, using the value VS Code already records, for example:

```json
"permission_level": "default" | "autoApprove" | "autopilot"
```

For tool calls made inside a subagent, the value should be the level actually applied to that call (see #329564 on subsessions inheriting the parent level).

### Alternative

Let the hook delegate the decision instead of exposing the level: a hook result meaning "ask only if the current permission level would ask anyway", for example `"permissionDecision": "ask"` with a `"respectAutoApprove": true` flag. VS Code keeps the logic, and the hook never needs to know the level.

### Security considerations

The field only lets a hook relax its own `ask` in modes where the user already chose to skip confirmations. It cannot override a `deny`, and VS Code remains the source of truth for the level.

### Related

- #293631 - agent identifier in hook input
- #301152 - `model` field in hook input
- #297815 - Allow all and Autopilot behavior
- github/copilot-sdk#2810 - same request for the Copilot SDK, where hooks are moving

### Environment

VS Code 1.140.0 (07f806f), Windows x64.

issues.title: Incorrect handling of completions in the Debug REPL

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.141.0 (run from source code, commit 5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35)
- OS Version: Windows 11

The debug console has some bugs and deviations from the DAP w.r.t. the replacement range of a completion item:

**1. Bug: Debug REPL ignores `item.start` from DAP completions.**

The [replacement range calculation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/repl.ts#L282) always replaces `length` characters immediately before the cursor. An explicit `item.start` is used for filtering, but not for the edit itself.

This makes it impossible to consume/overwrite text behind the current cursor, even though this should be possible according to the DAP.

Expected behavior: when `item.start` is provided, replace from `item.start` to `item.start + item.length`. I implemented this [here](https://github.com/ManuelHentschel/vscode/blob/621f9ec3b8f0c6342dedf7091647476e20e31ee8/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/repl.ts#L301-L305) and can provide a PR.

**2. Bug: Multiline history completions duplicate preceding lines.**

This is a separate bug in VS Code's own history suggestions, rather than a DAP adapter issue.
The [history replacement range](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/repl.ts#L319) is limited to the current line by `position.delta()`, while the inserted text contains the entire history entry.

To reproduce: With a Python debug session active and `debug.console.historySuggestions` enabled, execute in the REPL:

```python
if True:
    print(0)
```

Then enter the following, with `|` marking the cursor:

```python
if True:
    pr|
```

Accept the history suggestion for the previously executed command. The resulting input is:

```python
if True:
if True:
    print(0)
```

Expected behavior: complete the command once, or withhold the suggestion if its replacement range is unsupported. Accepting a history suggestion should not duplicate preceding lines.

**3. Clarification needed: deviations from the DAP**

Some behavior w.r.t. replaced ranges deviates from the DAP but is consistent otherwise.
This should be clarified or the DAP should be adapted accordingly:

1. Vscode uses zero-based indexing for `item.start`, but advertises `columnsStartAt1: true`,
which implies 1-based indexing for `item.start` according to the [DAP definition](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/621f9ec3b8f0c6342dedf7091647476e20e31ee8/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/common/debugProtocol.d.ts#L2326).


2. If `item.start` is omitted, vscode replaces `length` characters up to the cursor.
The [DAP definition](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/621f9ec3b8f0c6342dedf7091647476e20e31ee8/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/common/debugProtocol.d.ts#L2326) specifies that it should instead default to the cursor position.

3. Vscode only handles single-line replacement ranges correctly. Being single-line is required for [internal completion representations](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35/src/vs/editor/common/languages.ts#L615-L616), but not stated in the DAP. The [related code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/5e86c7c4c2eb99b22e631e0aa4eb05f6b8b53f35/src/vs/workbench/contrib/debug/browser/repl.ts#L282-L322) mixes offset- and position-based range computations, which leads to messy behavior for multi-line ranges. A clean implementation should either filter out multi-line ranges early, or handle them correctly, leaving them to be filtered out later.

As far as I'm aware, these deviations do not cause problems most of the time, since existing debug adapter implementations seem to work around them. However, they make implementing a new adapter unnecessarily confusing, and should be explicitly stated somewhere or updated in the DAP itself.

Related topics:
- https://github.com/microsoft/debug-adapter-protocol/issues/138 (`start`/`length` interpretation)
- https://github.com/microsoft/debug-adapter-protocol/issues/285 (0- vs 1-based indexing)
- https://github.com/mfussenegger/nvim-dap/pull/1507 (similar discussion for nvim-dap)

## Summary

GPT-6 Luna is visible in the VS Code Agents window model picker, but every request fails when using my ChatGPT subscription.

## Environment

- ChatGPT plan: Plus

1. Enable `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled`.
2. Open the VS Code Agents window.

4. Start a Codex Agent Host session.
5. Select GPT-6 Luna (possibly all gpt models later than 5.6 generation).
6. Send any prompt.

The request fails immediately with the 400 error above.

GPT-6 Luna should run through my ChatGPT Plus subscription. The same account can use GPT-6 Luna through the standalone OpenAI Codex extension.

releases.name: February 2026
releases.body:
Welcome to the February 2026 release of Visual Studio Code. This release makes agents practical for longer-running and more complex tasks, giving you more control and visibility, new ways to extend agents, and smarter session management.

[Agent plugins](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_agent-plugins-experimental): install prepackaged bundles of skills, tools, and hooks from the Extensions view

[Agentic browser tools](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_agentic-browser-tools-experimental): let the agent drive the browser to interact with your app and verify its own changes

[Session memory](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_session-memory-for-plans): persist plans and guidance across conversation turns

[Context compaction](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_context-compaction): manually compact conversation history to free up context space

[Fork a chat session](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_fork-a-chat-session): create a new, independent session that inherits conversation history to explore alternative approaches

[Agent Debug panel](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_agent-debug-panel-preview): get real-time visibility into agent events, tool calls, and loaded customizations

[Chat accessibility](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_accessibility): use chat to its fullest with screen reader improvements, keyboard navigation, and notification signals

[Create agent customizations from chat](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_create-agent-customizations-from-chat): generate prompts, skills, agents, and hooks directly from a conversation

[Kitty graphics protocol](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_terminal): render high-fidelity images directly in the integrated terminal

For the complete release notes go to [Updates](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110) on [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/).

Insiders: Want to see new features as soon as possible? You can download the nightly [Insiders](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders) build and try the latest updates as soon as they are available. And for the latest Visual Studio Code news, updates, and content, follow us on Twitter [@code](https://twitter.com/code)!

Happy Coding!

In this release, we are further evolving VS Code to make it the **home for multi-agent development**. * **Chat UX**: chat just feels better and snappier with faster streaming, improved reasoning results, and a revamped editor inline chat * **Agent Session Management**: it's now easier to delegate tasks to agents across local, background, and cloud and jump in when needed * **Agent Customization**: build your own workflows using agent orchestrations, and have consistent results with Agent Skills and organization-wide customizations * **Agent Extensibility**: reuse your knowledge with Claude agent support and new Anthropic model capabilities, and enjoy rich chat interactions with MCP Apps * **Agent Optimizations**: agents work smarter with Copilot Memory and experience faster code search with external indexing * **Agent Security & Trust**: feel confident running terminal commands with sandboxing and effective auto-approval rules * **Workbench & productivity**: test your apps without leaving the editor with the new integrated browser

Welcome to the June 2025 release of Visual Studio Code. There are many updates in this version that we hope you'll like, some of the key highlights include:

## Chat

- Explore and contribute to the open sourced GitHub Copilot Chat extension ([Read our blog post](https://code.visualstudio.com/blogs/2025/06/30/openSourceAIEditorFirstMilestone)).
- Generate custom instructions that reflect your project's conventions ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_generate-custom-instructions)).
- Use custom modes to tailor chat for tasks like planning or research ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_chat-mode-improvements)).
- Automatically approve selected terminal commands ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_terminal-auto-approval-experimental)).
- Edit and resubmit previous chat requests ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_edit-previous-requests-experimental)).


## MCP

- MCP support is now generally available in VS Code ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_mcp-support-in-vs-code-is-generally-available)).
- Easily install and manage MCP servers with the MCP view and gallery ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_mcp-server-discovery-and-installation)).
- MCP servers as first-class resources in profiles and Settings Sync ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_mcp-servers-as-first-class-resources)).

## Editor experience

- Delegate tasks to Copilot coding agent and let it handle them in the background ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_start-a-coding-agent-session-preview)).
- Scroll the editor on middle click ([Show more](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_102#_scroll-on-middle-click)).
If you'd like to read these release notes online, go to [Updates](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates) on [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/). Insiders: Want to try new features as soon as possible? You can download the nightly [Insiders](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders) build and try the latest updates as soon as they are available.

Welcome to the March 2025 release of Visual Studio Code. There are many updates in this version that we hope you'll like, some of the key highlights include:

* **Agent mode**
  * Agent mode is available in VS Code Stable. Enable it by setting `chat.agent.enabled:true` ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_agent-mode-is-available-in-vs-code-stable)).
  * Extend agent mode with Model Context Protocol (MCP) server tools ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_model-context-protocol-server-support)).
  * Try the new built-in tools in agent mode for fetching web content, finding symbol references, and deep thinking ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_agent-mode-tools)).

* **Code editing**
  * Next Edit Suggestions is now generally available ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_next-edit-suggestions-general-availability)).
  * Benefit from fewer distractions such as diagnostics events while AI edits are applied in the editor ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_ai-edits-improvements)).

* **Chat**
  * Use your own API keys to access more language models in chat (preview) ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_bring-your-own-key-byok-preview)).
  * Easily switch between ask, edit, and agent mode from the unified chat experience ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_unified-chat-experience)).
  * Experience improved workspace search speed and accuracy with instant remote workspace indexing ([more...](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_99#_faster-workspace-searches-with-instant-indexing)).

* **Notebook editing**

releases.name: October 2021
releases.body:
Welcome to the October 2021 release of Visual Studio Code. In addition to releasing a preview of [vscode.dev](https://vscode.dev/), we announced in the [October iteration plan](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/134730) that we would focus on housekeeping GitHub issues and pull requests (see our [issue cleanup guide](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Issue-Grooming)). Across all of our VS Code repositories, we closed (either triaged or fixed) **4163** issues. While we closed issues, you created **2222** new issues. The main [vscode repository](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues) now has **2491** open feature requests and **1246** open bugs. In addition, we closed **194** pull requests.

As in previous years, we used the [live tracker](https://vscode-issue-tracker.netlify.com/) from [Benjamin Lannon](https://github.com/lannonbr) to track our progress:

![Burn down chart of VS Code issues](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-docs/raw/main/release-notes/images/1_62/october-issue-cleanup.png)

Given the focus on shipping `vscode.dev`, not everybody on the team had cycles for clean-up, so some issue clean-up will continue in November. After housekeeping, we also addressed feature requests and community [pull requests](#pull-requests).

**Watch a highlight** of the new features in this version in the VS Code team's release party. You can find the [recording of the event](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IKvtYHfzE3g) on our YouTube channel.

**Join us live** at the [VS Code team's livestream](https://code.visualstudio.com/livestream) on Thursday, September 2 at 8am Pacific (4pm London) to see a demo of what's new in this release, and ask us questions live.

**Insiders:** Want to try new features as soon as possible? You can download the nightly [Insiders](https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders) build and try the latest updates as soon as they are available.
